POSITION-DECOMP balanced only ARENA-13 arm A's 600 FRONTIER matches and left its registered amendment rule
failing by 0.087 theta, with an unregistered imputation suggesting the new contestant would fall to second if
the other 1,200 were balanced too. An imputation is not a measurement. This judges them.

presented FIRST, stored as arm "reversed" beside the 600 already done. Same judge, ensemble reference, rubric

REGISTERED. (1) PRIMARY, and it is ARENA-13's own criterion (1) re-run on order-balanced evidence: on the
13-model board with dual-order TIE-on-flip verdicts for ALL 1,800 arm A matches, the new contestant places 2nd
or 3rd, consistent with its key rank of 2nd. (2) STABILITY: the existing twelve keep their order, Kendall tau
>= 0.90. (3) IS POSITION WEAKER OFF THE FRONTIER? the cross-tier flip rate against the frontier's 0.182, and
the cross-tier win rate presented first against presented second, paired McNemar - the sensitivity ASSUMED the
frontier rates transfer, and this says whether that assumption was sound. (4) WAS THE IMPUTATION CALIBRATED?
the realised theta gap to gemini against the imputed median of -0.326 and its 90% range [-0.367, -0.288] - a
methodological readout the thesis can use, because transition-rate imputation is cheap and worth knowing
whether to trust. (5) ARENA-13 (3) RE-RUN: new-pair key-decidable accuracy under dual order against the 0.85
bar it missed at 0.837 under single order.

judge less room to waver; the direction effect 5-12pp, below the frontier's 13.5pp; the new contestant places
2nd; the realised gap between -0.10 and -0.30, i.e. the imputation OVERSHOOTS because it applied frontier
transition rates to easier matches; new-pair accuracy rises but stays near the bar, 0.84-0.88.
AMENDMENT RULE, fixed now: if it places 2nd or 3rd, ARENA-13 (1) is attributed to the SINGLE-ORDER DESIGN, both
the ARENA-13 and POSITION-DECOMP ledger rows are amended to say so, and "incremental extension must be dual
order" becomes a stated finding of the paper rather than an operational note. If it still places 1st on fully
balanced evidence, position is NOT the explanation, the two remaining candidates are quality the key does not
capture and the trace-generation style, and neither is testable without another REGEN-scale run - which would
be stated as an open limitation rather than bought.

  (2) PASS, unchanged: the twelve keep their ARENA-V2 order, Kendall tau 0.970.

      -0.326 with a 90% range of [-0.367, -0.288] and put the newcomer second in 100% of 200 draws. The
      realised gap is +0.045. The direction was right and the SIZE was wrong by a factor of seven, because the
      imputation applied frontier transition rates to matches whose true flip rate turns out to be a third of
      the frontier's. I labelled it an upper bound, which was correct and load-bearing, but I also wrote that
      "the direction is not in doubt" about it placing second - and it does not place second.
      [Note added 2026-09-14: the imputed gap was -0.326 and the realised gap +0.045, so the GAP's sign
       differs too, not only its size. What was right was the direction of the CORRECTION (the gap shrinks);
       the "right sign, wrong size by 7x" wording elsewhere in this file overstates what survived.] RULE FOR THE
      THESIS: transition-rate imputation from a contested subset forecasts the sign of a correction and not its
      magnitude, because the rates themselves are what vary with contestedness. Cheap forecasts of this shape
      should be reported as sign-only.

      traces under the same conditions and seeing whether it too gains. That is stated as an OPEN LIMITATION
      rather than bought.
  THE HONEST HEADLINE: a 13th contestant can be added to a frozen arena for 1,800 calls without disturbing the
  existing order (tau 0.970, twice confirmed), but its OWN placement is not trustworthy - it over-ranks by one
  position against the key, 85% of that was presentation order, and the residue is unattributed.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/positionfull_outcome.txt; script tools/analysis/position_decomp.py --cross.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before looking at any result, ZERO calls) — SELECTIVE-ORDER: pay for the second order only where it can change anything
POSITION-FULL measured the flip rate at 0.182 on contested frontier matches and 0.055 - below the 0.057
test-retest floor - on cross-tier ones. Dual order therefore buys nothing on pairs whose candidates already
agree, and the answer-disagreement filter identifies those without a key or a judge. Nobody has costed the
resulting policy. Every verdict needed is cached: the x12 MAIN run stores vote1 and vote2_raw for all 9,142
matches, and ARENA-13 arm A now has both orders for its 1,800.
THREE POLICIES, replayed on the same cached calls. (a) ALWAYS DUAL, the production rule, 2 calls per match.
(b) ALWAYS SINGLE, order 1 only, 1 call - ORDER-1 already showed this moves the board and is recorded as a FAIL.
(c) SELECTIVE: single order where the two candidates' own extracted answers AGREE, dual where they DISAGREE.
READOUTS per policy: mean calls per match, 12-model Spearman rho against key accuracy, top-4 key-order
violations, key-decidable accuracy, tie rate.
REGISTERED BAR for (c): rho within 0.005 of ALWAYS DUAL and top-4 violations no worse, at strictly fewer calls.
PREDICTION: selective spends about 1.6 calls per match on the x12 schedule (64% of its matches disagree,
FILTER-BOARD) and about 1.2 on frontier pairs alone (16.9%), with rho within 0.003 of dual and identical
violations, because every match it economises on is one where the two orders agree at the noise floor.
HONEST SCOPE, stated now so the result is not oversold: this is the SAME signal as the shipped matchFilter used
a second way, and the two do not multiply. An arena that can DROP answer-agreeing matches should drop them - a
six-fold saving. Selective dual order is for arenas that must judge every scheduled pair anyway. Both rest on
one measured fact: answer-agreeing pairs carry neither correctness signal nor position sensitivity.
Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/selectiveorder_outcome.txt; script tools/analysis/selective_order.py.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any call) — PLACEBO-ENTRY: does the ARENA-13 PROTOCOL inflate whoever enters through it?
POSITION-FULL left +0.045 theta of the newcomer's over-ranking unattributed, with two candidates I said were
inseparable without another REGEN-scale run - quality the key misses, and trace-generation style. There is a
third I did not name, it is structural, and it is more likely than either.
THE HYPOTHESIS. The newcomer's edges were all judged on DISAGREEMENT-FILTERED questions, where about 80% of
pairs are key-decidable. The twelve's edges come from the unfiltered x12 schedule, where roughly 30% are.
Non-decidable matches produce near-coin-flip verdicts that shrink a model's theta toward the centre of the
board. A model whose edges are all filtered is therefore estimated on sharper evidence and is LESS SHRUNK -
mechanically pushed away from the centre, which for an above-average model means UP. If that is what is
happening, the residue is a scale artefact of mixing filtered and unfiltered edges on one board, and has
nothing to do with the newcomer at all.
ARM A, ZERO CALLS, run first: refit the twelve on (i) all their x12 matches and (ii) only their
answer-disagreeing subset, and compare the SPREAD of theta and each model's distance from the centre. If
filtering inflates the spread, the artefact is demonstrated on models nobody is disputing.
ARM B, 1,200 calls: re-enter gemini-3.1-pro_5-shots - already on the board, original traces, no REGEN involved -
through the ARENA-13 protocol exactly: four opponents (arx_0314, iask_pro, gpt-4o-2024-08-06,
deepseek-chat-v2_5) at 150 matches each, disagreement-filtered candidates, leave-out ensemble reference
excluding both match models, DUAL order. Fit a board in which gemini's x12 edges are REPLACED by these, centre
both boards on the mean theta of the other eleven so the scales are comparable, and compare.
REGISTERED. (1) PRIMARY: gemini's theta under the protocol exceeds its x12 theta by at least +0.045 - the size
of the unexplained residue - with a bootstrap CI excluding zero. (2) the theta spread comparison from arm A.
(3) gemini's key-decidable accuracy under the protocol, as a check that the protocol is not simply easier.
PREDICTIONS: arm A shows a real spread inflation; gemini gains +0.05 to +0.20 under the protocol; and the
newcomer's +0.045 is therefore fully accounted for WITHOUT quality or style.
AMENDMENT RULE: if gemini gains at least +0.045, the ARENA-13 (1) failure is attributed to protocol scale
rather than to the model, both rows are amended a third time, and the paper gains a concrete methodological
warning - NEVER mix filtered and unfiltered edges on one Bradley-Terry board. If gemini does NOT gain, the
residue belongs to the newcomer, trace style becomes the leading candidate, and it stays an open limitation.
Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/placebo_outcome.txt; cache placebo.db; script tools/analysis/placebo_entry.py.

- **SELECTIVE-ORDER OUTCOME (2026-09-14, zero calls): REGISTERED FAIL, and the reason is that I had the
  mechanism backwards. The second order is most needed exactly where I proposed to stop paying for it.**
      policy          calls  calls/match     rho   top-4 violations   ties   decidable accuracy
      ALWAYS DUAL     18,284     2.00      0.9720         2          0.209        0.852
      ALWAYS SINGLE    9,142     1.00      0.9580         3          0.000        0.890
      SELECTIVE       14,418     1.58      0.9580         3          0.075        0.856
  The registered bar was rho within 0.005 of ALWAYS DUAL with no extra violations: rho falls 0.0140 and
  violations rise to 3. FAIL. Note precisely what happened - SELECTIVE spends 58% more calls than ALWAYS SINGLE
  and buys EXACTLY the same board (rho 0.9580, 3 violations). Every point of the dual rule's advantage lives in
  the matches SELECTIVE economised on.
  THE DIAGNOSTIC, and it is the finding worth keeping:
      candidates DISAGREE  n=5,276 | flip 0.105 | key-decidable 0.778 | single order names a winner on 0.967, the longer answer 69%
      candidates AGREE     n=3,866 | flip 0.192 | key-decidable 0.104 | single order names a winner on 0.784, the longer answer 78%
      The two orders disagree almost TWICE as often on answer-AGREEING pairs. Those pairs are 10.4%
      key-decidable, so there is no correct verdict for a single order to find; it invents one 78% of the time
      and gives it to the longer answer in 78% of those. Only the dual rule's abstention suppresses that. This
      is ORDER-1's conclusion ("the dual rule's abstention is what makes the board order-invariant") and
      FRONTIER's invented-winner mechanism, now shown to be the same fact seen twice.
  WHERE MY REASONING WENT WRONG, stated plainly because the error is instructive. POSITION-FULL found flips at
  0.182 on frontier matches and 0.055 on cross-tier ones, and I generalised that to "flips concentrate on
  contested pairs, so agreeing pairs are safe to judge once". But every ARENA-13 match was already
  answer-disagreement filtered, so its cross-tier/frontier split is a cut WITHIN disagreeing pairs. "Cross-tier"
  and "answer-agreeing" are different cuts and I treated them as the same one.
  THE CORRECTED STATEMENT, which both datasets support: THE FLIP RATE MEASURES THE ABSENCE OF DECISIVE
  EVIDENCE, whatever its source. Among answer-disagreeing pairs it tracks how contested the pair is (0.182
  frontier against 0.055 cross-tier). Among answer-agreeing pairs it is high regardless (0.192), because there
  is no evidence at all. Dual order earns its second call in both regimes and there is no cheap subset to skip.
  CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SCHEDULER: the shipped answer-disagreement filter remains the right economy and is now
  better motivated - it does not merely save six-fold on frontier pairs, it removes the matches with the
  HIGHEST flip rate and the strongest length preference, which is where a single-order arena would do most of
  its damage. Dual order stays mandatory on whatever is scheduled. The two mechanisms are complements, not
  alternatives as the registration supposed.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/selectiveorder_outcome.txt; script tools/analysis/selective_order.py.

- **PLACEBO-ENTRY OUTCOME (2026-09-14): the hypothesis is NOT CONFIRMED, the free precursor that supported it
  was misleading, and a free check I added afterwards dissolves the question entirely - the residue was never
  distinguishable from zero.** 1,192 calls, 2 content-filter refusals.
  (2) ARM A, zero calls, looked supportive: refitting the twelve on their answer-disagreeing subset widens the
      theta scale by 13% (SD 1.785 against 1.574) and moves the top models out from the board centre by +0.17
      to +0.37 - four to eight times the residue being explained.
  (1) ARM B, the direct test: NOT CONFIRMED. Re-entering gemini through the ARENA-13 protocol - its own
      original traces, no REGEN, 599 dual-order matches on disagreement-filtered questions with the leave-out
      ensemble reference - moves its theta by -0.043, 95% CI [-0.196, +0.109], against a registered bar of
      +0.045 with a CI excluding zero.
      CORRECTION (2026-09-14, found by the ledger audit within the hour, before anything downstream used it):
      the first version of this row reported +0.013 against gemini's theta over ALL ELEVEN x12 opponents. The
      protocol only ever faced FOUR, so that was a comparison between two different quantities. Against the
      MATCHED four-opponent baseline (theta +2.389 rather than +2.333) the delta is -0.043 - the opposite SIGN.
      The registered bar is unmet either way, but the direction reported was an artefact of the baseline, and
      the script now computes the matched comparator.
      POWER, which the registration should have stated and did not: the realised CI half-width is 0.152 against
      a +0.045 bar, so this arm could NOT have confirmed the hypothesis even had it been true at the registered
      size. NOT CONFIRMED here is absence of evidence, not evidence of absence, and the amendment rule that
      would have concluded "the residue belongs to the newcomer, trace style is the leading candidate" is
      WITHDRAWN rather than applied. Nothing about trace style is claimed.
      WHY THE TWO ARMS APPEAR TO DISAGREE, reconciled: arm A filters gemini's edges against all eleven
      opponents and refits EVERY other model on filtered evidence too, so it measures a global rescaling of the
      board; arm B changes ONE model's edges, against four opponents, which is the actual ARENA-13
      configuration. A global rescaling is not a relative advantage and the two are not the same quantity.
      RULE FOR THE THESIS: cheap proxies for board-level effects have systematically overstated them in this
      programme - arm A here, and POSITION-DECOMP's imputation wrong by a factor of seven earlier the same day.
      Quote a proxy for its sign at most, and never in place of the direct test when the direct test is
      affordable.
      A likely reason the filtering effect is so small here: filtering removes matches the KEY cannot decide,
      but the judge is only 0.664 accurate on the decidable pairs it is left with, so the judge's own noise
      simply replaces the key's non-decidability as the source of shrinkage.
  (4) FREE, UNREGISTERED, AND IT SETTLES THE WHOLE LINE. Bootstrapping the newcomer's dual-order theta gap to
      gemini over its 1,800 matches: +0.045 with a 95% CI of [-0.068, +0.186]. THE GAP INCLUDES ZERO. The
      arena does not separate these two models at this budget in either direction, so the residue needs no
      mechanism: there is nothing there to explain. Quality-not-captured-by-the-key and trace-generation style
      are both withdrawn as open questions, not because they were ruled out but because the effect they were
      invoked to explain is not resolvable.
  WHAT THIS DOES TO ARENA-13 (1), and it is a criticism of my own registration. The criterion asked whether the
  newcomer "places 2nd or 3rd" - a RANK test on a POINT ESTIMATE, with no resolution check. It failed three
  times (single order, frontier-balanced, fully balanced) on a theta gap whose confidence interval spans zero
  throughout. A rank criterion cannot distinguish "over-ranks" from "unresolved", and mine did not. The honest
  statement is that the ORDERING BETWEEN THE NEWCOMER AND GEMINI IS UNRESOLVED at 1,800 matches, which is a
  different and more defensible claim than the over-ranking I have been reporting since ARENA-13.
  METHODOLOGICAL RULE ADOPTED, and it should be applied to the whole ledger: every rank-based pass/fail
  criterion needs an accompanying resolution check - a CI on the quantity that determines the rank - before it
  can be read as evidence of mis-ranking rather than of insufficient evidence. This applies retrospectively to
  ARENA-V2-X20's top-6 clause and to any future LADDER-INSERT.
  CONSISTENT WITH: M3 (placement of a newcomer needs ~400 matches for +-1 rank, and "within +-1" falls to 61%
  at 46 models) and the whole frontier line - the top of the board is exactly where separation is hardest, and
  gemini and the newcomer differ by 6.4pp on the key, inside the band where nothing in this campaign resolves.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/placebo_outcome.txt; script tools/analysis/placebo_entry.py.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any call) — TEMP-0: is the 5.7% test-retest floor a property of LLM judging, or a default we never set?
Found by the ledger audit: NO judge call in this campaign has ever set a temperature. rejudge_reasoning.call_judge
posts {model, max_tokens, messages} and nothing else, so every verdict in every experiment ran at the provider
default. Only the throughput probes (azure_concurrency_sweep, azure_ratelimit_probe) set temperature 0.
DECOMP then measured the consequence without knowing the cause: on 299 matches whose two arms had BYTE-IDENTICAL
prompts the verdicts disagreed 5.7% of the time, from which I concluded that paired effects below roughly 3pp
cannot be read off a single pass. The rubric line - RK-1b at +1.3pp, RUBRIC-512 at +1.8pp, J3-R at +1.4pp - was
fought entirely inside that floor. A second, independent measurement of the same thing exists in the rubric kit:
three replicates of a byte-identical control at 0.8676 / 0.8581 / 0.8591, between-session SD 0.52pp.
DESIGN. The same 299 stratum-SAME matches from ARENA-13 arm A, re-judged TWICE at temperature 0, everything else
byte-identical to the existing arms: grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning, the leave-out ensemble reference, the routed
anchor rubric, v2 mechanics, the forward presentation order, the same prompt construction. 598 calls, stored as
arms t0a and t0b. The only change to shared code is an optional TEMPERATURE global that is omitted from the
request body when unset, so every existing script keeps posting a byte-identical body.
PILOT GATE, before the 598: 10 pairs of identical calls at temperature 0. Some deployments ignore the parameter.
If fewer than 8 of the 10 pairs return identical content the run is ABANDONED and reported as "the deployment
does not honour temperature", which is itself the answer to the question.
REGISTERED. (1) PRIMARY: the disagreement rate between the two temperature-0 passes, against DECOMP's 0.057 on
exactly these questions, with a bootstrap CI on the paired difference. BAR: below 0.02 adopts temperature 0 for
every future paired arm. (2) IS IT THE SAME JUDGE? the agreement between the temperature-0 verdicts and the
existing default-temperature verdicts on the same matches, and the two win rates - a floor that drops but a
verdict distribution that shifts would mean temperature 0 is a different judge, not a quieter one, and the
campaign's results would NOT transfer. (3) POWER: the minimum detectable paired effect at n=600 and n=1,000
under each floor, via SE = sqrt(d/n).
PREDICTIONS: disagreement 0.00-0.03, not exactly zero (batched inference is not bit-deterministic even at
temperature 0); agreement with the default-temperature verdicts 0.93-0.97 with win rates within 3pp; the
minimum detectable effect roughly halves.
WHAT IT CHANGES EITHER WAY. If the floor drops, every sub-3pp null in the rubric line becomes re-testable at a
fraction of its historic cost, future paired tests gain about 2x effective power for no marginal spend, and J7
(verdict sampling at temperature 0.7) is retired as pointing the wrong way. If it does NOT drop, the +-3pp
reading rule becomes a measured constraint on LLM-judge experiments rather than an incidental observation, and
the dual-order abstention rule is further justified. The campaign's existing results stand either way - they
were all run under the same default - but their PRECISION is reinterpreted.
Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/temp0_outcome.txt; cache arena13.db (arms t0a, t0b);
script tools/analysis/temp0.py.

### TEMP-0 AMENDMENT (2026-09-14, recorded BEFORE the 598 calls and before any scored result)
The registered pilot gate - "10 pairs of identical calls at temperature 0; fewer than 8 of the 10 returning
identical content abandons the run" - came out 0 of 10. I did not abandon, and the reason is that the gate as
written cannot distinguish the failure it was built to catch. Its purpose was to detect a deployment that
silently ignores the temperature parameter. But 0 of 10 byte-identical is equally consistent with "temperature
honoured, batched inference simply not bit-deterministic", which is the normal behaviour of a hosted MoE
deployment, so the instrument is confounded rather than failed.
THE CONTROL IT WAS MISSING, run before deciding anything: the same 10 prompts twice at the PROVIDER DEFAULT.
    temperature 0      n=10 | byte-identical 0 | same VERDICT 10
    provider default   n=10 | byte-identical 0 | same VERDICT  8
Byte-identity is zero in BOTH conditions, so it carries no information here at all; verdict stability differs in
the predicted direction. The gate is therefore recorded as UNINFORMATIVE AS SPECIFIED, replaced by the
verdict-stability comparison above, and the run proceeds.
WHAT IS NOT CHANGED, because this is exactly the pattern the ledger audit flagged as criterion substitution
after a failure (C-7, the STACK-v2 flip guard): the registered PRIMARY is untouched - disagreement between the
two temperature-0 passes below 0.02 adopts temperature 0 - as are readouts (2) and (3) and every prediction.
Only the gate instrument changed, and it changed towards a stricter question (verdict stability) rather than a
looser one. n=10 is a smoke test, not evidence; the 299-match run is what measures it.

- **TEMP-0 OUTCOME (2026-09-14): the 5.7% floor is NOT an unset default. Temperature 0 changes the judge's
  prose and not its mind, and the +-3pp reading rule survives as a measured constraint.** 598 calls, 0 errors.
  (1) PRIMARY, on the same 299 byte-identical-prompt matches DECOMP used:
        provider default   disagreement 0.057
        temperature 0      disagreement 0.050
        difference -0.007, bootstrap 95% CI [-0.030, +0.017] - includes zero. Registered bar (below 0.02) NOT met.
      The parameter IS reaching the deployment and IS doing something: byte-identical responses go from 0.000 at
      the default, over all 299, to 0.177 at temperature 0. But 82% of temperature-0 pairs still differ in
      wording, and the verdict flips just as often. Determinism of the text and stability of the decision are
      different things, and only the first responds to temperature here.
  (2) AND IT IS THE SAME JUDGE, which is what makes (1) worth having rather than merely disappointing:
      agreement with the default-temperature verdicts 0.940; the new contestant's win rate 0.779 under both,
      8:8 discordant, McNemar p=1.00. Temperature 0 is a quieter judge in style, not a different one in
      judgement, so nothing already measured is invalidated by having run at the default.
  (3) POWER barely moves: the minimum detectable paired effect at n=600 goes 0.019 -> 0.018, at n=1,000
      0.015 -> 0.014. There is no free doubling of power available here.
  MY PREDICTION WAS WRONG: I predicted 0.00-0.03 disagreement at temperature 0 and it is 0.050.
  AND THE PILOT WAS NOISE, which is a small lesson in the very thing being measured. The amended gate showed
  verdict stability 10/10 at temperature 0 against 8/10 at the default and I read it as "temperature IS doing
  something". At n=10 that difference is 2 matches; the 299-match measurement puts the true gap at 0.7pp with an
  interval spanning zero. A smoke test cannot see an effect the size of the effect under study - which is
  precisely the +-3pp rule this experiment was testing, applied to itself.
  WHAT THIS SETTLES FOR THE PAPER. The test-retest floor of an LLM judge on contested pairs is a property of the
  judge, not of a sampling parameter left at its default: it survives temperature 0 essentially intact. So the
  rule that paired effects below roughly 3pp cannot be read off a single pass is a MEASURED CONSTRAINT on
  LLM-judge experiments, not an incidental observation about this deployment, and the campaign's sub-3pp nulls -
  RK-1b at +1.3pp, RUBRIC-512 at +1.8pp, J3-R at +1.4pp - were fought inside a floor that no configuration
  choice would have removed. It also further justifies the dual-order abstention rule, which converts part of
  this irreducible noise into an abstention rather than a coin-flip verdict.
  CONSEQUENCE FOR THE QUEUE: J7 (verdict sampling at temperature 0.7) is CLOSED on this evidence. Its premise
  was that sampling temperature is the lever on verdict stability; the lever moves the floor by 0.7pp with an
  interval containing zero, and in the wrong direction to be worth 0.7.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/temp0_outcome.txt; script tools/analysis/temp0.py.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any call) — PAIR-NOREF: does the displacement finding hold in the format we actually deploy?
FORMAT-REF's clean toggle is the strongest result of the campaign: showing a reference raises the REF
coefficient by +1.811 [+1.507, +2.121] AND LOWERS the KEY coefficient by -0.560 [-0.862, -0.289] - a reference
does not supplement the judge's own assessment of correctness, it displaces it. That toggle exists in POINTWISE
ONLY, the format where KEY is +0.258 +- 0.157 and barely distinguishable from zero, and the arena deploys
PAIRWISE. The pairwise no-reference comparator already on disk (rejudge_grok.db) is v1 prompt + cell rubric, so
it differs from the pairwise-with-reference arm in prompt version AND rubric level AND reference; it is not a
toggle, and the "+11.8pp pairwise reference effect" quoted in the POINTWISE row inherits all three confounds.
The clean pairwise reference effect on record is J2-R's +7.6pp, on a different judge.
DESIGN. R3's 944 KEY-DECIDABLE matches, pairwise, dual order, grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning, v2 mechanics, clean
anchor rubric - byte-identical to stack_v2_promptv2_grok.db in every respect except that the reference block is
removed from the question and the verify sentence is swapped exactly as pointwise_judge.py does it (VERIFY_REF
-> VERIFY_NOREF): the judge is told to work out the correct answer for itself instead of checking a supplied
one. 1,888 calls. Temperature is left at the provider default, as in every arm it is compared against - TEMP-0
showed the choice moves the floor by 0.7pp with an interval spanning zero.
REGISTERED. (1) PRIMARY: refit the CONSENSUS-FIT signed-contrast logistic on the paired matches and report
delta KEY with a bootstrap CI. DISPLACEMENT REPLICATES if delta KEY < 0 with a CI excluding zero - the judge
weights correctness LESS when a reference is present, in the deployed format. (2) delta REF against the
pointwise +1.811, and delta REF-KEY. (3) the clean pairwise reference effect on ACCURACY, to set beside J2-R's
+7.6pp (different judge) and RECIPE-GROK's +12.0pp (bundled with prompt and rubric). (4) tie rate with and
without the reference, since POINTWISE found ties double without one and the accuracy convention scores ties as
errors.
PREDICTIONS: delta KEY between -0.3 and -0.8, i.e. displacement replicates but smaller than pointwise's -0.560
because pairwise weights correctness more to begin with (KEY +0.996 against +0.258); delta REF +1.2 to +2.0;
the accuracy effect +6 to +10pp, below the confounded +11.8 and near J2-R's +7.6; ties rise 3-8pp without the
reference.
IF DELTA KEY IS NOT NEGATIVE the displacement finding is pointwise-only, the paper must say so, and the lead
claim narrows from "a reference displaces the judge's reasoning" to "a reference displaces the judge's
reasoning when it grades, and merely outweighs it when it compares". That is a real and reportable difference,
and it is why this run is worth 1,888 calls rather than being assumed.
Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/pairnoref_outcome.txt; cache pairnoref.db; script tools/analysis/pair_noref.py.

- **PAIR-NOREF OUTCOME (2026-09-14): DISPLACEMENT DOES NOT REPLICATE in the deployed format. The lead claim
  narrows exactly as the registration said it would, and the run pays for itself twice over.** 1,882 calls,
  0 errors, 944 key-decidable R3 matches, paired.
      arm                          KEY      REF     REF-KEY
      pairwise WITH a reference   +0.981   +2.279   +1.298
      pairwise WITHOUT one        +0.959   +0.682   -0.276
      delta KEY     -0.022  95% CI [-0.240, +0.191]
      delta REF     -1.596  95% CI [-1.904, -1.388]
  (1) PRIMARY FAILS. Removing the reference leaves the KEY coefficient where it was. In pointwise the same
      toggle moved it by -0.560, and this CI EXCLUDES -0.560, so the two formats genuinely differ rather than
      being indistinguishable at this sample size. THE CLAIM NARROWS, in the wording fixed before the run:
      a reference DISPLACES the judge's own assessment of correctness WHEN IT GRADES, and merely OUTWEIGHS it
      when it COMPARES. Pairwise gains +1.60 of reference-following without giving up any correctness-weighting;
      pointwise trades one for the other. That is a sharper claim than the one I was going to make, and it has a
      natural reading: grading one answer in isolation leaves nothing to compare against except the reference,
      while comparing two answers preserves a second source of evidence the reference cannot crowd out.
  (3) AND IT DELIVERS THE CLEAN NUMBER THE PROGRAMME LACKED. The reference is worth +12.6pp in the deployed
      pairwise configuration (0.864 against 0.738, 144:25, p=1.6e-21) - the first estimate not confounded with
      prompt version or rubric level. It supersedes the +11.8pp quoted in the POINTWISE 2x2 row, whose
      comparator was a v1-prompt, cell-rubric cache, and it sits well above J2-R's clean +7.6pp on Mistral.
      My prediction of +6 to +10pp was too low.
  (4) TIES more than double without a reference: 0.070 -> 0.177. Prediction 3-8pp, observed +10.7pp.
  THE DECOMPOSITION THAT MATTERS, and it changes what the +12.6pp means. Ties score as errors, so that headline
  mixes discrimination with abstention. On the verdicts the judge actually COMMITS to, accuracy is 0.929 with a
  reference and 0.897 without - a gap of +3.2pp against the +12.6pp headline. SO 74% OF THE REFERENCE'S
  APPARENT ACCURACY VALUE IS THE JUDGE ABSTAINING LESS, and 26% is better discrimination.
  A PROGRAMME-LEVEL FINDING, now visible in three independent places on the same day: RK-1b's data card is ~86%
  abstention reduction (+0.25pp conditional on committing, against +1.7pp headline); AGGREGATE's tie-break buys
  +8.0pp by resolving abstentions and nothing else; and the reference itself is 74% abstention reduction. On a
  benchmark where ties are scored as errors, MOST OF WHAT THIS CAMPAIGN HAS MEASURED AS "ACCURACY" IS THE RATE
  AT WHICH THE JUDGE IS WILLING TO COMMIT. The paper should report decisive-and-correct and correct-given-
  committed as two separate numbers everywhere, because interventions that look interchangeable on the first
  are not on the second - and the cheapest lever on the first, by a wide margin, is the tie rule.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/pairnoref_outcome.txt; script tools/analysis/pair_noref.py.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any call) — ARENA-V3-COMPILED: the paper's board from the interventions that actually survived
SUPERSEDES the ARENA-V3 registered 2026-09-11, which is WITHDRAWN. That design spent ~18.3k calls deploying the
RK-1b data card at arena scale, and the card has since been restated as ~86% abstention reduction (+0.25pp
conditional on the judge committing), Holm-adjusted p 0.35 across its family, failed replication at p=0.073, and
a PASS that depends on which of three byte-identical controls was drawn. AGGREGATE's replicate tie-break
addresses the same abstention mechanism far better (+8.0pp for ~16% more calls), so the two are substitutes and
the card is the weaker one. Rather than cancel outright, this rebuilds the run around what the campaign has
actually established.
WHAT GOES IN, each with the result that earned it: the answer-disagreement FILTER (SCHEDULING, FILTER-BOARD -
keeps 99.8% of decidable pairs at a fraction of the matches and improves the pairwise board); DUAL ORDER,
mandatory (POSITION-FULL - 13.5pp of position on contested pairs, and SELECTIVE-ORDER showed there is no cheap
subset to skip); the reasoning REFERENCE (PAIR-NOREF - +12.6pp clean in this exact format); and AGGREGATE's
REPLICATE TIE-BREAK, the strongest lever the programme has found per call. WHAT STAYS OUT: the RK-1b card, for
the reasons above.
COST, and this is the point of the reframe: the first three are already in the x12 MAIN cache, so the only new
spend is the tie-break on the ties that survive filtering. 5,276 of 9,142 matches pass the filter (57.7%); 625
of those are dual-order TIES; 2 calls each = 1,250 CALLS, against 18,300 for the withdrawn design.
THREE BOARDS, all 12 models, all from one judge (Mistral-Large-3, the x12 MAIN judge - disclosed, because
JUDGE-SWAP later adopted grok for re-judge runs and ARENA-13's board mixed the two, which it should not have):
  A  ARENA-V2 as published: all 9,142 dual-order verdicts
  B  + answer-disagreement filter: 5,276 matches, ZERO new calls
  C  + replicate tie-break on B's 625 ties: 1,250 calls
REGISTERED. (1) PRIMARY: board C's decisive-and-correct accuracy exceeds ARENA-V2's 0.852 by at least 3pp on
the common matches, paired McNemar p < 0.05. (2) BOARD: C's 12-model rho >= 0.967 and top-4 violations <= 1,
both reported WITH BOOTSTRAP CIs - the ledger audit found that no theta, rho or violation count in this
programme has ever carried one, and this run fixes that for the board that goes in the paper. (3) COST: B and C
together consume <= 70% of the calls of the unfiltered dual-order board while (2) holds. (4) DUAL REPORTING,
descriptive but required from now on: decisive-and-correct AND correct-given-committed for all three boards,
because PAIR-NOREF, RK-1b and AGGREGATE together show that most of what this campaign has called accuracy is
the rate at which the judge commits.
PREDICTIONS: C's accuracy 0.88-0.92 against A's 0.852; rho within 0.005 of 0.972; 1 violation; cost about 65%;
and correct-given-committed nearly flat across A, B and C (roughly 0.92) while decisive-and-correct rises -
which, if it holds, is the cleanest possible statement of the abstention finding.
FALSIFIER: if correct-given-committed rises materially too, then the filter and the tie-break improve
discrimination as well as decisiveness, and the abstention framing is too strong.
Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/arenav3_outcome.txt; cache arenav3.db; script tools/analysis/arena_v3_compiled.py.

### Cross-file discrepancy resolved (2026-09-14, ledger audit findings D4/D5)
arena13_outcome.txt and consensusfit_outcome.txt print slightly different values for the same quantities -
gemini agreement/key 0.865/0.912 against 0.863/0.913, iask 0.878/0.811 against 0.877/0.817, the newcomer's key
accuracy 0.853 against 0.849. Neither file is wrong; they use different DENOMINATORS, and neither said so:
  * over ALL pool questions the model answered: newcomer key accuracy 0.8494 (n=3,434) - what consensus_fit
    reports, because jf.gt_and_lengths and the cot cache are keyed on the whole pool;
  * over only the questions where the leave-out ensemble has a DECISIVE majority: 0.8559 (n=3,325) - what the
    arena13 consensus probe reports, because that is the subset its reference exists on.
The gap is 0.65pp and it moves every model in the same direction, so no comparison between models changes. The
ledger and the ARENA-13 outcome use the arena13 variant; CONSENSUS-FIT (4) uses the other, which is why its
"+0.018 agreement" differs in the third decimal from the ARENA-13 table's "1.7pp". RULE: any table mixing key
accuracy with reference agreement must state the denominator, because the two are naturally computed on
different subsets and the difference is the same order as the effects being discussed.

- **ARENA-V3-COMPILED OUTCOME (2026-09-14): the paper's board, for 1,250 calls instead of 18,300. Two criteria
  pass, the primary misses its bar, and the free arm turns out to be the best part.** 619 tie-break matches
  judged (3 skipped for a missing reference), 0 errors.
      board                      matches   calls    ties   decisive-and-correct   correct-given-committed
      A  ARENA-V2, as published    9,142  18,284   0.209   0.852 [0.842, 0.863]     0.918 [0.910, 0.926]
      B  + disagreement filter     5,276  10,552   0.118   0.846 [0.836, 0.858]     0.912 [0.904, 0.922]
      C  + replicate tie-break     5,276  11,802   0.051   0.868 [0.858, 0.879]     0.903 [0.893, 0.911]
      board                          rho          rho 95% CI    top-4 violations   viol 95% CI
      A                            0.9720      0.9580-0.9860           2              1-3
      B                            0.9860      0.9720-0.9860           1              1-2
      C                            0.9860      0.9720-0.9860           1              1-2
      (ORACLE-BOARD, the key as verdict on the same schedule: rho 1.0000, 0 violations)
  (1) PRIMARY FAILS. On the 4,106 common decidable matches C scores 0.868 against A's 0.846, +2.2pp, against a
      registered bar of +3pp. The discordance is 0:92 - by construction C can only differ where A abstained, so
      it never loses a match A won - and McNemar is p=4.0e-28, but the EFFECT SIZE misses. Reported as a FAIL.
      Note the two rates are quoted on the SAME matches here; the headline 0.852 and 0.868 in the table above
      are each board's rate on its own decidable set and are NOT directly comparable, which is the population
      mismatch this campaign has made repeatedly and which the audit flagged as C-6.
  (2) PASS: rho 0.9860 and 1 top-4 violation, against bars of 0.967 and <=1.
  (3) PASS: 11,802 calls against 18,284, i.e. 65%, under the 70% bar.
  (4) THE REGISTERED PREDICTION HOLDS, AND IT IS THE RESULT: decisive-and-correct rises 0.852 -> 0.868 while
      correct-given-committed FALLS 0.918 -> 0.903. The tie-break does not make the judge better at judging; it
      makes it decide, and the decisions it adds are worse than its average - which is exactly AGGREGATE's
      measurement (ties resolve at 0.75-0.86 against 0.93 on already-committed verdicts) reappearing at board
      scale. The falsifier (correct-given-committed rising too) did not fire.
  THE BEST PART IS ARM B, AND IT IS FREE. Filtering alone - no new calls at all, just discarding the matches
  whose candidates already agree - takes rho from 0.9720 to 0.9860 and top-4 violations from 2 to 1, at 58% of
  the calls. Every published board in this campaign could have been better and cheaper.
  BUT THE CIs SAY BE CAREFUL, and this is the discipline the audit asked for applied to a result of my own:
  A's rho CI is [0.958, 0.986] and B's is [0.972, 0.986]. They OVERLAP heavily. The board improvement is a
  point-estimate improvement that this many matches cannot resolve, and the violation CIs (1-3 against 1-2)
  overlap too. The honest claim is "the filter does not cost board quality and halves the bill", not "the
  filter improves the board". The cost result is the solid one; the quality result is directional.
  WHAT GOES IN THE PAPER: board C, with its CIs, and the recipe that produced it - cheap judge, one reasoning
  reference per question, v2 verify-first mechanics, the routed anchor rubric, the answer-disagreement filter,
  dual order, and a replicate tie-break on what remains. Not the RK-1b data card. Total cost 11,802 judge calls
  for a 12-model board at rho 0.986, against 18,284 for the published one at 0.972.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/arenav3_outcome.txt; script tools/analysis/arena_v3_compiled.py.

### Two registered-criteria hygiene notes (2026-09-14, audit findings C-7 and C-8)
C-7, CRITERION SUBSTITUTION AFTER A FAILURE. STACK-v2's registered criterion (5) was a flip rate at or below
12.8%; the observed rate was 13.9%, a FAIL. FLIP-PROV then retired that guard in favour of "decidable flip
<= 8%", which the data passes. The physics behind the change is right - POSITION-DECOMP later showed the 13.9%
is roughly 6pp position on 6pp stochasticity, and FLIP-PROV's own decidable flip rate was 5.4% - but the
SEQUENCE is a guard being re-specified after it failed, which is the pattern a reviewer will flag. Both must be
reported: criterion (5) FAILED as registered, and the re-specified guard passes. The same discipline was applied
prospectively to TEMP-0's pilot gate on the same day, where the amendment was recorded before any spending and
moved to a stricter question rather than a looser one.
C-8, A BAR WHOSE MEANING DEPENDS ON A LATER CHOICE. ARENA-13 criterion (3) was "key-decidable accuracy >= 0.85".
It scored 0.837 under single-order judging and 0.793 under dual order - the same verdicts, a worse number,
because the dual rule converts disagreements into abstentions and the accuracy convention scores abstentions as
errors. A bar whose value depends on an aggregation convention chosen after registration is not frozen. RULE
ADOPTED: register accuracy bars TOGETHER WITH the tie convention they are to be evaluated under, and report
decisive-and-correct alongside correct-given-committed so the convention cannot silently move the number. This
is what ARENA-V3-COMPILED does.

### POOL-ASSERTION PASS (2026-09-14, closing audit item 7)
The audit asked for a pool assertion in every Python analysis that consumes a Kotlin artefact, noting that only
19 of 92 scripts had one. Rather than edit 92 files, the scripts were classified by HOW they obtain the reserved
side, because only one of the three ways can drift:
  (a) ADDRESSED BY EXPLICIT POOL ID (11 scripts, e.g. `WHERE pool_id='p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae'`) - cannot drift, since
      the id is the content hash of the set. No change needed.
  (b) READ eval_results.is_reserved (14 scripts) - THE DRIFT VECTOR. That column mirrors whichever pool is
      ACTIVE, and every construction run activates its own split, so a script reading the flag while a sweep
      pool is active silently scores a different 30%. This is the 2026-09-09 INCIDENT exactly.
  (c) RE-DERIVE THEIR OWN SPLIT - only the multi-corpus router and leaf router genuinely did this, and both were
      fixed earlier today with `--clean`. The other 30-odd hits of `random.Random` are bootstrap and permutation
      seeds, not splits: a false positive of the grep the audit's count appears to rest on.
IN CLASS (b), the state was better than 19/92 suggested but not clean: eight scripts already called
assert_frozen_pool, one (refit_bt_from_matches) mentions the column only in a comment explaining that it
deliberately does not use it, and THREE HAD NO PIN AT ALL - j6_rubrics.py, rubric_kit.py and rubric_kit2.py.
All three are in the rubric line, which is precisely where the pool-mismatch incident happened and whose
conclusions the incident forced a re-analysis of. That is the finding this pass produced.
FIX: pool_guard now exposes a one-line `assert_pool_of_record()` that opens the dataset DB read-only and raises
unless the pool of record is active; it is called as the first statement of the __main__ block in the five
scripts that lacked it (the three above plus prompt_audit and regen_contestant, which pin by id and now also
catch a flag/id disagreement). Guarding inside __main__ rather than at import means it never fires when one
script imports another. VERIFIED: all 96 analysis scripts parse, and prompt_audit's output is byte-identical
with the guard in place, since the pool of record is currently active.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before looking at any result, ZERO calls) — four probes opened by the relaxed design constraints
The author relaxed three constraints that had been shaping the design: the 14 MMLU-Pro ANCHORS may be dropped
(they were inherited to keep comparability with the dataset, not because the method needs them); the online
ranking only has to work PER TIER, with cost, speed and power consumption as further router axes; and the
"specific judges" line is redirected from cell-specific PROSE to cell-specific REFERENCES. Each relaxation makes
a different question answerable from data already on disk.

TIER-RECOVERY. If the product is tiers rather than a total order, the budget question changes. Tiers are defined
here from the KEY, not from the judge: two models are in the same tier when their key-accuracy gap is below
0.017, which is 2 SE at n=3,445 and, not coincidentally, exactly the arx/iask gap the campaign could never
resolve. Resampling the x12 verdicts at budgets 250..9,144, 200 draws each, measure the share of draws whose
judged board recovers the KEY's tier partition exactly, and its adjusted Rand index.
REGISTERED: the budget at which exact tier recovery exceeds 95% of draws, against the 2,000 at which rho >= 0.93
and the never at which top-4 violations reach <= 1. PREDICTION: tiers recover by 250-500 matches, an order of
magnitude cheaper than the ordering the campaign spent itself on.

ANCHOR-VALUE. Does the anchor layer earn its place in ROUTING? Compare, on the pool of record, the deployed
descent (anchor first, then leaf within it) against flat nearest-centroid over all 87 leaves ignoring anchors.
The union build already answered this for six corpora - flatLeaf 81.6% against descent 72.1% - and the answer
there was that anchors HURT. This asks it for MMLU-Pro alone, where the anchors are the dataset's own categories
and therefore at their most favourable.
REGISTERED: routing agreement with the deployed assignment, and per-anchor purity under both rules. PREDICTION:
flat routing matches or beats descent, which would say the anchors are a reporting convenience rather than a
routing mechanism - and that dropping them costs nothing.

REF-BY-CELL. The redirect says a cell-specific judge should mean a cell-specific REFERENCE. That is only worth
building if reference accuracy varies enough by cell to select on. Two full reference sets exist over the pool:
grok-reasoning (0.860 overall) and mistral (0.663). Per anchor and per leaf, compute both accuracies, the oracle
per-cell choice, and the gain of that oracle over always using the stronger one.
REGISTERED: (1) the spread of grok-reasoning's accuracy across anchors; (2) the number of cells in which the
WEAKER reference is better; (3) the oracle per-cell selection gain over always-grok. PREDICTION: spread 0.15-0.30
across anchors, the weaker reference better in 1-3 cells, and an oracle gain of 1-3pp - enough to matter given
that the judge transcribes the reference, and enough to justify per-cell reference selection in the design.

TIER-ROUTER. With tiers plus cost as the product, what does routing actually buy and what does it cost? For each
anchor, tier the models by key accuracy under the same 0.017 rule, route to the best tier, then pick the CHEAPEST
member of it, using mean generated length as the cost proxy (the only one in this dataset).
REGISTERED: accuracy of (a) the single best model overall, (b) per-anchor best model, (c) per-anchor best TIER
then cheapest member; and the generated-token cost of each. PREDICTION: (c) loses 0-1pp against (b) while cutting
cost materially, which would make tier-routing the right product shape and would turn the campaign's hardest
negative - the frontier is not orderable - into something the router never needs to ask.
Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/newcontext_probes.txt; script tools/analysis/newcontext_probes.py.

- **SIX PROBES ON THE RELAXED CONSTRAINTS (2026-09-14, zero calls): two clean answers, one clean negative, one
  test that had to be rebuilt, and one finding that changes what a tiered product can be trusted to say.**

  **ANCHOR-VALUE: the anchors do not earn their place, and dropping them costs nothing.** Routing the 3,445 pool
  questions by flat nearest-leaf-centroid, ignoring the anchor layer entirely, against the deployed
  anchor-then-leaf descent: the two agree on 83.5% of questions, and category purity of the routed anchor is
  0.764 flat against 0.753 descent - flat is BETTER by 1.1pp. This is MMLU-Pro, where the anchors ARE the
  dataset's own categories and therefore at their most favourable, and the union build already gave flatLeaf
  81.6% against descent 72.1%. Two corpora, same direction. The anchor layer is a reporting convenience that
  keeps results comparable to the published benchmark; it is not a routing mechanism, and the design is free to
  drop it.

  **REF-BY-CELL: per-cell reference SELECTION buys nothing, but reference QUALITY varies enormously.**
  grok-reasoning against mistral as the reference, per anchor: grok is better in all 13, so the oracle per-cell
  choice gains exactly +0.0000 over always-grok. But grok's own accuracy spans 0.224 across cells - 0.952 in
  Math, 0.951 in Business, 0.921 in Physics, down to 0.750 in Law, 0.744 in Engineering, 0.727 in History.
  Since the judge transcribes the reference (0.922 when it is right, 0.226 when it is wrong), that spread is
  the dominant term in per-cell judge quality. THE DESIGN CONSEQUENCE IS NOT "choose a reference per cell", it
  is "KNOW PER CELL HOW GOOD YOUR REFERENCE IS" - and treat a 0.73 cell differently from a 0.95 cell, by
  escalating, by widening the reported uncertainty, or by declining to rank there at all.

  **TIER-ROUTER: MMLU-Pro cannot demonstrate tier-and-cost routing, because the best model is also the
  cheapest.** Best single, per-anchor best, and per-anchor-best-tier-then-cheapest are byte-identical: 0.9126
  accuracy at 882 mean characters. gemini wins every anchor (ROUTER-REGRET-MMLU) and is also the shortest
  generator in its own tier, so every policy selects it. A null about the corpus, not about the idea.

  **TIER-ROUTER-U: on the six-corpus union the idea works, and well.** 6,482 questions, 18 models, cells =
  (source, domain), cost proxy = parameter count parsed from the model name:
      policy                            accuracy   mean params
      best single                        0.5543       72.0 B
      per-cell best                      0.6169       46.1 B
      per-cell best TIER, smallest       0.6143       38.3 B
  Tier-then-smallest gives up 0.26pp against per-cell best while using 83% of its parameters, and beats the
  best single model by 6.0pp at 53% of its size. That is the product shape: route to a tier, choose within it
  on cost. CAVEAT: parameter count is a crude proxy and the union DB carries no token counts or latencies, so
  this orders models by size rather than by price.

  **TIER-RECOVERY: the first version of this test was the ordering problem in a costume, and failed.** Asking
  whether the judged board reproduces the KEY's gap-based tier partition gives 0% exact recovery at every
  coarseness (10, 8, 5 and 2 tiers) and every budget (250 to 9,142), with adjusted Rand peaking at 0.54. But a
  tier defined by a gap borrowed from the key's accuracy scale is not what a product needs, and comparing a BT
  logit scale against it required a rescaling that distorts the very gaps being tested. The question was wrong.

  **TIER-HONEST: the right question, and the answer is the important one. A tiered board is honest where it is
  already right, and CONFIDENTLY WRONG exactly where it is wrong.** Bootstrapping the board 400 times and
  asking, per pair, how often model A outranks model B:
    - ACROSS-TIER pairs, which the key genuinely separates: the arena separates 62 of 64 at 95% confidence and
      **0 of them point the wrong way**. Where the key says there is a real gap, the arena never gets the
      direction wrong.
    - WITHIN-TIER pairs, which the key ties: the arena separates **2 of 2** at 95% confidence. Both are
      overconfident, and one is the campaign's known inversion - it is 100% sure iask beats arx, and the key
      says the opposite by 1.7pp.
    - Letting the arena tier ITSELF, grouping models it cannot separate at 95%, produces 10 tiers containing
      **2 cross-tier key inversions**: iask tiered above arx (0.817 against 0.834) and command-r above
      Llama-3.1-8B (0.363 against 0.371).
  THE FINDING: **a bootstrap CI on a BT strength is confidently wrong precisely where the judge is
  systematically biased.** Resampling matches captures sampling noise; it cannot see a bias that is present in
  every sample. The arx/iask inversion is systematic - it is the length preference - so no amount of resampling
  reveals it, and the interval tightens around the wrong answer. A tiered product built on bootstrap intervals
  would confidently merge or separate exactly the pairs this campaign already knows it gets wrong.
  WHAT A TIERED PRODUCT THEREFORE NEEDS, and this is the design answer: an uncertainty estimate that includes
  the judge's SYSTEMATIC error, not only its sampling error. Three candidates, all already measured here: the
  5.7% test-retest floor as a variance component; the reference's per-cell accuracy (REF-BY-CELL, 0.73-0.95) as
  a prior on how much to trust a cell at all; and the answer-agreement rate between the two models, which is
  what the disagreement filter already computes for free and which predicts decidability at 0.796 against
  0.0004. A tier boundary should be drawn where those say the arena cannot see, not where the bootstrap says it
  can.
  PROCESS NOTE: the inversion counter in the first run of TIER-HONEST required an inversion to EXCEED the 0.017
  tier gap and reported 0. The one real inversion sits exactly on that threshold. Corrected before recording;
  the corrected count is 2.
  Outputs experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/{newcontext_probes.txt, tier_design_probes.txt};
  scripts tools/analysis/newcontext_probes.py, tools/analysis/tier_design_probes.py.

- **LEAF-PROFILE-CLEAN (2026-09-14, zero calls): the one result saying sub-anchor capability is REAL was
  measured largely on the questions that built the leaves, and it does not survive being cleaned.** Found by the
  design workflow, not by the ledger audit, which had missed it.
  `leaf_profile_evidence.py` calls `ff.keyed_questions()`, which returns ALL 10,925 keyed questions with no
  reserved-side filter. Only 3,130 of them (28.6%) are on the tree's held-out side, so arm A - the registered
  test of whether a per-leaf model x cell interaction exists in the ground truth - was computed mostly on the
  questions the leaves were fitted to separate. Leaves optimised to split those questions will show an
  interaction on them; that is close to circular.
      arm A, as published (all 10,925 keyed questions): pooled p=0.005, anchors significant 10/14 -> REAL
      arm A, restricted to the held-out pool (3,130):   pooled p=0.010, anchors significant  3/13 -> NOT SHOWN
  The registered criterion was "pooled p < 0.05 AND at least half the anchors individually p < 0.05". On clean
  data the pooled half still passes and the per-anchor half collapses, so the criterion FAILS.
  POWER CAVEAT, stated because it is the obvious objection and it is partly right: n falls 3.5x, from 10,925 to
  3,130 questions, so per-anchor tests lose roughly 1.9x in standard error and some of the 10 -> 3 collapse is
  power rather than contamination. The pooled test, which keeps most of its power, survives at p=0.010. The
  honest statement is therefore NOT "sub-anchor structure is absent" but "the evidence that it is present does
  not survive being restricted to data the tree never saw, at the criterion it was registered under".
  WHY IT MATTERS. This was the one result in the programme pointing the other way from LEAF-POWER (leaf worse
  than anchor at every budget, 5/5 seeds), LEAF-SHRINK (lambda=0 best), LEAF-POWERED (+-2pp ceiling) and MC-LEAF
  (leaves do not beat designed domains). It was the reason to keep asking whether a finer profile was reachable.
  With it weakened, the anchor is the reporting ceiling on evidence rather than on budget, and the design should
  stop treating sub-anchor rows as a someday feature.
  THIRD CONTAMINATION OF THE SAME CLASS. The pool incident (2026-09-09, 71% of judged questions on the tree's
  train side), the multi-corpus split (2026-09-14, ~70% overlap at chance), and now this - all three are an [CORRECTED 2026-09-27 by INCONSISTENCIES-PASS (RP01, A3): "71% of judged questions" (L2212) names the wrong denominator: 71% is 2,437 (by content; 70.4% = 2,425 by id) of the POOL's 3,445 judgeable questions (incident doc L10-L13); the judged set's share was never computed]
  analysis reading a question set that was not pinned to the tree's own held-out pool, and all three happened
  with a written rule in force. The pool-assertion pass earlier today classified scripts by HOW they obtain the
  reserved side and fixed class (b); this is a fourth class the classification missed - a script that obtains a
  question set from a HELPER which does no filtering at all. `ff.keyed_questions()` has no pool argument and
  cannot assert one. The standing rule is amended: a helper that returns questions must take the pool as an
  argument, and any analysis that does not pass one is treated as contaminated until shown otherwise.
  Output: run `python tools/analysis/leaf_profile_evidence.py --reserved`.

- **F2-CLEAN (2026-09-14, zero calls): H-5's headline does not survive a proper held-out design.** The leaf
  layer's advantage over MMLU-Pro's own category labels, LOO Brier improvement per 1,000:
      population                                    n      leaf - category      verdict
      ALL questions (the published headline)      7,754   +3.15 [+2.07, +4.20]   WINS
      DISAGREEMENT subset (already in the file)   1,998   +2.48 [-0.55, +5.26]   TIE
      RESERVED only                               3,269   +2.12 [+0.55, +3.73]   WINS
      RESERVED, cells fitted on TRAIN only        3,269   +0.74 [-0.90, +2.39]   TIE
  THE LAST ROW IS THE ONLY CLEAN ONE and it is a tie. Leave-one-out removes the scored question from its own
  cell mean, but it cannot remove the fact that the question helped CHOOSE the cell boundaries - that is
  structural, not statistical. Scoring on held-out questions whose leaf membership was fixed without them, with
  the cell statistic fitted on the train side, is the only design in which the leaves were not tuned to what
  scores them. Under it the leaf advantage falls from +3.15 to +0.74 and its interval covers zero.
  WHAT CHANGES. H-5 reads "sub-anchor cells carry capability information the labels miss" and cites this
  +3.15. The claim as worded is not supported. What survives: the STRATUM layer is stable across every
  population (+1.06, +0.84, +0.67, +0.85 - never significant on clean data either, but never collapsing), and
  the registered PRIMARY of F2 was always a FAIL (anchor - category +0.14, TIE, and -0.05 on clean data). So
  F2's registered outcome is unchanged; it is the secondary that carried H-5, and the secondary was the
  contaminated one.
  WITH LEAF-PROFILE-CLEAN, the case for sub-anchor structure is now empty on held-out data: arm A fails its
  registered criterion (3/13 anchors), F2's leaf secondary is a tie, LEAF-POWER has leaf worse than anchor in
  5/5 seeds at every budget, LEAF-SHRINK puts lambda=0 best, LEAF-POWERED caps a leaf rubric at +-2pp, and
  MC-LEAF's leaves do not beat designed domains. The anchor is the reporting ceiling ON EVIDENCE, not on budget.
  NOTE ON THE FILE'S OWN HEADER, which is confusing and should be read carefully: the line "questions 7754
  (train-side via text join 6734, reserved 1020)" counts train-side membership by a TEXT JOIN, which is a
  different and weaker statistic than membership in the frozen tree's reserved assignment. By the latter, 3,269
  of the 7,754 scored questions are reserved. The 1,020 is the clean-subset intersection from the pool incident. [ID-ONLY 2026-09-23 (CLAIMS-SWEEP-BRACKETS, registrar): pool 1,020 CLEAN (p2dca judgeable minus p8a29); verified by id only, not by content; reviewed twins on this pool (reviews 1df2cf1, 8ebfa7a): frozen tree 12 exact / 23 norm-v1 (option-set 22 / ordered 11); bareq512_s42 15 / 28 (26 / 13); see docs/judge_v2_program.md L14280-L14340 (CONTENT-DISJOINT-SPLIT-AUDIT) and L14455-L14487 (SPLIT-FOLLOWUPS).]
  STILL OPEN: F5 (uncertified leaves carry capability info, +2.18/1000) and F6 (the key-only tree comparison)
  take their questions from the same unfiltered helper, n=10,925 with no pool filter, and F6 is worse - it
  scores trees built on DIFFERENT splits against one common unfiltered set. Both need the same treatment.
  Output experiment_results/free_tests_f_output.txt (regenerated with the clean rows).

- **RESOLVE-CALIB (2026-09-14, zero calls): of the three statistical objections raised against the design, one
  does not reproduce, one is real and now has a concrete fix, and one holds as stated.**
  (A) THE SUPPORT CONSTANT - OBJECTION DOES NOT REPRODUCE. The stress pass said the measured bootstrap gives
      k ~= 4.8 against the design's k=3, making every resolution claim 1.5-4x optimistic. Measuring it directly
      - a BT board per anchor, bootstrapped over QUESTIONS, k = q*SE^2 per (anchor, model) cell, 168 cells -
      gives k median **2.06** (p10 1.33, p90 3.02). k=3 therefore OVERSTATES the per-cell SE by 1.21x and the
      design's resolution is CONSERVATIVE, not optimistic. At the measured k, SE=0.20 needs 51 distinct
      questions per cell rather than 75, which makes the atlas slightly MORE feasible than the design claims.
  (B) THE SEPARATION CERTIFICATE - OBJECTION REAL, AND THE FIX IS ONE NUMBER. Calibrated on all
      **891 (anchor, model-pair) edges** with a key gap above 2pp, rather than the 66 global pairs the design
      used:
          threshold   called   declined   wrong-direction   95% upper bound
            0.900       800        91          2.00%             2.97%
            0.950       772       119          1.68%             2.59%
            0.975       732       159          0.82%             1.47%
            0.990       714       177          0.84%             1.51%
            1.000       667       224          0.60%             1.19%
      The design's target of ZERO wrong separations is unattainable at any threshold, exactly as objected - but
      the real rate at its chosen 0.95 is **1.68%**, not the 3.7% the stress pass estimated from 66 edges.
      ACTIONABLE: move the certificate from 0.95 to **0.975**, which halves the wrong-direction rate to 0.82%
      (95% upper bound 1.47%) at the cost of declining 40 more edges out of 891. State the target as a rate with
      an upper bound, never as a zero count - on 66 edges a 0% observation cannot be distinguished from 4%.
  (C) CROSS-CELL SCALE - OBJECTION HOLDS. Fitting each anchor's own board on the shared roster, the theta
      standard deviation runs **0.937 (Business) to 1.630 (Physics), a 1.7x spread**. A tier map that compares
      raw theta across anchors is comparing numbers on scales that differ by that factor. Either publish
      theta/SD with the SD beside it, or publish independent within-anchor boards and make no cross-anchor
      statement at all. The design does the latter for its refusals and the former implicitly in its atlas; it
      must pick one.
  PROCESS NOTE: my first version of (B) inflated the interval as |p-0.5|/f, which is unsatisfiable for f > 1.11
  and duly reported 0 edges called at every f above 1. The quantity the design actually sets is the confidence
  threshold; sweeping that is the correct instrument. Corrected before recording.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/resolve_calibration.txt; script tools/analysis/resolve_calibration.py.

Splitting 3,130 questions three ways leaves CERT-IMMEDIATE at [ID-ONLY 2026-09-23 (CLAIMS-SWEEP-BRACKETS, registrar): pool bareq512_s42 (p2dca); verified by id only, not by content; reviewed twins on this pool (reviews 1df2cf1, 8ebfa7a): 37 exact / 70 norm-v1 EVAL texts among members of bareq512_s42 (20260909_212117); judged-row option-set 64 / ordered 31; labelling and induction ON: 28 norm-only twins in induction corpora (exact), 26 twin texts in labelling prompts; see docs/judge_v2_program.md L14280-L14340 (CONTENT-DISJOINT-SPLIT-AUDIT) and L14455-L14487 (SPLIT-FOLLOWUPS).]
  roughly 80 questions, which will not support its interval. F5's registered PRIMARY - "positive within
