[ID-ONLY 2026-09-23 (CLAIMS-SWEEP-BRACKETS, registrar): pool bareq512_s42 (p2dca); verified by id only, not by content; reviewed twins on this pool (reviews 1df2cf1, 8ebfa7a): 37 exact / 70 norm-v1 EVAL texts among members of bareq512_s42 (20260909_212117); judged-row option-set 64 / ordered 31; labelling and induction ON: 28 norm-only twins in induction corpora (exact), 26 twin texts in labelling prompts; see docs/judge_v2_program.md L14280-L14340 (CONTENT-DISJOINT-SPLIT-AUDIT) and L14455-L14487 (SPLIT-FOLLOWUPS).]
  F6 CANNOT BE CLEANED, and here is why it matters. F6 compares construction variants by scoring each tree's
  nearest-centroid cells on the same keyed question set. Each variant was built on its OWN split, so a common
  scoring set is training data for every tree in a different place. The validation CSVs record held-out COUNTS
  per leaf (MAIN_heldout_leaf_support.csv) but NOT the held-out question ids, so the per-tree held-out sets
  cannot be reconstructed from what was committed. That is a reproducibility gap in the sweep runs themselves,
  and the fix is forward-looking: record the reserved id list with every build.
  WHAT CAN BE SAID WITHOUT THE DATA, and it is not nothing. The contamination advantages each tree on its own
  training portion. F6's NEGATIVE findings are therefore conservative: abt2 loses 1.5-1.7/1000 to frozen DESPITE
  being scored partly on its own training questions, so its true loss is at least that. F6's NULL finding is the
  one at risk: "d512 loses no key-only information vs frozen" (-0.45/-0.27) is measured with the same advantage,
  so d512 may lose a little. Since D2 promoted bareq512 partly on that null, the promotion rests on a result
  whose direction of bias favours the promoted tree.
  THE CUMULATIVE PICTURE. Four key-only or key-level tests carried the claim that sub-anchor structure is real
  and useful: LEAF-PROFILE arm A (fails its registered criterion on held-out data, 3/13 anchors), F2 (+3.15 ->
  +0.74, tie), F5 (+2.98 -> +0.85), and F6 (uncorrectable, biased toward the promoted tree). Against them stand
  LEAF-POWER, LEAF-SHRINK, LEAF-POWERED and MC-LEAF, all negative and none contaminated in this way. The
  asymmetry is not an accident: the negative tests score models on held-out ARENA verdicts, while the positive
  ones score cells on questions that built them.
  Output experiment_results/free_tests_f4_f7_output.txt (regenerated with the clean row).

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any candidate is run) — REF-QUAL: qualify a reference before buying a re-judge
A better reference is the only lever measured to raise the judge's ceiling rather than move along it (ORACLE:
+16.4pp from a perfect one). It cannot buy the frontier ORDER - ORACLE handed the judge the answer key and
arx/iask still did not come out, p=0.29 - so the payoff is concentrated where the incumbent is WEAK, and
REF-BY-CELL measured that spread at 0.727 to 0.952 across anchors. ENSEMBLE-REF showed a stronger reference
cannot be assembled from inside the contestant set. So the question is which OUTSIDE model, and the answer is
worth 600 calls before it is worth 10,000.
THE INCUMBENT'S BASELINES, computed from cache (zero calls) so the gate is against measured numbers:
    discriminating subset (299 questions)      0.726
    History 0.680 | Engineering 0.780 | Law 0.714      <- the three weakest routed cells
    answer-agreement with the frontier: gemini 0.888, arx 0.870, iask 0.864, gpt-4o 0.790
DESIGN, per candidate: solve the 302 arx/iask discriminating questions and 100 questions from each of the three
weak cells under the contestants' own chain-of-thought prompt. About 600 calls.
REGISTERED READOUTS. (1) accuracy on the discriminating subset against 0.726; (2) accuracy per weak cell against
the three numbers above; (3) ANSWER-AGREEMENT with each of the twelve contestants against the incumbent's.
Readout (3) is the leakage term: DECOMP established that the inflation mechanism is answer agreement and not
vendor identity, so a candidate that mirrors a FRONTIER contestant more closely than grok-reasoning does will
inflate that contestant whatever badge it carries.
GATE, fixed now. PROMOTE to a full re-judge only if (1) beats the incumbent by at least 3pp AND (3) shows no
frontier contestant gaining more than 3pp of agreement. A candidate failing (1) cannot raise the ceiling; one
failing (3) buys accuracy and pays for it in bias exactly where the board is already weakest.
FAMILY NOTE, for choosing candidates. Of the families in the deployment catalogue, only MOONSHOT (Kimi) and
MICROSOFT (MAI) have no representative in the twelve-model roster; OpenAI is represented by gpt-4o at key 0.750
- inside the frontier group, the worst place for leakage to land - DeepSeek by deepseek-chat-v2_5 at 0.657, and
Cohere only by c4ai-command-r-v01 at 0.363, which is bottom-tier and therefore a harmless place for it to land.
Family is a proxy; readout (3) measures the thing itself.
Output experiment_results/judge_solve/refqual_<model>.txt; cache refqual_<model>.db; script tools/analysis/ref_qualify.py.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before looking at any result, ZERO calls) — SYSTEMATIC-SIGNAL: can a free signal predict where the bootstrap is confidently wrong?
TIER-HONEST found the failure mode that decides whether a tiered product is shippable: across-tier pairs are
separated 62 of 64 with ZERO wrong directions, while within-tier pairs are separated 2 of 2 - both overconfident,
one of them the arx/iask inversion the arena is 100% sure about and the key contradicts. A bootstrap interval
sees sampling noise and never a bias present in every sample, so it tightens around the wrong answer.
RESOLVE's answer is to widen each interval by a measured SYSTEMATIC budget, and it names three candidate signals
already in the data: the 5.7% test-retest floor, the per-cell reference accuracy (REF-BY-CELL, 0.727-0.952), and
the ANSWER-AGREEMENT rate between the two models, which the shipped disagreement filter already computes for
free. If none of them predicts a wrong call, the design's fix for its worst flaw does not work and the tier map
cannot be trusted at the boundaries that matter.
DESIGN, zero calls. Take the 891 (anchor, model-pair) edges from RESOLVE-CALIB - each with the arena's bootstrap
P(A above B) and the key's verdict on that anchor. For each edge compute three free predictors: (a) the two
models' ANSWER-AGREEMENT rate within that anchor; (b) the incumbent reference's accuracy in that anchor; (c) the
key gap between the two models there. Then ask whether the wrong-direction edges are distinguishable from the
right ones.
REGISTERED. (1) PRIMARY: among edges the arena CALLS at the 0.975 threshold, the mean answer-agreement of
wrong-direction edges minus that of correct ones, with a bootstrap CI - the signal works if that difference is
positive and its CI excludes zero. (2) the same for reference accuracy, expected NEGATIVE (a weaker reference
should predict error). (3) a two-predictor logistic of wrong-direction on agreement and reference accuracy, to
see whether either survives the other. (4) OPERATING POINT: if a signal works, the agreement threshold at which
declining edges would have removed the wrong calls, and how many correct calls that costs.
PREDICTIONS: answer-agreement is the stronger signal and gives a difference of +0.05 to +0.15; reference accuracy
is weaker and may not survive; and a usable operating point declines under 15% of called edges to remove most
wrong ones. POWER CAVEAT, stated now: at the 0.975 threshold RESOLVE-CALIB measured 0.82% wrong of 732 called,
so roughly SIX wrong edges. Six events cannot support a confident answer, and a null here must be reported as
UNDERPOWERED rather than as evidence the signal does not work.
Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/systematic_signal.txt; script tools/analysis/systematic_signal.py.

- **SYSTEMATIC-SIGNAL (2026-09-14, zero calls): CONFIRMED. Two free signals predict where the bootstrap is
  confidently wrong, and both survive each other.** This is the first validation of a RESOLVE component, and it
  addresses the design's worst flaw - TIER-HONEST's finding that a bootstrap interval tightens around the wrong
  answer wherever the judge is systematically biased.
  On the 891 (anchor, model-pair) edges, 739 called at the 0.975 threshold, of which 8 point the wrong way:
      predictor                          wrong    right    difference          95% CI
      answer-agreement                   0.704    0.437      +0.267      [+0.150, +0.374]
      reference accuracy in the anchor   0.765    0.852      -0.088      [-0.111, -0.052]
      key gap between the pair           0.066    0.356      -0.290      [-0.318, -0.261]
  All three exclude zero and all three point the predicted way. The key gap is the sanity check - close pairs
  are wrong more often, which must be true - and it is not available at deployment. The other two are FREE: the
  answer-agreement rate is what the shipped disagreement filter already computes, and the reference's per-cell
  accuracy is what REF-BY-CELL measured.
  [CORRECTED 2026-09-14 by SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET, three ways, before any of this was published outside the repo:
   (a) CALLING REFERENCE ACCURACY A "FREE" SIGNAL WAS WRONG. It is free of extra CALLS and it is KEY-DERIVED:
       rejudge_reference.references() returns the reference graded against the answer key (rejudge_reference.py
       lines 69 and 79) and lines 63-64 above average exactly that. It cannot be computed at deployment on
       unkeyed data. A per-cell reference accuracy CALIBRATED once on keyed data and carried as a constant is a
       legitimate deployment story - it is REF-BY-CELL's own framing - but it is a narrower claim than the one
       made here, and it does not transfer to new cells without new keyed data. The shipped budget therefore
       carries answer agreement ONLY, even though adding reference accuracy fits materially better (LOAO
       deviance 193.55 against 216.94).
   (b) THE DENOMINATOR IS SELECTED. The 0.82%/1.08% wrong-call rates rest on the key-gap >= 0.02 filter at line
       67, which is itself unavailable at deployment and which drops edges that are far MORE often wrong. On the
       honest denominator: 920 edges, 60 wrong, 748 called with 11 wrong = 1.47%.
   (c) 41% OF THE WRONG-DIRECTION LABELS ARE NOT ESTABLISHED. Exact two-sided McNemar on the two models'
       per-question correctness adjudicates 809 of the 891; 18 of the 44 "wrong" edges sit among the 82 it
       cannot. The effect survives - refitting the budget on established edges only takes b1 from 3.3133 to
       2.1430 - but a reader told "44 wrong edges" should be told that 18 of them rest on a direction the key
       does not settle.]
  (3) AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME SIGNAL. A two-predictor logistic over all 891 edges (44 wrong) gives
  answer-agreement **+1.511 +- 0.215 (z=+7.0)** and reference accuracy **-0.798 +- 0.190 (z=-4.2)**; each
  survives conditioning on the other. So a systematic budget should carry both terms: how much the two models
  agree, and how good the reference is in that cell.
  (4) BUT MY OPERATING-POINT TABLE WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT, and the table says so. Declining a called edge when
  the pair's agreement exceeds 0.70 removes 4 of the 8 wrong calls and costs 97 of the 731 correct ones; at 0.85
  it removes 2 and costs 11. As a HARD GATE the signal is poor, because at a 1.1% base rate any gate that
  catches half the errors throws away a lot of good calls. That is an argument against the gate, not against the
  signal - and RESOLVE does not propose a gate. It proposes widening the interval by a systematic budget, which
  is a CONTINUOUS use of exactly these two terms, and a continuous widener is not tested by a threshold sweep.
  The right follow-up is to fit the budget directly: choose the widening function so that the realised
  wrong-direction rate matches its nominal rate across agreement deciles. That is zero calls and is the
  remaining piece of RESOLVE's certificate.
  THE POWER CAVEAT I REGISTERED did not bite: I predicted the primary would rest on about six wrong edges and be
  underpowered. There are eight, but the effect is large enough (+0.267) that its interval clears zero anyway,
  and the logistic uses all 44 wrong edges across the full set. The registered prediction of a +0.05 to +0.15
  agreement difference was too small by a factor of two.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/systematic_signal.txt; script tools/analysis/systematic_signal.py.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any fit is run, ZERO calls) — SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET: fit the widener SYSTEMATIC-SIGNAL licensed
SYSTEMATIC-SIGNAL established that two free signals - the pair's answer-agreement in a cell and the reference's
accuracy in that cell - each predict where the bootstrap points the wrong way, and each survives the other
(z=+7.0 and z=-4.2 over 891 edges, 44 wrong). It also established what does NOT follow: used as a hard gate the
signals are poor, because at a 1.1% base rate a gate catching half the errors discards 13% of the good calls.
RESOLVE never proposed a gate. It proposed WIDENING each edge's interval by a systematic budget that is a
continuous function of those two signals, so that the realised wrong-direction rate matches the nominal rate the
certificate claims. That function has not been written down, let alone fitted. This fits it.
DESIGN, zero calls. Four functional forms, derived and fitted independently, each adversarially reviewed:
  (A) ADDITIVE VARIANCE  Var_total = Var_boot + g(agreement, reference accuracy); recompute P from the widened
      distribution. Standard, and assumes the systematic error is zero-mean, which a directional bias is not.
  (B) DIRECTIONAL SHIFT  a shift in the theta difference sized by the signals, plus a variance term. Fits the
      measured bias better and needs a deployment-available proxy for the shift's DIRECTION, which may not exist.
  (C) RECALIBRATION      map raw bootstrap P to a calibrated P on (P, agreement, reference accuracy). Needs the
      key to fit and may not transfer to a new roster.
  (D) CONFORMAL          no error model; per-stratum thresholds whose held-out wrong rate clears the target,
      with a finite-sample correction. The most honest at 44 events and the least informative.
REGISTERED CRITERIA, fixed now. A form is ADOPTABLE only if all four hold:
  (1) CALIBRATION under leave-one-ANCHOR-out (14 folds; NOT leave-one-edge-out, because edges within an anchor
      share a bootstrap and a reference accuracy): realised wrong-direction rate at or below nominal.
  (2) UTILITY: it still CALLS at least 60% of the 891 edges at a 95% nominal level. A budget that calls nothing
      is perfectly calibrated and useless, and refusing to speak is the failure mode this must not buy.
  (3) NO KEY AT INFERENCE: every input the function needs at deployment is available without the answer key.
  (4) PARAMETER DISCIPLINE: at most 3 free parameters, counting any threshold or bin boundary chosen by looking
      at the data. With 44 wrong edges and 8 at the operating threshold, more than that is fitting noise.
PREDICTIONS: (B) fits best in sample and fails (3), because the direction of the bias is exactly what is not
observable without the key; (A) and (C) pass (1) in sample and at least one degrades materially under
leave-one-anchor-out; (D) passes (1) and fails (2). And the headline prediction, stated now so it cannot be
retrofitted: the adopted budget WILL withdraw the arx/iask separation, because that pair is the single case the
whole exercise exists for - if a fitted budget leaves arx/iask confidently separated in the wrong direction, the
budget does not work whatever its aggregate calibration says.
NULL IS PUBLISHABLE. If no form clears all four, the honest output is that 44 wrong edges cannot support a
fitted systematic budget, and RESOLVE ships the conformal per-stratum threshold as a stated limitation rather
than a calibrated certificate.
Output docs/design/RESOLVE_budget.md; workflow fit-systematic-budget.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any run, ZERO calls) — PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST: does the sub-anchor capability profile survive a change of tree?
RESOLVE's deliverable is a GRANULAR CAPABILITY PROFILE: statements of the form "model m is stronger than its own
average in cell c". Every such statement is made relative to a partition that was itself estimated. Nothing in
the programme has ever asked whether those statements survive re-estimating the partition. They should be asked,
because two results now bracket the question from opposite sides: ANCHOR-VALUE says the anchor layer is a
reporting convenience rather than a routing mechanism, and LEAF-PROFILE-CLEAN says the one result claiming real
sub-anchor structure does not survive being restricted to held-out data. If a leaf-level profile also fails to
survive a change of tree, then the anchor is the reporting ceiling on THREE independent grounds and RESOLVE
should stop carrying sub-anchor rows as a someday feature.
WHY THIS IS NOW FREE. H10 was registered at ~18,000 calls because a different tree gives different per-cell
rubrics, so every match needed re-judging. The rubric line is CLOSED - induced prose is null everywhere and the
only surviving increment is the data-only leaf card, which REF-GATED-RUBRIC showed acts solely where the
reference is right. With rubric text out of the loop the counterfactual reduces to RE-CELLING THE SAME VERDICTS,
which costs nothing. This is H10's question answered at 0 calls instead of 18,000, and it is registered as its
own test rather than as H10 because the instrument is different.
DESIGN. Two trees built on the SAME clean reserved pool (p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae), same seed, differing in embedding [ID-ONLY 2026-09-23 (CLAIMS-SWEEP-BRACKETS, registrar): pool bareq512_s42 (p2dca); verified by id only, not by content; reviewed twins on this pool (reviews 1df2cf1, 8ebfa7a): 37 exact / 70 norm-v1 EVAL texts among members of bareq512_s42 (20260909_212117); judged-row option-set 64 / ordered 31; labelling and induction ON: 28 norm-only twins in induction corpora (exact), 26 twin texts in labelling prompts; see docs/judge_v2_program.md L14280-L14340 (CONTENT-DISJOINT-SPLIT-AUDIT) and L14455-L14487 (SPLIT-FOLLOWUPS).]
configuration: bareq512_s42 (87 leaves, 158 nodes) and abt2d512_s42 (47 leaves, 67 nodes). Identical question
sets, 3,445 each. Anchor assignment already measured at 99.7% agreement, which is expected and is NOT a test -
the anchors are the MMLU-Pro categories, pinned at depth 1, so an anchor-level counterfactual is a null by
construction and is reported as such. The test is at the LEAF level. Fit a per-leaf BT board from the x12 verdict
cache under each tree, centre each model's per-leaf strength by its global strength, and compare the two
profiles question by question.
REGISTERED CRITERIA, fixed now.
 (1) PRIMARY: the correlation between the two trees' centred per-(model, question) strengths, with a
     QUESTION-CLUSTERED bootstrap CI, against a null built from 200 random partitions matched on each tree's
     leaf-size distribution. Sub-anchor reporting is ADOPTABLE only if the observed correlation both exceeds the
     null's 95th percentile AND exceeds 0.50. Beating the null alone is not enough: a partition of the right
     shape recovers some structure trivially, and a profile that is real but only half-reproducible is not
     publishable as a per-cell claim.
 (2) SECONDARY: ROUTER AGREEMENT - how often the two trees' profiles name the same best model for the same
     question - and the realised key-decidable accuracy of each tree's leaf router against the single best
     model. LEAF-POWER predicts neither router beats the global best.
 (3) THE READER'S NUMBER: the SIGN-REVERSAL rate - the share of (model, question) profile statements whose sign
     flips between the two trees. This is what a reader needs in order to know what a published per-cell claim
     is worth, and it is reported whatever the primary does.
PREDICTIONS: correlation 0.3-0.6, clearly above the random-partition null but BELOW the 0.50 bar or only just
at it; router agreement under 50%; neither leaf router beats the global best model; sign-reversal rate 20-35%.
That is, I expect the profile to be real but not reproducible enough to publish per cell - which would make this
the third independent reason to treat the anchor as the reporting ceiling.
FALSIFIER, stated so the test can lose: if the correlation clears 0.50 and the null, and sign reversal comes in
under 15%, then sub-anchor reporting is supported, LEAF-PROFILE-CLEAN's power caveat is the better reading of
that result, and RESOLVE should carry leaf rows.
Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/profile_tree_robust.txt; script tools/analysis/profile_tree_robust.py.

- **PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST (2026-09-14, zero calls): the sub-anchor capability structure is REAL and survives a
  change of tree. The JUDGE cannot resolve it, and the blocker is questions-per-cell, not the tree, not the
  rubric and not the judge's quality.** This reconciles four results the programme had been reading as evidence
  that sub-anchor structure is absent. They were all measuring an estimate whose split-half reliability is 0.086.
  THE REGISTERED PRIMARY PASSES AND I AM REPORTING THAT IT WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT. Raw centred-strength
  correlation +0.9147, CI [+0.9115, +0.9179], against a size-matched random-partition null whose 95th percentile
  is +0.8764 - so it clears both registered conditions. But a RANDOM partition scores +0.8643, so the 0.50 bar I
  registered was miscalibrated: anything would clear it. The cause is a shrinkage artefact - a small cell pulls
  the whole BT vector toward zero, so the centred profile is roughly (s_c - 1) x theta_global and both trees end
  up proportional to the SAME global ordering whatever the partition. Only the +0.0504 margin over the null
  carries information. Flagged explicitly against the audit's C-7 criterion-substitution pattern: the registered
  criteria are reported as passing, and each replacement analysis below was written and committed to the script
  BEFORE its result was computed, which is the only thing that makes the substitution legitimate.
      (1b) AMENDMENT, model means removed:     judge r +0.4754 [+0.4613, +0.4901] vs null 95th pct +0.0258
      (2)  router agreement 0.598; leaf routers 0.8494 / 0.8515 against global best gemini 0.9068 - LEAF-POWER's
           prediction that neither beats the global best HELD, at -5.7pp and -5.5pp
      (3)  sign-reversal rate 0.072 overall, 0.039 restricted to |centred strength| >= 0.20
      (4)  KEY-derived cross-tree r +0.8143 vs null 95th pct +0.0348 - the judge-artefact explanation is REJECTED
      (5)  split-half reliability, same tree, disjoint halves: judge +0.0860 (SB R=0.158), key +0.7201 (R=0.837)
      (6)  stratified by how much the question's CELL COMPANY actually changes between trees:
             mean overlap 0.146   judge r +0.1895   key r +0.6836
             mean overlap 0.280   judge r +0.4815   key r +0.8112
             mean overlap 0.585   judge r +0.7497   key r +0.9406
  (5) AND (6) ARE THE RESULT. The judge's cross-tree agreement of +0.4754 is 5.5x its own independent-sample
  reliability of +0.0860 - two measurements sharing almost all their data agree far better than two sharing
  none, which is what shared data does and not what reproducible structure does. Stratifying confirms it
  directly: where the trees genuinely disagree about a question's company the judge falls to +0.1895 while the
  KEY holds at +0.6836. So the structure is a property of the QUESTIONS, it is tree-robust, and the judge's
  estimate of it is not. A disattenuation I wrote to separate noise from fidelity returned +1.1947 for the
  judge; a correlation cannot exceed 1, so its assumptions are broken and its verdict - which would have read
  "NOISE, not fidelity" - is discarded rather than reported.
  (7) THE ACTIONABLE NUMBER. Spearman-Brown from the measured R=0.158: reaching reliability 0.80 needs 21.3x the
  current per-cell evidence, about 1,127 questions per leaf against the 53 now available, or ~59,764 questions
  where the reserved pool holds 2,811. And it must come from NEW QUESTIONS, not more matches: TEMP-0 established
  the 5.7% test-retest floor is intrinsic and survives temperature 0, so re-judging adds no independent
  evidence. A reliable per-leaf capability profile is out of reach on MMLU-Pro at ANY call budget. That is a
  DATA limit, and it is the honest reason every leaf-level test in this programme has been underpowered.
  WHAT THIS CHANGES. LEAF-POWER, LEAF-SHRINK, LEAF-POWERED, MC-LEAF and LEAF-PROFILE-CLEAN were all read as
  evidence that sub-anchor structure is absent or does not survive. This says the structure is present and
  tree-robust in the key, and those tests were measuring a judge estimate with reliability 0.086. The correct
  statement is not "sub-anchor capability is not there" but "this corpus cannot resolve it, and no judge
  improvement fixes that". RESOLVE should publish the anchor as the reporting ceiling ON A DATA GROUND, state
  the questions-per-cell requirement, and stop treating leaf rows as a someday feature to be unlocked by a
  better judge or a better tree.
  REGISTERED PREDICTIONS, scored: correlation 0.3-0.6 HELD on the amended statistic (+0.4754), though (5)-(6)
  then showed that statistic is contaminated; "neither router beats the global best" HELD; router agreement
  under 50% FAILED (0.598); sign reversal 20-35% FAILED badly (0.072). My registered FALSIFIER fired by the
  letter - correlation clears 0.50 and its null, sign reversal is under 15% - which would have licensed
  sub-anchor reporting. It fired on the two statistics the controls show to be contaminated by shared data, and
  the falsifier is recorded as HAVING FIRED AND BEING WRONG rather than quietly dropped.
  ALSO: H10 is answered. It was registered at ~18,000 calls because a different tree gives different per-cell
  rubrics; the rubric line closed, so the counterfactual reduced to re-celling the same verdicts at 0 calls.
  ANCHOR LEVEL is reported as a null by construction, not a result: the two trees agree on 2,800 of 2,811
  questions (0.996) because the anchors ARE the pinned MMLU-Pro categories.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/profile_tree_robust.txt; script tools/analysis/profile_tree_robust.py.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any run, ZERO calls) — PROFILE-RELIABILITY: is the ANCHOR-level profile reliable, and at what cell size does reliability arrive?
PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST measured the judge's per-LEAF capability profile at a split-half reliability of 0.086
(Spearman-Brown R=0.158) on ~53 questions per cell, and concluded the anchor is the reporting ceiling. That
conclusion has an obvious hole in it which I am not entitled to leave unexamined: I never measured the ANCHOR.
RESOLVE's deliverable is a per-ANCHOR capability profile, so if anchor-level reliability is also poor then the
product is in question and not merely its finest layer. The leaf result gives no comfort either way, because
anchors carry roughly four times the questions and reliability is strongly size-dependent.
DESIGN, zero calls, identical instrument to PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST (5) so the numbers are comparable. Split each
cell's questions into two disjoint halves, build the judge-derived centred profile on each, correlate them
model-demeaned, Spearman-Brown to full length. Run it at three granularities - leaf, anchor, and the whole pool
as a floor check - and run the ANSWER KEY through the identical pipeline at each, as the instrument-independent
comparator. Then sweep cell size directly: bin cells by question count and report reliability per bin, to find
the size at which the judge's profile becomes usable.
REGISTERED CRITERIA, fixed now.
 (1) PRIMARY: the ANCHOR-level judge profile is publishable as a per-cell capability claim only if its
     Spearman-Brown reliability is at least 0.70. That is the conventional minimum for a group-level claim and
     it is being fixed here before the number is seen, not chosen afterwards to fit it.
 (2) The key-derived reliability at the same granularity, as the comparator that says whether any shortfall is
     the judge's or the cell's.
 (3) THE DESIGN NUMBER: the questions-per-cell at which judge reliability crosses 0.70, read off the size sweep.
     This is what a future corpus has to deliver per cell and it is the one number the design most needs.
PREDICTIONS: anchor-level judge reliability lands between 0.35 and 0.60 - better than the leaf's 0.158 by
roughly the 4x size ratio but still short of 0.70; the key clears 0.90 at anchor level; and the crossing point
comes in around 250-400 questions per cell. If that is right, MMLU-Pro's 14 anchors at ~200 questions each sit
just below the bar, and the honest statement is that even the ANCHOR profile is marginal on this corpus.
CONSEQUENCE, stated in advance so it cannot be softened later. If (1) fails, RESOLVE may not publish per-anchor
capability claims as measured quantities; it publishes the board and the routing layer, and the capability
profile becomes a stated aspiration with the questions-per-cell requirement attached. If (1) passes, the anchor
is confirmed as the reporting level on measured ground rather than by elimination.
Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/profile_reliability.txt; script tools/analysis/profile_reliability.py.

- **PROFILE-RELIABILITY (2026-09-14, zero calls): the ANCHOR profile misses the registered bar by 0.027, and the
  crossing point is 210 questions per cell — almost exactly where MMLU-Pro's anchors already sit.** The
  consequence was registered in advance and it fires.
      level         cells   q/cell    judge r   judge R(SB)   key R(SB)
      leaf              8       71     0.1467        0.2559      0.8135
      anchor           14      201     0.5069        0.6728      0.9135
      whole pool        1     2811        n/a           n/a         n/a   (undefined by construction)
  (1) PRIMARY: anchor-level judge Spearman-Brown reliability **0.6728 against a registered bar of 0.70 - FAIL**.
  The estimate is stable: split-half SD 0.0443 over 40 independent halvings, so R is good to about +-0.012, and
  the 0.0272 shortfall is larger than that. I am not rounding it up. The bar was fixed before the number was
  seen precisely so that a near miss could not be talked into a pass.
  CONSEQUENCE, as registered: **RESOLVE may not publish per-anchor capability claims as measured quantities.**
  It publishes the board and the routing layer; the granular capability profile becomes a stated aspiration
  carrying its questions-per-cell requirement. This is the deliverable the whole design was organised around,
  and it does not survive its own reliability check on this corpus.
  (2) THE SHORTFALL IS THE JUDGE'S, NOT THE CELL'S. At identical granularity the KEY reaches 0.9135 where the
  judge reaches 0.6728 (ratio 0.74), and at leaf level 0.8135 against 0.2559 (ratio 0.31). The cells carry a
  stable signal at both granularities; the judge's estimate of it is what degrades, and it degrades faster as
  the cells get smaller.
  (3) THE DESIGN NUMBER. Subsampling every anchor to a common size, with the cell definition held fixed:
      q/cell    50      75     100     150     200
      judge  0.1919  0.1665  0.3616  0.4356  0.6891
      key    0.7143  0.8285  0.8513  0.9164  0.9283
  Judge reliability does not reach 0.70 at any size this pool can supply (max 304 q/cell in one anchor), and
  Spearman-Brown from the 200-question point puts the crossing at about **210 questions per cell**. MMLU-Pro's
  anchors average 201. So the anchor layer sits essentially ON the threshold rather than comfortably above it,
  which is why it lands at 0.6728 - and it means the anchor profile is not merely unpublishable here, it is
  MARGINAL BY DESIGN and a corpus with slightly smaller categories would fail it outright.
  The key's column is the counterpoint worth keeping: it clears 0.70 at 50 questions per cell. A capability
  profile built from an answer key needs a quarter of the data a judge-built one does.
  REGISTERED PREDICTIONS, scored: "anchor between 0.35 and 0.60" FAILED - I was too pessimistic, it is 0.6728;
  "the key clears 0.90 at anchor level" HELD at 0.9135; "crossing at 250-400 q/cell" FAILED - it is ~210. Two
  of three predictions wrong, both in the direction of the judge being better than I expected, and the primary
  still fails.
  WHY THIS TEST EXISTED. PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST concluded the anchor is the reporting ceiling without ever
  measuring the anchor - it measured leaves and reasoned upward. That hole is now closed, and the answer is
  worse for the design than the inference was: the anchor is the ceiling AND the ceiling itself is marginal.
  COMPARABILITY NOTE: this reports leaf R=0.2559 where PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST reported 0.158, because that used a
  25-question floor and this uses 50, so this leaf row covers fewer and larger cells. Both are consistent with
  the size sweep, which is the instrument that settles it.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/profile_reliability.txt; script tools/analysis/profile_reliability.py.

- **REF-QUAL-KIMI, first attempt (2026-09-14, ~569 calls): VOID — my instrument was broken, not the candidate.**
  The gate printed a decisive FAIL (discriminating subset 0.423 against the incumbent's 0.725, **-0.302**) and
  that number is meaningless. **227 of 561 responses, 40.5%, came back with COMPLETELY EMPTY content**, and an
  empty answer scores as wrong, so the reported accuracy is a floor and not an estimate.
  THE CAUSE, diagnosed by re-issuing one of the empty questions and reading the fields the run never stored:
      finish_reason 'length' | completion_tokens 8192 of 8192 | content 0 chars | reasoning_content 27,234 chars
  Kimi-K2.6 spends its whole completion budget in the `reasoning_content` channel and never emits a final
  answer. MAX_TOKENS was 8192, the value every other judge in the programme has used without trouble because no
  previous judge reasoned this long. Re-issuing the same three empty questions at 32,768 tokens returns
  finish_reason 'stop' at 7,913 / 16,078 / 10,385 completion tokens, and **all three answer correctly** (D, E,
  H). Among the 334 responses that did parse, accuracy was **0.874** against the incumbent's 0.725 - which is
  NOT a claim that Kimi is better, because those are exactly the questions short enough to finish, a biased and
  easier subset. The honest statement is that the run measured nothing.
  WHAT IT WOULD HAVE COST. Recorded as a FAIL this would have rejected a candidate reference on a token limit,
  and the rejection would have looked clean: a large negative effect, a gate that passed its leakage check, and
  a tidy "600 calls spent instead of 10,000". Nothing in the output said the instrument had failed.
  THE FIX, and it is the part that generalises. (a) `rejudge_reasoning.call_judge_full()` added, returning
  finish_reason and the raw message alongside the existing four values; `call_judge` now delegates to it and
  keeps its 4-tuple, because three callers unpack exactly four values and the request payload must stay
  byte-identical for every existing script. (b) `ref_qualify` takes `--maxtok`, writes to its own cache so a
  voided run is preserved as evidence instead of overwritten, and stores finish_reason and completion_tokens.
  (c) A TRUNCATION GUARD prints before the gate whenever more than 5% of answers fail to parse, says the gate is
  not interpretable, and breaks down finish_reason among the unparsed. It fires correctly on the voided cache.
  CLASS OF DEFECT: a silent instrument failure that presents as a clean negative result. The programme has a
  written rule for population mismatches after three of them; this is the same shape in a different place - an
  output that cannot be distinguished from a valid one without a field the run did not record. The rule that
  follows: any run scoring a model's own answers must record finish_reason and refuse to report a verdict when
  the unparsed rate exceeds 5%.
  Re-running at 32,768 tokens; the void cache stays at refqual_Kimi_K2_6.db, the corrected one at
  refqual_Kimi_K2_6_mt32768.db.

- **SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET (2026-09-14, zero calls): all four registered criteria PASS, the registered headline
  prediction HELD, the registered FALLBACK is falsified — and three numbers I published earlier are corrected.**
  Four forms were derived and adversarially verified (additive variance 76, recalibration 72, conformal 54,
  directional shift 47). I then rebuilt the winner independently from the repo's own construction rather than
  accept it; the fit reproduces to the digit.
  THE ADOPTED FORM, two free parameters and no key at inference:
      tau(A) = exp(b0 + b1*A),  b0 = -3.2326, b1 = +3.3133
      c = min( c_raw , Phi( |m| / sqrt(s^2 + tau^2) ) ),   call iff c >= 0.975
  where A is the pair's answer agreement in the cell and m, s are the first two moments of theta_a - theta_b
  over the 300 bootstrap boards. tau = 0.107 / 0.288 / 0.778 at A = 0.30 / 0.60 / 0.90, against a per-anchor
  bootstrap s of median 0.246. Monotonicity verified: 0 of 891 edges are made MORE confident and no call is
  created. b1 > 0 is the direction SYSTEMATIC-SIGNAL predicted.
      certificate                     called   wrong   nominal   ratio
      raw (tau = 0)                      739       8      0.83    9.7x
      budget, in sample                  665       2      1.30    1.5x
      budget, LEAVE-ONE-ANCHOR-OUT       663       3      1.27    2.4x
  Out-of-fold nominal over all 891 edges is 48.7 against 44 observed - conservative.
  REGISTERED CRITERIA: (1) LOAO calibration PASS in aggregate; [OUTPUT OF RECORD 2026-09-23, registrar: criterion (1)'s output of record is now experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/systematic_budget_2026-09-23_corrected.txt (sha256 55ef9b3d453bf3a6...), which reads 'UNDETERMINED (nominal < 3)' on the CALLED set; the 2026-09-14 file is kept unchanged as history; see '## SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET-FIX M2 MET, and the output of record for SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET criterion (1) (2026-09-23, zer ...' at the END of this file.] at the operating point 3 against 1.27 is 2.4x
  and with three events that is neither calibrated nor detectably miscalibrated, whereas the raw certificate's
  8 against 0.83 is miscalibrated at p < 1e-4. The honest claim is that the budget REMOVES AN ESTABLISHED
  MISCALIBRATION AND REPLACES IT WITH ONE THAT IS NO LONGER DETECTABLE. (2) PASS, 74.4% of edges still called
  against a 60% floor. (3) PASS. (4) PASS, two parameters, no bins and no fitted threshold.
  REGISTERED HEADLINE PREDICTION HELD: arx/iask, the pair the whole exercise exists for, goes from a raw
  certificate of **1.0000 to 0.7805** and its call is withdrawn.
  REGISTERED FALLBACK FALSIFIED. The registration said that if no form cleared the bar, RESOLVE would ship the
  conformal per-stratum threshold as a stated limitation. That option is gone: its f = 1.865 collapses to
  exactly 1.000 when refitted on the edges whose key direction is established, so it was a fit to label noise.
  THREE CORRECTIONS TO NUMBERS I ALREADY PUBLISHED, all found by this test.
   (a) SYSTEMATIC-SIGNAL called per-cell reference accuracy a "FREE signal" available at deployment. **It is
       key-derived.** `rejudge_reference.references()` returns the reference graded against the answer key
       (rejudge_reference.py:69,79) and systematic_signal.py:63-64 averages exactly that. It is free of extra
       CALLS, not free of the KEY. The two-predictor fit is genuinely better (LOAO deviance 193.55 against
       216.94) and is NOT DEPLOYABLE, so the shipped budget carries agreement only. Registered criterion (3)
       is what forced the weaker model, and that is the criterion doing its job.
   (b) SYSTEMATIC-SIGNAL's 1.08% wrong-call rate rests on a key-gap >= 0.02 filter that is not available at
       deployment AND selects the population. On the honest denominator: **920 edges, 60 wrong, 748 called and
       11 wrong = 1.47%**, not 1.08%. Every published rate must be restated on the unfiltered set.
   (c) **41% of the wrong-direction labels are not established.** Exact two-sided McNemar on the two models'
       per-question correctness leaves 809 of 891 edges with an adjudicated direction; 18 of the 44 wrong
       edges sit among the 82 that are indeterminate. Refit on established edges only, b1 falls 3.3133 to
       **2.1430** - 65% of it, reduced but alive, and this is the same attack that killed the conformal form.
  AND ONE CORRECTION TO THE DERIVATION, which I caught by rebuilding rather than trusting. The specification
  claimed the pooled board carries TWO inversions and that the budget withdraws both. **There is one.** The
  Meta-Llama-3.1-8B vs command-r pair has a key gap of **-0.0018** (0.3686 against 0.3703, five questions in
  2,811) and the arena AGREES with the key on it - p = 0.0000 stable across three independent bootstrap seeds.
  The pooled board is 63 called / 1 wrong, going to 57 / 0. A second inversion exists (gemini vs iask, key gap
  0.0960) but the raw certificate never called it, c = 0.59.
  THAT CORRECTION REVERSES THE DERIVATION'S CHOICE ON ONE AXIS, so the adoption is split:
      PER-ANCHOR (739 raw calls, 8 wrong)        POOLED 66-pair board (63 raw calls, 1 wrong)
      budget out of fold  663 / 3 / -71 correct  budget            57 / 0 / -5 correct
      gate A < 0.65       608 / 3 / -126         gate A < 0.85     61 / 0 / -1
      gate A < 0.80       707 / 4 / -28          gate A < 0.90     63 / 1 / -0
  Per anchor the budget DOMINATES a hard gate at matched error: three wrong for 71 correct calls surrendered
  against the gate's 126. Pooled, a ONE-LINE GATE AT A < 0.85 STRICTLY DOMINATES IT - zero wrong for one
  correct call surrendered against the budget's five. The specification argued the opposite ("its advantage is
  on the pooled board"), and that argument rested entirely on the mislabelled command-r pair.
  ADOPTED: the fitted widener for PER-ANCHOR edges, where two parameters demonstrably pay for themselves; a
  plain agreement gate for the POOLED board, where they do not. Publishing a fitted parameter where a
  one-line rule does better would be paying for sophistication with reader trust.
  WHAT A READER MUST NOT CONCLUDE: that the certificate is calibrated (it is not - it is no longer detectably
  miscalibrated, on three events); that b1 = 3.31 travels to another roster (answer agreement is a property of
  this roster's answer distribution); or that this budgets systematic error in general (it budgets the
  high-agreement channel, and all three surviving wrong calls are LOW agreement, 0.475 / 0.476 / 0.605).
  Establishing calibration at the operating point needs about 9 expected wrong calls, roughly 7x this corpus.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/systematic_budget.txt; script tools/analysis/systematic_budget.py.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any run, ZERO calls) — BUDGET-TRANSFER: does the fitted widener survive a change of roster?
SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET ships tau(A) = exp(-3.2326 + 3.3133*A) and I recorded, as a stated limit, that it rests on
"one roster, one judge, one reference, one tree" and that "answer agreement is a property of this roster's
answer distribution. Nothing here tests transfer." That limit is testable at zero calls and leaving it untested
while shipping a fitted parameter would be indefensible. stack_v2_promptv2_x20.db holds 12,394 cached verdicts
over 20 models, all 20 carrying answer keys, with all 14 anchors above 200 matches.
THE DESIGN PROBLEM THAT CHANGES THE TEST. The x20 roster is a strict SUPERSET of x12: all twelve are in it, plus
eight (Mixtral-8x7B, Qwen1.5-110B, Qwen1.5-14B-Chat, arx_3, claude-3-5-haiku, claude-3-5-sonnet, gemma-7b,
gpt-4o-mini). So a naive "apply to x20" would be 66 of 190 pairs self-contaminated - the very pairs the budget
was fitted on. The test therefore decomposes the 190 pairs by provenance and reports them separately:
    SHARED   66 pairs, both models in x12          - in-sample, reported only as a sanity check
    CROSS    96 pairs, one new model, one old      - out of sample on one side
    INTERNAL 28 pairs, both models new             - FULLY out of sample, and this is the primary
REGISTERED CRITERIA, fixed now.
 (1) PRIMARY, on the INTERNAL pairs only, with the x12 parameters applied COLD and no refit: the realised
     wrong-direction rate among called edges is at or below the nominal rate the budget claims. Reported with
     the edge counts, because 28 pairs across 14 anchors may not carry enough wrong calls to decide anything,
     and if it does not, the answer is UNDERPOWERED and not PASS.
 (2) UTILITY: the cold budget still calls at least 60% of the x20 edges, the same bar the fit had to clear.
 (3) THE PARAMETER QUESTION: refit b1 on x20 alone. If the widener is a property of the JUDGE it should land
     inside the x12 anchor-clustered CI [1.72, 7.87]; if it is a property of the ROSTER it should not.
 (4) The raw certificate's own wrong-call rate on x20, so the comparison has a baseline on this roster rather
     than borrowing x12's 1.47%.
PREDICTIONS: b1 refit on x20 comes in LOWER than 3.31, because eight of the twenty are weak models that widen
key gaps and lower mean agreement, so fewer pairs are contested; the cold budget is CONSERVATIVE on x20 - it
over-widens and the realised rate lands comfortably below nominal - but for the uninteresting reason that the
added pairs are easy; and criterion (1) comes back UNDERPOWERED on the 28 internal pairs. If that is what
happens, the honest conclusion is that transfer is UNTESTED rather than demonstrated, and the shipped parameter
must be published as roster-specific.
FALSIFIER: if the cold budget's realised rate EXCEEDS nominal on x20, the parameter does not transfer and
RESOLVE must refit per roster or fall back to the agreement gate, which has no fitted parameter to transfer.
Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/budget_transfer.txt; script tools/analysis/budget_transfer.py.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any run, ZERO calls) — LOW-AGREEMENT: what predicts the errors the budget is blind to?
SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET leaves three wrong calls standing out of fold and all three are LOW agreement - 0.475, 0.476,
0.605 - while the widener grows with agreement and so barely touches them. Worse, the two Law survivors carry
the most solidly established key labels of the eight (exact McNemar p=0.0018 and 0.0015), so these are not
label noise; they are real inversions the budget cannot see. A budget that handles the high-agreement channel
and is blind to the rest should not be described as budgeting systematic error, and the blind spot should be
characterised rather than left as a footnote.
DESIGN, zero calls. Take the 891 edges. Split at the median agreement. Within the LOW-agreement half, compare
wrong-direction against correct edges on every predictor that is available WITHOUT the answer key at inference:
the bootstrap SD s, |m|, the raw confidence, the number of distinct questions behind the edge, the cell's tie
rate, the cell's answer-disagreement rate, and the mean absolute trace-length difference between the two models
in that cell (verbosity is the campaign's best-measured judge bias at +0.39 per 1k characters). The key gap is
included ONLY as a sanity check and is marked unavailable at deployment, exactly as SYSTEMATIC-SIGNAL did.
REGISTERED CRITERIA.
 (1) PRIMARY: a predictor works if the difference between wrong and correct LOW-agreement edges has a
     bootstrap CI excluding zero AND it survives a logistic that already contains agreement.
 (2) If one does, report what a two-channel budget - tau as a function of agreement AND the surviving predictor
     - would do to the three surviving wrong calls and to the number of edges called. A second channel is worth
     adding only if it removes wrong calls the current budget keeps, without falling below the 60% utility bar.
 (3) Whatever happens, report the count of wrong edges in the low-agreement half, because with 44 wrong overall
     the half that matters here may hold too few to support any claim.
PREDICTION: trace-length difference is the one that works, because verbosity is the judge's best-established
bias and a length gap is exactly the systematic error a question-resampling bootstrap cannot see. I also expect
(3) to bite - I expect roughly 20 wrong edges in the low-agreement half, which is thin, so a null here must be
reported as UNDERPOWERED and not as evidence of no second channel.
Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/low_agreement.txt; script tools/analysis/low_agreement.py.

- **BUDGET-TRANSFER (2026-09-14, zero calls): the registered FALSIFIER FIRED. The fitted widener does not
  transfer as a calibrated object, and the provenance decomposition shows the classic overfitting signature.**
  2,534 edges over the 20-model board, all 20 keyed, 14 anchors, x12 parameters applied cold.
      provenance  edges  rawcall  wrong   budgetcall  wrong   nominal   ratio
      INTERNAL      374      293      0          252      0      0.32    0.0x
      CROSS        1265      953     23          825      9      1.30    6.9x
      SHARED        895      685     10          611      0      1.03    0.0x
      ALL x20      2534     1931     33         1688      9      2.65    3.4x
  THE DECOMPOSITION IS THE RESULT. On SHARED - the 66 pairs the budget was FITTED on - it is perfect, 0 wrong.
  On CROSS, where one model is new, it is **6.9x miscalibrated**. Nothing about the judge, the tree or the
  reference changed between those two rows; only whether the pair was in the fitting set. That is what
  overfitting looks like, and it is visible only because the roster is a superset and the strata could be
  separated. The registered falsifier - "if the cold budget's realised rate EXCEEDS nominal on x20, the
  parameter does not transfer" - fires at 9 against 2.65 overall.
  (1) THE PRIMARY CANNOT DECIDE, and for a reason worse than the power caveat I registered: the INTERNAL
  stratum has **0 wrong calls in the RAW certificate** (293 called, 0 wrong). Its 26 wrong-direction edges are
  all among the 81 the raw certificate already declined. So the designated out-of-sample test had nothing to
  catch and could neither pass nor fail. I registered it as the primary on the reasoning that it was the only
  clean stratum; it is clean and it is empty.
  (3) AND THE PARAMETER QUESTION SPLITS THE SAME WAY. Refit on all of x20, b1 = **+3.2633** against x12's
  +3.3133 - almost identical, inside the anchor-clustered CI [1.72, 7.87], and this is what my script printed
  as "consistent with being a property of the JUDGE". That reading is too generous and I am withdrawing it:
  refit on the INTERNAL edges alone, **b1 = -0.5230**, the SIGN REVERSES. The +3.26 is carried by the pairs
  containing fitted models. On the only fully novel subset the relationship is not reproduced.
  (2)/(4) WHAT STILL HOLDS, and it is not nothing. Utility passes at 66.6% of edges called. And cold on a
  roster it never saw, the budget still BEATS the gate: 1,688 called / 9 wrong / 219 correct surrendered,
  against gate A<0.70's 1,667 / 11 / 242 and A<0.80's 1,855 / 21 / 64. The raw certificate's own rate on this
  roster is 1.71% (33 of 1,931), against 1.47% on x12 - so x20 is if anything the harder board. The widener
  REDUCES error out of roster; it is simply not CALIBRATED out of roster.
  ADOPTED READING: tau is a useful risk-ordering device and a roster-specific one. RESOLVE ships it with the
  parameters refitted per board and must not publish a nominal confidence from it on a roster it was not fitted
  on. The claim "removes an established miscalibration and replaces one no longer detectable" holds only
  in-roster; out of roster the replacement miscalibration is 6.9x and plainly detectable.
  PREDICTIONS SCORED: "b1 refit on x20 lower than 3.31" technically HELD (3.2633) but the margin is meaningless
  and the prediction was about the roster diluting the effect, which the INTERNAL refit shows it does far more
  drastically than I guessed; "criterion (1) comes back UNDERPOWERED on the internal pairs" HELD, though for a
  different reason than I gave; "the cold budget is conservative on x20" FAILED - it is 3.4x anti-conservative.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/budget_transfer.txt; script tools/analysis/budget_transfer.py.

- **LOW-AGREEMENT (2026-09-14, zero calls): my registered PREMISE was wrong, and correcting it vindicates the
  budget's design. The surviving errors are not low-agreement at all.**
  I registered this on the claim that the budget's three out-of-fold survivors "are LOW agreement - 0.475,
  0.476, 0.605 - while the widener grows with agreement and so barely touches them". The median agreement over
  the 891 edges is **0.441**. All three survivors are ABOVE it. They are low only relative to arx/iask at
  0.880, not low in the population, and the test I registered split at the wrong place.
  WHERE THE ERRORS ACTUALLY LIVE, which is the finding:
      agreement band    0.00-0.35  0.35-0.45  0.45-0.55  0.55-0.65  0.65-0.80  0.80-1.00
      wrong / edges         5/328      1/129      4/137      2/109     12/120     20/68
      rate                   1.5%       0.8%       2.9%       1.8%      10.0%     29.4%
  Thirty-eight of the 44 wrong edges sit in the upper half and the rate reaches **29.4% above agreement 0.80**.
  Widening with agreement is therefore exactly the right shape, and after the budget the wrong calls that
  survive sit in the fourth and fifth quintiles only - one each - with **Q1 through Q3 completely clean**. The
  blind spot I set out to characterise is not a low-agreement blind spot; it is the top of the same channel the
  budget already models, not yet widened enough.
  (1) WITHIN THE BOTTOM HALF, the registered primary found one key-free predictor that survives conditioning on
  agreement, and it is the one I predicted: **the LENGTH ADVANTAGE of the arena's own pick**. Wrong edges
  -0.338k characters against right edges +0.460k, difference **-0.799 [-0.994, -0.598]**, logistic coefficient
  -3.357 +- 0.821 (z=-4.1) with agreement in the model. The direction is the interesting part and it is not the
  naive one: **the arena is reliable when it picks the more verbose model and unreliable when it picks the
  tighter one.** Given the campaign's measured +0.39 per 1k characters, the reading is that the judge's
  verbosity preference usually coincides with the truth, and when the judge overrides its own bias it is more
  often wrong. Raw confidence (z=-4.8) and |mean theta gap| (z=-2.9) also survive but both are mechanically
  what the certificate already thresholds on; the cell tie rate does not survive (z=+1.8).
  (3) THE POWER CAVEAT BIT HARDER THAN I REGISTERED. I predicted roughly 20 wrong edges in the low half; there
  are **6**. Everything in (1) rests on six events and is DESCRIPTIVE, as the script says before reporting it.
  (2) A SECOND CHANNEL IS NOT WARRANTED. The two wrong calls the budget keeps in sample sit at the 8th and 10th
  percentile of |mean theta gap| among called edges - but |m| is already IN the budget formula, so that is not
  a new channel. And both have POSITIVE length advantage (+0.214k, +0.128k), the safe direction by (1), so the
  one genuinely new predictor would not flag them. The honest conclusion is that no second channel is
  supported: the single-channel budget already clears Q1-Q3 entirely, and the residue is a scale question in
  the channel it has, not a missing one.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/low_agreement.txt; script tools/analysis/low_agreement.py.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any run, ZERO calls) — BUDGET-LOMO: was leave-one-ANCHOR-out the wrong fold structure?
BUDGET-TRANSFER found the budget is perfect on the 66 model pairs it was fitted on (0 wrong, 0.0x) and 6.9x
miscalibrated on pairs containing a model it had not seen. That says the leakage runs along the MODEL axis. But
every validation the budget has passed — my leave-one-ANCHOR-out, and the derivation's leave-one-model-PAIR-out
— holds out an anchor or a single pair while leaving the MODELS in the fitting set. Leave-one-pair-out still
lets a model appear in 10 other pairs of the same fold. So the budget has never been validated along the axis
its own failure runs on, and the 2.4x LOAO figure I adopted may be an artefact of the fold structure rather
than a property of the budget.
DESIGN, zero calls. Leave-one-MODEL-out on the 891 x12 edges: for each of the 12 models remove EVERY edge
touching it, fit b0 and b1 on the remainder, and score the held-out edges with those parameters. Aggregate the
held-out calls and wrong directions across the 12 folds. Report LOAO, leave-one-pair-out and LOMO side by side
on the identical edge set so the three fold structures are directly comparable.
REGISTERED CRITERIA.
 (1) PRIMARY: the realised wrong-direction rate among LOMO-held-out called edges, against its nominal. The
     budget's calibration claim survives only if LOMO is of the same order as LOAO's 2.4x.
 (2) The spread of b1 across the 12 LOMO folds. A parameter that swings wildly when one model is withheld is
     fitting models, not a judge property.
 (3) Utility under LOMO: the fraction of edges still called.
PREDICTION: LOMO comes in materially worse than LOAO — I expect 4x to 8x, in line with BUDGET-TRANSFER's 6.9x
on CROSS — and b1 swings by more than a factor of two across folds. If that happens, the honest statement is
that my adopted 2.4x was measured with the wrong fold and the budget's calibration was never established even
in-roster, which would be a second and more damaging correction than BUDGET-TRANSFER's.
FALSIFIER FOR THE BUDGET ITSELF: if LOMO exceeds the raw certificate's own 9.7x, the widener adds nothing and
should be withdrawn in favour of the agreement gate, which has no parameter to leak.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any run, ZERO calls) — TIER-HONEST-X20: does the finding that motivated the whole budget line replicate with three times the edges?
TIER-HONEST is the result the entire RESOLVE budget line exists to answer: on x12 the board separated 62 of 64
across-tier pairs with ZERO wrong directions while separating 2 of 2 WITHIN-tier pairs, one of them the arx/iask
inversion it was 100% certain about. That is 66 pairs and two within-tier separations — a headline resting on
two events. The 20-model board gives 190 pairs at 12,394 cached verdicts, and it has never been analysed this
way. If the pattern does not replicate, the budget is a fix for a phenomenon measured on two events.
DESIGN, zero calls, the same instrument as TIER-HONEST: key tiers at the 0.017 gap, per-pair bootstrap over
questions, count separations at 95% and the wrong directions among them, split by within-tier and across-tier;
then let the board tier ITSELF by its own intervals and count cross-tier key inversions in its own tiering.
REGISTERED CRITERIA.
 (1) PRIMARY: the within-tier confident-separation count and how many point the wrong way, with the across-tier
     figures beside them. The x12 pattern replicates if within-tier separations are again confidently made and
     disproportionately wrong relative to across-tier ones.
 (2) The arena's own self-tiering and its cross-tier key inversions, as on x12 (which gave 10 tiers, 2
     inversions).
 (3) Since x20 contains the x12 roster, report the 66 shared pairs and the 124 new pairs separately — the
     shared ones are not an independent replication and must not be counted as one.
PREDICTION: the pattern replicates and strengthens, because eight of the added models sit in the crowded middle
where the key gaps are small; I expect within-tier separations in the low tens with a wrong-direction rate well
above the across-tier rate, and I expect the across-tier wrong count to be near zero as on x12.

## Registered 2026-09-14 (before any run, ZERO calls) — PROFILE-RELIABILITY-X20: does a bigger roster rescue the anchor profile?
PROFILE-RELIABILITY put the anchor-level judge profile at 0.6728 against a registered 0.70 bar and concluded
RESOLVE may not publish per-anchor capability claims as measured quantities. That was 12 models. A capability
profile over 20 models estimates more per-cell quantities from the same questions, so reliability could fall;
but the x20 cache also carries 12,394 verdicts against x12's 9,142, so support per cell rises. Which effect
dominates is not predictable from the x12 result and it decides whether the deliverable is rescued by a larger
board or buried by one.
DESIGN, zero calls: the identical instrument at the identical bar — disjoint half-splits of each cell's
questions, profiles built on each half, correlated model-demeaned, Spearman-Brown, averaged over 40 halvings —
run on the x20 verdicts at leaf and anchor level, with the answer key through the same pipeline as comparator.
REGISTERED CRITERION: the same 0.70 bar, fixed before the number is seen, and the same consequence. If x20
clears it where x12 did not, RESOLVE may publish per-anchor claims ON A BOARD OF THAT SIZE and must say so; if
it does not, the finding is roster-independent and the deliverable is closed rather than merely postponed.
PREDICTION: x20 lands BELOW x12's 0.6728, because 20 models is 190 pairwise comparisons to pin from the same
2,811 questions, and the extra verdicts do not compensate for the extra parameters. If so the honest reading is
that a bigger board makes the profile worse, not better, and no roster on this corpus will clear the bar.

- **PROFILE-RELIABILITY-X20 (2026-09-14, zero calls): a bigger roster does not rescue the anchor profile, it
  makes it worse. The granular-capability deliverable is CLOSED on a roster-independent ground.**
      level     cells  q/cell   judge r   judge R(SB)   key R(SB)
      leaf          7      64   -0.0160       -0.0326      0.8248
      anchor       14     189    0.4580        0.6283      0.9045
  Against the same registered 0.70 bar that x12 failed at 0.6728, the 20-model board comes in at **0.6283**,

  be pinned from the same questions and the extra verdicts do not compensate for the extra parameters - HELD.
  THE LEAF NUMBER IS THE STARKER ONE: at 20 models the judge-derived leaf profile has a Spearman-Brown
  reliability of **-0.0326**. It is not merely unreliable, it is anti-correlated between independent halves of
  the same cell - indistinguishable from noise, with the sign a coin flip. The KEY over the identical cells and
  the identical split reaches 0.8248 at leaf and 0.9045 at anchor, so the cells carry a perfectly stable signal
  at both granularities and it is entirely the judge's estimate that collapses.
  WHAT THIS SETTLES. PROFILE-RELIABILITY closed per-anchor capability claims on 12 models and left open whether
  a larger board would rescue them. It would not: the deliverable fails at 12 models and fails harder at 20.
  Combined with PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST (the structure is real and tree-robust in the key) and the 210-questions-
  per-cell crossing point, the complete statement is that a granular capability profile is unreachable on this
  corpus by any judge, any tree and any roster, for want of questions per cell - and that no part of that is a
  judge-quality problem to be fixed by a better model.

- **CORRECTION 2026-09-14, and it retracts my own headline from the same evening: BUDGET-TRANSFER's "the
  falsifier fired" was WRONG. The budget DOES transfer. I applied an inconsistent standard between two
  analyses in the same line.**
  BUDGET-TRANSFER reported CROSS at **6.9x** miscalibrated against SHARED at 0.0x, called that the overfitting
  signature, declared the registered falsifier fired, recorded the budget as roster-specific, and amended
  docs/design/RESOLVE_budget.md to forbid publishing a nominal confidence off the fitting roster. All of that
  rests on the wrong-direction LABELS, and I had already established hours earlier - in SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET
  section (4) - that 41% of those labels are not adjudicated by the key. **I applied the McNemar test to the
  x12 fit and did not apply it to the transfer analysis.** That is the error: not a bad inference from the
  numbers, but the same test used on one analysis and skipped on the next.
  APPLIED CONSISTENTLY, exact two-sided McNemar on the pair's per-question correctness in the anchor:
      stratum                     edges   called   wrong   nominal   ratio
      SHARED   all labels           895      611       0      1.03    0.0x
      SHARED   established only     826      599       0      0.95    0.0x
      CROSS    all labels          1265      825       9      1.30    6.9x
      CROSS    established only    1106      800       2      1.15    **1.7x**
      INTERNAL all labels           374      252       0      0.32    0.0x
      INTERNAL established only     331      242       0      0.29    0.0x
  **Only 2 of the 9 CROSS wrong calls rest on a key direction the key establishes.** The other seven have
  McNemar p from 0.134 to 1.000, and five of them are Meta-Llama-3.1-70B against gpt-4o-mini or
  claude-3-5-haiku - three models whose key accuracies are 0.630, 0.633 and 0.630, within 0.003 of each other
  and in the same tier. The arena separating three near-identical models is not a calibration failure of the
  widener; it is the key being unable to say who is better.
  SO EVERY PIECE OF THE HEADLINE DISSOLVES:
   (a) THE OVERFITTING SIGNATURE IS GONE. On established labels the three strata read 0.0x / 1.7x / 0.0x.
       There is no fitted-versus-unfitted gap, which is the whole thing I claimed to have found.
   (b) THE FALSIFIER DID NOT FIRE. It was registered as "realised exceeds nominal"; on interpretable labels
       CROSS is 1.7x, comparable to and in fact BETTER than the within-roster folds (LOAO 2.4x, LOPO 2.3x,
       LOMO 2.5x).
   (c) b1 REFIT ON ALL ESTABLISHED x20 EDGES IS **+4.1080**, inside the x12 anchor-clustered CI [1.72, 7.87].
       The parameter is consistent across rosters.
   (d) THE "SIGN REVERSAL" I RAISED AS AN ALARM WAS NOISE IN AN EMPTY STRATUM. INTERNAL has **zero wrong
       calls**, so the likelihood has no signal to fit and b1's sign there is arbitrary: -0.5230 on all labels,
       -0.1949 on established ones, with a constant outcome underneath. I withdrew my script's "property of the
       judge" reading on the strength of that number; the withdrawal was itself the error and the original
       reading was right.
  CORRECTED CONCLUSION: the budget transfers. Within roster it is 2.3-2.5x under every fold structure; on a
  different roster with interpretable labels it is 1.7x; the shape is stable and the scale swings 2.6x without
  moving the calibration. RESOLVE_budget.md correction 5 is rewritten accordingly and the prohibition on
  publishing a nominal confidence off the fitting roster is LIFTED, replaced by the real limitation: no
  certificate can be read on pairs whose key direction is not established, and 41% of this corpus's
  wrong-direction labels are in that class.
  WHAT THIS COSTS IN CREDIBILITY, stated plainly: I published a falsified-transfer headline, amended a design
  document on it, and retracted a correct reading of my own script, all within the hour, because I did not
  carry a test I had just written into the next analysis. The lesson is procedural and it is now a rule: any
  analysis in this line that counts wrong-direction edges must apply the McNemar establishment filter and
  report both figures, and no conclusion may rest on the unfiltered count alone.
  Output experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/budget_lomo.txt and the reconciliation in this entry.

- **REF-QUAL-KIMI, corrected run (2026-09-15, 569 calls at a 32,768-token cap, after two machine crashes and a
  clean hot-journal rollback): GATE (1) FAILS AS REGISTERED, GATE (3) PASSES, and the test is CONFOUNDED by my
  own design in a way no token budget repairs. Recorded as UNDECIDED-CONFOUNDED, DO NOT PROMOTE.**
  [record fix 2026-09-15: the void run's "227 completely empty" was 220 empty responses plus 7 non-empty
  responses that failed to parse; the 40.5% unparsed figure is unchanged.]
  559 of 569 answered; the 10 missing are HTTP 400 content-filter refusals on the same ten questions in every
  attempt (history, law, psychology; 8 of 10 in the weak cells, 6 in Law) - the Azure filter, not the model.
      (1) DISCRIMINATING n=298   candidate 0.705   incumbent 0.725   -0.020   -> FAIL against the +3pp bar
      (2) History         n= 97   0.773 vs 0.680   +0.093
          Engineering     n=100   0.760 vs 0.780   -0.020
          Law             n= 94   0.702 vs 0.702    0.000
      (3) worst frontier agreement gain +0.023 (gemini 0.782 vs 0.759)   -> PASS against the 3pp bar
  THE FOURTH NUMBER, non-termination at 32,768 tokens, which decides how (1) reads:
      DISCRIMINATING   33 of 299 answered (11.0%)   accuracy among TERMINATED 0.789
      Engineering      13 of 100 (13.0%)            accuracy among terminated 0.874
      History           0 of  98                    0.765
      Law               0 of  94                    0.702
      ALL              42 of 559 (7.5%)             0.789
  Every one of the 42 hit the cap with finish_reason 'length'; at 8,192 the rate was 40.5%. Terminated
  answers use a median of 5,044 completion tokens, p90 19,658, max 32,463 - so the cap sits right at the top
  of what a terminating answer needs, and the non-terminators are the hard quantitative material.
  SO THE GATE HINGES ON ONE CHOICE. Score a truncation as wrong - which is what a deployed reference would
  deliver, an empty reference on 11% of hard questions - and Kimi is -2.0pp, FAIL. Score only what
  terminated and Kimi is +6.4pp, a clear PASS. The registration did not say which, because I did not
  anticipate a reference that reasons past 32k tokens. I am applying the registered wording literally
  (accuracy on the subset, truncation counted as wrong), which is the deployment reading, and recording the
  other number beside it rather than choosing the one that flatters the candidate.
  AND THE COMPARISON IS NOT APPLES TO APPLES, WHICH I FOUND ONLY BY CHECKING WHY THE INCUMBENT NEVER TRUNCATES.
  The incumbent's 0.725 comes from grok-reasoning.db, solved by judge_solve_map.py under a JSON answer-only
  protocol: its stored raw is '{"answer": "D"}', 2,193 of its answers are SIX tokens, and its reasoning
  happened server-side and invisibly. Its empty-answer rate on these subsets is 0 of 302, 0 of 100, 0 of 100,
  0 of 100. Kimi was solved by ref_qualify.py under the CONTESTANTS' chain-of-thought prompt ("Think step by
  step ... the answer is (X)"), which I copied from regen_contestant.py without noticing it was not the
  incumbent's protocol. Two references, two prompts, two token regimes. A model's accuracy moves with its
  prompt whatever the model, so the -2.0pp / +6.4pp pair compares Kimi-with-CoT against grok-without, and
  neither number is the like-for-like the gate assumed. This is my design error in the instrument, the second
  one in this test after the 8,192 cap, and it is disclosed here rather than in a footnote.
  WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, in order of what each buys:
   (a) Re-solve Kimi under the incumbent's JSON answer-only protocol, ~569 calls. Removes the prompt confound.
       May not remove truncation - Kimi's reasoning happens in a visible channel the cap still binds - but it
       makes the accuracy comparison legitimate, which the 64k top-up alone does not.
   (b) Top up the 42 non-terminators at 65,536 tokens, ~42 calls. Removes only the truncation, on a
       comparison that is still confounded. Not worth doing on its own.
  DECISION: DO NOT PROMOTE on this evidence. Gate (1) fails as registered; the +6.4pp alternative reading
  rests on excluding the questions a reference is needed for most; and the comparison is confounded. The
  correct next step, if the user wants a decisive answer, is (a). Whatever that returns, the leakage readout
  (3) stands - a candidate that mirrors the frontier LESS than the incumbent does is a safe direction.
  INSTRUMENT RULE, added: ref_qualify must solve a candidate under the SAME protocol the incumbent was solved
  under, and must record which protocol that was. The JSON protocol is the incumbent's and is the one to use.
  Output experiment_results/judge_solve/refqual_Kimi_K2_6_mt32768.txt; cache refqual_Kimi_K2_6_mt32768.db.

## REVIEW of the 2026-09-14/15 session (2026-09-15, zero calls) — three headline conclusions are artefacts
An adversarial review was run over the 22 commits 426016e..c22bb41: five slice reviewers, each followed by a
checker that recomputed what the reviewer flagged, then one synthesis. Full report: docs/review_session_2026-09-14.md.
Before recording any of it I recomputed the three HIGH findings myself; all three hold.
 (1) EVERY x20 ANALYSIS RAN ON A BOARD THAT IS NOT THE BOARD OF RECORD. stack_v2_promptv2_x20.db holds 12,394
     verdicts on the 124 pairs involving a new model and ZERO on the 66 original pairs (SQL: CROSS 9,594,
     INTERNAL 2,800, SHARED 0). ARENA-V2-X20 registered the merged board, x12 9,142 + x20 12,394 = 21,536. So
     budget_transfer.py and x20_replications.py fitted a 20-model board in which the twelve originals were never
     compared directly. The SHARED/CROSS/INTERNAL strata do not mean fitted/half-fitted/unfitted, the
     "x20 contains x12" premise is false, and BUDGET-TRANSFER, its retraction, TIER-HONEST-X20 and
     PROFILE-RELIABILITY-X20 all inherit it. The review reports anchor R = 0.7183 on the merged board, which
     would PASS the 0.70 bar the sparse board failed at 0.6283. One read-only query would have shown this.
 (2) PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST'S NULL SHUFFLED ACROSS ANCHORS. shuffled_partition() permuted cells over the whole pool,
     destroying the anchor membership the two trees share on 2,800 of 2,811 questions. A within-anchor shuffle
     null (leaves permuted inside each anchor) puts the key's +0.8143 at its own median: +0.8164, 95th +0.8318.
     "The structure is real and tree-robust" measured the anchor profile, not sub-anchor structure. The
     reframing of LEAF-POWER, LEAF-SHRINK, LEAF-POWERED, MC-LEAF and LEAF-PROFILE-CLEAN as "measuring a 0.086
     estimate" falls with it, and the H10 closure inherits the problem.
 (3) TIER-HONEST-X20'S HEADLINE DOES NOT SURVIVE THE SESSION'S OWN McNEMAR RULE. Of the six "wrong" within-tier
     separations, exact McNemar over the pool establishes ONE (arx/iask, 179:123, p=0.0015); the other five are
     p=0.06 to 0.39. The rule was adopted 14 minutes after that outcome and never applied back to it.
FURTHER CONFIRMED BY THE CHECKERS (see the report for numbers and locations): SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET criterion (1)
"PASS" is carried by the 228 uncalled edges and is UNDETERMINED at the operating point; LOW-AGREEMENT reported
a SUBSTITUTED predictor as the registered prediction holding, and its effect is the label's sign; N4's
withdrawal stands but its mechanism is wrong (MMLU-Pro math migrates into the MATH anchors, 946 to 367, and
r=0.598 is carried by that point); the BUDGET-TRANSFER retraction over-corrected on two events where the
registration had pre-committed UNTESTED, and rewrote RESOLVE_budget.md by deletion; PROFILE-RELIABILITY's
"+-0.012" is a re-halving spread, not sampling uncertainty (jackknife: R in [0.49, 0.81]); the REF-QUAL guard
warns but does not refuse.
WHAT THE REVIEW UPHELD: six of six registrations precede their outcomes and the programme file has zero
deleted lines across the span; the x12 budget line reproduces to four decimals from committed code and its
widener is key-free and monotone; the pooled arx/iask inversion is key-established (McNemar 144:99, p=0.0047)
and replicates indirectly on entirely new verdicts (179:123, p=0.002); BUDGET-LOMO is a genuine
self-falsification; voided runs were voided; failed predictions were reported in their registered words.
PROCESS FAILURES NAMED, and adopted as rules: check the data object before reading strata into it; use
UNDETERMINED as a registered outcome instead of flipping a verdict twice on two events; a rule adopted
mid-session is applied backward in the same commit to every result it governs; name the key denominator
(3,445 pool / 2,811 judged / 2,646 x20-judged) every time; a null must preserve the structure the question
conditions on; ledger chips carry the narrative's qualifier; correct by insertion only.
CORRECTIONS IN PROGRESS, by insertion, as each rerun lands: seven ledger rows are chipped UNDER CORRECTION
(ledger v92). First: tools/analysis/x20_merged.py reruns TIER-HONEST and PROFILE-RELIABILITY on the merged
