## Registered 2026-09-15 (before any run) — six tests from the big picture after the review. Standing rules from the review apply to all six: every wrong-direction count carries its McNemar-established count on the anchor's judged questions; UNDETERMINED is a registered outcome; the key denominator is named; nulls preserve what the question conditions on; the data object is checked before strata are read into it.

### A. KEY-NOISE-CEILING (zero calls) — how much of the arena's remaining error is the key's own noise?
Eighteen of the 44 wrong-direction edges on x12 and eight of the nine within-tier separations on x20 sit on pairs
the key cannot adjudicate. That suggests the judge line has reached the point where the KEY, not the judge,
bounds what can be measured. Test it directly: for each anchor, split the judged questions into two halves;
the key's direction for a pair on half 1 against half 2 gives the key's OWN direction-agreement rate, averaged
over 40 halvings. That rate is the ceiling on any judge's direction-agreement with the key at this support.
Compare the arena's direction-agreement with the key (raw certificate, called edges) on (i) all edges, (ii)
established edges, against the key's split-half ceiling at the same support.
CRITERIA: (1) PRIMARY: arena direction-agreement on established edges vs the key's split-half ceiling. If the
arena is within 2pp of the ceiling, the measurable judge line on MMLU-Pro is CLOSED and further gains cannot
be shown on this corpus. (2) The gap on ALL edges, so the label-noise share is stated as a number.
(3) Per-anchor: which anchors are at ceiling and which are not.
PREDICTION: the arena is within 2pp of the ceiling on established edges overall, below it on Law and History,
and the all-edge gap is 3-5pp. FALSIFIER: an arena more than 5pp below the ceiling on established edges means
there is measurable judge headroom left and the "ceiling" story is wrong.

### B. KEY-TIE-DECLINE (zero calls) — a product rule wherever a key exists
Decline any separation whose pair's key direction is not established (exact McNemar p >= 0.05 on the cell's
judged questions), on top of the raw certificate and on top of the budget. Measure on x12 (891 edges) and on
the merged 20-model board: calls surrendered, wrong calls removed, and what remains.
CRITERIA: (1) PRIMARY: on the merged board, the decline rule removes at least 6 of the 8 within-tier wrong
separations for no more than 15% of across-tier calls surrendered. (2) Combined with the widener on x12, the
remaining wrong calls at 0.975 are all key-established (the residue is real error, not noise). (3) Report the
rule's cost in calls at every threshold 0.90-0.995.
PREDICTION: (1) holds - it removes 7 of 8 - at about 10% of across-tier calls; (2) holds with 2 remaining.
FALSIFIER: if it costs more than 25% of across-tier calls to remove the within-tier errors, the rule is too
blunt for a product and the widener alone is the recommendation.

### C. JUDGE-TRANSFER (zero calls) — does the widener transfer across JUDGE families?
Roster transfer is undetermined. Judge transfer has not been asked and is cheaper to power: the grok judge
cache stack_v2_kit2_grok.db carries 3,948 verdicts on 1,371 x12 questions across all 66 pairs, in two arms
(the arm without the leaf card is used, so the recipe matches the x12 Mistral cache). Fit tau on Mistral x12
(the shipped b0, b1), apply COLD to per-anchor edges built from grok verdicts; also refit on grok.
DATA CHECK FIRST: with ~100 questions per anchor the per-anchor floor of 200 matches will not be met
everywhere; report which anchors qualify at a 100-match floor and run only those, said plainly.
CRITERIA: (1) realised wrong-direction rate (all / established) against nominal on the grok edges with the
Mistral parameters; (2) b1 refit on grok inside the Mistral anchor-clustered CI [1.72, 7.87]; (3) utility.
PREDICTION: b1 refit on grok lands inside the CI (widening with agreement is a judge-family property) and the
cold ratio is 1.5-3x on established labels - the same band as in-roster. FALSIFIER: b1 refit outside the CI
or a cold ratio above 5x on established labels means the parameter is Mistral-specific and must be published
so. Expected to be UNDERPOWERED at the operating point; the b1 criterion is the one with power.

### D. KEY-SUBANCHOR-SCALE (zero calls) — is sub-anchor structure dead for taxonomy reasons or data reasons?
PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST (corrected) found the key-derived sub-anchor profile is not tree-robust on the 2,811
reserved questions (most-changed third: -0.071). The corrected extrapolation says 900-1,500 questions per leaf
would be needed. The snapshots carry train-side membership (node.queryIds), so the key-only test can run on
the full keyed set (~10,900 questions: train side + reserved) for both trees, at their native sizes (~125 and
~230 questions per leaf), with the within-anchor null and (model, anchor) demeaning; and at subsampled sizes
below that to draw the trend. Contamination note: this uses the TRAIN side by design - the question is
whether the KEY's own profile is tree-stable on the questions the trees were fitted to separate, which is the
most favourable case for sub-anchor structure. If it fails there it fails everywhere.
CRITERIA: (1) PRIMARY: (model, anchor)-demeaned cross-tree r on the most-changed third of questions, at the
full size, against its within-anchor null 95th pct. (2) The trend of that r with cell size. (3) Whether the
extrapolated 900-1,500 requirement is on the trend line.
PREDICTION: still negative or null on the most-changed third at full size, for both trees - sub-anchor
structure is not tree-stable even on the training questions, which closes it for TAXONOMY reasons. FALSIFIER:
a positive, null-clearing r on the most-changed third at full size reopens sub-anchor as a data question.

### E. ANCHOR-PROFILE-INTERVAL (zero calls) — is the 0.7183 pass a pass?
PROFILE-RELIABILITY-X20 passed the 0.70 bar at 0.7183 on the merged board, a point estimate with a wide
interval. Register the interval: leave-one-anchor-out jackknife on the 40-halving mean r, Spearman-Brown to R,
on x12 (0.6728) and on the merged board (0.7183). And decompose the gain: anchor R on the merged board for the
profile restricted to the 12 original models (same verdicts, 12 rows) against all 20, so "more verdicts on the
same pairs" is separated from "more models in the profile".
CRITERIA: (1) the jackknife 95% interval on the merged board, and whether its LOWER bound clears 0.70. If it
does not, the registered consequence is amended: RESOLVE may publish per-anchor claims on a board of this size
WITH the interval, not as a bare pass. (2) The decomposition.
PREDICTION: the lower bound does NOT clear 0.70 (interval roughly [0.55, 0.85]); the gain over x12 is mostly
"more verdicts", not "more models". FALSIFIER: a lower bound above 0.70 makes the pass unqualified.

### F. REF-QUAL-KIMI-JSON (~569 calls) — the matched-protocol re-solve
The two previous attempts were instrument failures (8,192-token cap; then an unmatched chain-of-thought
prompt against an incumbent solved with judge_solve_map's JSON answer-only prompt at 4,096 tokens). This run
solves Kimi-K2.6 under the incumbent's exact protocol (judge_solve_map.SYSTEM, user_prompt, parse_answer) with
a 32,768-token cap so the reasoning channel can finish, in its own cache.
CRITERIA, the registered gate unchanged plus one: (1) beat 0.726 on the discriminating subset by >= 3pp;
(3) no frontier contestant gains > 3pp of agreement; (4) NEW, registered now: non-termination on the
discriminating subset must be at or below 5%, or the candidate fails on deployability whatever its accuracy.
Accuracy among terminated answers is reported as a separate, non-gate number.
PREDICTION: non-termination falls below 5% under the answer-only prompt (the model reasons less when not
asked to show it), accuracy on the discriminating subset lands at 0.74-0.78 and passes (1), leakage passes
(3), and Kimi is PROMOTABLE. FALSIFIER: non-termination stays above 5% - then Kimi is not deployable as a
reference at any protocol and the line closes.
Outputs: experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/{key_noise_ceiling,key_tie_decline,judge_transfer,key_subanchor_scale,anchor_profile_interval}.txt; experiment_results/judge_solve/refqual_Kimi_K2_6_json_mt32768.{db,txt}.

## FRAMEWORK (2026-09-15, zero calls) — docs/design/FRAMEWORK.md: a framework to judge and rank every model on every question, designed from the record as it stands at v100
Produced by a fifteen-agent workflow: five readers mapped the record by CURRENT status (ledger row's last
bracket, programme's last entry) and listed the withdrawn readings a designer would reach for; three designers
worked from different angles - measurement-first (CERTATLAS), deployment-first (TIERMAP), cost-first (THRIFT);
each design was stressed on a statistical lens and a traceability/operations lens (scores 46-62 of 100; one
FATAL finding each on CERTATLAS and THRIFT; TIERMAP built four components and THRIFT seven on withdrawn or
superseded readings, all named and dropped); one synthesis resolved twenty-four disagreements, four of them by
zero-call recomputation from the committed edge tables, and wrote the document.
WHAT IT DELIVERS. For every (model, question): the extracted answer, correctness where a key or checker exists,
every dual-order verdict with provenance, the cell and the reference. Above the question: on keyed corpora the
board, the (model x anchor) profile and every pair direction come from the KEY at zero judge calls (ORACLE-BOARD
rho 1.000; key profile reliability 0.9135 against the judge's 0.67-0.72); judge calls on keyed cells buy a
calibration board and a canary. On unkeyed cells the judge is the instrument: STACK-v2 frozen, the
answer-disagreement filter, question-clustered Bradley-Terry with the agreement-shaped widener, publication at
0.975 with the calibration status printed beside every board. Tiers by the record's reading-down rule; a
certified partial order (ORDERED edges); per model a band (certified above / below / unseparated). The router
consumes the undominated set of a cell and picks within it on declared cost, measured latency or standardised
strength. On the pooled 20-model board of record under widener + key-tie decline at 0.975 the undominated set
is six models (iask, gemini, claude-3-5-sonnet, arx_3, gpt-4o, arx_0314) from 150 ORDERED edges of 190, 0
wrong, 0 cross-tier key inversions.
WHAT IT DECLINES, BY RULE: an order inside the frontier band; any capability row below the anchor; a
per-question RANK of models (a verdict carries 5.7% intrinsic disagreement and 41% of wrong-direction labels
are key-indeterminate); the word "calibrated" (criterion (1) UNDETERMINED at the operating point); a nominal
confidence from a widener fitted on another roster or judge; ORDERED-JUDGED edges from the cheap judge until
its own calibration board exists; per-query adaptivity, confidence gating, rubric induction, reference
ensembles, single or selective order (each measured null, dominated or refuted); and any preference claim -
every number is verification fidelity against a key, a checker, or a possibly wrong reference.
COST, in cheap-call equivalents: ~0 per keyed question; ~17 per unkeyed question on a 12-model board falling
to ~7 as the reference amortises; ~800 to place a newcomer as a band (a synthetic estimate; the one real
newcomer ended UNRESOLVED); ~3,100 per newcomer for full profile coverage; one calibration board per judge of
~9,000 keyed matches, the only line above the 4,000-match rule and the one that makes a judge's certificate
mean anything.
THREE THINGS THE SYNTHESIS CORRECTED IN THE RECORD, verified here before this entry: (a) the composed rule's
residue on the merged per-anchor edges is not "all Law" as KEY-TIE-DECLINE's entry said - it is 3 Law + 1
Philosophy, and all four are Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct; the escalation test is therefore model-anchored;
(b) RESOLVE's CERTATLAS wrote the GATE partition as [0, 100), inside EVAL; the framework sets [300, 400) with
the invariant |gate and eval| = 0; (c) the "ORDERED requires the key direction to agree" clause all three
designs carried is dropped, because it zeroes the wrong-direction rate by construction; a KEY-CONTRADICTED
class is added instead.
NINETEEN ZERO-CALL TESTS are registered as prerequisites before any judged spend, and five judged ones under
the cap; the first is KTD-CHECK, an independent recompute of KEY-TIE-DECLINE, because that test is the one of
the six without a check. The limits section is the longest in the document and is the part to read first.

## Block 2 launch record (2026-09-16) — dry-run reviews, Amendment 1, and CANARY-BASELINE pass 1 (600 calls)
The six judged scripts were dry-run at zero calls, reviewed by one adversarial checker each, fixed and re-verified
(commit 1e3b1ea). Three blockers were closed BEFORE any call: the canary had been written against the Mistral
board-of-record judge, not the deployed grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning the framework's Stage 3 fixes (D1); the
newcomer placement had used ARENA-13's in-roster ensemble as reference, which ENSEMBLE-REF rules out and which
contained each newcomer's sibling (D5); STACK-NORUBRIC dropped unparsed verdicts from the paired set, so a
truncation rate under the 5% guard could turn a FAIL into a PASS - verified with a synthetic 4%-length cache
(+0.000 PASS before, about -0.035 FAIL after; D3). Seven author-side decisions the reviewers refused to make in
code are recorded as Amendment 1 of docs/plan_2026-09-15.md; the one that deviates from the framework's letter
is D2 (temperature omitted on all six runs for byte-comparability with every cache of record; the explicit
literal belongs to the Kotlin path under JUDGE-WIRING).
CANARY-BASELINE pass 1: pool p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae; frozen set of 300 matches (hash 50af669ac6997f9f; 150 contested =
137 frontier + 13 key-tie, 150 cross-tier; 279 questions; 61 pairs), judge grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning, STACK-v2,
max_tokens 8192, temperature omitted, dual order; 12-match pilot then the rest; 600 calls, finish_reason stop on
all 600, 0 invalid (guard OK). Descriptives (not the verdict): contested tie 0.280 / flip 0.193, key-decidable
accuracy 0.769 (ties wrong) / 0.815 (ties half) on n=65; cross-tier tie 0.220 / flip 0.173, accuracy 0.923 /
0.949 on n=78. NO OUTCOME YET: the retest floor is pass 1 vs pass 2, and pass 2 is refused by the script before
2026-09-22; the prediction on record stays (floor 4-6% on the contested half, lower on cross-tier).
[CORRECTED 2026-09-22 by the pre-run READY, before the outcome is read (CANARY-BASELINE pass 2 pre-run reading rules; docs/reviews/READY_canary_pass2.md, ec538ff, defects 1, 2, 4, 5; inserted by the registrar at zero calls, before pass 2's outcome exists; the run may post meanwhile, because these rules gate the READING of the outcome, not the protocol): (i) BAND READING RULE (defect 4). The registered prediction "floor 4-6% on the contested half" is read on the contested-half floor ROUNDED TO 3 DECIMAL PLACES as the outcome prints it (%.3f), inclusive: printed 0.040 <= floor <= 0.060 is INSIDE, anything else OUTSIDE; the unrounded value (numerator / denominator, e.g. 9 / 149 = 0.060403) is written beside the verdict. The script's own comparison (canary_baseline.py L501, 0.04 <= floor <= 0.06 at float precision) is NOT the reading of record where the two differ (9 / 149 prints 0.060 -> INSIDE under this rule; the script would print "outside"); the same rule read K-SELECTION's P2. "Cross-tier lower than contested" is read on the two printed 3-dp values; equal printed values = "does not hold". The band is DESCRIPTIVE, not a criterion: at n = 150 it is about one SE wide (SE ~0.019 at a floor of 0.05), so its HELD / FAILED is nearly uninformative either way and is reported as such (READY, "Not applicable here"). The registered CRITERION stays "measured floor and agreement with interval" (FRAMEWORK item 21): it is scored READ / NOT READ from the FLOOR lines (contested, cross, all; question-clustered 95% CI, SE, DEFF) of experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/canary_baseline_outcome.txt. (ii) ALARM READING AT PASS 2 (defect 5). The alarm line of record is the machine-readable line "ALARM STATE: <NO ALARM | ALARM | UNDETERMINED>" in ARM-B-VINTAGE's format (ref_remint_outcome.txt line 2; read by exact string equality by whatever consumes it), which the script prints if it can and which the post-run reviewer otherwise writes into the outcome by insertion, beside the script's threshold line ("ALARM (Stage 9 arm A, ...): floor | at n=300 threshold floor + 3 SE | at n~1,000 threshold"). At pass 2 "ALARM" is NOT a permitted state: pass 2 IS the measurement of the set's own retest floor (FRAMEWORK L141: "the first epoch's two replicates ARE the measurement"), so plan Amendment 4 trigger (3) cannot fire at pass 2 by construction; it is live from the first epoch AFTER the floor is set. The rule: let F_c be the contested-half floor, read at 3 dp by rule (i), under BOTH conventions (B as printed, valid in both passes; A per rule (iv)). If F_c <= 0.114 under both (DECOMP's contested-frontier floor 0.057 = 17 / 299 plus 3 x sqrt(0.057 x 0.943 / 150) = 0.057 + 3 x 0.0189 = 0.1138, 0.114 at 3 dp; DECOMP is the comparator because it was measured on contested matches under the same requested judge), the line reads "ALARM STATE: NO ALARM" and the measured floors with their intervals and DEFF become the thresholds the next epoch reads (the "all" line's floor + 3 SE at n = 300 and at n~1,000 pooled, as the script prints; the contested and cross lines beside it). If F_c > 0.114 under either convention, the line reads "ALARM STATE: UNDETERMINED": pass 2 does NOT set the floor, no epoch reads a canary threshold, a THIRD pass (600 calls, same set, same protocol, its own dated registration section and, if the author's go is required for the spend, its own amendment) is required before any floor is set, and publication is NOT frozen (trigger (3) has not fired: a floor that far above DECOMP's on the same requested judge is evidence of drift or a redeploy between 09-16 and 09-22 that this pass pair cannot separate from an instrument effect, pass 1 carrying no fingerprint (rule (iii)); it is neither the null floor nor an alarm). A floor between the registered band and 0.114 is NO ALARM with the floor as measured; the band verdict is descriptive by rule (i). (iii) PROVENANCE (defect 1). Pass 1 recorded NO deployment fingerprint: canary_baseline.py's one() discarded the 2nd element of rejudge_reasoning.call_judge_full ("azure:" + the response's model string) and the verdicts table had no provider column; pass 1's judge identity is the REQUESTED model string grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning, and the only evidence of the deployment is the sibling caches of the same window (grok_calib.db provider1 / provider2 = azure:grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning x 9,142 on 09-16 / 17; newcomer_placement_steps.db x 800 on 09-19; stack_norubric.db; ref_checklist.db). Pass 2 takes path A of the READY's defect 1: the script records provider1 / provider2 per match (one per order) in canary_baseline_pass2.db and STOPS, caching nothing for the match, on any fingerprint other than azure:grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning (the one exemption being rr's deterministic content-filter sentinel, cached as an unusable row under rule 10); the engine-coder's change is in the working tree at the time of this bracket and the READY of record for pass 2 is RE-PINNED on it (a new LF sha and a re-review of the diff) before the pilot posts; should pass 2 post at the READY's sha 884ed3ccf5530f6f instead (path B), this sentence is the bracket the outcome and the ledger row carry. Consequence for plan Amendment 4: its re-use key (match, prompt bytes, fingerprint) is VERIFIABLE FROM PASS 2 ONWARD ONLY; pass 1's rows carry no fingerprint and are re-usable under the key only by the sibling-cache inference above, stated as such; the separation of trigger (1) (fingerprint change) from trigger (3) (canary alarm) exists from pass 2 onward. (iv) CONVENTION-A FLOOR (defect 2). The script pairs only matches VALID IN BOTH passes (L472) and prints that one convention (B); the post-run reviewer recomputes the convention-A floor from the two caches at zero calls (a match INVALID or non-terminated in either pass counts as a disagreement; denominator 300 all, 150 per half) and it is inserted beside the printed floor in the outcome, the ledger row and the record, with the number of pairs dropped by the script printed beside it (0 in pass 1, so the drop is pass 2's INVALID count); both conventions are reported, always (CONTEXT section 3). (v) OPERATOR CONDITIONS carried from the READY, for the post-run reviewer: every command with --pass 2 spelled out; canary_baseline_pass1.db sha256 5142795bdc8c5a8ec8d09a3a4f9cd6c84de206834aeab7ca11cea4761000690c and its run_meta "resumed" = ["2026-09-16 01:44:41"] unchanged after the run (defect 3); the pass-1 outcome text of record is the one at 7076615 / 0ba096f and the descriptives above, which --analyze's rewrite of canary_baseline_outcome.txt (mode "w", defect 7) does not alter in this record; the pilot line must read "done: ok 12, errors 0" (defect 6); the "all" line is the alarm statistic where a stratum floor is exactly 0 and its DEFF prints nan (defect 8). Nothing above changes the registered protocol, the set (50af669ac6997f9f), the cap, the judge, the reference (grok-reasoning.db v0, 536e3f463ced750b) or the 600 calls.]

## ESCALATE-LLAMA-LAW (2026-09-16, 666 calls) — FRAMEWORK item 24: FAIL, as predicted (JUDGE-2x2); escalation does not buy back the model-anchored residue
Registered: J1-R (grok-4-1-fast-reasoning + v1 cell rubric + grok-reasoning reference, cap 8192, temperature
omitted, dual order, flip -> TIE) on every Law and Philosophy match of Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (treatment)
and of the matched control Qwen1.5-72B-Chat, paired against the cheap judge on identical matches; criterion:
committed accuracy rises by more than the paired MDE at the known n, with no fall on the control. Deciding
thresholds fixed before launch (Amendment 1 D4): 0.136 treatment / 0.140 control (a priori d = 0.20).
Run: pool p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae; population 337 matches by anchor cell, 333 judgeable (4 have no cached reference:
3360, 4277, 4702, 6951); 333 of 333 cached, finish_reason stop on all 666 calls, 0 unparsed, guard OK on all three
subsets; key-decidable 84 treatment / 79 control (the registered 85 / 80 counted the two reference-less ones).
Comparator: Mistral STACK-v2 from stack_v2_promptv2_x12all.db, a PROXY for the shipped grok recipe judge
(JUDGE-SWAP 0.864 vs 0.865, p = 1.0); the 25-match overlap with the grok recipe cache reads the same way and is
underpowered (MDE 0.25).
Result. TREATMENT: A (ties wrong) J1-R 0.881 vs STACK-v2 0.857, +0.024, 5:3 McNemar p = 0.73; B (ties excluded)
0.934 vs 0.934, +0.000. Both far below the deciding 0.136 -> criterion FAILS under both conventions. CONTROL: A
0.911 vs 0.810, +0.101, 8:0 p = 0.008; B +0.042, 3:0 p = 0.25 -> no fall (OK). POOLED A +0.061 (13:3, p = 0.021),
B +0.020 (5:2, n.s.). Tie rates: J1-R 0.018 vs STACK-v2 0.092.
Reading. The reasoning judge's gain on these cells is a TIE-REMOVAL gain, not an accuracy-on-committed gain:
under B (committed verdicts only) treatment +0.000 and control +0.042 n.s. And the gain is LARGER on the control
model than on Llama-3.1-70B, the model the residue is anchored to: the four established wrong-direction edges of
KEY-TIE-DECLINE's composed rule (3 Law + 1 Philosophy, all Llama-3.1-70B) are not what a stronger judge fixes.
A model-anchored escalation rule at 10 cce per match is therefore NOT adopted; the framework's fallback for that
residue stays "unseparated, not certified".
Confound on the record: the J1-R cell rubric comes from the frozen tree (reserved split p8a29), 168 of the 250
questions on its train side; the comparator's bareq512 anchor rubric is clean. [CORRECTED 2026-09-23 by the SPLIT-FOLLOWUPS review (8ebfa7a): WRONG OBJECT and ID-ONLY. The 14 STACK-v2 anchor rubrics (rubric_ladder.db kind='anchor', ts 2026-09-07 23:54 to 09-08 00:09; ladder sha 4412f923 = the kit's) PREDATE bareq512_s42: rubric_ladder.py (f03cb30) induced them from TRAIN-side mmlu_pro texts assigned to the FROZEN tree 20260727_042523's leaf centroids, withholding p2dca by exact text, capped at 150 per anchor (seed 556). Their corpora hold 0 EXACT and 14 NORM-V1-ONLY twins of p2dca judged questions (Health 8, Law 4, Other 1, Philosophy 1; 5 in the 1,020 CLEAN; 45 before the cap). The STACK-v2 boards (x12, x20, GROK-CALIB, Kotlin c0d3f708, RECIPE-GROK) use 212117 only for routing and the anchor map. See the section '## SPLIT-FOLLOWUPS (2026-09-23, 0 calls; LINK-COPY-AUDIT, UNION-TREE-LABELLING-CHECK, CLAIMS-SWEEP) — the tree ...' at the END of this file.] Stratified: clean stratum
(46 pooled key-decidable) A +0.022, B +0.000; train-side (117) A +0.077 (11:2, p = 0.023), B +0.029 n.s. The
contamination direction favours J1-R, so it cannot manufacture a FAIL; the FAIL stands a fortiori on the clean
stratum. Test-retest side readout: 53 matches shared with the ledger's J1-R cache, verdict agreement 0.981.
Output: experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/escalate_llama_law.txt; cache escalate_llama_law_*.db (gitignored).

### STAGE3-MATH HELD (2026-09-16, before any call) — consequence of CHECKER-ANSWER-INGEST's HIGH finding
The plan made STAGE3-MATH (Block 2 f) conditional on item 7 landing and its dry-run passing on the real checker
table. The table landed and the dry-run passes on the `<think>` proxy (8-model cell D_c 0.994, min domain 0.985).
The checker's confirmed HIGH finding is that the proxy is not the NON_TERMINATED rule: raw lm-eval files cap MATH
generations at 1,024 tokens and 12-19% of the eval-side rows of Llama-3.1/3.3-70B, Qwen2.5-72B/Math and others end
abruptly at that cap with no `<think>` marker; under a consistently applied cap proxy the 8-model D_c is 0.8189
[0.7935, 0.8433] and 367 of GEN-ARENA's 1,800 judged MATH matches involve a cap-hit response. FRAMEWORK rule 9
(D_c < 0.95 -> no edge pass without a registered generative budget) and rule 10 (length = NON_TERMINATED, never a

## H9-REM construction-order shuffle: DEBUG FLAG IMPLEMENTED, ARM REGISTERED (2026-09-16, zero calls, NOT YET RUN)
The Block 3 prerequisite ("needs the debug flag implemented", docs/plan_2026-09-15.md). One TOML key,
`constructionOrderShuffleSeed = <long>`, permutes under a declared seed exactly the arbitrary-but-deterministic
orders the 2026-09-07 audit identified: the site order inside a depth in the split pass and the enumeration
order in the four merge passes (starved-leaf, sibling merge incl. the cluster[0] survivor choice, redundant
pairs, passthrough collapse). Not permuted, by design: the deepest-first depth schedule and the ascending-k
first-accept rule, both documented modelling decisions. Each permutation is a pure function of (seed,
iteration, pass tag) via JDK-specified java.util.Random + Collections.shuffle (taxonomy.operations.
ConstructionOrder), so an early-out in one pass cannot shift every later order.

refused at parse time on a run that constructs nothing (runPipeline = false or a union graft), same principle as
the matchFilter unknown-VALUE rule; (3) the runner refuses an effective value that did not come from the run's
own config file, so application.yml / environment binding cannot switch it on. RECORDED: the effective seed

one line in the config report and in fixed_point_certificate.txt on a shuffled arm only.

## Registered 2026-09-16 (before any code or run) — ANCHOR-FREE: the tree grown from the embeddings alone, no category anchors
Question. Every tree in the record was seeded with the corpus's category labels as depth-1 anchors; the loop only
proposes splits below them, and D4 showed it never splits the root. The framework says "the anchor layer is a
reporting convenience, not a routing mechanism" on evidence from anchored trees. Does a tree grown WITHOUT the
labels - every train query at the root, the same separation gate proposing k-way splits from depth 0 down -
recover the categories, certify structure, and carry capability information, and how does it compare with the
same-code anchored control o0 (experiment_configs/h9_order/o0_s42.toml, seed 42, label-free)?
Instrument. One TOML key, anchorFree = true, fail-closed (unknown value fatal; refused with excludeFromAnchoring,
without runPipeline, or with unionSnapshots), inert when absent (byte-identical DAG on o0's config, proven by the
existing inertness test pattern); with it: no category grouping, all train queries placed at the root with full
weight, the root admitted as a GROW site with the standard gate and ascending-k rule, depth-1 nodes no longer
treated as label anchors anywhere in the loop. Labelling, judging and final metrics OFF (zero LLM calls). The
readouts that assume depth-1 = category (anchor drift, the runner's Top-1) are NOT the measurement; the
measurement is a Python readout applied identically to the anchor-free tree and to o0:
  (1) held-out category purity: route the 3,445 pool questions to the nearest leaf centroid (the flatLeaf rule of
      MC-ROOT / DESIGN-PROBES), give every leaf its majority TRAIN category (train side routed the same way), score
      held-out top-1 majority-label agreement with Wilson CI; the anchored o0 under the identical instrument beside it;
  (2) structure: leaf count, depth, and certified sites from the site null on the snapshot (gradlew siteNull, 300
      reps), against o0's;
  (3) capability information: the key-only leaf-vs-category LOO Brier (F6's instrument) on the 10,925 keyed
      questions, and the split-half reliability of the KEY profile at the tree's depth-1 cells (profile_reliability's
      instrument), both beside o0's;
  (4) descriptive: the migration matrix TrueCategory x anchor-free depth-1 cell, and mu-match of leaves to o0's.
Criteria (registered): C1 purity within 10pp of o0 (o0 under the same instrument is the bar, not the runner's
0.772); C2 certified sites >= o0's minus 2; C3 key-only leaf information within 1/1000 LOO Brier of o0's.
Predictions: purity BELOW o0 by 10-25pp (labels are what the anchors buy: PREDICT C1 FAIL); leaves fewer, depth
similar; certification equal or lower (C2 borderline); C3 HELD (capability information lives in the geometry, not
the labels - the F6 finding); the migration matrix shows a few big cells straddling category pairs the record
already knows to be adjacent (Physics/Chemistry, Math/CS, Law/Philosophy). Falsifier of the framework sentence: if
C1 PASSES the anchors buy nothing but names and the sentence stands outright; if C1 FAILS while C3 HOLDS the
sentence narrows to "not a routing mechanism for capability, but the source of the category names".
Cost: one construction (~2 min) + one site null (~35 min) + zero-call readouts. Consequence: a row in the
ledger either way; no change to any tree of record.

## Registered 2026-09-17 (before any code or call) — REF-CHECKLIST: a per-question verification checklist as a reference in rubric form
Question. Every cell-level artefact (induced rubrics at four granularities, kits, cards, frontier-written and
contrastive rubrics) is null or decisiveness-only; every per-question artefact (the reference solve +12.6pp, the
checker 0.958, verify-first mechanics) moves the judge. The reference's known failure is leakage: it is an ANSWER,
the judge follows it 2:1 against its own reading, and agreement with it inflates whoever mirrors it (ARENA-13,
DECOMP, CONSENSUS-FIT). Does a reference that states the facts and steps a correct answer must contain, WITHOUT
the answer, carry the reference's value with less of its leakage, and help where the answer reference is wrong?
Hygiene. The checklist is derived from the judged question ALONE, at judgment time, by the reasoning model
(grok-4-1-fast-reasoning, the reference's own model), exactly as the reference solve is; nothing is induced over
the reserved split; no train-side material enters. Leakage audit on every checklist before use: no answer letter,
no verbatim correct-option text (the rubric leakage n-gram rule against the correct option and the distractors);
a checklist that fails is DROPPED and counted, never edited.
Instrument. Generation: one call per question of the R3 sample's 944 key-decidable matches (~900 questions),
JSON protocol, cap 8192, finish_reason recorded, guard 5% unparsed; cache judge_solve/checklist_grok-reasoning.db.
Judging: grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning, STACK-v2 mechanics (v2 verify-first + anchor rubric + confidence), dual
order, TIE on flip, cap 8192, temperature omitted (D2), on the 944 key-decidable R3 matches, three FRESH arms
interleaved in one session: REF (the recipe's answer-reference block, byte-identical to RECIPE-GROK = the session
control), CHECKLIST (the reference block replaced by the checklist under the same "produced independently, may be
wrong" wrapper), BOTH (answer reference + checklist). Comparators from cache: RECIPE-GROK (REF, other session;
gives the session floor with the fresh REF arm) and PAIR-NOREF (neither). 3 x 944 x 2 = 5,664 cheap calls +
~900 reasoning calls, under the 4,000-match rule.
Readouts and criteria. Key-decidable accuracy under conventions A and B per arm; paired McNemar and
question-clustered bootstrap CIs on the deltas; stratified by the answer reference correct / wrong; ties and
flips; answer-agreement of each arm's verdicts with every contestant (the CONSENSUS-FIT leakage predictor), the
gemini delta first; the checklist audit counts.
 (1) PRIMARY: BOTH vs REF on key-decidable, p < 0.05 either direction, reported with the session floor
     (REF-fresh vs RECIPE-GROK) beside it.
 (2) CHECKLIST vs REF: the falsifier line (see below).
 (3) reference-WRONG stratum: CHECKLIST and BOTH vs REF, paired.
 (4) leakage: gemini-agreement delta of CHECKLIST vs REF; expected NEGATIVE (less leakage).
Predictions. CHECKLIST below REF overall by 3-6pp (the judge wants the letter); BOTH within the session floor of
REF (the letter dominates); on the reference-wrong stratum CHECKLIST and BOTH above REF by >= 5pp (a wrong letter
and a right list of required steps are different objects); gemini agreement lower under CHECKLIST by >= 2pp.
Falsifier of the reference line as the record states it: CHECKLIST alone at or above REF on key-decidable
(then the value of a reference is verification structure, not the answer, and the leakage is avoidable).
Consequence if (1) PASSES upward: BOTH enters the recipe as a registered arm at +1 reasoning call per question;
if (3) holds and (1) does not: a reference-quality-gated switch is the next registration, not adopted here.

## REF-CHECKLIST (2026-09-17, 782 reasoning + 4,956 cheap calls) — PRIMARY FAIL; the value of a reference is the ANSWER, not the verification structure; the leakage is not avoidable by this route
Run: checklists for 782 questions (grok-4-1-fast-reasoning, 781 stop / 1 content_filter, 11 unparsed = 1.4%);
audit dropped 96 (letter 3, n-gram 22, short-option 59, numeral 12), 675 usable; 826 of the 944 key-decidable
R3 matches eligible, the same 826 in all three fresh arms (REF / CHECKLIST / BOTH, interleaved, grok-4-1-fast-
non-reasoning, STACK-v2, dual order, cap 8192, temperature omitted); guards 0.2% / 0 / 0; session floor REF-fresh
vs RECIPE-GROK -1.2pp [-2.9, +0.4], verdict disagreement 0.071 (DECOMP 0.057).
  arm (n = 826)      conv A   conv B   ties
  PAIR-NOREF (cache) 0.734    0.887    0.173
  CHECKLIST          0.749    0.893    0.161
  REF (fresh)        0.845    0.921    0.080
  BOTH               0.851    0.919    0.074
  RECIPE-GROK (cache)0.857    0.925    0.074
(1) PRIMARY BOTH vs REF: +0.6pp [-1.5, +2.7], 37:32, p = 0.63; inside the session floor -> FAIL (no gain).
(2) CHECKLIST vs REF: -9.6pp [-12.5, -6.7], 34:113, p = 4e-11; vs PAIR-NOREF +1.6pp [-1.6, +4.6], p = 0.32: the
    checklist is worth about as much as no reference at all. Prediction "3-6pp below REF" MISSED: worse.
(3) reference-WRONG stratum (n = 119): CHECKLIST +2.5pp [-6.6, +12.4], p = 0.71; BOTH -5.0pp [-12.5, +1.7],
    p = 0.24 -> the predicted >= 5pp rescue where the answer is wrong is NOT there. Reference-CORRECT stratum
    (n = 707): CHECKLIST -11.6pp; BOTH +1.6pp [-0.3, +3.6].
(4) leakage: gemini agreement CHECKLIST - REF -1.9pp (predicted <= -2pp: borderline), BOTH - REF -5.6pp; the
    CONSENSUS-FIT REF coefficient falls from +2.22 (REF) to +1.23 (CHECKLIST) and rises to +2.52 (BOTH);
    reference-mirroring rate REF 0.976 / CHECKLIST 0.924 / BOTH 0.982. The leakage does fall under the
    checklist - and so does everything else: ties double (0.080 -> 0.161) and accuracy falls to the no-reference
    level. Less leakage bought with less decision, not with better judgment.
Falsifier (CHECKLIST >= REF): NOT FIRED. Consequence: no recipe change.
Reading. A list of the facts and steps a correct answer must contain, produced by the same model whose answer
letter is worth +11.1pp, is worth +1.6pp n.s. The judge does not use verification structure; it uses the answer
(ORACLE, JUDGE-2x2, FORMAT-REF and PAIR-NOREF all said the reference outweighs or displaces the judge's own
reading, and this run says the same from the other side). Where the answer is wrong, the checklist does not
rescue it either, because the model that wrote the wrong answer wrote the checklist. The reference line's
statement is now sharper: the value of a reference is its correctness as an ANSWER, its leakage is the price of
that value, and no rubric-shaped substitute has been found at any granularity, cell or question. A recorded
selection effect: the 118 excluded matches are ones where the checklist named the answer; they are excluded from
all three arms alike, so the paired deltas are fair within the 826.
Output: experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/ref_checklist_outcome.txt; caches ref_checklist.db and
judge_solve/checklist_grok-reasoning.db (gitignored); checklist_audit.txt committed.

Question. The anchor-free tree of record (af_s42: z 2.0, mcs 55, 256-dim slice, bar 0.025; 81 leaves) certifies 16
of 69 split sites at the 300-rep site null (anchored control o0: 5 of 65). Certified sites have median n 621,
uncertified median n 259; the site p95 rises from ~0.028 at n ~4,500 to 0.05-0.09 below n ~400 while observed
separations sit at 0.03-0.05: small sites cannot clear a null this wide. Which construction levers raise the
certified COUNT on the anchor-free tree without spending its information or its support, and how much of any
gain is the null moving rather than the tree?
Hygiene. Every arm = af_s42.toml with ONE key changed (arm 4: width + the D2 bar-equalised bar, registered as
one "width at equal effective bar" knob; arm 6: one key against arm 1), own outputDir and ratings db; seed 42,
label-free, zero LLM calls; every tree is STRUCTURAL EVIDENCE ONLY; one construction at a time, none while the
ANCHOR-FREE-FULL site null runs; nothing touches snapshots_frozen.db or the tree of record.

record's site null as control; per-leaf held-out support; for all-but-top arms a CROSS-NULL at dropTop 0 on the
same snapshot (sites certified under BOTH nulls reported beside the arm's count). Arm 0, PRUNE, zero build
(tools/analysis/anchor_free_prune.py): views A (maximal all-certified prefix) and B (certified sites + bridging
uncertified ancestors) of the record's tree, routed and scored with the readout's functions.

## Registered 2026-09-17 (before running; the script exists, its --dry-run passed, no gain has been computed) — CAP-GATE-POSTHOC: would a CAPABILITY split gate accept the sites the geometric gate certifies? (zero judge calls, zero constructions; feasibility study before any "capability-gated construction")
Question. The construction accepts a split on geometry (ascending-k first accept on J, z-gate dJ >= 2 SE_dJ,
TaxonomyOperations.kt L997-1006) and certifies a site afterwards against its own 300-rep site null (cert_site_p95;
FRAMEWORK L53: "certification is a published certificate per node, never an admission gate"). A capability gate
would accept a split only when the children carry different model-performance profiles. Do the two gates accept
the same sites, a subset, or different ones, and how many sites clear BOTH (the joint gate)?
Instrument. tools/analysis/cap_gate_posthoc.py (docstring = this registration). Trees, read-only: af
(anchorfree/af/seed_42, 69 sites, 16 certified: site_null_af_s42.csv), af_abt2 (36 sites, 23 certified),

being computed at 512/0/300 reps into experiment_results/promoted/site_null_bareq512_s42.csv, started 19:35 before
this commit, zero calls, so the promoted tree's joint count is reported when it lands), and o0 (h9_order/o0/seed_42,
65 sites, 5 certified: the anchored same-code control of ANCHOR-FREE). A site = an internal node with >= 2 children
in the last snapshot (asserted equal to the site-null rows with their k and n; the anchored root, whose 14 children
are bootstrapped anchors, is not a site). Membership = nearest-leaf routing (the flatLeaf rule of F6 /
anchor_free_readout) and the leaf's ancestor chain; n is reported twice (n_site from the null, n_scored). Scored
set = the 10,925 keyed questions (46-model roster, OPTIONS-key join, F6's loader) minus the tree's own hash-verified
reserved pool minus the pool of record p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae: 5,602 questions on the p8a29 trees (af, abt2, bareq512,
o0), 7,795 on the promoted tree; the script asserts scored ∩ eval_ids(p2dca) = 0 per tree and prints it. Gain per
site = mean over its scored questions of the key-only LOO Brier gain of the CHILD cells over the PARENT cell
(free_tests_f4_f7.loo_imp restricted to the site, asserted equal to the vectorised form), in two forms: in-roster
(46 models) and LOMO (the child offset fit on 45 models, scored on the held-out 46th, cycled; additive in
probability, clipped). Gate: 1000 x mean LOMO gain >= t, t in {0, +0.5, +1, +2}; a fifth CI gate (question
bootstrap lower bound > 0, B = 200, seed 42, plug-in on the per-question LOO values as F6's boot_mean_ci). Readout
per tree: the per-site table; accepted / joint / certified-only / accepted-only / Jaccard per t; Spearman and
Pearson of the LOMO gain with observed separation, n_scored, log n, the margin (sep - p95) and depth; the depth
profile; certified vs uncertified median gain; a cross-tree summary.

evidence; embeddings_cache.db and mmlu_pro_dataset_cache_v2.db opened mode=ro; the first printed line is the
pool id; the readout refuses to print without --run. F2-CLEAN caveat carried on every table: the boundaries
were CHOSEN on these train-side questions; LOO removes a question from its cell mean, not from that choice.
Prior numbers relied on: leaf-over-marginal key-only +13.194 (af) / +14.016 (o0), depth-1-over-marginal
+3.491 / +10.418 (experiment_results/anchorfree/anchor_free_readout.txt L18-19); abt2 +12.798 / +4.318,
bareq512 +13.768 / +3.847 (their readouts L18-19); F5: uncertified leaves +2.18 [+1.01, +3.28], CERT-STRICT
+2.49, the certified depth-4 Math site +31.45 (experiment_results/free_tests_f4_f7_output.txt L13-15);
certified vs uncertified median site n on the record 622 / 259 (judge_v2_program.md L4577-4578). The arithmetic
behind the predictions: per-question site gains telescope along the chain, so sum_sites n_s x gain_s ~ N x leaf
gain; on the anchor-free tree ~9.7 of the 13.2 per 1000 live BELOW depth 1 across 68 gated sites, on the anchored
trees only ~3.6 of 14.0 live below the (ungated) anchors.
Criteria (scorable; each HELD / FAILED at the readout). Primary object: the af tree (69 sites, 16 certified).
  P1 median LOMO gain over the 69 af sites in [+1.0, +3.0] per 1000 (point +1.8). [The orchestrator's prior,
     recorded beside it: under +1.0.]
  P2 af accepted at t=0: 50-60 of 69; t=+0.5: 42-55; t=+1: 35-48; t=+2: 20-32.
  P3 JOINT gate at t=+1 on af: >= 11 of the 16 certified sites (point 13). [Orchestrator's prior: under 8.]
     Reading if HELD: the capability gate is a near-SUPERSET of the geometric certificate (geometry sufficient,
     not necessary); a capability-gated construction would ADD sites, not replace the trunk.

     Spearman(LOMO gain, n_scored) in [+0.20, +0.60]; Spearman(LOMO gain, sep - p95) in [+0.10, +0.50].

Falsifier (named before the run). If on af the joint count at t=+1 is < 8 of 16 AND the certified-minus-

## Registered 2026-09-17 (before running) — TOPIC-DIFFICULTY: does a difficulty axis inside a cell change the judge and the model order? (zero judge calls; tools/analysis/topic_difficulty.py)
Question. Every board of record is published per cell (14 anchors of bareq512_s42; leaves refused for support). Inside a
cell the questions span the whole difficulty range (roster accuracy on the key, quartiles 0.283 / 0.500 / 0.739 over the
2,811 judged questions). Does the judge behave differently on the easy and hard strata of the SAME cell (verification
fidelity, tie rate, length preference), and is the within-cell model order on hard questions the order on easy ones? If
so, the per-cell board hides a difficulty confound and its calibration statement (widener on agreement A_e) is read on a
mixture. Claim under test: per-cell boards are NOT difficulty-invariant.
Instrument. difficulty(q) = fraction of the keyed roster correct on q in eval_results (46 models; Meta-Llama-3-70B-Instruct
excluded; per-question denominator 44-46), a judgment-time artefact of the judged question, computed only on the judged
questions of pool p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae; nothing induced, no train-side material. Secondary instrument: the same over the 26
roster models NOT on the merged board (the strata then owe nothing to the contestants' own key rows). Identity check
eval_results <-> mmlu_pro through the OPTIONS key only (json-normalised options_json = mmlu_pro.options; never
question_text): on the 2,811 judged questions 2,688 match 1:1, 3 multi, 120 none, gt_answer = mmlu_pro.answer on 2,681
of 2,688 (the 7 + 120 go to the data-steward; the key used here is eval_results.is_correct, the key every board of record
reads via systematic_budget.build). Strata: rank terciles WITHIN each cell over the cell's judged questions (ties broken by
qid; cut values printed), one assignment per question shared by every arm; cells = the 14 anchors (the tree the boards
group by: systematic_budget.build / budget_transfer.edges_from route by r512.primary_routing("bareq512_s42") and take
r512.anchor_fn; the caches' `anchor` column agrees on 0 mismatches) and the 13 of 87 leaves with >= 45 judged questions
and >= 20 key-decidable merged-board matches in every tercile.
Hygiene. Caches opened mode=ro and inspected before use: MISTRAL-X12 stack_v2_promptv2_x12all.db 9,142 (2,811 q);
MISTRAL-MERGED = + stack_v2_promptv2_x20.db 12,394 (2,646 q, all in x12) = 21,536, the board of record and the PRIMARY
arm; GROK-CALIB grok_calib.db 9,142 (11 INVALID + 1 row with finish2 empty reclassified INVALID by rule 10); KOTLIN
kotlin_c0d3f708cbc3930e.db 9,123 (17 INVALID incl. 2 length + 1 content_filter; ref_correct not recorded there, taken from
the x12 cache by match_id, same reference kit). NON_TERMINATED is never a verdict, never a tie. Row counts pinned; a
mismatch refuses the readout. Conventions A (ties/INVALID/non-terminated wrong) and B (committed only) both reported;
wrong(established) by systematic_budget.mcnemar_edge over the STRATUM's judged questions; power rule on every wrong count
(nominal < 3 -> UNDETERMINED); a stratum under 20 key-decidable matches prints counts and no rate. Note the easy tercile
is thin on key-decidable pairs (both contestants usually right; the schedule is answer-disagreement filtered): merged
board Biology 44, Economics 66, Psychology 68 decidable in the easy tercile against 259 / 282 / 286 in the hard one. [CORRECTED 2026-09-17 by TOPIC-DIFFICULTY: "the schedule is answer-disagreement filtered" is false for these
caches: x12 34.3% of matches have the same predicted letter, x20 48.2% (checker); the easy tercile is thin on
key-decidable pairs because both contestants are usually right, not because of any filter.] [CORRECTED 2026-09-18 by PROFILE-R-FILTERED: the 34.3% / 48.2% same-letter shares counted both-missing predictions as equal (64 matches on x12, 134 on x20); same-letter proper is 33.6% / 47.2%; under the shipped MatchFilter rule (missing kept) the kept share is 66.4% / 52.8%. §PROFILE-R-FILTERED.]
Fits reused, not retyped: length = bias_audit.h3 (_logit3: P(winner = a) ~ 1 + dlen/1k + dkey, decisive only, the
+0.39/1k fit of record); board = jf.board_from -> rj.mm_fit (prior 0.5), reproduced by a vectorised copy asserted equal in
--selftest; question-clustered bootstrap B = 300 per stratum; certificate c_raw = max(p, 1-p) at 0.975.
Readouts. Per (arm, cell, tercile): accA, accB, tie rate (decidable and all), INVALID rate, reference-correct rate and
accA within reference-correct / -wrong, beta_len (SE, n), called / wrong(established) / nominal / status. Per (arm,
anchor): Spearman(easy order, hard order) with a question-bootstrap 95% interval AND a within-cell permutation null (tercile
labels shuffled over the cell's questions, sizes preserved, 200 perms), the key's own easy-vs-hard order Spearman beside
it (the capability part of the shift), Spearman(judge, key) per tercile, rho(easy, mid), rho(mid, hard); a stratum with a

bootstrap (questions resampled within each (anchor, tercile) slice). Residue block: the four KTD-CHECK edges have 0-12

rank on each stratum board and the established wrong edges naming it. Deployability line: Spearman(difficulty, key-free

Criteria (scored on MISTRAL-MERGED; MISTRAL-X12, GROK-CALIB, KOTLIN are the replication; each prediction HELD/FAILED):
 (C1) accA hard - easy, pooled over anchors, question-clustered 95% interval excludes 0 (negative).

 (C3) beta_len(hard) - beta_len(easy) z >= 1.96 (independent strata, Hessian SEs).
 (C4) rho(easy, hard) below the 5th percentile of the within-cell permutation null in >= 7 of 14 anchors.
 (C5) Llama-3.1-70B wrong-direction rate (judge gives the opponent on pairs the key gives to Llama) rises >= 10pp from the

      UNDETERMINED by support and says so).

rho(easy, hard) 0.6-0.8 within anchors, interval excluding 1; the Law/Philosophy under-rating is a hard-stratum effect.
Predictions (builder, recorded blind before any outcome exists): C1 HELD at -8 to -15pp on MISTRAL-MERGED, same sign on
all three replication arms; the reference-correct rate falls from ~0.95 (easy) to ~0.65 (hard) and within the

as low (0.5-0.7): most of the order shift is capability structure the key also shows, the judge's excess is small; C5

not a hard-stratum effect; on the easy tercile Llama-3.1-70B ranks below its key rank already. Leaves: accuracy
readable on 13, order REFUSED or within null on most (support). Deployability: Spearman(difficulty, plurality
agreement) 0.6-0.8, the key-free proxy the widener already carries.
Falsifier. If C1 fails AND C4 fails (no accuracy contrast survives its interval and the easy-vs-hard order is within the
within-cell null in > 7 anchors), the claim is overturned: per-cell boards are difficulty-invariant and no
difficulty term belongs in the board or the widener. If C1 or C4 holds, the record's implicit statement that a per-cell
board is one homogeneous object (FRAMEWORK Stage 4, widener on A_e alone) is overturned at the reading level;
consequence = a registered difficulty-stratified reading (or the key-free proxy as a second widener covariate), never a
key input at inference (systematic_budget's rule).
Cost. Zero judge calls; ~85,000 BT refits at ~1 ms each, a few minutes; writes
experiment_results/topic_difficulty/topic_difficulty_outcome.txt (+ _rows.csv) once, from complete caches only.
Author-side decisions taken by the builder: cells from bareq512_s42 (the tree the boards group by); 46-model
instrument roster with the 26 non-contestants as the secondary; rank terciles within cell; MISTRAL-MERGED primary;
rule 10 applied in loading; KOTLIN ref_correct from the x12 cache by match_id; wrong(established) from the stratum's own
B = 300 bootstrap with no widener; the order criterion uses a within-cell permutation null (a bootstrap interval of a
Spearman essentially never contains 1, so "interval excludes 1" would be vacuous); C5 widened from the four named edges

## Registered 2026-09-17 (before running; the script exists, its --dry-run passed, no outcome computed) — BOUNDARY-DISAGREEMENT: is judge disagreement concentrated at the tree's cell boundaries? (zero judge calls; the MULTI-OWNERSHIP mechanism test)
Question. The author's MULTI-OWNERSHIP idea (dual-cell judging of questions near a cell boundary) presumes a
mechanism: that a judged question with a low routing margin is where the judge cannot decide: more ties, more
order flips, more INVALID, more wrong(established) verdicts, a less stable model order. No test of record has
measured a per-question routing margin against a verdict. If the mechanism is absent the line closes at zero
calls; if present the bill is stated (Q1 = 562 questions / 4,513 merged matches; the Kotlin two-candidate set =
314 questions / 2,652 merged matches; dry run 2026-09-17) and no arm is launched without its own registration.
Instrument. Tree of record for the boards: the promoted bareq512_s42 (experiment_results/promoted/bareq512_s42/
seed_42 = snapshot 20260909_212117_Headless_Run_Auto_ge, 158 nodes / 87 leaves / sliceDim 512; manifest split
pool p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae; the run dir's leaf vmfMu equal snapshots.db's to 5e-7). The boards WERE fitted on it, not
on the frozen 20260727_042523 artefact: systematic_budget.build() routes with r512.primary_routing("bareq512_s42")
(systematic_budget.py L55) and every verdict cache's `anchor` column equals anchor_of(that routing) on all rows
(9,142 / 12,394 / 9,142 / 9,123); the caches' `node_id` is the frozen tree's leaf that SCHEDULED the x12 match
(stack_judge.all_x12_matches L59-62 reads match_history at rejudge_grok.SNAP_MAIN L58), so the frozen tree is
offered only behind --frozen as a secondary. Secondary tree: anchor-free af/seed_42 (150 nodes / 81 leaves /
2 depth-1 cells / sliceDim 256; manifest split p8a29d8f3ff75aa55, NOT the pool of record; descriptive only).
Per judged question, the flatLeaf rule of anchor_free_readout (first-sliceDim slice of the stored 4096-d
embedding, unit norm, cosine vs every leaf's unit vmfMu; sliced L103 / full_vectors L92 reused):
  m_leaf = cos(best leaf) - cos(second-best leaf) [PRIMARY]; m_d1 = the same over the 14 depth-1 centroids;
  m_rec = cos(leaf of record) - max cos(other leaf) (negative on 416 of 2,808 where the flatLeaf rule and the
  Kotlin routeReserved primary leaf disagree; the two agree on 2,392 of 2,808); two-candidate flag = the Kotlin
  router listed 2 leaves (n_leaves = 2 in bareq512_s42_reserved_leaf_assignments.csv; 410 of 3,445 pool, 314 of
  2,808 judged), the router's own multi-owner set. Join eval question_id -> mmlu_pro by the OPTIONS key
  (whitespace-stripped option list, every model's options_json row; 3,441 of 3,445 unique, 4 ambiguous dropped,
  0 none; Meta-Llama-3-70B-Instruct excluded). The cell for the fixed effects is the cell of record (Kotlin
  primary leaf, 87; its depth-1 anchor, 14). Margin population P0 = the 2,808 of 2,811 x12-judged questions with
  a margin; quintile cut-points 0.0175 / 0.0394 / 0.0666 / 0.1024 bin every cache (x20, grok, kotlin judged sets
  are subsets of x12's: 2,646 / 2,811 / 2,801).
Outcomes (caches of record, all mode=ro; row semantics checked: winner in {a, b, TIE, INVALID}; flip = 1 iff the
two orders disagree, then winner = TIE, 0 contradicting rows; TIE with flip = 0 = both orders TIE; invalid = 1 iff
winner = INVALID, in the Kotlin cache also finish length/content_filter; Mistral caches have no finish column and
0 invalid rows; grok_calib has one finish2 = '' row with a parsed verdict, kept valid). Objects: x12
stack_v2_promptv2_x12all.db 9,142 / 2,811 q; x20 12,394 / 2,646 q (zero verdicts on the 66 original pairs, so no
board from it alone); merged = 21,536 (board of record, x20_merged.merged_rows L27); grok_calib.db 9,142 on the
x12 match ids; kotlin_c0d3f708cbc3930e.db 9,123 on the same match ids. One cache = one object; never a fit across
judges. Per question: tie share, flip share, both-tie share, INVALID share, disagreement = 1 - committed share;
on KEY-DECIDABLE matches (the two models' key correctness differs) wrong under convention A (TIE/INVALID wrong,
denominator all key-decidable) and B (committed only); wrong(established) = the same on matches whose (anchor,
pair) edge has exact two-sided McNemar p < 0.05 on the anchor's JUDGED questions in that cache
(systematic_budget.mcnemar_edge L169); cross-judge disagreement x12 vs grok / kotlin on the same match id.
Analysis. Each outcome per m_leaf quintile (also m_d1 and the af margin) with a question-clustered bootstrap
95% interval (B = 2,000, seed 42) and Q1 - Q5 with its interval; Spearman of m_leaf with per-question tie, flip,
disagreement and wrongA shares (question bootstrap); logistic flip (and tie) on z(m_leaf) with no / anchor / leaf
fixed effects, cluster-robust by question, cells without outcome variation dropped and counted; the same plus
key difficulty (mean ARENA12 key correctness) to separate "boundary" from "hard"; order stability per quintile:
rejudge_grok.mm_fit (MM, Jeffreys 0.5 prior; a vectorised copy asserted equal on every point fit and on the first
bootstrap draw against rows -> mm_fit), Spearman with the key accuracy over the quintile's questions, and the

     REVERSED. Power note: a quintile holds ~560 questions; on x12 alone (~1,850 matches per quintile) the tie

  Q1 - Q5 interval covers 0; the two-candidate flag moves the tie share by < 2pp with an interval covering 0;

questions carry the disagreement) is OVERTURNED: dual-cell judging targets nothing; no E4 judged arm; the line

## CAP-GATE-POSTHOC (2026-09-17, zero judge calls; EXPLORATORY) — the capability gate accepts a DIFFERENT SET from the geometric certificate at every registered threshold (t=+1: 24 of 69 accepted, 9 of 16 certified, Jaccard 0.29); the falsifier did not fire AND P3 failed, so the outcome lies in the unregistered gap between the two registered branches; the t=0 line is not a zero line and the certified contrast is mostly site size
Run per the registration: tools/analysis/cap_gate_posthoc.py --run with --tree passed explicitly for all five trees
(script unchanged since the registration commit 7073c97; a first promoted-only run was moved to *_promotedonly.* and
is not the outcome). The promoted tree's first site null landed at 19:52 (experiment_results/promoted/
site_null_bareq512_s42.csv: 70 sites, 10 certified at cert_site_p95, 300 reps, 512/0), so the promoted joint count is
reported. Scored set 5,602 questions on the p8a29 trees (af, abt2, bareq512, o0) and 7,795 on the promoted tree;

## Registered 2026-09-17 (before any code or call) — PROFILE-DEVIATION-CERT: does the (model, anchor) deviation term carry certifiable content beyond the global theta? (zero judge calls; plan docs/agents/plans/2026-09-17_continual_capability_profile_leads.md A1; lens docs/agents/leads/2026-09-17_arena_profile.md L1)
Question. Every published profile row is theta_ac = theta_a + delta_ac on the anchor's own board, and the record has never
published delta_ac with a certificate of its own: the anchor profile's board-level R (0.7183 [0.6076, 0.8291], merged;

any model's deviation from its own global standing is distinguishable from zero. Claim under test: delta_ac carries
certifiable content beyond theta_m, i.e. for some (model, anchor) cells the record may say "m is certified above / below
its own standing in anchor c". That sentence is the first that would make the atlas a PROFILE rather than a re-indexed
global score. The cell is the ANCHOR: this registration is at the anchor and nowhere below it (sub-anchor rows closed
twice, PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST and KEY-SUBANCHOR-SCALE; no cell size reopens them).
Hygiene. Caches opened mode=ro and row counts pinned before any fit: MISTRAL-MERGED = stack_v2_promptv2_x12all.db 9,142
(2,811 judged q) + stack_v2_promptv2_x20.db 12,394 (2,646 q) = 21,536 verdicts, 20 models, the board of record; x20 is
never read alone (zero verdicts on the 66 original pairs). Pool p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae, verified by `pool_guard.py --pool` as
the first printed line; only JUDGED questions enter (per anchor 119-304). Anchors = the 14 bareq512_s42 anchors the
boards group by (r512.primary_routing / r512.anchor_fn; the caches' `anchor` column agrees on 0 mismatches). Key =
eval_results.is_correct as systematic_budget.build reads it (46-model roster, Meta-Llama-3-70B-Instruct excluded, join by
the OPTIONS key, never question_text); all 20 contestants are keyed (BUDGET-TRANSFER). No train-side material; nothing
induced; no leaf, no sub-anchor row. The Jeffreys prior (rj.mm_fit DEFAULT_PRIOR_STRENGTH 0.5) is printed with its
per-anchor shrinkage (1.23-1.82x, K-RECONCILE checker (3)); routing attenuation (~20% proportional at 19%, ROUTING-
ATTENUATION) is a caveat on the MAGNITUDE of every deviation, not on its sign, and is printed once.
Instrument. (a) Draw matrix from x20_merged.merged_rows(): per resample, questions resampled WITHIN each anchor
(question-clustered, B >= 2,000, seed 42 printed; resamples cached to disk so the reviewer recomputes from the same
draws), and on the SAME resample both the per-anchor board (jf.board_from -> rj.mm_fit, prior 0.5) and the pooled board
over all judged questions; delta_ac = theta_ac(per-anchor fit) - theta_m(pooled fit) per draw; point = the fit on the
unresampled data; SD_ac = the draw SD. (b) Critical value: the MAXT-MULTIPLICITY construction applied to the deviation
object, q_cell(dev) = the 95th percentile over draws of max over the anchor's 20 models of |delta*_ac - delta_hat_ac| /
SD_ac (raw-z reading; the widened-q reading printed beside; the hybrid reading is NOT used, MAXT-MULTIPLICITY checker (1));
MAXT's pair-level merged per-anchor q (3.43-3.80) printed beside for scale. A deviation is CERTIFIED iff |delta_ac| /
SD_ac >= q_cell(dev); the marginal 1.96 count is printed as a second column and is not the count of record. (c) Key
comparator on the same cells: dev_key_mc = acc_mc - acc_m over the anchor's judged questions vs all 2,811 judged
questions, question-bootstrap SD from the same resamples, certified iff |dev_key| / SD >= q_cell(dev, key) computed the
same way on the key resamples; ESTABLISHED iff the exact two-sided Fisher test on the model's in-anchor vs out-of-anchor
correctness (2 x 2 over judged questions, integer arithmetic) gives p < 0.05. [Registrar's note: the plan writes "by
McNemar against the pool mean"; McNemar needs a paired binary object and the in/out contrast has none, so the exact
test on the 2 x 2 is registered and the plan's wording is recorded here as an inconsistency for the author.] (d)
Variance share = var_cells(delta_ac) / (var_cells(delta_ac) + var_models(theta_m)) over the 280 cells, key and judge,
with the mean bootstrap variance of delta subtracted and printed beside (sampling share). (e) wrong(established):
judge-certified deviations whose key deviation has the OPPOSITE sign and is established under (c).
Readouts and criteria (each scored HELD / FAILED; denominators named):
 (C1) key-certified share = certified key cells / 280 (20 models x 14 anchors), per anchor and overall.
 (C2) judge-certified share = certified judge cells / 280, per anchor and overall; the certified list per model, each
      row carrying the anchor's PROFILE-INTERVAL-ALL C2 class (PASS Physics, Math; PASS-WITH-INTERVAL Law, Psychology,
      Business, Chemistry, Philosophy, Other, History; FAIL Engineering, Biology, Computer science, Economics, Health).
      Rows in FAIL anchors are published PREDICTIVE-ONLY whatever the deviation test says (counted in C2, never a claim).
 (C3) wrong(established) among judge-certified deviations (e), with the denominator = judge-certified count.
 (C4) variance share of delta vs theta, key and judge, with the sampling share beside.
 (C5) agreement of the certified sets: of the judge-certified cells, the share whose key deviation has the same sign
      (descriptive; the sign agreement of ALL 280 cells printed beside as the null-ish baseline).

asserted equal across draws up to the draw's own INVALID rows). Established labels by systematic_budget.mcnemar_edge on
the anchor's JUDGED questions: the label and the agreement covariate A (the contestants' answer agreement, key-free) are
properties of the edge and identical across draws; only m and s (the judge's verdicts) differ. Both conventions are
printed where a rate appears; no key input at inference (A only). Free parameters: b0, b1, b2 = 3, the SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET
criterion (4) ceiling exactly.
Instrument. systematic_budget's helpers (build, mcnemar_edge, established, nll, fit, summarise), extended by ONE term:
tau(A, D) = exp(b0 + b1 A + b2 D), D = 0 for the GROK-CALIB draw and 1 for the Kotlin draw, fitted on the union of the two
draws' established edges (each edge appears twice, once per draw, with its own m and s). Identification: delta-deviance
of b1 = 0 (b0, b2 free) against b1 free, read at 3.84; both single-draw values (4.47 / 2.26) and both single-draw b1
(+2.72 / +2.05) printed beside; pooled b1 with a question-clustered bootstrap interval (questions resampled, both
draws' boards recomputed from the same resample, B = 300). Power statement: parametric simulation from the fitted pooled
model at true b1 = +2.7 (b0, b2 at their fits), 1,000 simulated label sets on the single-draw established population (~26
events) and on the pooled one (~52), P(delta-deviance >= 3.84) each. LOAO at 0.975 on the pooled fit: called /
wrong(established) / nominal, printed for the pooled edge set AND per draw under the pooled parameters (the pooled
nominal counts each edge twice and says so); utility = called / all edges per draw (D6: LOAO-called over ALL edges).
Readouts and criteria (scored HELD / FAILED):
 (C1) pooled delta-deviance >= 3.84 -> b1 identified on the pooled established labels -> "ORDERED-JUDGED available for
      grok" rests on the pooled evidence of both draws; < 3.84 -> NOT identified, the power statement is mandatory beside
      every identification the record prints, and every grok cell is BANDED-JUDGED (the Stage 6 fallback), a registered
      outcome.
 (C2) the power statement at ~26 and ~52 events, printed whatever C1 does.
 (C3) LOAO on the pooled fit: called / wrong(established) / nominal per draw and pooled; status by the power rule
      (nominal < 3 -> calibration UNDETERMINED).
 (C4) utility >= 60% per draw (D6).
Predictions (the plan's, recorded blind): pooled delta-deviance 3.5-5.5 (the interval straddles 3.84 at its lower end;
"identified" is scored separately from the interval); LOAO wrong 2-4 (established 1-2) per draw; nominal ~2.2; status
UNDETERMINED. Registrar's blind addition: b2 within [-1, +1] (the two draws are one instrument inside the 1.9pp floor).
Falsifier. Pooled delta-deviance < 2.5. It overturns GROK-CALIB's consequence "ORDERED-JUDGED available for grok": item
26's criterion is unmet on the evidence rather than on a draw, every grok-judged cell is BANDED-JUDGED, and FRAMEWORK
item 26 / Stage 6 carry that bracket until a larger established population exists (which needs new questions, not
re-draws: TEMP-0 / DECOMP put the floor inside the judge).
Cost and consequence. 0 calls; minutes of CPU; writes experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/item26_pooled.txt once, from

ORDERED-JUDGED on the same judge, because the certificate is read on pooled draws with a power number beside it.

## Registered 2026-09-17 (before any code or call) — REF-QUALITY-MONITOR: is per-cell reference-correct rate the continual per-cell quality signal? with DIFFICULTY-PROXY-WIDENER as the secondary leg, registered expecting UNDETERMINED (zero calls; plan A4; lens docs/agents/leads/2026-09-17_judge_continual.md Lead 2, 2026-09-17_arena_profile.md L9)
Question. TOPIC-DIFFICULTY found that 72-79% of a cell's easy-to-hard accuracy drop is the reference's (reference-correct
98.4 -> 93.7 -> 77.7%; judge residual within reference-correct -4.5pp), and its consequence names two registrations: the
key-free plurality proxy as a widener covariate, and no key input at inference. Primary question: across the boards of
record, is the per-(anchor, cache) reference-correct rate on keyed audit mass a sufficient per-cell statistic for the
judge's key-decidable accuracy, so that a continual pipeline can MONITOR each cell's quality from the reference alone?
Secondary (the proxy leg): does the key-free plurality-agreement proxy (Spearman 0.785 with key difficulty) predict
wrong(established) edges as a second covariate in the widener, LOAO, at matched utility? The monitor MONITORS; it never
gates (gating on reference agreement, ABSTAIN, REF-CONF, J2-D closed) and it is not a signal of reference accuracy at
inference (withdrawn as key-derived in SYSTEMATIC-BUDGET correction (a)).
Hygiene. Four caches, mode=ro, counts pinned: x12 MAIN stack_v2_promptv2_x12all.db 9,142 (2,811 q); GROK-CALIB
grok_calib.db 9,142 (11 INVALID, +1 reclassified by rule 10); KOTLIN kotlin_c0d3f708cbc3930e.db 9,123 (17 INVALID;
ref_correct taken from the x12 cache by match_id as TOPIC-DIFFICULTY did, same reference kit); x20
stack_v2_promptv2_x20.db 12,394 (2,646 q; its own ref_correct column; 124 new pairs only, zero verdicts on the 66 original
pairs, so its cells are a different SCHEDULE on the same questions, printed as such). Pool p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae; anchors =
the 14 bareq512_s42 anchors; key = eval_results.is_correct via systematic_budget.build (46 models, Meta-Llama-3-70B-Instruct
excluded, OPTIONS-key join). Reference-correct rate and accuracy are judgment-time artefacts of judged questions;
nothing induced. Conventions A (ties / INVALID / NON_TERMINATED wrong) and B (committed only) both. Denominator
hazard, stated before any number: x12, GROK-CALIB and KOTLIN judge the SAME matches under ONE reference vintage, so their
per-anchor reference-correct rates are identical up to the 19 dropped matches; the 14 x 4 = 56 cells carry 14 + x20's
14 independent reference readings and four judge draws of accuracy, and the "epoch proxy = cache" varies the judge,
not the reference. The registered 56-cell Spearman is the plan's; the 14-cell Spearman per cache is printed beside it
as the honest denominator, and the outcome names which one it scores on (both, explicitly).
Instrument, primary. Per (anchor, cache): key-decidable matches n, reference-correct rate (ref_letter == key), accuracy A
and B, accuracy within reference-correct and within reference-wrong (the TOPIC-DIFFICULTY decomposition per cell),
INVALID rate. Spearman(reference-correct rate, accuracy A) across the 56 cells with a question-bootstrap interval
(questions resampled within anchor, B = 300), the same for B, the same per cache across 14 anchors, and per anchor
across 4 caches (descriptive). Residual: accuracy A within reference-correct per cell, its range and its Spearman with
the reference rate (if the judge's own residual tracks the reference rate the monitor is confounded; printed).
Instrument, secondary (DIFFICULTY-PROXY-WIDENER). On the x12 MAIN edges (891 filtered / 920 unfiltered, UNFILTERED-ADOPT;
809 established), per-edge P = the key-free plurality proxy of TOPIC-DIFFICULTY (per question, the share of the 46-model
roster's predicted letters on the plurality letter; per edge, the mean over the edge's judged questions), tau(A, P) =
exp(b0 + b1 A + b2 P) fitted on established labels by systematic_budget's nll / fit; delta-deviance of b2 = 0 against
3.84; the profile likelihood of b2 (identification profile); LOAO at 0.975: called / wrong(established) / nominal against
the A-only widener at MATCHED utility (the A-only threshold moved until called counts equal); power statement by
parametric simulation at a plausible b2 (the in-sample fit) on ~26-40 events. P is computable without the key at
inference (roster letters only); no key enters the deployed form.
Readouts and criteria (scored HELD / FAILED):
 (C1) Spearman(reference-correct rate, accuracy A) across the 14 x 4 cells >= 0.8 (interval printed; the per-cache

[CORRECTED 2026-09-18 by REVIEW (pre-run, PROFILE-DEVIATION-CERT): the registered judge deviation delta_ac = theta_ac(per-anchor MM, prior 0.5) - theta_m(pooled MM, prior 0.5) is biased by construction. The Jeffreys prior is one 0.5/0.5 pseudo-match per observed pair: ~190 pseudo-matches against 695-2,881 real matches per anchor but against 21,536 pooled, so under the exact null (every anchor shares theta_m) delta_hat ~ -(1 - k_pool/k_anchor)*theta_m with per-anchor shrinkage k = 1.16x (Math) .. 1.69x (Business) against 1.02x pooled. Measured: on the record the slope of delta_hat on theta_m over the 280 cells is -0.2185 (r -0.761); under a null on the real match schedule (verdicts ~ BT(theta_m), tie rate 0.225, B = 400, 10 replicates) the slope is -0.2145 and 129/140 = 92.1% of anchor families carry >= 1 false certificate at nominal 5% (cells 17.5%; 43% of the cells of models with |theta_m| >= 1.5); the script's synthetic selftest gives 113/140 = 80.7%. READING OF RECORD for (b), (d), (e), C2-C5, predictions P2-P4 and the falsifier: the PRIOR-MATCHED deviation delta'_ac = theta_ac(per-anchor MM, prior 0.5, the published row, unchanged) - theta'_m,c(pooled MM with the prior scaled by pooled matches / anchor matches, so both fits carry the same prior-to-data weight; the MM fixed point is invariant to a common scaling of wins and prior), SD_ac and q_cell(dev) from the same within-anchor question resamples and the same max-t construction (q unchanged, 3.0-3.1). Null family rate of this reading: 4/140 = 2.9% on the real schedule, 5/140 = 3.6% synthetic. The registered reading is printed beside every count as "registered; biased by construction (null family rate 80.7-92.1% at nominal 5%)" and is not scored; (c) and C1 (the key comparator) are unchanged. Alternatives declined: prior 0 in both fits (2.1%, unbiased, but changes the published row and can diverge on resamples); permutation-centred delta (12.9% at 40 permutations, the bias estimate's own variance not propagated). The widened-q reading beside is taken on delta' with tau_mc = RMS over the model's in-anchor pairs of the budget_transfer widener (a mapping the registration did not fix). Cost: the prior-matched reading attenuates |delta'| further for |theta_m| > 1.5 (planted |delta| = 1.2 recovered 3/6 vs 4/6 in the selftest, where the registered reading's recoveries include artefact-inflated cells); a certified SIGN is preserved (shrinkage is monotone), a magnitude is not published (ROUTING-ATTENUATION caveat stands). profile_deviation_cert.py is amended to this reading before --run; file names unchanged.]
