[CORRECTED 2026-09-23 by the IFEVAL RULING (docs/agents/leads/2026-09-23_ifeval_ruling.md, af116f8, zero calls): the IFEval rung 0.658 is PERMANENT - IFEval has no question-level checker output (its verifier emits a predicate ON a response: prompt_level_strict_acc = all(inst_level_strict_acc), asserted at checker_answer_ingest.py L513 / L528), so finding 2's 'the checker's OUTPUT, not its specification' is unrealisable there and a per-response pass vector is an ORACLE-CLASS object that may never be quoted beside MATH's 0.958. Structural, not remediable; REF-FORM-BY-CELL's closure does not cover it.] Before any
agent corpus is judged, the record needs (1) a rule set under which a corpus is ADMITTED, refused or admitted for description
only, verified by command on ingested tables, and (2) a first application. This registration is both: the rule set (a)-(e)
below, and its first application as a zero-call pilot on the BFCL-Result 2025-12-16 multi_turn archive. The pilot decides
which BFCL strata may carry JUDGED cells and which are PREDICTIVE-ONLY with checker-built rows on terminated episodes; it
judges nothing and ranks nothing.
The rule set (as drafted in judge_loop2.md §2, registered here in substance). An agent corpus = (task, agent) episodes with
a tool log and a final state. It is admitted as-is only if the five parts are verified BY COMMAND on the ingested tables,
then a checker pilot is read. Failure of any part is a refusal, not a warning.
 (a) SPLIT. Per item: stem + content_key under SplitSide norm-v1, side = f(item) asserted per row in both languages
     (GATE = hash in [300, 400); SPLIT-FUNCTION-IMPL); family_id write-once for templated or parameterised tasks so a family
     sits on ONE side; the pool id exported as a file and declared in the config; TRAIN-ONLY tree state asserted per row;
     any artefact induced over EVAL episodes is contamination (the p8a29/p2dca incident, 71%; ~70% again in MC-E2E).
 (b) CHECKER OUTPUT TABLE. One row per (task, agent): a normalised OUTPUT (pass/fail vector, final-state diff or exact
     target), a checker table sha, a termination proxy VERSIONED like checker_answers_v2, and the reading rule fixed in the
     table's header. D_c (decidable share) is read under the STRICT reading = terminated AND checker-decided over ALL
     admitted episodes (cap-hit episodes stay in the denominator: rule 10). One MATH table read 0.9840 / 0.8268 / 0.6701
     under three readings (CHECKER-ANSWER-INGEST): the reading is fixed before the number. Reference_state for the cell is
     CHECKER_OUTPUT (FRAMEWORK L37); a task specification, a step list or a process rubric is NEVER a reference (GEN-ARENA);
     a reasoning model's own trajectory as CACHED_SOLVE is not admissible until plan C5 sizes it and a REF-QUAL pass under
     one recorded protocol with a trajectory leakage audit exists (none does).
 (c) TERMINATION AS A CLASS. finish_reason and completion_tokens per STEP and per EPISODE where the corpus records them; the
     step cap and the episode cap (steps, tokens, wall-clock) declared per corpus at admission; a cap-hit episode is
     NON_TERMINATED, a class, never a verdict, never a tie, never dropped from the denominator (FRAMEWORK L236 guard 10;
     CONTEXT rule 10); the admitted-population denominator printed on every row (the 9,307 of 11,144 form).
 (d) THE JUDGED ARTEFACT. Tool log + final state under a stated per-episode artefact cap (tokens); per agent: deployment
     fingerprint, provider, response id, tokens, latency where the corpus records them, UNSTAMPED where it does not. Before
     any judged pilot: the item-19 per-model max_tokens probe on the trace-shaped prompt (50 calls per judge model,
     FRAMEWORK L372) AND an input-side fit check; an artefact over the cap is a class (ARTEFACT_OVER_CAP), never silently
     truncated; a match with one is not judged.
 (e) DESIGNED STRATUM. A (source, domain) stratum per task; the anchor is the terminal reporting unit (sub-anchor rows
     closed: PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST, KEY-SUBANCHOR-SCALE); routing value lives at the family layer (MC-E2E +3.38pp clean;
     MC-LEAF: leaves lose to domains as a router).
What "agent capability" is measured AS: per task family (anchor) with an outcome checker, the agent's CHECKER-BUILT accuracy
row on terminated episodes with a question-bootstrap interval at 0 judge calls (the key is the verdict there: ORACLE-BOARD
rho 1.000); a band per agent and the undominated set per family. The judge's product on such a corpus is never the ranking:
a CALIBRATION board of the deployed recipe on the checker's cells and a CANARY. No per-trajectory rank; no "better process"
claim; no row below the family; no checker, no number.
Enforcement clause. A stratum whose pilot D_c is under 0.95 at the point is REFUSED for judged cells in that stratum and KEPT
for checker-built rows on terminated episodes only, the terminated share printed beside every number; no edge pass is
scheduled on it. A stratum with fewer than 120 EVAL-side tasks (the support rule, FRAMEWORK L117) is admitted for [CORRECTED 2026-09-27 by INCONSISTENCIES-PASS (RP01, A10): "FRAMEWORK L117" is a wrong pointer: FRAMEWORK L117 (Profile reliability) contains no "120" (checked at HEAD and at 62c4084, f5e447b, 3dd0900, 8f9f81e); the 120 floor is the leaf rule borrowed from the query-support design effect (120-190 distinct questions at SE 0.15), taken "without a power derivation for anchors" (L7431 bracket); the current support arithmetic is FRAMEWORK L207's K-RECONCILE bracket (63-136 questions for SE 0.15). No number changes]
description only (UNDETERMINED as a profile cell).
First application: the BFCL-Result multi_turn pilot. Corpus of record: the BFCL-Result archive (github.com/HuanzhiMao/
BFCL-Result, Apache-2.0), date folder 2025-12-16, multi_turn only: 800 entries = 4 categories x 200 (base, miss_func,
miss_param, long_context; ids multi_turn_<category>_N), one harness, 158 model directories on identical inputs, a hard cap of [CORRECTED 2026-09-27 by INCONSISTENCIES-PASS (RP01, A4): 109 model directories, not 158: the GitHub contents API for HuanzhiMao/BFCL-Result 2025-12-16/result returns 109 entries, all of type dir, at the pin 6830ed13 (L6944; re-run by the registrar on 2026-09-27) and at HEAD cadd76a8 (RP01's run); nothing in the record supports 158]
20 steps within a turn after which the harness force-terminates and BFCL marks the entry incorrect (survey §1.5). Score files
carry, per (model, category), line 1 {accuracy, correct_count, total_count} and then one record per FAILED entry (id,
valid=false, error text = the state-mismatch or response-mismatch OUTPUT, model_result_decoded, possible_answer,
inference_log); passes are the complement. Result files carry the decoded call sequence and the step count per turn; NO
finish_reason token exists in the archive (survey (c) PART), so the termination proxy is bfcl_term_v1 = any turn's step count
>= 20 -> CAP_HIT; an entry absent from the result file or carrying a harness/API error -> ERROR; else TERMINATED. Both are
classes in the denominator. family_id = the base scenario index N (the four augmentations of one base scenario share the
stem), asserted wholly on one side; the stem = the scenario dialogue + the tool schema (the alternative, tool-schema-only
stems, is NOT registered here and would be a separate registration; survey §2(3)).
Agents: >= 3 required by the rule; the pilot targets 8 (night schedule decision 5; the survey's (f) threshold): the candidate
list is claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-FC, gpt-5.2-2025-12-11, gemini-2.5-flash, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp-FC, Qwen_Qwen3-32B-FC,
grok-4-1-fast-reasoning-FC, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-FC, xLAM-2-70b, the exact list being the author's to confirm; the pilot
file records the list actually ingested, and a pilot with any >= 3 of them is valid under this registration. An agent
directory missing any of the four multi_turn score or result files is recorded and excluded from the pilot (not silently
dropped: the count is printed). Agent identity = (harness "BFCL 2025-12-16", model directory name); the same model name in
another date folder is another agent.
Hygiene. Network only; no LLM call of any kind; no DB of record is opened (the ingest script imports no pool_guard and never
opens mmlu_pro_dataset_cache_v2.db, snapshots.db, embeddings_cache.db or any verdict cache; it may therefore run while the
night construction chain holds the pool). Raw files downloaded to experiment_results/agent/raw/bfcl_result_2025-12-16/ with
the archive commit sha and per-file sha256 in a provenance table; ingested into a NEW experiment_results/agent/
bfcl_result_2025-12-16.db (tasks, episodes, checker, provenance), whose gitignore status is checked with git check-ignore -v
before writing (.gitignore is never edited; if the path is not ignored the operator stops and reports). Pass/fail vector =
all 200 ids of the category minus the score file's listed failures, asserted equal to line 1's total_count / correct_count
per (agent, category); a mismatch refuses the file. The split under (a) is computed and asserted per row on the tasks
table (side per family; straddling families = 0 asserted) and the EVAL-side id list is exported write-once as
experiment_configs/reserved_pool_frozen_bfcl_<id>.json with its id printed; no tree is built, nothing is induced, nothing is
routed. The 50-row hand-labelled reproduction subset is drawn by seed 42, stratified over the 4 categories, and hand-read by
the operator BEFORE the pilot's D_c is printed (the labels file is written first and named in the pilot file).
Instrument (the pilot). 300 episodes drawn question-stratified: 75 per category, each category's 75 spread as evenly as the
agent count allows over the ingested agents (seed 42; the draw's (task, agent) list written beside the pilot); per stratum
(category) and pooled: strict D_c = (TERMINATED and checker-decided) / all drawn episodes with a Wilson 95% interval;
cap-hit share and ERROR share per agent over the drawn episodes and, DESCRIPTIVELY, over the agent's full 800 (registrar's
addition: the full-table D_c per category x agent is printed beside the pilot so the pilot's interval can be checked against
the population it was drawn from; the full-table numbers are not scored); the 50-row reproduction = share of the 50 on which
the script's (pass/fail, termination class) equals the hand label. Every checker verdict is BFCL's own (state-based /
response-based); this pilot re-checks nothing.
Readouts and criteria (each scored HELD / FAILED; denominators named):
 (C1) parts (a)-(e) verified by command on the ingested tables: (a) side asserted per row, 0 straddling families, pool file
      written; (b) the checker table with its sha and the header reading rule; (c) bfcl_term_v1 classes with counts per agent
      per category, denominator = the agent's 800; (d) the artefact (decoded call sequence + final-state text where present)
      with its token count per episode, the per-episode cap DECLARED in the pilot file (a number the author sets before the
      item-19 probe; the pilot only prints the length distribution), fingerprint / provider / response id UNSTAMPED (the
      archive carries none); (e) stratum = (BFCL, category), 4 strata, 200 tasks each. A part that cannot be verified is
      FAILED and the corpus is not admitted as-is.
 (C2) strict D_c per stratum with Wilson intervals on the 300-episode pilot, and pooled; PASS-AT-POINT (>= 0.95 at the point)
      or PREDICTIVE-ONLY per stratum.
 (C3) cap-hit share per agent (drawn episodes; denominator = the agent's drawn count) and ERROR share.
 (C4) the 50-row reproduction >= 0.98 (49 of 50 or better).
Predictions (the lead's, judge_loop2.md §2, recorded blind; labelled): P1 strict D_c < 0.95 at the point in at least 2 of
the 4 strata, long_context the lowest; P2 (the plan A10 figure, by analogy with MATH's CHECKER-ANSWER-INGEST 12-19%
cap-hit rows): the median agent's cap-hit share on its full 800 lies in [0.12, 0.19]; P3 judged cells PREDICTIVE-ONLY on day
one in at least one stratum (implied by P1); P4 checker-built rows publishable on terminated episodes in all 4 strata
(terminated share >= 0.60 per stratum). Registrar's blind addition: C4 HELD (the archive's pass list is machine-written, so
the reproduction should be near 1.0; a failure there is an ingest bug, not a corpus property).
Falsifier (of the admission test itself, as drafted). A corpus that passes (a)-(e) and the pilot and whose FIRST judged
pilot is refused by the truncation guard (> 5% unparsed or non-terminated on the deciding subset), or whose full-run strict
D_c falls below 0.95 in a stratum that passed the pilot: the pilot was not predictive, and the test is amended (pilot size,
stratification) by insertion before any further spend. It overturns the rule set's claim that a 300-episode pilot at
0.95-at-point predicts judgeability; it does not overturn any BFCL number. UNDETERMINED is an outcome: a stratum with
fewer than 120 EVAL-side tasks is admitted for description only.
Cost and consequence. 0 LLM calls; network (score files tens of MB, result files ~200 MB for 8 agents); the ingest and pilot
run in minutes. Writes experiment_results/agent/bfcl_admission_pilot.txt once (+ bfcl_admission_pilot_draw.csv, the 300
(task, agent) rows; bfcl_admission_pilot_labels.csv, the 50 hand labels). Consequence if C1-C4 HELD and a stratum PASSES
at the point: that stratum may receive the item-19 probe (50 calls per judge, a separate launch) and then a first judged
pilot <= 4,000 matches under STACK-v2 rubric-less mechanics (the GEN-ARENA / STAGE3 family; the rubric line stays closed);
a full calibration board at the x12 shape (~9,000 matches, ~20,000 cce) crosses the 4,000-match rule and needs the author's
go (plan C7). Strata under 0.95 carry checker-built rows on terminated episodes only. Nothing judged is scheduled by this
registration.
Closed lines not touched: no rubric (rubric text at every granularity closed; the judged pilot, if any, is rubric-less by
the corpus having none); no specification reference (GEN-ARENA); no gating, ensemble, confidence or two-reference variant;
no trajectory reference (the checker OUTPUT is the reference state); no judge temperature; no sub-anchor row; no order
inside a frontier band. Nothing in CONTEXT §5 is reopened; this is a new corpus class with a new object (the episode), not
a variant of a closed line. Ledger and programme grepped for the id: 0 / 0 before this section.
Prior results this registration touches, with their ledger ids: CHECKER-ANSWER-INGEST (three readings of one table; 12-19%

## Registered 2026-09-18 (before any code or call) — MODEL-VINTAGE-CANARY: when may a row still be called by a contestant's name? a DEFINITION of contestant drift and a null-first alarm rule (zero judge calls; contestant generation is the author's cost and is NOT launched by this registration; plan A9; lead docs/agents/leads/2026-09-17_judge_loop2.md §1)
Question. The record tests drift only for the judge (CANARY-BASELINE, arm A; FRAMEWORK guard 19 "the existing canary sees
judge drift only", L245) and the reference (arm B, never run); nothing covers a CONTESTANT whose name is constant and whose
weights or serving stack change. Every verdict of record was posted on FROZEN answer text (eval_results.model_output), so a
drifting model changes no existing verdict; what it changes is whether a row may still be called by that model's name.
This registration defines when it may not, and the null that must be read before any alarm fires. Nothing runs under it:
a first pass is a separate launch on the author's decision (contestant generation cost), and the definition is scorable
only from the files that pass would write.
Definition (the rule). Model drift = ANSWER-CONTENT drift on the canary question set: the 279 distinct questions of the
CANARY-BASELINE set (hash 50af669ac6997f9f, 300 matches / 279 qids / 12 x12-roster models; NOT the 300 matches, because the
object is per model: every roster model is regenerated on all 279, n_m = 279 per model, 278 for iask_pro). For roster
model m: vintage v0 = the cached eval_results rows; vintage v1 = a fresh generation under a RECORDED protocol P = (harness
prompt bytes, sampling setting as an explicit literal or an explicit "omitted", max_tokens, provider, deployment
fingerprint, extractor version); agreement a_m = share of the 279 on which extract(v1) == extract(v0). The extractor is one
versioned function (extract-v1) applied to BOTH the cached model_output and the new output; BEFORE any generation it must
reproduce the cached pred column at >= 0.99 per model (zero-cost pre-check; if it does not, the extractor, not the model,
is the object: the CHECKER-ANSWER-INGEST lesson of three readings of one table).
[CORRECTED 2026-09-22 by the pre-run READY, before the outcome is written (MODEL-VINTAGE-CANARY precheck; docs/reviews/READY_model_vintage_precheck.md, e685fbf, registration inconsistency 1): "reproduce the cached pred column" carries no blank rule in the registration. The registered reading of C1 is STRICT: extract-v1(model_output) == pred per row with both-blank = agree, blank on one side = disagree, differing letters = disagree; the denominator is the 279 canary questions per model (278 iask_pro), no row excluded. The committed-rows agreement (a letter on both sides) is printed beside it as DESCRIPTIVE only and is never used for C1. The instrument (tools/analysis/model_vintage_canary.py, LF sha bedbbdaefdfb8a954e6b6d944f98ed05b1cabf5b2a8137cdd16507e823581115, extract-v1 b9782bef338e4815) scores exactly this reading.]
Null, read FIRST on fixed checkpoints (the REF-SC analogue; the null-first rule). Seven roster models are published
weights and therefore fixed checkpoints: Llama-2-7b-hf, Llama-2-13b-hf, Meta-Llama-3_1-8B, Meta-Llama-3_1-70B-Instruct,
Qwen1.5-72B-Chat, Yi-6b-Chat, c4ai-command-r-v01. Two floors are read on them under P, per model and pooled:
  F_gen = agreement between two generations of the same checkpoint under P (the sampling floor; the TEMP-0 analogue: for
          the judge, temperature 0 left 82% of responses different in wording and the flip rate unchanged, 0.050 vs 0.057,
          so a greedy setting is expected to raise F_gen for open weights but is not assumed to reach 1.0);
  F_cache = agreement between v1 and the cached v0 of the same checkpoint (the harness + extractor + sampling floor: the
          cached vintage's harness is not on record, eval_results carrying no generation provenance, so F_cache bounds what
          "agreement with the cached vintage" can mean for ANY model, including the API ones).
The alarm floor is F = pooled F_cache over the fixed checkpoints (question-weighted), with its per-model spread. If the
per-model F_cache spread exceeds 3 SE of the pooled value, the null is UNDETERMINED and NO alarm fires this pass (a
registered outcome), because the cached rows were then not produced under one harness. No alarm is ever read against
REF-SC's 0.94 directly: that is a two-prompt figure for a different object (two solves of the reference model), quoted
here only to fix the arithmetic of the rule.
[CORRECTED 2026-09-22 by the pre-run READY, before the outcome is written (MODEL-VINTAGE-CANARY precheck; docs/reviews/READY_model_vintage_precheck.md, e685fbf, registration inconsistency 2): the sentences above assume ONE harness behind the cached pred column, to be detected at C2 by the spread test. The reviewer's zero-call recomputation (NOT of record until --precheck --run writes model_vintage_extractor_check.txt; recorded here so that the expectation is on record ahead of the file) shows at least THREE submitter harnesses behind pred: tier-1-only with a blank on a tier-1 miss for the five local checkpoints (Llama-2-7b-hf, Llama-2-13b-hf, Qwen1.5-72B-Chat, Yi-6b-Chat, c4ai-command-r-v01; tier-1-only reproduces all five at 1.0000 over the full 12k-row table); a constant "G" stored on letterless repetition loops for the Llama-3.1 pair (Meta-Llama-3_1-8B, Meta-Llama-3_1-70B-Instruct; 21 / 21 canary disagreements are pred G / extract blank); the three-tier extractor for the API models (deepseek-chat-v2_5, gemini-3.1-pro_5-shots, gpt-4o-2024-08-06, iask_pro at 1.0000; arx_0314 277 / 279 = 0.9928 with a 2-row residual). Under the strict reading of C1 the expectation is therefore ~5 of 12 models at >= 0.99 (the reviewer's figures: 0.9677, 0.9606, 0.9785, 0.9462, 0.8674, 0.9247, 0.9928, 0.9355, 1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000, 1.0000), i.e. C1 FAILED under the registered 12 of 12 AND under the registrar's >= 10 of 12; no single versioned function can reach either bar (maximum 7 of 12 tier-1-only, 5 of 12 three-tier). This is the registration's own "the extractor, not the model, is the object" branch, not an instrument defect, and the amendment it anticipates ("amended by insertion before generation") CANNOT be a new regex. It is one of two, chosen by the AUTHOR before any generation (--ingest refuses until the choice is registered by insertion): (a) a per-model harness_id stamp on v0, the registration's own forward-only field (Consequence paragraph below: vintage_id, harness_id, sampling, max_tokens, fingerprint, extractor_version) applied to the legacy rows, with C1 and F_cache scored PER HARNESS (extract-v1 fixed, the harness named per model); or (b) C1 re-defined on committed rows (a letter on both sides; three-tier gives 12 of 12 with arx_0314 277 / 279 = 0.9928), which is a criterion SUBSTITUTION (review_session_2026-09-14 C-7) and is recorded SUBSTITUTED beside the strict figure, never as "C1 HELD". The drift statistic a_m = extract(v1) == extract(v0) uses ONE extractor on both sides and never reads pred: C1's failure leaves its arithmetic intact; what it says is that vintage v0 as extract-v1 reads it differs from the board's pred on 2-13% of rows for 7 models, which is what C2's spread test was registered to catch. The outcome file records "C1 as registered: FAILED / registrar's addition: FAILED" as printed; any committed-rows figure quoted as a pass is flagged SUBSTITUTED.] [CORRECTED 2026-09-22 by the author's decision (registrar, insertion only): the author chose option (a), "Go with option (a) for MODEL-VINTAGE"; the per-model harness_id stamp on v0 with C1 and F_cache scored per harness is registered as its own section "Registered 2026-09-22 (before any code or call) — MODEL-VINTAGE-CANARY amendment (a)" at the end of this file (harness families H-tier1-blank / H-constantG / H-threetier fixed there before the stamp run; option (b) not taken); the precheck outcome section precedes it.]
Alarm rule. Model m alarms iff a_m < F - 3 x sqrt(F(1-F)/n_m). At F = 0.94, n = 279 the threshold is 0.897 (SE 0.0142,
3 SE = 4.3pp); at F = 0.90 it is 0.846. One-sided; read per model; never pooled across models. Secondary, DESCRIPTIVE, never
the alarm: the accuracy delta of m on the 279 keyed questions (exact two-sided McNemar v1 vs v0, integer arithmetic), which
separates directional drift (accuracy moved) from re-sampling (accuracy flat); per-anchor agreement printed (14 anchors x
~20 questions) as description only, never a row.
Consequence (FRAMEWORK guard 12 extended by insertion to contestant vintages, in the outcome commit, not now). A model
below the alarm is a NEW VINTAGE m@v1: it re-enters through the online-operation path as a new model (keyed cells 0 calls;
~800 cce to a band, ~3,100 cce for profile coverage, NEWCOMER-PLACEMENT-LIVE / FRAMEWORK L189); its v0 rows stay published
under the v0 label with the answer-table hash; v0 and v1 verdicts never share a fit. A model above the alarm keeps its rows
and gets the stamp "vintage v0 confirmed at a_m on 279 q, pass k". Every eval_results row used by a board carries,
forward-only, (model_name, vintage_id = sha of the model's answer column, harness_id, sampling, max_tokens, fingerprint,
extractor_version); legacy rows get vintage_id only, the other fields UNSTAMPED (the FRAMEWORK L37 pattern for the
reference cache).
Hygiene. EVAL side only (the 279 are pool p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae questions; `pool_guard.py --pool p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae` is the
first printed line of every script under this id); the canary set is loaded from experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/
canary_set.json and hash-verified (50af669ac6997f9f), never re-frozen; mmlu_pro_dataset_cache_v2.db opened mode=ro (a pool
reader: never while a construction or a site null runs); the reference is NOT re-minted by this arm (that is arm B / plan
C2); NO judge call is posted (a_m is computed at ingest); Meta-Llama-3-70B-Instruct excluded (asserted absent); the
contestant sampling setting RECORDED per generation (the D2 analogue); output cap recorded; finish_reason recorded, and a
capped generation is NON_TERMINATED, neither an agreement nor a disagreement (kept in the denominator print, excluded from
a_m's numerator and denominator, refused above 5% per model: rule 10); provider content-filter refusals cached as unusable
rows, never re-posted (rule 10). New generations are written to a NEW cache experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/
model_vintage_v1.db, never into eval_results.
Instrument (what a pass would run, in order; none of it runs under this registration). (0) extract-v1 pre-check on the
cached rows, 0 cost: tools/analysis/model_vintage_canary.py --precheck -> experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/
model_vintage_extractor_check.txt (per-model reproduction of pred on the 279; C1). (1) Null pass: two generations per fixed
checkpoint under P (the author hosts or rents; 7 models x 279 x 2); F_gen and F_cache per model and pooled with the spread
test (C2). (2) Roster pass: one generation per remaining roster model under P (5 API models x 279); a_m with a Wilson
interval, the alarm decision per model (C3), the McNemar accuracy delta beside it (C4). (3) Outcome file, write-once from
a complete cache: experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/model_vintage_canary_pass1.txt.
Readouts and criteria (each scored HELD / FAILED; denominators named: the 279 canary questions per model, 278 iask_pro,
minus NON_TERMINATED rows printed per model):
 (C1) extract-v1 reproduces the cached pred at >= 0.99 per model on the 279 (12 of 12 models). [CORRECTED 2026-09-22 by MODEL-VINTAGE-CANARY amendment (a) (registrar, insertion only; the precheck outcome: 5 of 12, FAILED as registered and under the >= 10 of 12 addition): C1 is re-scored PER HARNESS as C1-H in the amendment section at the end of this file (HELD iff every model reproduces at >= 0.99 under its own family's extractor variant, memberships fixed before the run); this 12-of-12 one-extractor figure stays FAILED of record beside it.]
 (C2) F_gen and F_cache read on >= 5 of the 7 fixed checkpoints with per-model F_cache spread inside 3 SE of the pooled

## Registered 2026-09-18 (before any code or call) — CAP-PRUNE: does a capability rule that survives as a held-out-replicating PRUNE keep only the trunk? capability gate would be an additive second admission rule". The checker's null and held-out columns are recorded in the

that must REPLICATE out of sample as a PRUNE (keep a site iff its gain beats its own train-side null AND is positive
held-out) keeps only the trunk, so the "different sites" the gate accepts are small, deep sites whose gains do not

 SOLVE STAGE (reasoning calls, no judge): every eligible question with >= 1 key-decidable x12 MAIN match on the four
 anchors (461 by the conservative regex; <= 600 by the script's final regex, count printed by --dry-run), one PoT
 solve each, executed, scored against the key; the incumbent's letter and correctness on the SAME questions from
 grok-reasoning.db. Pilot 12 solves first (finish_reason, execution status, degenerate share).
 JUDGED STAGE, decided by the solve stage at zero further reads of any verdict: stratum DIFF = key-decidable eligible
 matches whose PoT letter differs from the incumbent's OR where PoT yields no letter (the only matches whose two
 prompts differ; DECOMP's logic: in stratum SAME the prompts are byte-identical and any arm difference is
 test-retest noise). Both arms judge every DIFF match (expected 100-300 matches) plus a SAME-stratum floor sample of
 200 matches drawn with seed 42 (in-session test-retest AND, on the control arm, the byte-identity check against
 GROK-CALIB's cached verdict). Cap 800 matches; if DIFF exceeds 600 it is subsampled to 600 with seed 42 and the
 subsampling is printed. Arms interleaved in one session; 4 calls per match.
 CELL AGGREGATE: A_P(cell) - A_C(cell) = sum over DIFF of (P - C) / kd_eligible(cell), SAME contributing its measured
 discordance as the floor; convention A (TIE / INVALID / NON_TERMINATED wrong) and B (committed only) both reported;
 wrong(established) per cell by systematic_budget.mcnemar_edge on the cell's JUDGED questions.

INSTRUMENT AND HYGIENE. Split: every artefact is derived from the judged question alone at judgment time (rule 1);
nothing reads TRAIN; no other reserved question is read; the PoT cache is a new vintage on <= 600 questions, NOT the
reference of record, and no board is refit from it. Solves and judge calls both through rr.call_judge_full (rule 9)
with the solve process setting rr.JUDGE_MODEL = "grok-4-1-fast-reasoning" and rr.MAX_TOKENS = 4,096 (the incumbent's
cap, judge_solve_map.call default) in its own process and own cache; the judge process posts the unchanged body (cap
8,192); any local body copy asserts against rr.payload_body's source. Control-arm payload SHAs are asserted equal per
match to experiment_results/judge_wiring/board/payload_shas_python.csv (both orders) - the session-floor arm is
provably the cached bytes. Pilot 12 judged matches read by the truncation guard (refuse above 5% unparsed on the
deciding subset); NON_TERMINATED never a verdict, never a tie; a content-filter 400 cached as unusable, never
re-posted, kept in the guard denominator. Dry-run at zero calls prints the pool id first, the eligible count, the
DIFF / SAME sizes once the solve cache exists, and the exact bill. --analyze refuses a cache short of the schedule.

note and is the author's to accept before the pilot.

READOUTS. (R1) Solve stage, per cell and pooled, on the eligible questions: PoT yield; status table (picked /
no_pick / blocked / timeout / error / degenerate / content_filter / length); PoT reference-correct among yielded and
under the deployment reading (no-yield = wrong); the incumbent's on the same questions; fix (incumbent wrong -> PoT

comparator. (R2) Leakage on the reference itself, no judge call: per-contestant answer agreement of the PoT letter
vs the incumbent's letter on the eligible questions (REF-QUAL gate (3)'s table, all 12 contestants, gemini named);
(R3) Judged: A and B per cell and pooled under the deployment and fallback readings; the DIFF stratum split into
fixed (control wrong -> PoT right), broken (right -> wrong), both-wrong-different, no-yield, each with arm P minus
control and a question-clustered bootstrap CI (B = 1,000, seed 42); the SAME-floor discordance; the control-arm vs
GROK-CALIB discordance on the same matches (the session floor); wrong(established) per cell; the CONSENSUS-FIT
KEY / REF signed-contrast logistic on arm P's verdicts beside the control's (the leakage coefficient), and
per-contestant agreement of arm P's verdicts. (R4) Descriptive: gains by TOPIC-DIFFICULTY tercile.

CRITERIA (scored explicitly HELD / FAILED).
 C1 (the form is a lever on the REFERENCE): PoT reference-correct among YIELDED eligible questions exceeds the
     incumbent's on the same questions by >= 2pp pooled, fix : break by exact McNemar p < 0.05.
 C2 (the judge transcribes it): on the FIXED matches, arm P minus control (convention A) >= +0.40, question-clustered
     CI excluding 0; on the BROKEN matches the mirror <= -0.40 (the symmetric check; a one-sided transcriber is a
     finding, not a pass).
 C3 (a cell gain that could ship): pooled QUANT4 deployment-reading gain >= the session floor (the control-vs-cache
     discordance converted to an accuracy SE on the deciding set) AND >= +1.0pp with CI excluding 0, under BOTH
     conventions. Per-cell C3 on Math / Physics / Chemistry only; Engineering descriptive.
PREDICTIONS (numbers). Solve stage: yield 0.80-0.92 of eligible; degenerate programs <= 5%; PoT reference-correct
among yielded Math 0.95-0.98, Physics 0.92-0.96, Chemistry 0.88-0.93, Engineering 0.80-0.88; fix rate on
incumbent-wrong eligible questions 0.25-0.40 (against CoT's 0.12), break rate 0.01-0.03; pooled among-yielded
gain +1 to +3pp (C1 HELD at the low edge); deployment reading (no-yield wrong) -3 to +2pp. Judged: fixed-match gain
+0.45 to +0.65 and broken-match loss -0.45 to -0.65 (ORACLE's +0.573 stratum, the cell identity 0.905 / 0.309: C2
HELD); no-yield matches -0.08 to -0.14 (PAIR-NOREF's 0.738 vs 0.849); SAME-floor discordance 4-8% and control-vs-cache
4-8% (DECOMP 5.7%); pooled QUANT4 deployment-reading gain -1.5 to +1.5pp (C3 FAILED, inside the floor: the expected
outcome), fallback reading +0.5 to +1.5pp; Engineering the only cell with a point gain above +2pp, UNDETERMINED by
support; gemini agreement of the PoT letter within +-3pp of the incumbent's (the reference is the same model; the
coupling REF-QUAL-KIMI-JSON recorded applies in proportion to the accuracy gain).
FALSIFIER, and what each overturns.
 F1: C1 FAILED - PoT is not more often right (or yields too little). The form is not a lever on this corpus's
     quantitative side: the incumbent's residual errors are not execution errors, and the reframing's "+3-5pp where
     reference correctness rises" has no application on MMLU-Pro's quantitative cells. The line closes at the solve
     bill (no judge call is made: the judged stage is conditional on C1).
 F2: C1 HELD and C2 FAILED - a more-often-right reference in the unchanged wrapper does not move the judge. The
     transcriber model fails: this would overturn ORACLE's stratum reading (+0.573 wrong -> key) and CONSENSUS-FIT's
     REF dominance, and is the outcome worth the money.
 F3: C1 and C2 HELD, C3 FAILED - the lever exists and is bounded by the reference-wrong share (7.8% of eligible
     matches here): the paper's sentence is the BOUND (ceiling +3.4pp on MMLU-Pro's quantitative side), and the form
     lever is priced for corpora where the incumbent is weak (TOPIC-DIFFICULTY's hard stratum at 77.7%
     reference-correct), not adopted here.
 UNDETERMINED is a registered outcome for every cell below support and for C3 if the guard refuses the deciding set.
BILL. Solve stage: <= 600 reasoning solves x 10 cce = <= 6,000 cce (expected 461-560 solves, 4,600-5,600 cce), plus
12 pilot solves inside that count; local execution is free. Judged stage, conditional on C1: (DIFF + 200 SAME) matches
x 2 arms x 2 orders = expected 1,200-2,000 judge calls, cap 800 matches = 3,200 calls. Total expected ~6,500-7,500
cce, maximum ~9,200 cce; no single run crosses the 4,000-match rule; the go is the author's (the judged block
precedent). Pilot: 12 solves, then 12 judged matches under the truncation guard, then the run, then --analyze.
WHAT IT DOES NOT REOPEN. Reference ensembles, gating on agreement, confidence, two-reference variants (ENSEMBLE-REF,
J2-D, REF-CONF, ABSTAIN): one reference per question, chosen by a property of the question fixed before any call,
never by an answer; the fallback reading is post hoc, flagged, never an arm. Checklists / rubric-shaped references

### Engineering note for the chosen form (what must exist before the dry-run; engine-coder in a worktree, reviewer READY at zero calls)

1. tools/analysis/pot_runner.py (~120 lines, no network, no DB, selftest at import time or `--selftest`).
   - Input: the model's program text, the question's option list. Prelude prepended by the runner: `OPTIONS = [...]`
     (the option strings), `pick(value, rel_tol=0.02)` (parses the first number of every option incl. unit-stripped
     scientific notation, chooses the nearest option by relative distance if unique within rel_tol, prints
     `ANSWER: <letter>`; ties or no parse -> prints `ANSWER: NONE`), `pick_text(s)` (exact / case-folded match of a
     string against the options). The letter of record is what the program PRINTS; nothing the model writes in prose
     is parsed.
   - Static guard BEFORE execution (a refused program = status blocked, no reference): any of `import os`, `sys`,
     `subprocess`, `socket`, `shutil`, `pathlib`, `urllib`, `http`, `requests`, `ctypes`, `importlib`, `multiprocessing`,
     `threading`, `signal`, and the tokens `open(`, `exec(`, `eval(`, `__import__`, `input(`, `__builtins__`,
     `globals(`, `compile(`. Allowed imports: math, cmath, fractions, decimal, itertools, functools, statistics, re,
     numpy, sympy, scipy (numpy 1.26.3 / sympy 1.12 / scipy 1.14.1 are installed under the project's Python 3.11.1).
   - Execution: `[sys.executable, "-I", "-S", "-E", "-B", path]`, cwd = a fresh directory under the session scratchpad
     (never ROOT: `.env` with the API keys lives there), env = {SystemRoot, PATH to the interpreter's directory only},
     stdin DEVNULL, wall-clock 10 s then kill (status timeout), stdout capped at 8 kB, stderr kept (status error on a
     non-zero exit). Degenerate detection (status degenerate, no reference): the program contains no call to pick /
     pick_text, or prints a letter without any arithmetic operator or numeric literal beyond the OPTIONS list.
   - HAZARD, to be accepted by the author before the pilot: Windows offers no seccomp; the blocklist is textual and can
     in principle be evaded (encoded strings, attribute tricks). Mitigations are -I -S -E (no site, no PYTHON* env, no
     user site-packages), an empty environment, a scratch cwd, the 10 s kill, and the blocklist. The alternative that
     removes the hazard is a container runner (`docker run --rm --network none --read-only --memory 512m` on a
     python:3.11 image with numpy/sympy/scipy, ~40 more lines, needs Docker or WSL on the machine); the specialist
     recommends it if Docker is available, and the blocklist runner with the hazard disclosed if not. Either runner
     must pass the same 6-case selftest (correct pick, no pick, blocked import, timeout, exception, degenerate).

2. tools/analysis/pot_ref.py (~250 lines): the solve stage. Population = eligible quantitative questions with >= 1
   key-decidable x12 MAIN match (rule and regex printed by --dry-run with the count; pool id printed first).
   Solve prompt (the protocol of record for this vintage, stored in the cache's meta table): system = "Solve the
   multiple-choice problem by writing ONE self-contained Python 3 program ... compute the answer numerically in the
   units of the options, then call pick(value) (or pick_text(s) for a non-numeric answer) as the LAST statement; do
   not print a letter yourself; allowed imports: ..."; user = the incumbent's user_prompt(qtext, opts) byte for byte.
   Call: rr.call_judge_full with rr.PROVIDER azure, rr.JUDGE_MODEL grok-4-1-fast-reasoning, rr.MAX_TOKENS 4,096 (the
   incumbent's; asserted in the script against judge_solve_map.call's default), temperature omitted; the body asserted
   against rr.payload_body's source text. Cache experiment_results/judge_solve/grok-reasoning-pot.db: table `answers`
   with the incumbent's exact schema (question_id, answer, gt, correct, raw, tokens, latency, ts; answer '' on no
   yield so rejudge_reference.references() drops it and the judge stage falls to the no-reference form without any
   new code path) plus `pot_detail` (question_id, code, stdout, stderr, exit_code, wall, status, finish_reason,
   response_id). `--dry-run` (0 calls), `--pilot 12`, `--run`, `--report` (R1, R2, C1 scored; writes
   pot_ref_outcome.txt only from a complete cache; refuses if content_filter + length exceed 5% of the population).

3. tools/analysis/refform_cell.py (~300 lines): the judged stage. Strata builder from the two solve caches on x12
   MAIN's key-decidable eligible quantitative matches (grok_calib.db for the match list and the cached control
   verdicts); seed-42 draws; two arms interleaved; per arm `rref.set_reference("grok-reasoning" | "grok-reasoning-pot")`
   and exactly stack_judge's `one()` construction (system_for(anchor), rj.build_user_prompt, rr.call_judge_full,
   rj.parse_judge, rj.combine_orders; NON_TERMINATED / content_filter recorded from finish_reason and never a verdict);
   control-arm payload SHA asserted per match against payload_shas_python.csv (both orders) before posting; cache
   experiment_results/x12_crossdomain/refform_cell.db (verdicts with arm, finish1/2, tok1/2, rid1/2, sha1/2, stratum);
   `--dry-run` prints DIFF / SAME sizes and the bill; `--pilot 12` writes refform_cell_PILOT.txt read by the guard;
   `--analyze` refuses a partial cache and writes R3 / R4, C2 / C3 scored, both conventions, wrong(established)
   (systematic_budget.mcnemar_edge), the CONSENSUS-FIT fit on arm P (consensus_fit's match-level logistic), and the
   per-contestant agreement table.

4. Not needed: any change to stack_judge.py, rejudge_reference.py (with_reference untouched), prompt_v2.py, the Kotlin
   path, or any DB of record. The suite is unaffected (Python only); the two new scripts carry `--selftest`.

## Registered 2026-09-18 (before any code or call) — JUDGE-BY-CELL: is there any cell in which one cheap judge beats another by more than the test-retest floor, stably across draws? (zero calls; the MODEL form of the specialised-judge hypothesis)

QUESTION. The second open form of the author's hypothesis: not the prompt (closed) and not the reference (REF-FORM-
BY-CELL above), but the judge MODEL chosen per cell. RECIPE-GROK found the recipe, not the judge, carries the gain
(STACK-v2 on Mistral 0.865 / top cluster 0.699 vs grok 0.864 / 0.722 on R3's 944 key-decidable; JUDGE-2x2: judge
competence irrelevant once the reference is fixed). That is an aggregate statement; nobody has read it per cell. If
one judge family beats the other in some cell by more than the floor and the winner is stable across two draws of
the same judge on identical bytes, a per-cell judge choice is a lever; if every per-cell difference is inside the
floor or its sign does not replicate, judge routing is CLOSED at zero calls.

INSTRUMENT (tools/analysis/judge_by_cell.py, zero calls, refuses a cache short of 9,123 / 9,142 / 9,142 rows). For
each of the 14 anchors and for the three pairings (M vs GP, M vs GK, GP vs GK):
 (i)  paired key-decidable accuracy difference under convention A (TIE / INVALID / NON_TERMINATED wrong) and B
      (committed verdicts only, the pair's both-committed matches), with a question-clustered bootstrap 95% CI
      (B = 1,000, seed 42, resampling questions within the anchor) and the exact McNemar on the discordant matches
      beside it; wrong(established) per anchor per judge by systematic_budget.mcnemar_edge on the anchor's judged
      questions; decidable tie rate and flip rate per judge per anchor (the decisiveness readout, since STACK-NORUBRIC
      showed judge differences can be decisiveness, not discrimination).
 (ii) the BAR: |delta| > 0.057 (DECOMP's test-retest floor, applied as registered by the lead; conservative, since
      5.7% is a verdict-discordance rate and an accuracy gap at n ~ 300 kd matches has SE ~ 2.5pp) AND the CI
      excluding 0, under BOTH conventions. The EMPIRICAL floor per anchor is the GP vs GK difference (the identical
      judge on identical bytes): printed beside every M-vs-grok difference, with its 14-cell max.
 (iii) STABILITY: for each anchor, the sign of (M - GP) and (M - GK); a cell "winner" exists only if both grok draws
      agree on the sign and both clear the bar.
 (iv) THE LEVER TEST, cross-fitted: split the key-decidable questions of each anchor in half by question (seed 42,
      100 random splits); choose the per-cell judge on half A (M or grok, by convention-A accuracy), read the routed
      accuracy on half B, against the best SINGLE judge chosen on half A; report the mean cross-fitted gain with its
      interval over the splits. The in-sample routed gain is printed beside it as the optimism bound.
 (v)  Overall: M vs GP and M vs GK key-decidable A and B on the common set, the aggregate the cells sit under.

CRITERIA. C1 (a cell winner exists): at least one anchor clears (ii) against BOTH grok draws with the same sign
(iii). C2 (routing is a lever): the cross-fitted routed gain (iv) > 0 with the interval over splits excluding 0 and
the point >= +1.0pp. C3 (the grok-vs-grok floor): the 14-cell max |GP - GK| under convention A <= 0.057 (if a single
judge's two draws differ by more than the bar in some cell, the bar cannot separate judges there and that cell is
UNDETERMINED for C1 whatever M reads). VERDICT RULE fixed now: judge routing is a lever only if C1 AND C2 hold; if
C1 fails, or C1 holds on a cell where C3 fails, or C2 fails, judge routing is CLOSED at zero calls and the record's
sentence is "the judge model is interchangeable per cell to within the floor".
PREDICTIONS (numbers). Overall M vs GP |delta| <= 1.5pp under A and <= 1.0pp under B (RECIPE-GROK 0.865 vs 0.864 on
R3; GROK-CALIB A 0.848 / B 0.916; Kotlin A 0.852 / B 0.917; the Mistral x12all figure is the ARENA-V2 cache and is
expected 0.845-0.860 on this denominator). Per anchor: no anchor clears the bar under both conventions against both
grok draws (C1 FAILED); the 14-cell max of |M - grok| 4-7pp on the smallest anchors (Business, Philosophy, History,
~140-200 kd matches each) with CIs including 0; the same-judge max |GP - GK| 2-5pp (C3 HELD); cross-fitted routed
gain -1.0 to +0.5pp with an interval including 0 (C2 FAILED); in-sample routed gain +1 to +2pp (the optimism of
choosing on the data read). Decisiveness: Mistral's decidable tie rate lower than grok's in every anchor by 1-3pp
(STACK-v2 5.6% vs GROK-CALIB / Kotlin 6.9%), the one systematic per-cell difference, and it is decisiveness.

~3% of the committed verdict under this recipe. Decisiveness is the residual per-cell difference and it does not
follow the registered direction (P7).

      status on >= 95% of MSWE-agent episodes (denominator: every (instance, MSWE-agent agent) episode with a report.json);

      any count: exit status in the submitted class -> TERMINATED; in the cap class (max steps / iterations, cost or

      FRAMEWORK L236 guard 10); trajectory missing or a harness / API error -> ERROR; a status string outside the map ->
      UNKNOWN, counted as not recovered toward C2 and printed. The class map from status strings is written into the
      script and the checker header BEFORE --build, from the --dry-run enumeration; it is not re-drawn after the D_c count.
      HELD iff recovered >= 0.95.

MDE / power at the measured floor beyond the recomputation above (the file's literal is at 0.057); anything about the
reference vintage (arm B, ARM-B-VINTAGE NO ALARM) or the contestants (MODEL-VINTAGE-CANARY).

## Registered 2026-09-22 (before any code or call) — TOPIC-PARTITION-20NG: on a corpus with ground-truth topic labels the construction has never seen (20 Newsgroups, 20 labels under 7 groups), does the anchor-free recipe of record build and certify, partition the embedding space better than k-means / Ward / HDBSCAN at the same number of parts, and identify topics at its certified sites? (zero judge calls; 1 ingest + 1 smoke build + 2 constructions + 2 site nulls [+ 1 contingency pair]; embeddings local; plan Amendment 8)

AUTHOR'S SENTENCE (2026-09-22, in chat): "Start an agent to work on the construction, maybe using another dataset to
see how my framework could benefit to partitioning of the embedding space and topic identification." This answers plan
2026-09-18 §5 question 2 (does the anchor-free line continue past R1 / R2?) in one direction: it continues on a NEW
corpus as a construction study; it does not reopen any MMLU-Pro lever.

QUESTION. Every tree in the record was built on question corpora whose labels are exam categories (MMLU-Pro 14; union
52 strata), and every partition readout is a held-out category purity against those labels (ANCHOR-FREE C1 0.715 free
vs 0.757 anchored; REDRAW 4.3 pp clean gap). [REGISTRAR 2026-09-22 at registration, insertion only: the record's table
at L4316 reads leaf-level held-out purity 0.715 [0.700, 0.730] free vs 0.779 [0.764, 0.792] anchored (o0); 0.757 is
o0's DEPTH-1 cell purity (14 cells; the free tree's depth-1 reads 0.188 over 2 cells). The lead's number stands as
written; no criterion or prediction reads it.] No row of the record compares the taxonomy to an unconstrained
clustering of the same vectors, and no row reads certification against a label HIERARCHY. Three claims the record has
not tested:
  Q1 (partition): at the same number of parts, the certified taxonomy partitions the embedding space no better than
    k-means (F1). The record's own reading (plan 2026-09-18 L23-25; FW L179-180; FW L53) is that the tree earns its
    place through the split discipline, the support per cell and the certificate, not through partition quality; Q1
    tests whether that modesty is forced.
  Q2 (topics): certification selects the topic-aligned sites (the certified split at a node aligns with the label
    hierarchy more than an uncertified split at a comparable depth), and the depth-1 split is a coarse-group split
    (the analogue of the quantitative / discursive sites of MMLU-Pro). The record's current reading of the certificate
    is geometric ("more than this node's own elongation", separation_null_by_size.md L322-333; CAP-GATE / CAP-PRUNE:
    certificate and capability content select nearly independently); Q2 asks whether it is topic-informative on a
    corpus with discrete topics.
  Q3 (transfer): the recipe of record carries to a new corpus without re-tuning: the flat bar 0.025 at the 256-dim
    slice builds a tree with more than 20 leaves and certifies the root and at least one depth-1 site; and the
    FRAMEWORK per-corpus pair (512-dim slice, bar 0.0145; FW L51-53; anchor-free twin = ANCHOR-FREE-CERT arm 4
    af_bareq512: 92 leaves / 87 sites / 10 certified on MMLU-Pro) builds as well. separation_null_by_size.md L20-23
    says the bar 0.025 "is unchanged"; that sentence was made on MMLU-Pro at one N and one slice.

CORPUS (the lead's decision; the author wrote "prefer 20 Newsgroups"). 20 Newsgroups, bydate, subset='all',
sklearn.datasets.fetch_20newsgroups(subset='all', remove=('headers','footers','quotes'), shuffle=False): 18,846
documents, 20 labels (628 talk.religion.misc .. 999 rec.sport.hockey) under 7 top-level groups comp (5 labels, 4,891
docs) / rec (4; 3,979) / sci (4; 3,952) / talk (4; 3,253) / soc.religion.christian (997) / misc.forsale (975) /
alt.atheism (799). Why: (a) the engine already carries DatasetType.TWENTY_NEWSGROUPS with table twenty_newsgroups
(MMLUDatasetFetcher.kt L152-159; CorpusRegistry.kt L79); (b) a known two-level topic hierarchy with known overlaps
(the religion triad, the comp.* quintet, the politics triad): the ceiling is documented, not discovered; (c) no LLM
cost: the only fetch is sklearn's 20news-bydate.tar.gz (~14 MB), DECLARED HERE as the one network fetch of this study,
performed once by the engine-coder during the ingest's development into the sklearn data home and reused by the chain
(the COST-AXES-INGEST defect-2 pattern, an undeclared builder-side fetch, is thereby avoided). Not chosen: arXiv
abstracts (no local copy; a download of its own); ag_news (2,000 rows / 4 topics: too coarse for Q2; used only as the
zero-download smoke below); the multi-corpus union (already built and read; not redone).

INSTRUMENT.
  I0 Ingest (tools/ingest/twenty_newsgroups_ingest.py; Python; --fetch, --dry-run, --selftest on a synthetic
    mini-corpus, --manifest). Writes a SEPARATE root-level dataset DB `twenty_newsgroups_cache_v1.db` (gitignored by
    .gitignore L58 `*.db`; NOT under experiment_results/, whose *.db are re-included by L145), never
    mmlu_pro_dataset_cache_v2.db (data-steward H1: the built-in loader joins any corpus table to eval_question_link by
    local rowid, MMLUDatasetFetcher.kt L498-506, so a 20NG row in the DB of record would inherit an MMLU-Pro eval id).
    Design N (namespaced): twenty_newsgroups(id = ingest order, question = body.strip(), category = the raw 20-label
    string as sklearn target_names gives it, cot_content = '', options = '[]', answer = category) +
    eval_question_link(question_id = k >= 1, mmlu_pro_row_id = rowid, question_text, has_embedding 0) +
    corpus_questions(question_id = 8,000,000 + k, text) so that the split records a real pool in the separate DB,
    `pool_guard.py --pool <id>` verifies it (via a `--db` argument, inert when absent, or a registry entry), and the
    [POOL-PIN] / TRAIN-ONLY-at-save guards run (data-steward H2/H3; TWENTY_NEWSGROUPS offset 8,000,000,
    CorpusRegistry.kt L90/L109). Ingest rules, fixed now because they change the corpus the seed splits: (1) text =
    stripped body; (2) drop any document whose norm-v1 text (split_side.norm: NFKC, case-fold, whitespace runs to one
    space) is shorter than 100 characters; (3) drop ALL copies of any norm-v1 collision (cross-posts and duplicates,
    label-agreeing or not); (4) no NUL bytes; (5) the table must hold >= 2,000 rows (the engine's HF fallback
    short-circuit, MMLUDatasetFetcher.kt L961); the ingest asserts it; (6) the manifest prints the counts (raw 18,846;
    dropped short; dropped duplicate; kept; per label) and sha256 over `SELECT id, question, category ORDER BY id`;
    (7) leak count: documents whose body contains any of the 20 label strings (kept; a sensitivity row in the
    readout). Zero-collision preflight (read-only) after ingest: exact and norm-v1 matches of 20NG texts against
    embeddings_cache.db (embeddings.query, queries.raw_text), mmlu_pro.question and multicorpus corpus_questions.text
    must be 0 (the chain refuses otherwise).

  I2 T1 = the recipe of record of the clean free tree R1 af_clean_s42 (K-SELECTION bracket: "R1 af_clean_s42 remains
    the clean free tree of record"): experiment_configs/topic_partition/ng_af_s42.toml =
    experiment_configs/anchorfree/redraw/af_clean_s42.toml with EXACTLY these differences: datasetType =
    "TWENTY_NEWSGROUPS"; corpusDbPath = "twenty_newsgroups_cache_v1.db"; outputDir =

  I5 Site null: `gradlew siteNull` (build.gradle.kts L184-202; SeparationNullBySizeTest siteNull arm) at 300 reps,

    the arm's dag_snapshots.jsonl (last snapshot) and snapshots.db mode=ro&immutable=1 (leaf queryIds,

      a cell centroid (anchor_free_readout.py route L154-157) for the tree's leaves (unit vmfMu), k-means
      (renormalised cluster_centers_), Ward (renormalised train-member mean), HDBSCAN (non-noise member mean); purity

      (sklearn arithmetic) and ARI at 20 labels and at 7 groups. Baselines on TRAIN vectors only: KMeans(n_clusters =
      L = the tree's leaf count, n_init 10, seeds 0-4); reference rows k = 20 and k = 7 (5 seeds);
      AgglomerativeClustering(ward, n_clusters = L); sklearn.cluster.HDBSCAN(min_cluster_size 55) with its own k and
      its train noise fraction; random partition = the tree's held-out cell assignment with labels permuted (5 seeds)
      = the chance floor at the tree's cell-size profile; one sensitivity row k-means at k = L on the FULL 4096-d
      vectors. Seed spread = max - min over the 5 k-means seeds; paired comparator = k-means seed 0; interval = 1,000
      held-out bootstrap resamples with the partitions FIXED (no refit), percentile CI on NMI(20)_tree -
      NMI(20)_kmeans0, ARI difference beside. Per cell: held-out support (median; cells < 30), cells with no held-out
      arrival.
    Q2 (denominator = the site's TRAIN members; site = internal node with >= 2 children; member set = union of
      descendant leaves' queryIds; a doc under two children goes to the child of higher cosine; leaf slots vs distinct
      ids printed): per site NMI_20 and NMI_7 of the child partition vs the labels on the site's members, label
      entropy H_20 (sites with H = 0 printed, not dropped), per child majority group / label and share; depth-1
      children: majority 7-group and share; migration matrix 7-group x depth-1 cell (train and held-out); depth-d cuts
      d = 1..8 (partition into the deepest nodes at depth <= d) -> NMI_7, NMI_20 per depth and the argmax depth for
      the 7 groups; per label the node of any depth with max Jaccard(member set, label set on TRAIN) -> depth, J, n;
      median best depth and median best J (20 labels; 7 groups); per leaf max Jaccard to a label and the share of
      leaves at J >= 0.5. Certification vs alignment: Y_s = NMI_20(s); (i) raw certified - uncertified mean gap
      (confounded by size and depth: record medians 620 vs 248); (ii) depth-stratified gap, strata {0-1, 2, 3, 4, >=
      5}, weighted by min(n_cert, n_uncert) per stratum; (iii) OLS Y ~ cert + log n + depth with HC1 SE; (iv)
      one-sided permutation p over 1,000 permutations of the certified flag WITHIN depth strata (direction
      pre-declared: certified higher). All at 20 labels and at 7 groups. Sensitivity rows: excluding leak documents
      (rule 7); documents > 8,000 chars (Ollama truncates long inputs silently: no numCtx on the embedding model,
      ArcLLMProvider.kt L86-110).
    Q3: built (guard did not fire) and leaf count (> 7; > 20); root and depth-1 observed k-way separations and
      refused-k rows from proposals.csv; root / depth-1 p95 and margins beside R1's (root 0.042461 / 0.037214 / 1.141;
      discursive 0.059496 / 0.028375 / 2.097; quantitative 0.025148 / 0.033733 / 0.746) and K-SELECTION R1' n00000004
      (0.056502 / 0.033471 / 1.688); certified share vs R1's 14 of 69 = 20.3% with the per-draw band 10-16 of 64-69,
      and by site-size band (record base rates over the four free draws: n < 200 3/66; 200-400 11/103; 400-800 14/52;
      >= 800 24/47), with the stated caveat that p95 falls with n, so a larger corpus certifies more easily and the
      share is not like-for-like; depth-blocked leaves (depth 8, n >= 110); iterations to stop; the deflated
      certificate column printed as a diagnostic, never as the certificate.

CRITERIA (scored HELD / FAILED / UNDETERMINED explicitly; the arm of record for C1-C3 is T1; T1b is scored beside on
C3 and REPORTED on C1-C2).

FALSIFIERS.
  F1 (C1 FAILED): the taxonomy's held-out NMI is not above k-means's at the same k by more than the seed spread.
    Leaves standing FW L53 / L179-180 and plan L23-25 ("the tree earns its place through routing, question support and
    the split"); overturns any reading that the certified taxonomy is a better flat partition of the embedding space
    than an unconstrained clustering at the same k. F1' (tree below k-means by > 0.05 NMI with the CI excluding 0):
    the size floor and the greedy top-down cuts cost partition quality, a limitation to print in the construction
    chapter.
  F2 (C2 FAILED): certification does not select topic-aligned nodes once depth is held fixed. Overturns "the
    certificate is topic-informative"; the geometric reading of the certificate (elongation beyond the node's own
    null; CAP-GATE / CAP-PRUNE independence) extends from capability content to topic content. C2 HELD gives the
    record a sentence it does not have.
  F3 (C3 FAILED): the recipe of record does not build on 20NG at bar 0.025. Overturns the transfer of the flat bar;
    separation_null_by_size.md L20-23 narrows to "unchanged for MMLU-Pro at this slice and N"; the isotropic floor did
    not move (it is dimension- and n-dependent, not corpus-dependent); the corpus's within-node geometry is less
    separated. T2 then measures whether the bar-equalised rule restores a build.

VERDICT RULE (the only sentences of record). With C3 HELD and C1 FAILED: "On a corpus with known topics the
anchor-free recipe of record builds and certifies, and partitions the embedding space no better than k-means at the
same number of parts; its value on this corpus is the split discipline, the support per cell and the certificate, not
the partition." With C1 HELD: "... partitions the embedding space better than k-means at the same number of parts by
<delta> NMI [CI]", printed with the k = 20 reference row beside so that the number is read against the label count,
not only the leaf count. C2 HELD: "the certificate is topic-informative on a corpus with discrete topics (stratified
gap <g>, p <p>)"; C2 FAILED: "the certificate reads geometry, not topic boundaries, on this corpus". C3 PARTIAL /
FAILED sentences as in F3. T1b adds one clause: "the per-corpus pair (512 / 0.0145) builds / does not build on this
corpus".

WHAT THE STUDY CANNOT SHOW (ceilings, stated now). (1) Nothing about capability: 20NG has no models, keys or eval
rows; ANCHOR-FREE's C3 (key-only Brier) and every profile reading have no analogue; no arena, no board, no judge. (2)
Embedding-model dependence: one model (qwen3-embedding, 4096-d, sliced); the nomic/gemma caches hold MMLU-Pro texts
only. (3) The bar's size dependence: one N per arm; p95 falls with n, so certification at 13k train is easier than at
8.1k and the certified-share comparison with the record is descriptive. (4) The 20-topic ceiling: the religion triad,
the comp.* quintet and the politics triad overlap in any embedding; k-means at k = 20 on comparable sentence
embeddings reads NMI ~0.5-0.65 in the literature; the absolute numbers are bounded by the corpus and only the same-k
contrasts are the test. (5) Header stripping removes the Subject line (topic signal lost) and leaves quoting stubs;
long posts are truncated by Ollama's default context; both are shared by every method and change absolute levels, not
the contrasts. (6) One seed / one split: no re-draw; leaf count and certified fringe are per-draw objects (REDRAW); a
re-draw arm is not registered.

## Registered 2026-09-23 (before any code or call) — IFEVAL-RESPONSE-ORACLE: with an EXECUTED per-response constraint-checker vector attached to each trace, does the IFEval judge's INDECISION collapse (COULD-NOT-VERIFY) or persist (WOULD-NOT-COMMIT)? (judged; 1,628 calls under plan Amendment 9; a decisiveness-and-obedience instrument, NEVER a rung of the reference ladder)
Question. GEN-ARENA's IFEval cell failed as much by REFUSING TO COMMIT as by being wrong: key-decidable accuracy 0.658,
decidable ties 0.256, flips 0.380, against MATH's 0.935 / 0.055 / 0.237 (docs/multi_corpus_design.md, the GEN-ARENA
result of 2026-09-13). Two hypotheses the record cannot separate: COULD-NOT-VERIFY (the judge failed to count the
constraints itself, so doing the counting for it collapses the ties and the flips) against WOULD-NOT-COMMIT (the
failure is abstention and order instability of the kind DECOMP and the position line describe, so ties and flips barely
move even when accuracy jumps). THIS TEST SEPARATES THEM, and it asks nothing else. THE NAME IS NOT
"CHECKER-OUTPUT" BY RULING: the IFEVAL RULING of 2026-09-23 (docs/agents/leads/2026-09-23_ifeval_ruling.md, af116f8,
judge-design-specialist, zero calls) establishes that IFEval HAS NO QUESTION-LEVEL CHECKER OUTPUT to give - MATH's
verifier emits a canonical answer string that exists before any response, IFEval's emits a PREDICATE ON A RESPONSE
(prompt_level_strict_acc = all(inst_level_strict_acc), the identity asserted row by row at tools/analysis/
checker_answer_ingest.py L513 / L528) - so what this test attaches is a PER-RESPONSE ORACLE, an ORACLE-CLASS object
stronger than ORACLE's question-level key, and the ladder's IFEval rung STAYS AT SPECIFICATION 0.658 PERMANENTLY
whatever this test reads. That ruling's structural finding is recorded by insertion at the GEN-ARENA result, in
FRAMEWORK's stage-1 lines and at the programme's three ladder statements (2026-09-23, commit of that bracket batch).
FORBIDDEN BY THIS REGISTRATION, IN THE OUTCOME, THE LEDGER, THE THESIS AND THE BLOG: any sentence that places this
test's accuracy beside MATH's 0.958 or on the reference ladder, for TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS - (1) the reference objects
are not the same kind (question-level canonical answer vs per-response predicate), and (2) no IFEval cap-hit proxy
exists, so the populations differ: checker_answers_v2.db is MATH-ONLY, v1's `non_terminated` column is the

Instrument (the ruling's section (6) is the instrument, and this paragraph is it). TWO ARMS, INTERLEAVED MATCH BY MATCH
IN THE SAME SESSION, on the same 407 matches: CONTROL = the GEN-ARENA IFEval prompt reproduced BYTE-IDENTICALLY (same
system string, tools/analysis/generative_arena.py L35; same per-source rubric string, L39 - IF THAT STRING IS REWORDED
THE ARM BECOMES A RUBRIC-TEXT ARM AND IS REFUSED ON THAT GROUND ALONE; same question-appended
"[Constraints the response must satisfy]" block, L100-L112). TREATMENT = the same prompt PLUS a per-response oracle
block attached to EACH TRACE. THE BLOCK, VERBATIM SHAPE:
      [Instruction checker output for this response - produced by executed checker code, not by a model]
      - punctuation:no_comma - PASS
      - detectable_format:number_highlighted_sections (num_highlights: 3) - FAIL
      - length_constraints:number_words (relation: at least, num_words: 300) - PASS
one line per entry of `instruction_ids` IN THE CHECKER'S OWN ORDER; the constraint id verbatim; its NON-NULL `kwargs`
slots in parentheses, in the stored order, `key: value`; an em-dash; PASS or FAIL from the corresponding element of
`strict_vector`. NO aggregate line, NO "3 of 3", NO `all_pass_strict`, NO overall verdict, NO loose fields, NO
comparison between the two responses, and NO instruction to the judge about what to do with the block beyond the
existing system and rubric strings. The header names the producer and says it is EXECUTED CODE, and it deliberately
does NOT reuse the STACK-v2 solve wrapper "[Reference solution - produced independently, may be wrong]"
(tools/analysis/rejudge_reference.py L83-L85), which would be a false label here.
THE ORDER HAZARD, THE LOAD-BEARING IMPLEMENTATION CLAUSE. GEN-ARENA's reference is appended to the QUESTION
(generative_arena.py L112: `q = text + reference(source, target)`) and is ORDER-INVARIANT; a per-response block is not.
The assembler must build the two user prompts from the pair (trace, vector) and re-derive the A/B labelling FROM THE
ORDER ACTUALLY POSTED. A transposition here produces swapped vectors in the second order and an artefact
indistinguishable from a catastrophic position effect. REQUIRED DRY-RUN ASSERTION, PRINTED: for a sample match, the
vector shown for Model A in order 1 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the vector shown for Model B in order 2, and vice versa.
CONVENTIONS AND GUARD: cap 8192; TEMPERATURE OMITTED (plan Amendment 1 D2); judge grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning; DUAL
ORDER, TIE ON FLIP; INVALID on parse failure or `finish_reason` length; every call through
rejudge_reasoning.call_judge_full, any local body copy asserted against rejudge_reasoning.payload_body; confidence
requested, NEVER gated. BOTH TIE CONVENTIONS ALWAYS (A: ties / INVALID / non-terminated counted wrong; B: committed
verdicts only); no accuracy is ever quoted without its convention. NON_TERMINATED is never a verdict and never a tie
(rule 10): rows whose contestant trace is `non_terminated` in checker_answers_v1.db (the unclosed-`<think>` proxy, the
ONLY proxy IFEval has) are excluded from the deciding subset and the count is printed. GUARD: --dry-run at zero calls
printing the population line, both assembled orders for one match and the transposition assertion; then a 12-MATCH
PILOT IN BOTH ARMS, INTERLEAVED (48 calls, inside the count), read by the truncation guard, REFUSING above 5% unparsed
on the deciding subset; --analyze exits non-zero on a partial cache and writes no REGISTERED line while the cache is
short of the schedule. WHY 838 CALLS IS REFUSED: the cheaper form compares a fresh treatment arm against a cache
written on 2026-09-13, ten days and an unmeasured amount of provider drift ago, and the two headline readouts (tie
rate, flip rate) are precisely the soft quantities drift moves; the GEN-ARENA cache is therefore used ONLY as a DRIFT
READOUT (control-vs-cache agreement on the same matches) and NEVER as the comparator of record. The 100-match control
is also declined: at 100 matches the drift estimate's own SE is ~6.7pp, larger than the floor it would certify.
Readouts and criteria (numbered, scored HELD / FAILED / UNDETERMINED; denominators named):
 (C1) THE OBEDIENCE FLOOR (GEN-ARENA's criterion 1, RENAMED BY THE RULING: it is no longer verification fidelity). The
      share of key-decidable matches on which the judge commits to the contestant that a correct, per-response
      reference names; denominator = the 407 key-decidable IFEval matches less the NON_TERMINATED exclusions (the
      deciding subset, printed). Bar 0.85, both conventions, with the question-clustered interval over the 162
      questions. Its complement is the DISOBEDIENCE RATE, a number the record has on no corpus, and it bounds the
      judge's irreducible error under the strongest reference that can exist. HELD iff >= 0.85 under convention A.
 (C2) DECISIVENESS, PAIRED ON THE SAME MATCHES (the reason to run at all). The DECIDABLE TIE RATE, control vs
      treatment, exact McNemar on the discordant pairs; denominator = the deciding subset, the same matches in both
      arms. SCOREABLE ONLY AT |delta| >= 10pp (the power paragraph below): a smaller move is recorded UNDETERMINED by
      support, never as "no change". HELD iff the tie rate falls by >= 10pp with McNemar p < 0.05 (COULD-NOT-VERIFY).
 (C3) THE FLIP RATE, same pairing, same denominator, same McNemar treatment and the same 10pp scoreability floor.
 (C4) NON_TERMINATED ACCOUNTING per rule 10: the excluded rows counted and printed per contestant over the 407, with
      the RECORDED LIMIT that IFEval's only proxy is the unclosed-`<think>` one (no cl100k cap-hit proxy exists for
      this corpus, checker_answers_v2.db being MATH-only; harness cap 1,280).
 (C5) THE LEAKAGE READOUT, PRINTED, NO BAR: per-contestant agreement - the share of committed verdicts that follow the
      all-pass contestant, per model and pooled, beside every accuracy; plus the DRIFT readout (control-vs-cache
      agreement on the same matches, denominator the deciding subset).
DECLARED NOT SCORED, BEFORE THE RUN, AND WHY (each for two independent reasons; nothing in the outcome may quote them):
 - GEN-ARENA CRITERION 2 (per-corpus board Spearman rho >= 0.85): (i) VACUOUS - under a per-response vector the judged
   board is a noisy transcription of the key board, so rho measures obedience, not recovery of a key ordering; (ii)
   NOT COMPUTABLE - this schedule judges only the 407 key-decidable matches, while the GEN-ARENA IFEval board was
   fitted on all 1,200, and a BT fit on a correctness-selected subset is a biased board.
 - GEN-ARENA CRITERION 3, THE BRIDGE (judged argmax == key argmax): vacuous for the same reason, not computable for the
   same reason, AND CLOSED ON THE MERITS - ORACLE established that a perfect reference buys 16.4pp and still misses the
   frontier order, and CONTEXT section 5 closes the frontier order (FRONTIER, AGGREGATE, ORACLE). The IFEval bridge
   broke at a judged top-two gap of 0.040 logits, the third independent appearance of the frontier near-tie.
 - THE EXPLORATORY ROUTER-COST READOUT (IFEval -0.6pp +- 3.8): not scored, same mechanism.
 - CONSENSUS-FIT's KEY / REF SIGNED-CONTRAST LOGISTIC: NOT ESTIMABLE here - the reference and the key coincide by
   construction, the two regressors are collinear and no REF coefficient exists. The standing strata-by-reference-
   correctness requirement is met by REPORTING THAT THE REFERENCE-WRONG STRATUM IS EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION, which is
   itself the reason this arm says nothing whatever about the reference ceiling.
POWER OF RECORD (fixed before the run; the ruling's section 4). 407 matches over 162 distinct reserved questions
(~2.5 decidable matches per question); the record's design-effect rule is a median 2.0x and worst 3.7x understatement
of match-level SEs, so n_eff = 204 (worst case 110). Single-arm question-clustered SE 3.3pp at A = 0.658 and 1.8pp at
A = 0.93. Paired difference SE = sqrt(d / n_eff): 2.2pp at discordance 0.10, 3.1pp at 0.20, 3.8pp at 0.30. MDE at 80%
power, two-sided 0.05 (2.80 x SE): 6.2 / 8.8 / 10.7pp, and 8.5 / 12.0 / 14.7pp at DEFF 3.7. CAN SETTLE: the accuracy
move an oracle reference should produce (0.658 -> 0.88-0.96, +22 to +30pp), a tie-rate collapse of the size
COULD-NOT-VERIFY predicts (0.256 -> under 0.10, about -16pp), a flip-rate move of comparable size. CANNOT SETTLE:
anything at or near the 5.7pp judge test-retest floor (DECOMP) - a 5pp tie-rate change is indistinguishable from
session noise here; any per-model or per-constraint-family breakdown; any board, rho or argmax claim; anything about
the 793 non-decidable matches; anything about the reference ceiling. A NULL ON DECISIVENESS IS REPORTABLE ONLY AS "the
tie rate did not move by more than about 9pp", NEVER AS "the tie rate did not move".

Falsifier. IF THE TIE RATE DOES NOT FALL BY MORE THAN THE MDE WHILE ACCURACY RISES ABOVE 0.88, the IFEval failure is
WOULD-NOT-COMMIT: the abstention and order-instability line owns it, NO REFERENCE OF ANY STRENGTH REPAIRS THE RUNG, and
GEN-ARENA finding 2's reading of the IFEval cell ("the judge abstains or flips rather than counting constraints",
implying that counting for it would fix the cell) is overturned as a mechanism while its numbers stand. The converse
outcome (ties and flips collapse) confirms COULD-NOT-VERIFY and bounds what a checker can buy on a
constraint-satisfaction corpus - and STILL does not create a ladder rung (section 1 of the ruling). UNDETERMINED is a
registered outcome: any move below 10pp on C2 / C3 is UNDETERMINED BY SUPPORT, and a control arm outside P4's bands
makes the session, not the treatment, the finding.

WHAT THIS RUN DOES NOT SHOW (the lead's registered ceilings (1)-(6), re-affirmed by the reviewer, plus his (7)-(12); all twelve are of record).
(1) Nothing about CAPABILITY: no models, keys, eval rows, arena, board or judge on 20NG; ANCHOR-FREE's key-only Brier has no analogue here.
(2) ONE EMBEDDING MODEL (qwen3-embedding, 4096-d, sliced to 256 on T1 / 512 on T1b).
(3) The BAR'S SIZE DEPENDENCE IS UNCONTROLLED: p95 falls with n, so an 11.8k train side certifies more easily than MMLU-Pro's 8.1k and the 16/101 against 14/69 comparison is DESCRIPTIVE, not like-for-like.
(4) The 20-TOPIC CEILING: the religion triad, the comp.* quintet and the politics triad overlap in any embedding, so absolute levels are corpus-bound and only the SAME-k contrasts are the test.
(5) Header stripping and Ollama's silent truncation of long inputs (306 kept documents above 8,000 chars) move absolute levels for EVERY method.
(6) ONE SEED, ONE SPLIT, NO RE-DRAW.
(7) "CERTIFICATION SELECTS TOPIC-ALIGNED NODES" DOES NOT SURVIVE A SIZE CONTROL: C2 is HELD at its registered bar, but the estimate rests on 11 effective site-pairs, one stratum supplies 6, two strata read negative, and an added size stratification takes p to 0.13. The record may say the certificate IS topic-informative on this corpus AT THE REGISTERED INSTRUMENT; it may NOT say the effect is established, robust, or independent of site size.
(8) NOTHING ABOUT THE CERTIFICATE ON THE 512 / 0.0145 RECIPE: T1b built but never certified; the whole Q2 question is unanswered for the per-corpus pair.
(9) THE DEPTH CURVE, THE JACCARDS AND THE PER-SITE NMIs ARE TRAIN-SIDE; only Q1's purity/NMI/ARI and the depth-1 purities are held-out. No statement about generalisation of the depth structure is supported.
(10) NOTHING ABOUT ROUTING, SUPPORT OR THE SPLIT DISCIPLINE AS VALUES: the verdict sentence's clause is the registered CONTRAST to the partition claim, not a measured finding; the only support figure here is descriptive (median held-out support 40 per leaf; 23 of 110 leaves below 30).
(11) HDBSCAN IS NOT A FAIR THIRD BASELINE ON THIS CORPUS: at mcs = 55 it labels 92.7% of TRAIN as noise and returns k = 3, so its NMI20 0.2407 says almost nothing about density clustering's ceiling here. "THE TAXONOMY BEATS HDBSCAN" MUST NOT BE WRITTEN.
(12) NOTHING ABOUT A SECOND DRAW: leaf count, certified fringe and the depth of the NMI peak are per-draw objects (REDRAW); this run has no re-draw arm.

The QUALIFIED POSITIVE is thin and never travels without its bracket: the certificate is topic-informative at the registered instrument (gap 0.0740, p 0.0480), on 11 effective site-pairs, not size-controlled. ## Standing defect recorded 2026-09-23 (insertion only; zero calls; nothing above is rewritten) — TOPIC-PARTITION-20NG: pre-run bracket (e)'s four UNDETERMINED conditions are NOT IMPLEMENTED in the C2 criterion, and implementing them is a SCORING change that needs a registrar ruling before the next run of this instrument

WHAT WAS FOUND, AND BY WHOM. The engine-coder, while closing post-run review defect D1 (the numpy-bool identity dispatch; fix merged at 74208e8), found the same class of gap one layer up, in the criterion itself rather than in the printer.

THE DEFECT. Pre-run bracket (e) (programme L10841-L10862, 8949550; the research-lead's decision on the registrar's open reading 1) rules that C2 reads UNDETERMINED, and F2 does NOT fire, when the comparison has no support: (i) fewer than 2 certified sites on the arm, OR (ii) fewer than 2 uncertified sites, OR (iii) the total depth-stratum weight sum(min(n_cert, n_uncert)) over {0-1, 2, 3, 4, >= 5} = 0, OR (iv) the permutation distribution is degenerate (fewer than 2 distinct values over the 1,000 within-stratum permutations). NONE OF THOSE FOUR CONDITIONS IS IMPLEMENTED IN THE CODE. tools/analysis/topic_partition.py decides C2 at a single expression (the stratified gap is not None and > 0, the permutation p is not None and < 0.05, and the OLS cert coefficient > 0) and takes its UNDETERMINED path only when the arm is not built or has no complete site null. On any draw that hits (i)-(iv) the readout would therefore print C2 FAILED and F2 WOULD FIRE on an instrument that measured nothing — a FALSE FALSIFICATION of "the certificate is topic-informative", which is exactly the outcome bracket (e) was written to prevent.

WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT TOUCH. NO RECORDED NUMBER MOVES. All four conditions were FALSE on the 2026-09-23 draw of record (16 certified sites, 85 uncertified, total stratum weight 11, a non-degenerate permutation distribution), the reviewer verified exactly that when he confirmed C2's HELD/FAILED path was the right one, and the outcome section at L11425-L11509 and ledger row TOPIC-PARTITION-20NG (v122) stand unchanged. The defect is about the NEXT draw, not this one.

THE DECISION IT NEEDS, AND WHO MAY MAKE IT. Implementing bracket (e) is a SCORING CHANGE: it changes when C2 takes UNDETERMINED rather than FAILED, and therefore when F2 fires. It is NOT a coder's judgement and NOT an editorial fix.
