## Registrar's ruling 2026-09-23 (amendment by insertion; zero calls; nothing above is rewritten, nothing recorded moves) — TOPIC-PARTITION-20NG bracket (e) is ADOPTED AS ALREADY REGISTERED: making the code print UNDETERMINED where the registration already says UNDETERMINED is CONFORMANCE, not a new scoring decision; only the MECHANICS are ruled here, (a)-(e)

THE RULING, AND WHY IT IS NOT A NEW SCORING CHOICE. Pre-run bracket (e) (programme L10841-L10862, 8949550) is REGISTERED TEXT: C2 reads UNDETERMINED, and F2 does NOT fire, when the comparison has no contrast to read — (i) fewer than 2 certified sites, (ii) fewer than 2 uncertified sites, (iii) total depth-stratum weight sum(min(n_cert, n_uncert)) = 0, or (iv) a degenerate permutation distribution (fewer than 2 distinct values over the 1,000 within-stratum permutations). The standing defect recorded at L11511-L11524 is that the CODE never implemented it and would instead print C2 FAILED and fire F2 on an empty instrument. Making the code do what the registration already says is CONFORMANCE. The scoring rule does not change: it is applied as written, for the first time. What genuinely needed deciding was only the mechanics, and they are ruled as follows and registered by this insertion.

(a) EVALUATION ORDER. The four no-contrast conditions are evaluated BEFORE the verdict expression. A draw with no contrast can never reach `strat > 0 and p < 0.05 and beta[1] > 0`; the verdict expression is only ever evaluated on a draw that HAS a contrast.

(b) NAMED REASON, WITH ITS COUNT. Each of the four prints its own named reason and the number that fired it: certified n, uncertified n, the total stratum weight, or the permutation's distinct-value count. A reader must be able to tell an EMPTY INSTRUMENT from a MEASURED NULL at a glance, which is exactly what the 2026-09-23 outcome could not have done had the draw gone the other way. Bracket (e)'s own registered sentence ("the instrument had no certified/uncertified contrast to read at matched depth") stays the sentence of record on that path, with the raw certified-minus-uncertified gap and the per-stratum counts still printed beside it.

(c) F2 MAY NOT FIRE ON AN UNDETERMINED C2. A falsifier that fires on an empty instrument is a FALSE FALSIFICATION, and preventing that is the whole point of (e). F2 fires only on a MEASURED null: a computed stratified gap <= 0, or a computed permutation p >= 0.05, with all four no-contrast conditions false. On the UNDETERMINED path F2 is recorded as NOT FIRED, and neither C2 VERDICT-RULE sentence (the HELD one or the FAILED one) is of record.

(d) IT DOES NOT APPLY BACKWARD. The 2026-09-23 draw had all four conditions FALSE (16 certified sites, 85 uncertified, total weight 11, a non-degenerate permutation distribution; the adversarial reviewer verified exactly this when he confirmed the HELD/FAILED path was the right one). The outcome section L11425-L11509, the sentences of record, ledger v122 and its v123 bracket therefore STAND UNCHANGED and NO RECORDED NUMBER MOVES. This ruling is prospective: it binds the next run of this instrument, not any recorded one.

(e) SELFTEST. Each of the four conditions gets ONE selftest assertion, and the pinned count is raised in the same commit: SELFTEST_CHECKS 55 -> 59 (tools/analysis/topic_partition.py L87). Each assertion must check BOTH the NAMED REASON of (b) AND that F2 DID NOT FIRE.

THE CODE CHANGE THIS REGISTERS (engine-coder, zero calls, queue item TP20-C2-CONFORMANCE). Implement (a)-(e) in tools/analysis/topic_partition.py at the point the C2 verdict is decided (today one expression, with tribool() already normalising the result and c2_sentence() already TOTAL over HELD / FAILED / UNDETERMINED with bracket (e)'s wording on the None path — the fix at 74208e8 left exactly the four conditions unimplemented). BYTE-INERTNESS IS PART OF THE DELIVERABLE: on any draw that HAS a contrast the change must be byte-inert, and the coder must PROVE it by showing that the 2026-09-23 inputs still produce an IDENTICAL verdict block (the criterion lines, the falsifier readings and the sentences of record, character for character, apart from the script_sha field). A change that alters one character of that block on the recorded draw is refused.

INSTRUMENT STATUS UNTIL IT LANDS. tools/analysis/topic_partition.py remains NOT READY for any run that could READ C2: the D1 identity bug is fixed (74208e8) and bracket (c)(12)'s assertions landed (32 -> 55), but a run that could hit any of the four no-contrast conditions would still score C2 FAILED and fire F2 against this ruling. A READY on the conformance commit, with the byte-inertness proof and the four new assertions driven, is the gate.

THE T1b ADDENDUM IS EXPLICITLY UNAFFECTED. TOPIC-PARTITION-20NG-T1B-NULL (registered at L11525-L11553) MAY NOT TOUCH C2 at all — it may not pool T1b's sites into it, may not re-run the permutation and may not restate 16 certified / 85 uncertified — so it cannot reach the four conditions and needs neither this ruling nor the conformance commit before it runs. Its own gates are unchanged (an instrument, a READY, one rule-7 window with -DsiteNullHeap=14g and -PnullReps=300).

WHO DECIDED WHAT, AND WHY. The orchestrating research-lead ruled on 2026-09-23, on inspection of the standing defect, that (e) is registered text and its implementation is conformance rather than a new scoring choice, and fixed the mechanics (a)-(e) above; the registrar records it here by insertion in the same session, creates the queue item for the code change and marks the instrument's status. No author authorisation is needed and none is claimed: no money, no judge call, no machine time above the rule-7 window already registered, and no criterion, denominator, prediction or falsifier text is altered — (e) is applied as written.

    available at judgment time - if it were, there would be nothing to judge. The treatment arm is a BOUND, not a
    recipe.

    together by construction, and the run cannot say what fraction of the tie collapse would survive a reference that
    INFORMS WITHOUT DECIDING.

    INADEQUATE for anything near the 5.7pp DECOMP test-retest floor. No stratum, cell, leaf or per-model breakdown is
    supported.

    2026-09-13 cache, ABOVE CANARY-BASELINE's 0.087 retest floor. Harmless against a 25pp effect; IT BARS ANY FUTURE

 7. The NON_TERMINATED path was never exercised (0 of 407) and IFEval has no cap-hit proxy at all, so this run's
    truncation accounting is weaker than MATH's even though it reports 0.
 8. Nothing here touches rubric text, ensembles, gating, confidence, order policy, temperature or the frontier order -

## Registration defect recorded 2026-09-23 (insertion only; zero calls; nothing above is rewritten, no recorded number moves) — BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT: C1 IS OVER-DETERMINED (a FAILED clause and an UNDETERMINED clause both fire on the same data), and the registration span of record is L10965-L11237, not the L10965-L11146 the outcome file and run_meta print

Recorded by the registrar on the post-run review docs/reviews/2026-09-23_bfcl_judged_pilot_post.md (1cda83f, defects D1 and D8). This
section corrects the BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT registration (this file L10965-L11237) BY INSERTION AT THE END OF THE FILE, following the
2026-09-23 precedent of the TOPIC-PARTITION-20NG standing-defect and ruling sections: nothing in the registration is rewritten and no line
number above this point moves.

(A) THE DEFECT. The registration's C1 states, in one sentence, "C1 is HELD iff A under convention A is ABOVE 0.75 by the lower end of its
DEFF-inflated interval; FAILED iff the POINT is <= 0.75 (the falsifier); UNDETERMINED if the interval straddles 0.75, or if the deciding
subset falls below 300 matches once C2's non-judgeable class is removed" (L11093-L11095), and the falsifier paragraph restates the
UNDETERMINED trigger at L11140-L11142. THESE TWO CLAUSES ARE NOT DISJOINT. Any point at or below 0.75 whose interval reaches above 0.75
fires BOTH, and that is exactly what happened: the point is 0.7402 and both intervals contain 0.75 ([0.6590, 0.8132] percentile,
[0.6639, 0.8164] normal). The defect is IN THE REGISTRATION, not in the run.

(B) WHAT WAS RECORDED INSTEAD, AND WHY IT IS A SUBSTITUTION. The outcome file resolved the conflict silently in favour of FAILED by
reading the UNDETERMINED trigger as amendment item (5)(d)'s TWO-INTERVAL-DISAGREEMENT test ("if the two intervals disagree about the 0.75
bar, C1 is UNDETERMINED") and observing that the percentile and normal intervals AGREE. That is a different and narrower criterion:
agreeing about the bar is not the same as lying above or below it. Replacing a registered trigger with a narrower one is CRITERION
SUBSTITUTION (C-7), and the result of record is therefore C1 = FAILED AT THE POINT / UNDETERMINED BY INTERVAL.

(C) THE RULING, WHICH GOVERNS THIS TEST AND EVERY FUTURE TEST THAT INHERITS THIS WORDING. Amendment item (5)(d) governs WHICH INTERVAL IS
OF RECORD (the point +- 1.96 x the clustered-bootstrap SE, with the percentile interval printed beside it) and adds a SECOND, INDEPENDENT
UNDETERMINED trigger for the case where the two forms disagree about the bar. IT DOES NOT NARROW, REPLACE OR REPEAL THE REGISTERED
STRADDLE CLAUSE. A registration that carries a point clause and an interval clause over the same bar MUST BE SCORED ON BOTH, and the
outcome carries both verdicts joined, in the narrative's words: "FAILED AT THE POINT / UNDETERMINED BY INTERVAL". A falsifier's CONSEQUENCE
attaches to the clause that fires it — here the point — so the "for Agents" bridge stays withdrawn as a measured claim on this corpus,
while the falsifier's POSITIVE SENTENCE (a mechanism claim) is struck for the separate reason recorded at D2 in the outcome section above.
FOR FUTURE REGISTRATIONS: a criterion with a bar states, in one place, whether the POINT or the INTERVAL decides it, and if both are
scored it says so; a registration that does not is defective and is scored on every clause it wrote.

(D) THE SPAN OF RECORD. The BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT registration section spans THIS FILE L10965-L11237, comprising the registration proper
(22c5d5f), the BFCL-REF-ORACLE reference ruling at L11001 and the five-item amendment at L11190-L11237 (both 6ccf2f7). The outcome file's
header and the cache's run_meta.registration print L10965-L11146, which EXCLUDES the amendment — including the item (5)(d) the outcome
cites by name. The outcome file is write-once and run_meta is inside a completed cache; THIS SECTION AND THE D8 BRACKET ABOVE ARE THE
CORRECTION OF RECORD. The record file docs/agents/results/BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT.json already carried L10965-L11237 and is unaffected.

      sub-classes counted separately. NO BAR IS SET ON ANY OF THESE, DELIBERATELY: at n = 57 and the pilot's measured DEFF
      3.60, n_eff is about 16 and the MDE at 80% power is about ±0.35 — too coarse for a verdict, and a bar the design
      cannot reach is a bar that manufactures a result. C2 IS HELD IFF (a)-(d) ARE COMPUTED AND PRINTED WITH THEIR
      DENOMINATORS AND INTERVALS; it is FAILED if any of them is omitted or printed without its denominator.
 (C3) THE PAIRED PER-ORDER STATISTIC, COMPUTED AND PRINTED, NO BAR. This is a PAIRED design — the same 200 (mid, arm)
      cells are observed twice — and the paired test of record is THE EXACT TWO-SIDED McNEMAR TEST on the 200 cells for
      the binary outcome "named the FIRST-SHOWN side", with its discordant counts b and c and its exact p printed. WHY
      McNEMAR AND NOT A TWO-PROPORTION TEST: the two passes are on the same cells, so the between-match and between-task
      variance is common to both and cancels; only the DISCORDANT cells carry information, and the exact binomial form is
      the record's own convention for a paired judged comparison (wrong(established) by exact two-sided McNemar,
      CONTEXT.md §3; IFEVAL-RESPONSE-ORACLE's exact McNemar p = 5.42e-26). WHY IT CARRIES NO BAR HERE: the 100 were
      SELECTED on being ties in pass 1, so a McNemar at the MATCH level against pass 1 is degenerate by construction (one
      discordant direction is empty before the run) and any McNemar on this set measures regression to the mean as much as
      instability. The per-ORDER form above escapes the degeneracy (a cell's pass-1 vote is not TIE for 194 of the 200) [CORRECTED 2026-09-23 by the registrar (the READY-WITH-CONDITIONS review docs/reviews/READY_bfcl_flip_reseed.md (fdd6a99)): 154, not 194: the 100 carry 46 TIE votes of 200 (24 + 14 + 2 x 3 + 2 from the flip table), consistent with the pilot's 870 non-tie votes = 916 - 46; no criterion or bar moves.]
      but not the selection, so it is reported as a DIRECTION and never as a verdict. C3 IS HELD IFF b, c and the exact p
      are computed and printed with the 200-cell denominator and the words "selected set, direction not verdict".
 (C4) INSTRUMENT COUNTS AND THE BYTE-IDENTITY GATE, PRINTED, NO BAR EXCEPT WHERE A REFUSAL IS NAMED. (a) THE BYTE-IDENTITY
      GATE: 200 of 200 payload shas equal to the pilot's for the same (mid, arm), and the system prompt hash equal to
      951ec3a0a063b5a8 — ANY SHORTFALL REFUSES THE RUN. SUPPORT AND MDE, STATED BEFORE THE RUN (this paragraph exists because BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT was registered at DEFF ~1.4 and
MEASURED 3.60, and that gap is why its C1 came back underpowered; the registration does not repeat it). EXPECTED SUPPORT:
100 matches over the distinct tasks the dry-run prints (at most 49, and concentrated: 11 of 49 tasks carry 50% or more of
the pilot's ties and 5 tasks carry 32 of the 100). THE PLANNING DEFF IS THE MEASURED 3.60, NOT AN ASSUMPTION, and a
PESSIMISTIC 5.0 is carried beside it. At DEFF 3.60, n_eff = 27.8: SE(R) = 0.095 at R = 0.5, 0.053 at R = 0.913, 0.078 at
R = 0.218, so the MDE at 80% power and alpha 0.05 two-sided is ±0.265 (±0.186 at 50% power). At DEFF 5.0, n_eff = 20.0:
SE(R) = 0.112 at R = 0.5 and the MDE is ±0.313. THE DESIGN IS ADEQUATE FOR THE QUESTION IT ASKS AND FOR NO OTHER: the two
registered anchors are 0.695 apart, which is 2.6 × the MDE at the planning DEFF and 2.2 × at the pessimistic one, so the
clustered interval of R separates 0.913 from 0.218 comfortably — at R = 0.913 it reads about [0.808, 1.000] and at
R = 0.218 about [0.065, 0.371], both far from the bar 0.566. WHAT THE DESIGN CANNOT DO, REGISTERED IN ADVANCE: it cannot
resolve 0.913 from 0.75, nor 0.30 from 0.218, nor any pair closer than about 0.27; it cannot estimate R to better than
about ±0.10 even at the favourable end; and it therefore licenses NO statement of the form "the flips reproduce at X%"
with a tight interval. C1 is a TWO-HYPOTHESIS DISCRIMINATION at a pre-set bar, and the outcome section must say so in
those words.

FALSIFIER. IF R'S TASK-CLUSTERED INTERVAL LIES WHOLLY BELOW 0.566, the reading that the pilot's 100 order-flip ties and
their one-sided (57 / 0) signature are a STABLE PER-MATCH PROPERTY of the deployed recipe on this corpus IS OVERTURNED. In
that case the 0.2183 tie rate is recorded as a MARGINAL rate generated at a noisy decision boundary, the flip SET is not a
stable object, and a standing consequence is adopted by insertion: NO LATER TEST ON THIS CORPUS MAY RE-POST A SELECTED
MATCH SET AND READ THE RESULT AS A PER-MATCH MEASUREMENT (a selected-set re-post would then be measuring regression to the
mean). WHAT THE FALSIFIER DOES NOT OVERTURN, named here so no reader over-reads it: it overturns NO number of
BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT — A = 0.7402, A = 0.9469, the 19 wrong-committed (0.0415), the tie rate 0.2183 and the MARGINAL
first-position rate 0.5862 of 870 non-tie votes (z = 5.09) are all MARGINAL quantities and stand whatever R is; it
overturns no board, no profile, no tier, no rung of the reference ladder and no MMLU-Pro result; it does not overturn
CANARY-BASELINE pass 2's 0.087 floor or DECOMP's 5.7% test-retest floor, which were measured on OTHER corpora and on
UNSELECTED sets and are used here only as anchors. SYMMETRICALLY, C1 HELD overturns nothing either: it establishes that
the flips are reproducible and NOT that position bias (rather than template mis-fit) causes them — a stable effect is
consistent with BOTH, and separating those two is BFCL-FINAL-STATE-SWAP's job, not this one's. UNDETERMINED IS A
REGISTERED OUTCOME HERE and is recorded as such.

WHAT THIS RUN WILL NOT SHOW, REGISTERED BEFORE IT RUNS. (1) It does not observe "a different 100 flipping", because no
match that was DECISIVE in pass 1 is re-posted: a control arm over the 358 committed matches is NOT bought at this budget.
The "different 100" leg is answered INDIRECTLY, through the noise anchor 0.2183, and that inference RESTS ON A STATED
ASSUMPTION — that the corpus's marginal tie rate is itself stable across sessions — which this run cannot check and which
the outcome section must name beside every reading of C1. (2) It says nothing about WHY a flip happens: position bias,
template mis-fit and corpus difficulty all predict reproduction, so C1 HELD does not choose among them. (3) It says nothing
about fidelity: no rung, no ladder, no bar at 0.75, no "for Agents" bridge. (4) It gives no profile cell, no agent ranking,
no per-trajectory and no process claim — 57 EVAL tasks against the 120-question support rule, exactly as the pilot.
(5) It is not a calibration of the judge: 100 selected matches on one corpus.

QUESTION. BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT's outcome section (this file L11772-L11988) records, in the paragraph "THE THIRD HYPOTHESIS,
WHICH THE OUTCOME FILE NEVER NAMES", that the frozen v2 verify-first block — kept verbatim for comparability with
STAGE3-MATH's 0.958 rung — instructs the judge to extract each model's "FINAL ANSWER" and check it against the
reference, which is MMLU-Pro furniture on a tool-call trace THAT HAS NO FINAL ANSWER, ONLY A FINAL STATE. THE QUESTION
IS: DOES THAT MIS-FIT EXPLAIN THE INDECISION? The thing to move is the TIE RATE 0.2183 = 100/458, the highest of any arm
in the record (REF-CHECKLIST's table at L4427-L4432, n = 826: PAIR-NOREF 0.173, CHECKLIST 0.161, REF 0.080, RECIPE-GROK
0.074). This test changes FOUR STRINGS in the inherited block and NOTHING ELSE, re-posts the SAME 458 deciding matches in
BOTH orders, and reads the tie rate as a PAIRED comparison against the pilot's. It measures NO fidelity rung, buys NO
profile cell, and cannot confirm or refute position bias or corpus difficulty.

THE EXACT PROMPT DELTA, BOTH STRINGS QUOTED, FIXED HERE BEFORE ANY CODE. The object is the string returned by
tools/analysis/prompt_v2.v2_system_template() — the INHERITED verify-first block that sits ABOVE the $systemPrompt and
$rubric slots. FOUR LITERAL REPLACEMENTS, IN THIS ORDER, EACH REQUIRED TO MATCH EXACTLY ONCE (the instrument asserts
count == 1 per replacement and count == 4 in total, and REFUSES otherwise):
 (1) FROM: "extract each model's FINAL ANSWER and check it"
     TO:   "extract each model's FINAL STATE and check it"
 (2) FROM: "A response whose final answer is wrong cannot win"
     TO:   "A response whose final state is wrong cannot win"
 (3) FROM: "against a response whose final answer is right, whatever its reasoning looks like."
     TO:   "against a response whose final state is right, whatever its reasoning looks like."
 (4) FROM: "When BOTH final answers are right:"
     TO:   "When BOTH final states are right:"
The rendered lines of record in the pilot's template, for the reader who wants to see them in place, are
"Before critiquing, extract each model's FINAL ANSWER and check it against the reference and" /
"against your own reading of the question. A response whose final answer is wrong cannot win" /
"against a response whose final answer is right, whatever its reasoning looks like." / (blank) /
"When BOTH final answers are right:".
NOTHING ELSE IN THE TEMPLATE IS TOUCHED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE AND REGISTERED: the block's other MMLU-Pro furniture —
"the question", "the response", "its reasoning", "Correctness first", the both-correct tie-breaking paragraph, the
confidence sentence — STAYS WORD FOR WORD. This test therefore asks ONE narrow question: does naming the right OBJECT
(state, not answer) move the indecision? A NULL RESULT DOES NOT CLEAR TEMPLATE MIS-FIT IN GENERAL; it clears THESE FOUR
STRINGS, and the outcome section must say so in those words.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE CLOSED RUBRIC LINE, STATED SO A FUTURE READER DOES NOT REOPEN A CLOSED LINE BY ACCIDENT. CONTEXT.md
§5 closes "rubric text at every granularity (RUBRIC, LADDER, RUBRIC-512-R, J6, RK-1, LEAF-POWERED, STACK-NORUBRIC)" and
"rubric-shaped references (REF-CHECKLIST)". EVERY ONE OF THOSE TESTS VARIES THE CONTENT OF THE $rubric SLOT — induced
text, per-anchor text, per-leaf text, contrastive or frontier-written text, a data-only card, or the slot removed
altogether — and every one of them reads its result as a FIDELITY DELTA (agreement with a key or a reference). THIS TEST
DOES NONE OF THAT. (i) THE $rubric SLOT IS BYTE-IDENTICAL: RUBRIC_BFCL is unchanged and the byte-identity gate refuses the
run if it is not. (ii) NOTHING IS INDUCED: there is no anchor, no leaf, no cell, no per-question and no per-task text;
four literal strings in a FROZEN, CORPUS-INDEPENDENT template are replaced. (iii) THE OBJECT IS DIFFERENT: the rubric line
asked "does BETTER RUBRIC TEXT buy agreement?" and the record answered NO at every granularity; this asks "does the
inherited template NAME THE RIGHT OBJECT when the artefact is a trace?" — a template-fit question about what the judge is
told to extract, not a question about how the judge is told to grade. (iv) THE PRIMARY ENDPOINT IS DIFFERENT: it is a TIE
RATE (decisiveness), not an agreement rate (fidelity); the fidelity numbers here are SECONDARY and exist to check for
harm, not to reopen a rubric claim. (v) NOTHING THIS TEST CAN RETURN OVERTURNS A RUBRIC RESULT: if the tie rate moves,
that is a fact about a verify-first template on trace-shaped artefacts and says nothing about rubric value on MMLU-Pro; if
it does not move, that is equally silent. The same check is recorded for the other closed lines below.

READOUTS AND CRITERIA (numbered; each scored HELD / FAILED / UNDETERMINED explicitly; denominators named). THE 2026-09-23
REGISTRATION-DEFECT RULING ("a criterion with a bar states, IN ONE PLACE, whether the POINT or the INTERVAL decides it,
and if both are scored it says so") IS APPLIED DELIBERATELY: C1 HAS EXACTLY ONE DECIDING STATISTIC — THE PAIRED DELTA'S
TASK-CLUSTERED INTERVAL — AND THREE DISJOINT OUTCOMES; THE POINT DECIDES NOTHING, AND THE McNEMAR p IS A REQUIRED
COMPANION, NOT A SECOND DECIDING CLAUSE.

 (C1) THE TIE RATE, THE PRIMARY ENDPOINT AND THE ONLY BARRED ONE. T_swap = the order-flip TIE share on the 458 deciding
      matches under the swapped prompt (denominator 458 matches over 49 TASKS, the cluster unit). THE DECIDING STATISTIC
      IS THE PAIRED DELTA Δ = T_swap − 0.2183, computed MATCH BY MATCH over the same 458 mids, and its TASK-CLUSTERED
      INTERVAL: point ± 1.96 × the task-clustered bootstrap SE of Δ (clusters = the 49 tasks, B = 2000, seed 42), with the
      percentile interval, B, the cluster count, the MEASURED DEFF for Δ and the exact two-sided McNemar on the 458 paired
      TIE / not-TIE outcomes (its discordant counts b and c and its exact p) ALL PRINTED BESIDE IT. THE BAR IS −0.05, set
      here and never after, at the scale of the record's own retest churn (CANARY 0.087, DECOMP 0.057) so that a verdict
      requires a move the session confound cannot manufacture. C1 IS HELD (the four strings EXPLAIN a material part of the
      indecision) IFF Δ'S CLUSTERED INTERVAL LIES WHOLLY BELOW −0.05. C1 IS FAILED (they do NOT) IFF Δ'S CLUSTERED
      INTERVAL LIES WHOLLY ABOVE −0.05 — which includes every interval containing 0 and every positive interval. C1 IS
      UNDETERMINED IFF THE INTERVAL CONTAINS −0.05, OR IF FEWER THAN 300 OF THE 458 MATCHES YIELD A USABLE DUAL-ORDER
      OUTCOME, OR IF THE BYTE-IDENTITY GATE DID NOT PASS 916 OF 916, OR IF UNUSABLE ROWS EXCEED 5% OF THE POSTED CALLS.
      These are disjoint and exhaustive over one statistic. [CORRECTED 2026-09-23 by the registrar (BFCL separator defects, D2): NOT disjoint as written, because a validity trigger (fewer than 300 usable, the gate short of 916 of 916, or unusable rows above 5%) can fire while the interval lies wholly on one side of -0.05. RULING: the validity triggers are evaluated FIRST and PRE-EMPT the verdict expression; if one fires C1 is UNDETERMINED (BY TRIGGER), the interval is printed but not scored and the falsifier is not evaluated; otherwise the interval's three disjoint outcomes apply; see the section '## Registration defects recorded 2026-09-23 (insertion only; zero calls; no recorded number moves) — BFCL-FLIP-RESEED and BFCL-FINAL-STATE-SWAP: ...' at the END of this file.] REQUIRED COMPANION, not a deciding clause: the exact McNemar
      p is printed with every reading of C1, and a HELD verdict whose McNemar p exceeds 0.01 is recorded as

SUPPORT AND MDE, STATED BEFORE THE RUN (this paragraph exists because BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT was registered at DEFF ~1.4 and
MEASURED 3.60, and that gap is why its C1 came back underpowered; the registration does not repeat it). EXPECTED SUPPORT:
458 PAIRED matches over 49 TASK clusters — the same denominator and the same clusters as the pilot, so the support is
KNOWN and not estimated. TWO PLANNING QUANTITIES ARE CARRIED, BOTH NAMED AS PLANNING QUANTITIES. (i) UNPAIRED, FOR
REFERENCE ONLY: at T = 0.22 and n = 458 the naive SE is 0.0193, and at the pilot's MEASURED level-DEFF 3.60 the clustered
SE is 0.0366, so an UNPAIRED comparison of two tie rates would have an MDE of ±0.102 at 80% power — too coarse for a
−0.05 bar, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY THIS TEST IS PAIRED AND WHY C1'S STATISTIC IS THE PAIRED DELTA. (ii) PAIRED, THE DESIGN
OF RECORD: the delta's variance is driven by the DISCORDANT pairs, and the planning assumption is a discordance rate
d = 0.20 (about 92 of 458) with a DELTA-DEFF of 2.0 (the QUERY-SUPPORT median; paired deltas cluster far less than levels
because the between-task level is common to both passes). Under those, SE(Δ) = sqrt(0.20 / 458 × 2.0) = 0.0295, the MDE
at 80% power and alpha 0.05 two-sided is ±0.083, and the MDE at 50% power is ±0.058. AT d = 0.10 the SE is 0.0209 and the
MDE ±0.058; at d = 0.30 with DELTA-DEFF 3.0 the SE is 0.0443 and the MDE ±0.124. THE DESIGN IS ADEQUATE FOR THE QUESTION
IT ASKS AND FOR NO OTHER: it can distinguish "the tie rate moved by about 8 points or more" from "it did not move", which
is the question the −0.05 bar and the P1 prediction of −0.07 are written against. [CORRECTED 2026-09-23 by the registrar (D-S1, NOT READY review a45cdd8): the MDEs above are distances from 0, but C1 is decided against the BAR −0.05; against the bar, at SE 0.0296, HELD needs Δ̂ < −0.108 and FAILED Δ̂ > +0.008, so at P1 (Δ ≈ −0.07) P(UNDETERMINED) ≈ 0.90, and 80% power needs a true Δ <= −0.133 or >= +0.033. VERDICT LINE UNDER THE SUPPORT RULE: SCOREABLE for a large template effect (true Δ <= −0.133, 80% power); at the registered prediction P1 (Δ ≈ −0.07) the design is DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY and will read UNDETERMINED about 90% of the time. The arithmetic above reproduces; only the reference point was wrong. ## Registered 2026-09-23 (before any code or call) — TIE-MECHANICS: is the canary's "every retest disagreement sits at the tie boundary, and no decisive match reverses" a property of the judge, or the arithmetic that independent per-call vote changes force through the dual-order TIE-on-flip rule? (zero calls; a CONSISTENCY CHECK on the two CANARY-BASELINE caches)

Registered by the registrar on 2026-09-23 BEFORE ANY CODE, at the END of this file so that no line number above this point moves.
Zero judge calls; no DB of record opened by the registrar; the arithmetic below is combinatorics on RECORDED counts.

QUESTION. CANARY-BASELINE pass 2 (outcome section of 2026-09-22; record docs/agents/results/CANARY-BASELINE.json, numbers_of_record
"tie_boundary" and "per_order_raw_vote_disagreement") recorded, on the frozen 300 matches (set hash 50af669ac6997f9f, 279 questions):
26 of 300 dual-order verdicts changed between passes, ALL 26 TIE <-> decisive (16 TIE -> decisive, 10 decisive -> TIE); 0 direct
reversals among the 215 matches decisive in both passes; "23 further matches change a raw order vote and keep the verdict"; and 59 of
the 600 (match, order) raw votes changed between passes (0.098). A research lead asks whether this pattern is a judge property or is
FORCED under the dual-order TIE rule by independent per-call changes at rate about 0.098.

THE PREMISE, CORRECTED BEFORE REGISTERING (the registrar's arithmetic on the three recorded counts; the instrument re-counts them at
row level). The relayed framing reads "one-change matches observed 49 against about 53 expected; two-change matches about 2.9
expected, observed 0 reversals", with the one-change cell called powered (SE about 6.6) and the two-change cell unpowered. THREE
CORRECTIONS. (i) 49 = 26 + 23 is the number of matches with AT LEAST ONE changed order vote, not exactly one. (ii) With T = 59 changed
votes over those 49 matches, n1 + n2 = 49 and n1 + 2 x n2 = 59, so the record IMPLIES n1 = 39 matches with exactly one changed vote and
n2 = 10 with BOTH changed; "0 reversals" is a SUBSET of n2 (a reversal needs both orders to move to the opposite side), not n2 itself.
(iii) Given T, n1 = T - 2 x n2: the one-change and two-change cells are ONE STATISTIC, not a powered cell beside an unpowered one. The
relayed 53 and 2.9 are the UNCONDITIONAL expectations at p = 59/600 = 0.0983 (300 x 2 x p x (1 - p) = 53.2, SD 6.6; 300 x p^2 = 2.90).

THE NULL MODEL, EXACT AND WITHOUT A NUISANCE PARAMETER. Under i.i.d. per-call change, conditional on T = 59 the set of changed cells is
a uniformly random 59-subset of the 600 (match, order) cells. Then E0[n2 | T] = M x T(T - 1) / (N(N - 1)) = 300 x 59 x 58 / (600 x 599)
= 2.856, and by simulation (200,000 random 59-subsets, the registrar, 2026-09-23): SD0 1.52, P0(n2 >= 6) = 0.0502, P0(n2 >= 7) =
0.0146, P0(n2 >= 8) = 0.0034, P0(n2 >= 10) = 0.0001, P0(n2 = 0) = 0.042. THE RECORD-IMPLIED n2 = 10 IS THEREFORE ALREADY FAR IN THE
UPPER TAIL: the two orders of a match appear to change TOGETHER more often than independence allows. The registration does not
treat the implied count as observed: it is a prediction, and the instrument must reproduce the counts from the caches.

WHY THE PRECONDITION IS FORMALLY UNMET. FRAMEWORK L95 (Stage 6, "Separation certificate") redefines the pair's answer agreement A over
the cell's EVAL-side questions because under the filtered schedule the judged questions "would be enriched for disagreement and bias A
downward on exactly the high-agreement pairs the widener budgets", and ends: "The redefinition needs a zero-call refit
(A-REDEFINE-REFIT) before the filtered schedule is the default." A-REDEFINE-REFIT (this file, the bullet at L3675 "- **A-REDEFINE-REFIT
(2026-09-15, zero calls): PASS as a consistency check; no power against the filtered-schedule bias it was registered for; ...**";
record A-REDEFINE-REFIT.json) was run on x12's UNIFORM schedule, where A_eval and A_judged correlate 0.997, "so zero deltas are
guaranteed by construction". It never saw a filtered board. The precondition is therefore unmet, and this test is the refit on a
filtered board. A_eval itself is schedule-independent BY CONSTRUCTION (it is computed over the cell's eval-side questions whatever was
judged), so what remains to test is whether the filter's SELECTION of judged matches moves the certified edges - their direction
against the key and their confidence - beyond the effect of simply having fewer matches.

PROFILE-R-FILTERED: ..."). Three arms on the x12 board of record (9,142 Mistral verdicts, 14 anchors, the 920-edge set):

(D1) 951ec3a0a063b5a8 IS NOT A SYSTEM-PROMPT HASH. A TRANSCRIPTION DEFECT IN TODAY'S REGISTRATIONS: the digits were copied
correctly, the MEANING was not. The BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT record defines it (this file L11933, "1,216 payloads PLUS THE SYSTEM PROMPT
under EACH sha in separate processes and hashed the concatenation — 951ec3a0a063b5a8", restated at L11975, "assembled payloads plus
the system prompt hash to 951ec3a0a063b5a8 under BOTH shas") as a SCHEDULE-WIDE PAYLOAD ANCHOR over all 1,216 assembled payloads
and the system prompt. The two separator registrations call it "system prompt sha" / "the system prompt hashes to" at seven sites:
BFCL-FLIP-RESEED L12128, L12143, L12194 and P5 L12210; BFCL-FINAL-STATE-SWAP L12376, L12475, L12587 (all _as_of 2ead19e). READ
LITERALLY, FLIP's refusal clause ("requires the system prompt to hash to 951ec3a0a063b5a8") would refuse every launch, because no
system prompt hashes to it. THE SYSTEM PROMPT ALONE hashes to 058faa54f0697ad9: RE-DERIVED BY THE REGISTRAR from code constants
without opening any DB (bfcl_judged_pilot.system_prompt() at HEAD, whose file is the pinned version, LF sha16 5e9db53b894eeccb;
sha256 of the UTF-8 string, first 16 hex; 2,683 characters; the module's DB guard recorded zero connections), and it equals the

the instrument re-assembles all 1,216 payloads and the system prompt THROUGH THE PARENT MODULE (bfcl_judged_pilot.py at the pinned
sha) with the parent's concatenation rule, and the result MUST EQUAL 951ec3a0a063b5a8, else the run is refused; (ii) THE SYSTEM
PROMPT CHECK is BYTE-IDENTITY to the parent's system_prompt() with ITS OWN sha, 058faa54f0697ad9, printed and pinned (for SWAP: the
NEW system prompt's sha printed beside 058faa54f0697ad9, the character diff showing exactly the four replacements); (iii) THE PILOT
CACHE STORES NO PER-CELL PAYLOAD HASH, so "the pilot's sha for the same cell" in both registrations means the PARENT MODULE'S
RE-ASSEMBLY of that cell, tied to pass 1 ONLY THROUGH THE ANCHOR in (i); the READY must state this and must not describe the
per-cell comparison as a comparison with a stored value. No number of BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT moves.

(D2) C1 CAN RETURN TWO VERDICTS IN BOTH TESTS; RULING: VALIDITY TRIGGERS TAKE PRECEDENCE. Both registrations list, beside the
interval clauses, VALIDITY TRIGGERS (FLIP: fewer than 90 of the 100 usable; the byte-identity gate short of 200 of 200. SWAP: fewer
than 300 of the 458 usable; the gate short of 916 of 916; unusable rows above 5% of the posted calls) and call the outcomes "disjoint
and exhaustive over one statistic". They are not: a trigger can fire while the interval lies wholly on one side of the bar, which is
the over-determination class of the 2026-09-23 BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT ruling (this file, "## Registration defect recorded 2026-09-23 ...
BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT: C1 IS OVER-DETERMINED"). THE RULING, ADOPTING THE COORDINATOR'S RECOMMENDATION: THE VALIDITY TRIGGERS ARE
EVALUATED FIRST AND PRE-EMPT THE VERDICT EXPRESSION. If any trigger fires, C1 is "UNDETERMINED (BY TRIGGER: <the trigger>)", the
interval is PRINTED but NOT SCORED, and THE FALSIFIER IS NOT EVALUATED; only if no trigger fires is the interval read, with its three
disjoint outcomes. WHY THIS AND NOT THE OTHER WAY: a fired trigger means the premise under which the interval was registered (the
support it was sized for, or the one-knob identity of the instrument) failed, so the interval is not a trustworthy measurement of the
registered object; scoring it would score a different object. WHY THIS IS CONSISTENT WITH THE BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT RULING: that ruling
governs TWO CLAUSES OVER THE SAME BAR (a point clause and an interval clause), which must both be scored; a validity trigger is not
a clause over the bar but a precondition of the measurement, and precondition-first is the structure already merged for
TP20-C2-CONFORMANCE (1494527, READY 2ab566b: bracket (e)'s conditions are evaluated before the verdict expression and pre-empt it).
The byte-identity gate is in both registrations ALSO a refusal before any call; the trigger form covers only the case where it is
checked at --analyze. THIS RULING IS THE RULE FOR EVERY FUTURE REGISTRATION: validity conditions are written as refusals or as
pre-empting triggers, never as a third clause beside the bar (the five registrations of 2026-09-23 at L12710-L13360 _as_of 2ead19e
are already written that way). The instruments' "NO VERDICT - OVER-DETERMINED ON THIS DATA" branch is to be replaced by the
precedence above; the READY confirms it.

## Registration defect recorded 2026-09-23 (insertion only; zero calls; no bar, prediction or falsifier moves) — BFCL-FINAL-STATE-SWAP D-S1: the Support MDE was computed against 0, but C1 decides against the bar at −0.05; the power-against-the-bar table, C1's restated verdict line, and the coordinator's spend decision

Recorded by the registrar on the NOT READY review docs/reviews/NOT_READY_bfcl_final_state_swap.md (a45cdd8; instrument
bfcl_final_state_swap.py LF 1c67847de8de2efe on bfcl-separators @ 5f459b2), blocker D-S1. Appended at the END of this file; the
Support paragraph of the registration carries a dated bracket inserted into its existing lines, so no line moves.

(A) THE DEFECT. The registration's "SUPPORT AND MDE, STATED BEFORE THE RUN" paragraph (the BFCL-FINAL-STATE-SWAP registration,
L12504-L12522 _as_of a645d06) computes SE(Δ) = sqrt(0.20 / 458 x 2.0) = 0.0295 and an MDE of ±0.083 at 80% power, ±0.058 at 50%
(±0.058 / ±0.124 at the other planning corners), and concludes that the design "can distinguish 'the tie rate moved by about 8
points or more' from 'it did not move', which is the question the −0.05 bar and the P1 prediction of −0.07 are written against".
THE ARITHMETIC REPRODUCES (0.0296 / 0.083 / 0.058 / 0.0209 / 0.124); THE REFERENCE POINT IS WRONG. Those MDEs are distances from
0, but C1 is decided by the paired interval's position relative to the BAR −0.05 (HELD iff wholly below −0.05, FAILED iff wholly
above), so the power that matters is power against the bar.

(B) POWER AGAINST THE BAR, re-derived by the registrar (normal approximation, two-sided 95% interval, the planning values d = 0.20
and delta-DEFF 2.0, SE 0.02955; the coordinator's and the reviewer's figures reproduce):
 - HELD requires Δ̂ < −0.050 − 1.96 x 0.02955 = −0.1079; FAILED requires Δ̂ > −0.050 + 1.96 x 0.02955 = +0.0079.
 - true Δ = −0.0683 (the registered prediction P1, T_swap 0.15): P(HELD) 0.090, P(FAILED) 0.005, P(UNDETERMINED) 0.905.
 - true Δ = −0.10: P(HELD) 0.394, P(UNDETERMINED) 0.606.
 - true Δ = 0 (no template effect): P(FAILED) 0.394, P(UNDETERMINED) 0.606, P(HELD) 0.000.
 - 80% POWER requires a true Δ <= −0.1328 (for HELD) or >= +0.0328 (for FAILED).
 - n is FIXED at 458, the whole deciding set: no budget buys more support. At the pessimistic corner (d = 0.30, delta-DEFF 3.0,
   SE 0.0443) every figure above is worse.

(C) C1'S VERDICT LINE UNDER THE SUPPORT RULE, RESTATED (this replaces, by the last-bracket rule, the paragraph's "THE DESIGN IS
ADEQUATE FOR THE QUESTION IT ASKS"): **SCOREABLE for a large template effect (true Δ <= −0.133, 80% power); at the registered
prediction P1 (Δ ≈ −0.07) the design is DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY and will read UNDETERMINED about 90% of the time.** Under no effect it
reads FAILED about 39% of the time and never HELD. The criteria, the bar −0.05, P1 and the falsifier are UNCHANGED; the outcome
section must quote this line beside C1 whatever C1 reads, with the MEASURED delta-DEFF and the realised P(UNDETERMINED).

(D) THE SPEND DECISION — A COORDINATOR DECISION UNDER THE AUTHOR'S DELEGATION, recorded here, in plan Amendment 11 by a dated
bracket, and in the queue item's go field. The author said on 2026-09-23 "no need to wait for my approval" (budget under plan
Amendment 11). DECISION: PROCEED with the 916 calls. REASON (the coordinator's): the design detects a LARGE template effect with 80%
power and reads FAILED 39% of the time under no effect, so it separates "the template mis-fit is large" from "it is absent", even
though it cannot resolve the registered point prediction. IFEVAL-RESPONSE-ORACLE shows that a trace-attached intervention can move
a tie rate a great deal, so a large effect is a live possibility; THAT RESULT MAY NOT BE QUOTED AS AN EXPECTATION FOR THIS TEST
(the closed-line ruling, docs/agents/leads/2026-09-23_bfcl_final_state_swap_ruling.md, forbids it) and is cited only as why
"large" is not implausible. THE DECISION IS TAKEN KNOWING THAT THE MOST LIKELY SINGLE OUTCOME IS UNDETERMINED. It is not the
registrar's decision and not the author's own words beyond the quoted delegation; it changes no criterion and does not itself make
the instrument READY (a record-only re-review is to issue READY for the UNCHANGED script sha 1c67847de8de2efe).

(E) LAUNCH CONDITION ADDED (review finding (b), applying to both instruments): an unusable match counts as not-TIE (D4(a), confirmed
as registered), which below SWAP's 5% trigger can move Δ by up to −0.098 toward HELD, larger than the distance to the bar. The
post-run readout MUST print the usable-only Δ and its interval beside the literal one and say whether C1's verdict differs (NOT
READY condition 4). And review finding (a): the go gate checks that the READY FILE EXISTS, not what it says nor which script sha it
names, so a NOT READY verdict filed under the READY name would open it (D-S3); until the engine-coder's fix (gate_state() requires
the script's LF sha16 inside the READY file) the run-operator verifies the READY's verdict word and the named sha by reading the

## Registrar's rulings 2026-09-23 (amendment by insertion; zero calls; before any real-data run; nothing above is rewritten) — CERT-UNDER-FILTER: five builder choices ruled (no C3 trigger and P5 never HELD on an absent fit; one C1 support trigger REGISTERED at fewer than 12 connected anchors; the stack_judge stub admitted; the pinned copy of build() admitted; the majority sign primary), and the builder's disclosed readings recorded

sentence of the registration carries a dated bracket inserted into its existing line, so no line moves.

(R1) THE UNREGISTERED TRIGGER ON C3 IS RULED OUT, AND P5 IS NEVER HELD ON AN ABSENT FIT. The builder added "a validity trigger at W_F
<= 14 events, taken from Support (g)" and scored P5 HELD "if ddev < 3.84, OR if no ddev can be computed while that trigger fires".
Support (g) is a STRUCTURAL STATEMENT ("at 14 or fewer events b1 is unidentifiable at any budget of THIS board"), not a registered
trigger, and C3 is DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY, so no trigger is needed on it. RULING: (a) there is NO trigger on C3; the condition W_F <= 14
is PRINTED beside C3 as a descriptive flag, "b1 structurally unidentifiable at this event count (Support (g))", deciding nothing;
(b) P5 ("C3: delta-deviance < 3.84 (UNDETERMINED)") is scored ONLY on a computed delta-deviance: HELD iff ddev < 3.84, FAILED iff
ddev >= 3.84; if no ddev can be computed (the fit does not converge, or b1 is unidentified), P5 is UNDETERMINED. [RULED 2026-09-23 (review acd054a, D2): an inner-search failure or a non-finite I makes that fit NO FIT (reason printed), never a refusal of the run; C1 is unaffected. See the section '## Registrar's rulings 2026-09-23 (amendment by insertion; zero calls; before any code change and any real-data run) — C ...' at the END of this file.] A prediction may not
pass on an absence of evidence; the coordinator's reading is adopted.

(R2) ONE C1 TRIGGER IS REGISTERED HERE, ON SUPPORT, AND RECONCILED WITH C4. The standing precedence rule (7da2ec5) says registered
triggers are evaluated first; it does not create triggers. The registration already says (C4) that an anchor whose graph DISCONNECTS
under F is UNDETERMINED BY CONSTRUCTION for C1-C3 and leaves their denominators, counted. RULING, registered now, before any data:
(a) disconnected anchors are ALWAYS removed from C1-C3's denominators and named (C4 as written); so is an anchor that falls below
build()'s 200-row floor under ANY arm (R4(c)); (b) C1 IS UNDETERMINED (BY TRIGGER: SUPPORT) IFF FEWER THAN 12 OF THE 14 ANCHORS
REMAIN IN C1'S DENOMINATOR, evaluated FIRST under the standing rule (the interval printed, not scored; the falsifier not evaluated);
(c) otherwise C1 is scored on the remaining anchors' cluster bootstrap with its three disjoint outcomes. SOURCE OF THE THRESHOLD:
the Support (planning DEFF 1.6 transported from a 14-anchor bootstrap, MDE 15.0 edges on 809 edges) describes 14 clusters; losing
up to two anchors (at most one seventh of the edges) is within the planning range 1.6-3.0, and losing more means the registered
Support no longer describes the run. The builder's "fewer than 2 connected anchors" is subsumed. Prediction P6 (0 anchors
disconnect) is unchanged.

(R3) THE REFUSING stack_judge STUB IS ADMITTED as satisfying the registration's intent ("MAY NOT import stack_judge" means its code
may not be LOADED or EXECUTED, so its read-write open_cache() can never touch a cache of record), on three conditions the READY

check covers the other modules systematic_budget imports at load: none may open a DB at import.

(R4) A PINNED, BIT-IDENTITY-PROVEN COPY OF build()'s PER-ANCHOR LOOP IS ADMITTED where the registration said "imported, never
re-implemented", because the intent of that phrase is NO DIVERGENCE from the function of record, and importing build() itself is

CONDITIONS: (a) at launch the instrument hashes the source of systematic_budget.build (the pin 128baa007a44a219, its rendering

an absent or empty one is printed. Under immutable=1 the refusal prevents silently omitting committed rows; under plain mode=ro it

(4) VOTE-FRAME-CERT, ARM-KEYED SINGLE-ORDER TABLES: A SIXTH CLASS IS ADMITTED, NAMED NOT-DUAL-ORDER, OUTSIDE THE FIVE AND NOT A KIND
OF UNCERTIFIABLE. The schema-only enumeration rule necessarily catches a table keyed by an order-valued column that in fact holds a
single order. RULING: a table is NOT-DUAL-ORDER iff, row-level, no match (or key) has rows under two or more order values; a cache
whose every candidate table is NOT-DUAL-ORDER receives the class NOT-DUAL-ORDER (a cache with any dual-order table is classed on its

CACHES ONLY (enumerated minus NOT-DUAL-ORDER): P1 counts them, P2 and P3 take them as denominator, and P4 counts UNCERTIFIABLE among
them, so a NOT-DUAL-ORDER cache never satisfies P4. The raw enumeration count and the NOT-DUAL-ORDER count are printed beside.

A SOURCE PREDICTION BEARING ON P2 (">= 80% CERTIFIED-POSITIONAL"), recorded as a prediction and NOT as a finding: from reading each

STANDING RULE 1 — THE RULE-7 NO-READERS GUARD, OPERATIONAL FORM (the READY's ruling, section 4, adopted as standing because it resolves an
ambiguity that blocked this proof once). "0 tools/analysis/*.py processes" is the RULE-7 NO-READERS GUARD, not a quiet-machine
requirement. Its operational form, checked before each leg (and, for a two-leg proof, after the restore): W1 an exclusive-open probe shows
every pool DB (embeddings_cache.db, snapshots.db, snapshots_frozen.db and their -wal / -shm) FREE, never run while a leg's JVM is running;
W2 a process list with PIDs: a tools/analysis process carrying --selftest is ADMITTED while W1 is FREE; any other tools/analysis or
tools/chains process, any --dry-run (dry-runs open caches), any construction (bootRun / TaxoArenaApplication), any Gradle worker not
belonging to the leg and any pool_guard.py are REFUSED; W3 the admitted PIDs are printed beside each leg's wall time; W4 at least 12 GB free
physical memory before each leg; W5 the orchestrator announces the window, and no git write touches src/ inside it. A breach found at a
check is a FAILED PRECONDITION (the window is repeated), never a criterion outcome.

STANDING RULE 2 — THE VACUITY PRINCIPLE FOR INERTNESS PROOFS (the READY's D3 HIGH, adopted beyond this test). A byte-identity proof over
OUTPUTS is VACUOUS unless it also proves, by execution, that the CHANGED CODE ACTUALLY RAN in the changed leg: identical bytes cannot
distinguish "leg B ran the new code" from "leg B ran the old code" (a stale compile, a build-cache hit, a missed file-system change, an
agent reverting the file). Every future inertness / byte-identity proof registers a DISCRIMINATOR that reads the executed artefact (here
R9: the count of the renamed identifiers in the compiled class files, 0 after leg A and > 0 after leg B) and treats its failure as a void
leg, not as a verdict.

Both rules are also inserted as dated brackets into CONTEXT.md section 4 rules 7 and 11.

## Registrar's ruling 2026-09-23 (amendment by insertion; zero calls; before any real-data run) — CERT-UNDER-FILTER: 'b1 unidentified' DEFINED as (quasi-)complete separation of the wrong / right established edges in the widener's covariate A, detected on the data before any fit; P5 and C3 read it identically; two builder readings confirmed

Recorded by the registrar on the coordinator's relay of the build (commit 4cd0bfa, cert_under_filter.py LF sha16 409da54119dde59f as
relayed; R1-R6 implemented; 45/45 branches; 20/20 mutants killed), BEFORE ANY REAL-DATA RUN. It completes ruling R1 of the section
"## Registrar's rulings 2026-09-23 (...) — CERT-UNDER-FILTER: five builder choices ruled ..." (8469780).

THE GAP. R1 scores P5 only on a computed delta-deviance and reads it UNDETERMINED if none can be computed, but gave "b1 unidentified" no
operational definition. The builder read "cannot be computed" as no fit possible (zero wrong or zero right events) or a non-finite ddev,
and correctly invented no magnitude or convergence rule. On its synthetic U a fit with b1 running to +720 and a FINITE ddev of 1.06 would
then score P5 HELD: a coefficient in the hundreds is the signature of (quasi-)complete separation, where the maximum-likelihood estimate
does not exist and the optimiser stops wherever it stops. P5 would PASS on a fit that identified nothing, the "pass on absence of
evidence" class R1 refused. [CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (the coordinator's mis-characterisation, recorded by the registrar): the +720 case is NOT separated (wrong A 0.382-0.634, right A 0.320-0.640 overlap); it is a FLAT likelihood (a step in tau at A about 0.35, profile curvature 0), the case this ruling disclosed and left untriggered. See the section '## Registrar's ruling 2026-09-23 (amendment by insertion; zero calls; before any real-data run) — CERT-UNDER-FILTER: 'b1 unidentif ...' at the END of this file.]

RULING (the coordinator's recommendation, ACCEPTED and made precise). "b1 UNIDENTIFIED" MEANS (QUASI-)COMPLETE SEPARATION, DETECTED
DETERMINISTICALLY ON THE DATA BEFORE ANY FIT, NEVER BY A THRESHOLD ON A FITTED VALUE. The widener's covariate is the pair's answer
agreement A (the eval-side A of the registered parameter pair, tau(A) = exp(b0 + b1 A)); b1 is the coefficient on A. On the edge set the
fit uses (the arm's established edges with their wrong / right labels), let A_w be the A values of the wrong edges and A_r those of the
right edges. SEPARATION holds iff max(A_w) <= min(A_r) OR max(A_r) <= min(A_w) (the two ranges do not overlap; equality at the boundary
is QUASI-complete separation and counts). Together with the existing conditions (zero wrong or zero right events; a non-finite ddev),
separation makes the fit "NO FIT (b1 unidentified: <reason>)". Then P5 is UNDETERMINED, and a ddev and b1, if the optimiser returns them,
are printed as DESCRIPTIVE and decide nothing. WHY A DATA CONDITION AND NOT A |b1| CAP: a cap is an arbitrary number and would itself be
a new decision rule; separation is the mathematical reason no finite b1 exists, it is checkable before the fit, and it does not depend on
the optimiser. DISCLOSED LIMIT: range non-overlap is the standard separation condition for a single covariate; the widener's likelihood
also involves each edge's m and s, so a fit can in principle be flat without range separation. That case is NOT a registered trigger;
the instrument prints |b1| and the profile-likelihood curvature at the optimum beside every fit, descriptively, so a reader sees it, and
nothing is decided on them. ## Registrar's ruling 2026-09-23 (amendment by insertion; zero calls; before any real-data run) — VOTE-FRAME-CERT, review finding H3: an E-COMB certificate (no raw text stored) REQUIRES a pinned per-cache SOURCE CHECK of the writer's combiner, else the cache is UNCERTIFIABLE; the review's three verdicts recorded

Recorded by the registrar on the READY review docs/reviews/NOT_READY_vote_frame_family.md (14edeb4; branch vote-frame-instruments @ d237e56, scripts re-derived by the
reviewer as sha256[:16] of the LF bytes: vote_frame_cert.py 3217ee2d78dd4421, tie_mechanics.py b3df664f904849ab, position_index_all.py
5f6ac8e44049aa6c; CRLF renderings 258d495b0cce9dbf / 354848c6194b297b / d274357f9bef9179; git blobs f2db3c83 / abcfd28c / a658e677).

VERDICTS OF THE REVIEW, RECORDED: VOTE-FRAME-CERT NOT READY (blockers B1, B2); POSITION-INDEX-ALL NOT READY (it reads through
vfc.unit_votes, so B1 and B2 apply, plus H1 and H2); TIE-MECHANICS READY-WITH-CONDITIONS (T-C1, T-C2). The review's B1 is its own ruling
on the order-1 change: an order-1 vote that contradicts the re-parse of its own raw text refutes BOTH hypotheses and is MIXED (row ids
listed), never a warning; the demotion had certified an all-transposed order-1 fixture (s = 0.333 against 0.750). The registrar
concurs: the 04379d7 ruling that the fwd arm is AMBIGUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION says it cannot DISCRIMINATE the frames, not that a
contradiction on it is tolerated. B2, H1, H2 and M1-M3 are with the builder.

H3, THE REGISTRATION-LEVEL QUESTION. For caches that store NO raw text (rubric_ladder, rubric_swap, rubric_contrast: the E-COMB evidence
path), the certificate re-derives the stored COMBINED winner / flip from the two stored votes with combine_orders and with its
untransposed twin. Without raw text that check CANNOT distinguish "order 2 stored contestant-labelled with a correct combiner" from
"order 2 stored positional with a combiner that forgets the transposition" (or, symmetrically, positional against a double-transposing
combiner): both store the same (v1, v2, combined). An E-COMB certificate is therefore CONDITIONAL ON THE WRITER'S COMBINER, and a sign
bug in that combiner is exactly the failure for which position-bias correction was once removed (2026-09-05).

RULING (the coordinator's suggestion, ACCEPTED and made precise). An E-COMB-only cache is CERTIFIED (POSITIONAL or CONTESTANT) ONLY IF,
in addition to the 100% re-derivation, a PER-CACHE SOURCE CHECK OF THE WRITER'S COMBINER passes:
 (a) the writer is the script WRITER_OF names for that cache, and its source is taken AT THE BLOB THAT WROTE THE CACHE: the script sha
     pinned in the cache's own run_meta where it exists, else the last commit of that script at or before the cache's first write,
     stated with its evidence; a writer whose run-time blob cannot be pinned FAILS the check;
 (b) the combiner the writer calls to fill the combined column is read with ast (never executed) at that blob, and the check asserts
     that it IS rejudge_grok.combine_orders (imported by name, rejudge_grok at the same run-time pin) or is AST-equivalent to it, i.e.
     applies exactly one transposition to the order-2 vote before comparing; any other combiner FAILS the check; [AMENDED 2026-09-23 by the registrar (re-review bc2ea7b, D1 HIGH): the 'AST-equivalent' arm is WITHDRAWN: it passed four adversarial combiners with the WRONG frame (C3, C4, C5, C9). The combiner is verified ONLY if it is AST-IDENTICAL to rejudge_grok.combine_orders at the pinned blob, or a direct call to it; anything else is UNCERTIFIABLE, 'combiner not verified'. See the section '## Registrar's amendment 2026-09-23 (insertion only; zero calls; before any real-data run) — H3(b) of 0104e44 NARROWED:  ...' at the END of this file.]
 (c) the check's result, the writer, the pinned blob and the evidence of the pin are printed per cache.
A cache whose check FAILS or cannot be run is classed UNCERTIFIABLE (reason printed: "E-COMB, combiner not verified"), never
CERTIFIED; it is excluded from POSITION-INDEX-ALL like every uncertified cache and counts toward P4. As the reviewer asks, the index
prints E-COMB-certified caches as their own line in C5, so a reader sees which part of the result rests on source-verified combiners
rather than on raw text. The READY verifies (a)-(c) per cache by execution on the three caches named above.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it changes no bar, prediction value or falsifier and adds no trigger; it narrows when the CERTIFIED classes may be
reached; it reads no data. The builder implements it together with B1, B2, H1, H2 and M1-M3; then the re-review.

## Registrar's ruling 2026-09-23 (amendment by insertion; zero calls; before any real-data run) — CERT-UNDER-FILTER: 'b1 unidentified' EXTENDED to SINGULAR OBSERVED INFORMATION at the optimum (a flat profile), with a stated round-off tolerance; the coordinator's mis-characterisation of the +720 case corrected

Recorded by the registrar on the coordinator's relay of the implementation of c669926 (commit 0f44893: 50/50 branches, 28/28 mutants killed
under python and -O, asserts converted to explicit raises, as relayed), BEFORE ANY REAL-DATA RUN.

(A) CORRECTION, THE COORDINATOR'S (recorded by insertion; c669926's text is not rewritten, a bracket is inserted beside it). The ruling of
c669926 was motivated by the synthetic "b1 +720, ddev 1.06" fit, called "the signature of (quasi-)complete separation". IT IS NOT
SEPARATED: the builder measured the covariate ranges, wrong edges A in 0.382-0.634 and right edges A in 0.320-0.640, which OVERLAP. Its
runaway comes from a FLAT LIKELIHOOD: the optimum is a step in tau at A about 0.35, with PROFILE CURVATURE 0 at the optimum. That is exactly
the limit c669926 DISCLOSED and did not make a trigger, so under c669926 as written the case reads IDENTIFIED and, were it F's fit, P5 would
score HELD: the "pass on absence of evidence" outcome R1 set out to close. The builder correctly did not bend the definition; it pinned the
literal reading and prints a CONFLICT line on every selftest run.

(B) RULING: "b1 UNIDENTIFIED" IS EXTENDED BY SINGULAR OBSERVED INFORMATION (the coordinator's suggestion, ACCEPTED, with the tolerance stated
here). Let l(b1) be the PROFILE log-likelihood in b1 (b0 re-maximised at each b1) and b1* the optimiser's value. The observed information
is I = -l''(b1*), estimated by the central second difference with step h = 1e-4 x max(1, |b1*|):
I = -( l(b1* + h) - 2 l(b1*) + l(b1* - h) ) / h^2. The fit is UNIDENTIFIED (reason printed: "b1 unidentified: singular observed
information") iff I <= 0, OR I x h^2 <= 16 x eps x max(1, |l(b1*)|), with eps = 2^-52 = 2.22e-16 (float64 machine epsilon). THE TOLERANCE'S
SOURCE: the round-off error of that second difference is bounded by about 4 x eps x |l| (three evaluations, coefficients 1, 2, 1, each
carrying at most eps x |l| relative error), so a curvature whose second difference is below that bound is not distinguishable from zero
at the precision of the computation; the factor 16 is that bound times a 4x margin for the error of the inner re-maximisation of b0, and it
is REGISTERED HERE, not inferred. [RULED 2026-09-23 (review acd054a, D5): the 16 is multiplicative (4 x 4) and carries NO check on the inner error; the inner error estimate is printed as DESCRIPTIVE; the builder's INNER_MARGIN = 12 is removed. See the section '## Registrar's rulings 2026-09-23 (amendment by insertion; zero calls; before any code change and any real-data run) — C ...' at the END of this file.] It is "zero to machine precision relative to the log-likelihood's scale", not a magnitude cap on b1 and
not a floor chosen to decide cases. WHY THIS IS THE SAME GROUND AS SEPARATION: when the observed information is singular, no finite
standard error for b1 exists and b1 is not locally identified. CHECK AGAINST THE BUILDER'S CASES: the flat case (curvature 0) is UNIDENTIFIED;
the overlapping well-fitting set (b1 +5.39, ddev 9.95, curvature 0.17) stays IDENTIFIED, since 0.17 is many orders of magnitude above the
round-off bound. The instrument prints I, h, l(b1*) and the bound on every fit.

(C) CONSEQUENCES, as c669926 for separation. With separation, zero wrong or zero right events, or a non-finite ddev, singular observed
information makes the fit "NO FIT (b1 unidentified: <reason>)"; P5 is then UNDETERMINED; the optimiser's b1 and ddev, if returned, are
printed as DESCRIPTIVE and decide nothing. The SAME definition applies to C3's NO FIT, on every arm and under each convention. The
c669926 sentence "That case is NOT a registered trigger" is superseded for the singular-information case; a profile that is merely shallow
but not singular (I above the bound) remains IDENTIFIED and is only printed.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it changes no bar, prediction value or falsifier; it defines an existing branch more completely and adds no trigger on
C1; it reads no data. The builder implements it (the selftest must execute both the flat case, reading UNIDENTIFIED, and the curvature-0.17
case, reading IDENTIFIED, under python and -O); then the READY review.

SENTENCE OF RECORD (the reviewer's, verbatim): "BFCL-FINAL-STATE-SWAP (916 judge calls, 0 unusable; the 458 deciding matches of BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT over 49 tasks, both orders, user turns byte-identical to the pilot's): replacing "final answer" with "final state" in the four registered strings of the inherited verify-first block left the dual-order tie rate at 98/458 = 0.2140 against the pilot's 100/458 = 0.2183. The paired delta is -0.0044, with task-clustered interval [-0.0387, +0.0300] (bootstrap SE 0.0175, measured delta-DEFF 1.15, n_eff 398, MDE +-0.049). The interval lies wholly above the -0.05 bar, so C1 is FAILED: these four strings do not carry a share of the pilot's indecision of 5 points or more. The point is DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY (R2) and is not a move (McNemar b 29 / c 27, p 0.89). There is no harm: agreement delta +0.0066 (lower end -0.0246) and wrong-committed delta -0.0022 (upper end +0.0090). Of the three hypotheses the pilot left open, template mis-fit at the granularity of these four strings is refuted. Position bias and corpus difficulty survive, and neither is established. The 0.2183 stands as an unexplained decisiveness collapse."

WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW (the reviewer's list, in full):
 1. That the template is irrelevant to BFCL. Only these four strings (one referent, answer -> state) are cleared. The rest of the inherited furniture ('the question', 'the response', 'its reasoning') was deliberately left. Any further edit is governed by fence F3: a different F1-qualifying referent plus a pre-registered argument, and two readings close the line on this corpus.
 2. That the four strings have NO effect. The interval admits a reduction of up to about 3.9 points (lower end -0.0387), up to roughly a sixth of the 21.8-point tie rate. 'These four strings have no effect' must never be written.
 3. That the indecision is position bias, or that it is corpus difficulty. The test refutes one hypothesis and establishes neither of the others. The first-position rate 0.5700 (z 4.13) is descriptive, has no bar, and is not a replication of the pilot's 0.5862.
 4. Any movement at all. Delta -0.0044, the first-position shift 0.586 -> 0.570, the (Model B, Model B) count 0 -> 5 and the dA / dW points all sit inside the session floor (CANARY pass 2 0.087; DECOMP 5.7%). The two passes are different sessions 8.5 h apart, not interleaved. The discordance 56/458 = 0.122 sits at the upper edge of the CANARY retest interval [0.056, 0.122] and splits 29/27, which is what retest churn alone looks like.
 5. Anything about the reference ceiling. The reference-wrong stratum is empty by construction (R1), and the CONSENSUS-FIT KEY/REF contrast is not estimable.
 6. A rung, a ladder position, a 0.75-bar reading or a 'for Agents' claim. A_swap is never on the ladder.
 7. Anything about STACK-v2 or any other corpus (F5). No MMLU-Pro, MATH or IFEval number is touched.
 8. That the design was underpowered. It was better powered than planned (delta-DEFF 1.15 against a planning 2.0). The REALISED P(FAILED) 0.740 is observed power at the point estimate, not evidence about delta.

## Registrar's amendment 2026-09-23 (insertion only; zero calls; before any real-data run) — H3(b) of 0104e44 NARROWED: a combiner is verified ONLY if it is AST-IDENTICAL to rejudge_grok.combine_orders at the pinned blob, or a direct call to it; the 'AST-equivalent' arm is WITHDRAWN (re-review bc2ea7b, D1 HIGH)

THE DEFECT, IN THE REGISTRAR'S OWN RULING. H3(b) of 0104e44 (the section "## Registrar's ruling 2026-09-23 (...) — VOTE-FRAME-CERT, review finding H3: an E-COMB
certificate ...", L13967-L14002) passes a combiner that "IS rejudge_grok.combine_orders ... or is AST-equivalent to it, i.e. applies exactly one
transposition to the order-2 vote before comparing". The re-review (docs/reviews/READY_vote_frame_family_rr.md, bc2ea7b, D1 HIGH) built nine adversarial
combiners, and the equivalence arm as implemented passes FOUR that get the frame WRONG: C3 (the transposed value computed but never used), C4 (transpose,
then un-transpose via an if-expression), C5 (the flip inverted) and C9 (the winner is the raw order-2 vote). The builder stopped rather than implement a fix
that contradicts the ruling, and noted that the ruling's own "i.e." definition arguably admits C5 and C9: a syntactic "one transposition" description is not a
semantic definition, and D2's call-site check does not close it (a clean call site with a wrong combiner would still certify in the wrong frame). The
defect is the registrar's.

THE AMENDMENT (the coordinator's recommendation, ADOPTED). H3(b) now reads: the combiner the writer calls to fill the combined column is verified ONLY IF it
is AST-IDENTICAL to rejudge_grok.combine_orders AT THE PINNED rejudge_grok BLOB, or is a DIRECT CALL to rejudge_grok.combine_orders. [CLARIFIED 2026-09-23 by the registrar (rr2 776a2dd, D-A; within this text, not a new ruling): the PINNED rejudge_grok.combine_orders body must itself be AST-identical to the recipe's REF_COMBINE_ORDERS for a direct call, and a local def must match REF_COMBINE_ORDERS; otherwise UNCERTIFIABLE, reason (2). The literal reading had widened h3_rj_between to a false CERTIFIED-CONTESTANT; no effect on the record (rejudge_grok.py has one commit, fb8fb5b, with the REF body). See the section '## Registrar's record and rulings 2026-09-23 (insertion only; zero calls) — vote-frame delta re-review rr2 (776a2dd) and ...' at the END of this file.] THE "AST-EQUIVALENT"
ARM IS WITHDRAWN. Every other combiner makes the cache UNCERTIFIABLE with reason (2) "E-COMB, combiner not verified". Conditions (a) (the run-time pin), (c)
(printing) and D2's call-site check stand unchanged.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT DIRECTION: it is CONSERVATIVE. A wrong combiner can no longer certify a wrong frame; the price is that a correct but differently
written combiner (the reviewer's C6) reads UNCERTIFIABLE, never wrong-frame. ON THE RECORD IT CHANGES NOTHING: all three writers of record take the
AST-IDENTICAL arm (rubric_ladder L307, rubric_swap L187, rubric_value_contrast L165), and condition V-C2's "0 AST-equivalent lines" now holds by construction.

STATED LIMITS OF THE CHECK (conservative false FAILS, never false passes): (i) a correct combiner written differently (C6) reads UNCERTIFIABLE; (ii) the
builder's known two: an unrelated helper named like a combiner (combine_text) can be taken for the combiner call, and an aliased import (for example
`from rejudge_grok import combine_orders as co`) is not recognised as a direct call. Each is printed with its reason; none can certify a wrong frame.

refusal as a pass. RECORDED: THE EARLIER READYs OF THIS INSTRUMENT MISSED A VACUOUS SELFTEST CHECK (a refusal of the instrument's own input scored as a pass): the class
of the vacuity principle (CONTEXT section 4 rule 11). RE-RULING (the reviewer's wording, ADOPTED): stack_v2_promptv2_x12all.db is OPENED EXACTLY ONCE, BY load_real, WITH
THE URI file:<path>?mode=ro&immutable=1, AFTER CHECKING THAT ITS -wal IS ABSENT OR EMPTY; ANY OTHER OPEN OF IT REFUSES; connection_log applies the same rule. R3(i) and

sqlite3.connect(path) is refused.

(D2, HIGH) AN INNER-SEARCH FAILURE IS NO FIT FOR THAT FIT, NEVER A REFUSAL OF THE RUN. The builder's [C3-INNER] and [C3-INFO] refusals are an unregistered gate on the
DESCRIPTIVE C3 leg; they fire after C1 is computed, so one inner failure would void the whole outcome, including C1, the only barred endpoint (43 fits x 3 inner
searches exposed). R1(b) (8469780) already registers the consequence of non-convergence: "if no ddev can be computed (the fit does not converge, or b1 is unidentified),
P5 is UNDETERMINED". RULING: a failed inner re-maximisation of b0 (non-converged Brent, a scan that finds no interior optimum), and a non-finite I, make THAT FIT "NO FIT
(b1 unidentified: inner re-maximisation not resolved: <reason>)" (or "... non-finite observed information"), printed; P5 is UNDETERMINED if it is F's fit; C3 prints the
NO FIT; C1 and every other readout are unaffected. No refusal of the run arises from C3.

4 eps |l| times a 4x margin for the error of the inner re-maximisation: a MULTIPLICATIVE 4 x 4, with NO check on the inner error. The builder's additive reading
(16 - 4 = 12, INNER_MARGIN = 12, turned into a refusal) is an unregistered constant, decoupled from 16. RULING: there is NO registered check on the inner error beyond the
tight convergence already documented (Brent xtol 1e-12); the inner error estimate (g^2 / (2c)) is PRINTED AS DESCRIPTIVE beside every fit; INNER_MARGIN is removed.

For each recorded readout that the exposure touches, re-score its recorded headline statistic with the exposed questions removed and ask whether the shift lies outside the distribution of shifts produced by removing the SAME NUMBER of RANDOM non-exposed questions, matched by anchor. It is a SENSITIVITY readout: it can qualify a recorded number by insertion; it re-opens nothing and it DECIDES NOTHING about rebuild-or-disclose, which is the author's.

CLOSED LINES, CHECKED (CONTEXT.md section 5). It TOUCHES closed lines (rubric text at every granularity: RUBRIC, LADDER, RUBRIC-512-R, J6, LEAF-POWERED) but is not a variant of them: it proposes no rubric, prompt or recipe and posts nothing; it re-scores recorded verdicts. The result it could qualify, and the mechanism: a leak inflates the arm whose induction corpus held the key (the cell / leaf / anchor rubric arm), so removing exposed questions can only LOWER that arm's advantage in expectation; a FLAG in that direction qualifies the recorded number and REINFORCES the closure. A FLAG in the OPPOSITE direction on a SCOREABLE rubric cell whose de-exposed estimate leaves the recorded band (RUBRIC-512-SS / -R: above +1pp) would QUALIFY the closure sentence "induced cell rubrics are worth 0 to +1pp" by insertion; re-opening the line would still need its own registration.

READOUTS AND CRITERIA.
 (C0) VALIDITY, EVALUATED FIRST, PRE-EMPTING: each consumer's recorded headline reproduces TO THE DIGIT from its cache before any removal (the figures in (a)-(f)); the four exposed sets have 28 / 70 / 14 / 74 ids and match the data-steward's independent derivation; inputs unchanged after. A consumer that fails is UNDETERMINED (BY VALIDITY) on all its cells, excluded and listed; the others proceed.
 (C1) PER CELL, THE FLAG: FLAGGED iff the observed shift delta lies OUTSIDE the null's central 95% (below the 2.5th or above the 97.5th percentile); NOT FLAGGED otherwise. THE POINT delta AGAINST THE NULL'S QUANTILES DECIDES; there is no interval clause (rule 7). A cell with k = 0 is UNDETERMINED (BY SUPPORT). Observable that makes it FLAG at the planned n: a shift beyond the null edge, e.g. on RUBRIC-512-R x E70 about |delta| >= 0.23pp (1.96 x 0.115) against a bound of 2.05pp.
 (C2) CONSEQUENCE, DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY: per cell, whether the consumer's recorded verdict (its registered test at its registered level) is the same with and without the exposed questions; printed, deciding nothing.
 (C3) THE FAMILY READING: the count of FLAGGED cells out of the cells scored, against 13 x 0.05 = 0.65 expected under the global null (P(>= 2) = 0.14, P(>= 3) = 0.026 at 13 cells); a single FLAG is not evidence of a leak effect by itself; printed with the directions.

SUPPORT (mandatory; per cell; the planning k assumes each consumer's exposed share equals the exposed share of p2dca: 28 / 3,445 = 0.81%, 70 / 3,445 = 2.03%, 14 / 3,445 = 0.41%; the instrument prints the measured k).

Reason: the refusal names a state of a SHARED input, and a later arm writing that input destroys the evidence the remedy needs. "T1b runs regardless" (the registration's independence of arms) is read as independence of their SCORES, not a licence to run past a failed precondition on a shared input.

[RULING 2026-09-24, arena-specialist, zero calls, on ARCH-V2-G22 fresh-judge v2 (83f431b ruling 1), BEFORE any v2 run; POST-HOC-SPECIFIED with the rest of v2. (i) beta is ACCEPTABLE AS SPECIFIED: beta is unpenalised and u carries the ridge (sigma0 = 1.0), so at the MAP beta is the least-squares projection of the anchor-centred total effect (beta x keyacc + u) on keyacc; its estimand is the in-sample slope of the judge's total model preference on key accuracy, including any chance correlation of the non-quality part with keyacc, which no estimator can separate at 12 models. The "collinearity" reading came from a synthetic world whose generator u correlates -0.454 with keyacc (seed 13, 3 x 6 cells): the oracle projection there is 1.991 and beta-hat 1.998 recovers it (DEV). In board-shaped DEV synthetic worlds (14 x 12, generator beta 4.74) beta-hat is 4.41-4.77 at epsilon SD 0.34 and 4.08-4.47 at 0.80. (ii) CLARIFICATION: keyacc is MODEL-LEVEL, keyacc_m = the model's convention-A key accuracy pooled over all the anchors' judged questions (in the design legs, over the design's whole EVAL supply), broadcast to every anchor and centred per anchor over the models present. This is the subscript of the arena-specialist's ruling text and the object of the DEV diagnostic that motivated it (v_m against keyacc_m, Pearson 0.966); the insertion at 83f431b omitted the subscript. It keeps the quality term at the level of epsilon_m and of the LOMO SD, and keeps per-anchor measurement noise from small EVAL strata out of the fresh judge's per-anchor preferences. In DEV synthetic worlds the two forms differ by <= 0.08 in beta-hat. (iii) REJECTED: fitting u after beta (a two-stage estimator). It changes the likelihood, adds a knob, and the MAP already gives the projection. (iv) SELFTEST: compare beta-hat with the ORACLE PROJECTION of the generator's own total effect, never the generator's beta; board-shaped worlds (>= 12 models, >= 10 anchors), >= 3 seeds, |beta-hat - oracle| < 0.5 in each; the comment "identified only through the ridge" is corrected by bracket.
