RULING ON FINDING 1, VERBATIM (relayed by the coordinator):
[RULING 2026-09-24, judge-design-specialist, zero calls, read-only, on ARCH-V2-INDUCE-RUBRIC-1 (b44227f) finding 1, the selection defect: DEDUPLICATE BY component_id, CORRECTED BEFORE ANY CALL. (a) DEFECT, CONFIRMED on gen_view_REG.db (sha256 690d06b8…, mode=ro&immutable=1): judge_v2.induction.select_inputs iterates `variant`, whose rows are keyed (corpus_version, variant_id). 7,098 variant_ids sit in both mmlu-pro-v2 and mc6 on TRAIN. Their duplicated rows are identical in stem, options and contract (0 differ). The duplicates share the sort key sha256(seed ‖ US ‖ variant_id), so they arrive side by side, and the registered n = 40 selection carries 24 distinct variants, 16 of them shown twice. This violates the registration's intent: 40 inputs, and input_variant_ids as a set. (b) THE AMENDMENT: select_inputs collapses the candidate rows to distinct variant_id, asserting that every duplicate row is identical in (stem, options_sorted_json, contract_id) and refusing otherwise; it sorts by the UNCHANGED key sha256(seed ‖ US ‖ variant_id); it keeps the first variant of each COMPONENT (split side.component_id) until n = 40. The component is CK-CLOSE-v1's content unit: stem_key twins and family members are clustered in one component, and the split draws over components, so two inputs from one component would show the inducer the same question twice, which is the very harm the defect causes. item_id is weaker (two items of one component can be twins); variant_id is weaker still (two variants of one item). On the record the three keys select the SAME 40 (40 variants = 40 items = 40 components; sorted-set sha 32e9c7ca…; the builder's payload sha 3c0a0b08…), so the choice of key exercises no selection freedom now, and it binds every later induction. The witness prints the candidate rows, distinct variants, duplicates collapsed, and variants skipped by component. induction.py's blob pin in the registration (ae17ba25) is replaced by the amended blob, named with its hash kind; the registrar inserts the bracket that pins it. (c) STATUS: A PRE-CALL CORRECTION, NOT POST-HOC. No call was made; no reply, rubric or outcome was seen. What was seen is the selection's input list, a dry-run output the registration requires to be printed. The seed is not re-rolled and the sort key is not changed; the fix is mechanical and, on this data, does not depend on the key chosen. It is disclosed as "selection corrected before the first call (duplicate corpus rows); the registered seed kept". The falsifier and predictions are unchanged. (d) OTHER READERS IN E-J (403f897): loader.py L288 (variant lookup by variant_id) REFUSES a variant present in several corpus versions unless corpus_version is named, and its item, response and reference reads (L305, L317, L342, L350, L417) filter by corpus_version: safe. induction.check_inputs_bound L178 takes fetchone() by variant_id and is correct only because the duplicates are identical: amend it to fetch all rows and require them identical, the same assert as (b). side reads (induction L151, L202; loader L266, L310) are keyed by item_id, one row per item: safe. induce_run.py L307 (SELECT DISTINCT gt_raw, answer_text FROM response, the leak material): duplicates are harmless, safe. OUTSIDE E-J, flagged: any count or schedule over eval_view variant / item rows must name corpus_version, or it double-counts; the pilot's per-anchor question pool is mmlu-pro-v2 only, and the E-A schedule builder must filter on it.]

RULING ON FINDING 2, VERBATIM:
[RULING 2026-09-24, judge-design-specialist, zero calls, on ARCH-V2-INDUCE-RUBRIC-1 finding 2: TRANSPORT ERRORS. The builder's handling is CONFIRMED, with a limit and an accounting rule added. (a) Definition: a TRANSPORT ERROR is a call_judge_full invocation that RAISES (retries exhausted on 408, 429 or 5xx; a connection failure or timeout; a non-content-filter 4xx). It returns no model reply, so it is NOT a formal failure: the registered classes (NON_JSON, KEY, LENGTH, CONTENT_FILTER, VERBATIM) describe a reply. A content-filter 400 is returned, not raised, and stays a formal failure (rule 10). (b) Handling: a transport error STOPS the run fail-closed and does NOT consume one of the 3 attempts. It is written to the attempt log (timestamp, exception class and message, payload sha, "TRANSPORT, no reply"). A relaunch re-posts the IDENTICAL body (same payload sha, asserted); it never re-selects and never changes a byte. (c) Accounting: every errored invocation counts on the posting-day ledger (CANARY D2's unit: logical call_judge_full invocations) and is disclosed in the outcome beside the attempts. The registered ceiling of 3 applies to attempts (invocations that return a reply); errored invocations have their own limit of 3. At the 3rd transport error the run stops as UNDETERMINED BY INSTRUMENT, not by the model; the author's falsifier does not fire; a further relaunch needs a registrar bracket. A timeout after which the server may have generated text is still a transport error: nothing unseen can steer the artefact.]

THE AUTHOR'S CHOICES (main session, 2026-09-24; relayed by the coordinator; plan Amendment 20):
 (1) Question: "…840 questions were only ever answered by the quarantined Llama-3-70B model (228 of them on the evaluation side) and can never be judged. Drop them from the split entirely?" The author chose "Drop them (Recommended)". Option text: "Remove the 840 quarantined-only questions from the split universe. They can't be judged anyway, and they're the main source of the degree-symbol duplicates the old check missed. Cleaner split; changes the universe (21,384 → ~20,544 items)."
 (2) Question: "BBH (reasoning puzzles) has no natural cutoff between shared templates and real duplicates… How should the new check treat it?" The author chose "5% template mask (Recommended)". Option text: "Ignore phrases shared by more than 5% of a BBH task's questions (the templates), then merge real near-duplicates like the rest. Conservative; a stated policy choice since the data has no natural cutoff."

THE SPEC (the data-steward's draft, relayed by the coordinator; registered here before any code):
 CK-CLOSE-v2 = CK-CLOSE-v1 (all four conditions unchanged) + the universe rule U + three new closure edges P, D, O, added to the union-find in data_v2.split.compute BEFORE the strata and the draw.
 U (author choice 1): the split universe EXCLUDES every item with no corpus source_row AND no response from an ACTIVE (non-quarantined) model: 840 items on the superseded split (TRAIN 523, EVAL 228, GATE 89). The build prints the exact count and the ids' digest. df and all edges are computed over the universe AFTER U.
 UNITS: items, components, strata, the draw, the ratios 0.30 / 0.10, the rounding and the pool-id rule are EXACTLY as in data_v2 split.py. Components are formed over ALL items of the universe, on every side, before any draw: within-EVAL, within-TRAIN and cross-side families all merge, and none can straddle sides.
 TOKENS AND SHINGLES: tokens(s) = re.findall(r"\w+", s.casefold()) (= judge_v2.induction._tokens). A shingle is an exact 8-tuple of consecutive tokens; identity is exact tuple equality (an implementation may key on sha256 over the tokens joined by U+001F; Python hash() is FORBIDDEN). df(shingle) = the number of DISTINCT items of the universe (all corpora, all sides) holding it. An item's texts are its distinct variant.stem values across the build's corpora.
 EDGE P (passages in stems): items A != B are joined when some stem of A and some stem of B share a run of N = 20 or more consecutive tokens, EVERY 8-shingle of which is UNMASKED (the run lies on one diagonal of both texts). MASKING: for MMLU-Pro, GPQA, MATH, IFEval and MuSR a shingle is masked iff df > R = 6 (global); for BBH (author choice 2) a shingle is masked iff MORE THAN 5% of the items of the BBH item's own stratum (task) hold it, and the global R does not apply to BBH. The source is the item's stratum source (the modal vote).
 EDGE O (options): the same rule as P (N 20, R 6, BBH 5%), applied to each variant's options_sorted_json list joined by single spaces.
 EDGE D (the degree normaliser): a CLOSURE EDGE, NOT a key change: A and B are joined when split_side.stem_key(d(sA)) == split_side.stem_key(d(sB)) for some stems, where d first applies re.sub(r"\s*" + re.escape("\\textdegree") + r"(\{\})?\s*", "°", s) and then re.sub(r"\s*°\s*", "°", s). stem_key, the item ids and NORMALISER_VERSION stay norm-v1.
 IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT: a NEW module tools/analysis/passage_closure.py with its own PINS entry in data_v2/common.py; content_closure.py (blob 1533cb5a) and split_side.py (blob 05224b5a) are NOT edited (no re-ingest); split.py's RULE becomes "CK-CLOSE-v2".
 DETERMINISM: no seed enters the closure. DEV witness (not of record): the edge-set sha16 bd5e56db2ec18a0e under two PYTHONHASHSEED values, 0 collisions.
 PARAMETERS (DEV, measured, NOT of record): R = 6 sits on the rarity gap (2-6 vs >= 11, nothing at 7-10; counts flat from R 6 to R 10 in MMLU-Pro, MuSR, GPQA); R = 4 is too tight for MuSR. N = 20 is a POLICY CHOICE: there is no length gap; masked boilerplate (<= 41 tokens) can never reach N; the 15-19-token band (181 MMLU-Pro edges, near-variant problems) is DISCLOSED as residual. A similarity-ratio rule was tested and REJECTED (it joined different questions sharing a frame). The BBH 5% mask is a stated policy (no plateau). O is included (171 option-only edges: 121 degree twins also caught by D, 50 shared option menus). The INDUCE D1 8-token audit remains a SEPARATE per-use guard.
 EXPECTED EFFECTS (DEV-SIM, NOT of record, BEFORE U): components 21,374 -> 18,938; largest component 14 (BBH), MMLU-Pro largest 6; history 390 -> 293; multi-stratum components 34 -> 68; EVAL share 0.3001 [0.2984, 0.3027] over 20 DEV seeds; Kish (EVAL, upper bound) MMLU-Pro 1.185, BBH 1.80, MuSR 2.44. U changes these; the build prints them. RESIDUAL, DISCLOSED: the 15-19 band and the unjoined response-origin items (U removes most of them).

(a) How the slot enters, and what it would do
The rubric is not a hint; it is a criterion. judge_v2/payload.build_system (payload.py L197-L200) substitutes the rubric text verbatim into V2_SYSTEM_TEMPLATE under "Your rubric:", at the end of the system turn (GENERIC_SYSTEM persona); the template tells the judge to "CRITIQUE Model A: assess its reasoning against the rubric", and the user turn/SCHEMA ask for critiques "referencing your rubric". It is applied to both contestants' full responses. The rubric contradicts the template twice: (1) the template's bias suppression says ignore formatting ("all equal"), the rubric scores 0 for "extra text, explanations, or formatting"; (2) the template's verify-first block says a wrong final answer cannot beat a right one, the rubric says "No credit for reasoning" and puts every CoT response, right or wrong, at 0.
Predicted effect on the pilot: on answer-disagreement pairs, committed verdicts mostly inert (verify-first + reference dominate where the judge can tell which final answer is right); TIE-inflating where the judge is unsure (both score 0 → "equal"); and harmful to C1, not merely noisy: the slot's TEXT is identical for all contestants, but its EFFECT is not — it rewards a response property (terseness / closeness to a bare letter) that varies by model across the 46, so any rubric-following is a contestant-level bias correlated with style. It interacts with the causal length bias of record (+0.39/1k chars toward longer). The k=46 sub-board carries more style variety than ARENA12, so the bias need not cancel between rungs; its sign on beta is unknown. C1b (the level) is directly exposed: ties shrink |m| in cert.cbud_v, which moves the count of edges clearing THRESH 0.975.

(b) Why the inducer wrote a format spec (checked from the payload of record decoded read-only from attempts.db, mode=ro&immutable=1)
The user turn gives "Answer contract(s): MC_LETTER" (an opaque identifier with no description) and "Examples (questions only; no answers are shown)". Options are pipe-joined WITHOUT letters, in sorted order (options_sorted_json) — the model never saw an A-J label, hence "(A-Z)". No contestant response, response format or reference is shown or described. The system text says only that the rubric is for comparing "two model responses" and must fit "the type's answer contract". Given that, "output one uppercase letter" is the natural reading (96 completion tokens, finish_reason stop).
Verdict: an honest outcome of a design flaw in INDUCE-RUBRIC-1 as registered, not a run defect. The prompt (pinned shas 4c4bf36f and 7ed21eba) did not describe what the judge compares; V1-V4 were formal checks only (verbatim copy, leakage, content keys, write mode), none for fitness; the specialist's own ruling (2) (L15957-L15962) specified no fitness check. The record should say so.

(c) The options
(i) Accept + report TIE rate: DECLINED. It would put a component known to contradict the template into data meant for stage-1 reuse (ruling (3)(i)-(iii)) and G17/G21 adoption; its effect is contestant-dependent, so a TIE-rate print cannot correct it.
(ii) Empty slot as a registered deviation: DECLINED. No measured arm has an empty slot; it leaves "Your rubric:" empty under instructions to critique "against the rubric"; and it departs from the author's decision 2026-09-23 (2) (rubric re-induced from the generation side). GENERIC_RUBRIC (measured, zero cost) can only be reinstated by the author.
(iii) Re-induce under ARCH-V2-INDUCE-RUBRIC-2: ADOPTED, with this fix.
- Change only two things. INDUCTION_SYSTEM: state what the judge sees — the question with lettered options, a reference solution that may be wrong, and two full responses; responses are free-form text, usually step-by-step reasoning ending in one option letter as the final answer, and may be truncated, empty or state no letter; the rubric decides which response better answers the question — correctness of the final answer first, then soundness of the supporting reasoning; it must not reward or penalise length, formatting, or the presence or absence of an explanation. Keep the existing genericity and no-domain-facts clauses. User template: render MC_LETTER with a fixed description from the corpus CONTRACT (e.g. "one of the lettered options (A, B, C, ...); the final answer is one option letter"), taken from the MMLU-Pro protocol and the extractor, NOT from any EVAL row. The reviewer's 0-of-167,308 count is diagnostic only; the registration must not cite it as an input.

ATTEMPTS. A FORMAL FAILURE is any of: a non-JSON reply; a key other than "rubric"; finish_reason length; content_filter; the verbatim-copy refusal (any SHINGLE = 8-token run of an input stem or option); a V5 FITNESS failure (new). At most 3 attempts. ALL attempts are disclosed (reply sha, finish_reason, failure class). The FIRST VALID reply is of record; no best-of-n, no edits. Three formal failures read UNDETERMINED, and the slot goes to THE AUTHOR.
VALIDITY READOUTS. Each is scored PASS / FAIL from the files the run writes (outcome.txt, the artefact and the attempt cache); each has one deciding observable and no interval.
 V1 the verbatim audit (SHINGLE 8) of the reply of record against the 40 inputs' stems and options: FAILS if hits >= 1.
 V2 the leak check against EVAL key material (gt, answer text, other-variant references), run after the reply only: FAILS if hits >= 1. A V2 failure makes the artefact NOT OF RECORD. It is NEVER a formal failure and NEVER triggers a re-post (finding 3 (ii), L15996-L16007).
 V3 the content-key counts (refused sides by count; TRAIN only): FAILS if any selected input is not TRAIN or any EVAL hit is > 0.
 V4 the artefact written with mode x, committed, and its artefact_sha256 and rubric_sha256 pinned in the programme by the registrar: FAILS if the write is not mode x or the file is not committed.
 V5 FITNESS (NEW; zero calls; deterministic; checked on EVERY reply BEFORE it can be of record): (a) the rubric NAMES FINAL-ANSWER CORRECTNESS: at least one match of a registered "correctness" regex (for example final answer|correct (answer|option|choice)); AND (b) it matches NONE of a registered list of FORM-CONDITIONING regexes (for example no other text, extra text, (exactly|single) (one )?(uppercase )?letter, only the letter, \(a-z\), lowercase). The builder pins the exact regexes (case-insensitive rule stated) in the instrument, and the registrar pins their sha256 before the READY. FAILS if (a) has 0 matches or (b) has >= 1 match. A V5 failure is a FORMAL FAILURE: it consumes one of the 3 attempts and is disclosed with the matching pattern. The READY reviewer ALSO reads the rubric of record for fitness. **RULING**

OLD: `The judge sees the question with its lettered options, a reference solution that may be wrong, and the two responses in full. `

NEW: `The judge sees the question text without its options list, a reference solution that may be wrong (given as one option letter with that option's text), and the two responses in full, each followed, when its chosen letter can be read, by that letter with its option's text. `

- Keep the trailing space. The next sentence ("The responses are free-form text, … may state no letter.") stays as it is. The judge sees a placeholder rather than an empty string, but "may be … empty, or may state no letter" is still a true description of what the rubric must handle.

**Q2. The examples: keep them pipe-joined, in sorted order, unlettered**
- After Q1 the system text makes no claim about options being shown, so there is no contradiction.
- The contract description ("one of the lettered options (A, B, C, ...); the final answer is one option letter") describes the answer contract, and it is true.

**Q3. The MCQ-specific system text: add a guard, not a note**

**V5: probe evidence (zero calls; the builder's `induce_fitness.v5` at a02a9c1; REGEX_LIST_SHA256 cfcb9ca4… verified equal to the pin)**

Unfit rubrics. The builder's gate gives INDUCE-1 = FAIL (7 hits, as the selftest says) and **every one of B1-B11 = PASS**. Texts, exactly as probed:
- B1 "The final answer must be a single letter matching an option. Score 1 if the response is one letter and nothing else. Score 0 for a wrong letter, several letters, or any added commentary."
- B2 "Score 1 if the final answer is correct and the response consists solely of the option letter. Any reasoning, commentary or working lowers the score to 0."
- B3 "1. Check the final answer against the correct option.\n2. Penalize any response that includes reasoning or an explanation."
- B4 "1. The correct answer wins.\n2. When both are correct, prefer the response that states just its answer letter without elaboration."
- B5 "1. Final answer correctness first.\n2. Among correct responses, the more concise response wins."
- B6 "Score 1 if the final answer is exactly one letter (A-J) with no additional text; otherwise 0."
- B7 "1. Correct final answer first.\n2. If tied, the shorter response wins."
- B8 "Correct final answer wins; do not penalize length, but penalize extra text."
- B9 "Score 1 only if the final answer is correct AND the response follows the required answer format (a bare letter). Responses with explanations violate the format and score 0."
- B10 "Score 1 if the response is a capital letter only and the final answer is correct."
- B11 "The ideal response outputs one option letter as its final answer. Score 0 (incorrect) if: wrong or missing letter, multiple letters, or explanations." (INDUCE-1 with its literal trigger words removed.)

Fit rubrics. The builder's gate PASSES F0 (CONTROL_FIT_TEXT), F1, F3, F4 and F5, and **FAILS F2** (reward_form on "Do not prefer shorter"). Texts:
- F1 "1. Extract each response's final answer.\n2. The response with the correct final answer wins; the reference may be wrong, so verify it.\n3. If both are correct or both wrong, prefer the one with fewer reasoning errors or unsupported steps; else TIE.\n4. Length, formatting and explanations neither help nor hurt."
- F2 "A correct final answer beats a wrong or missing one. When final answers tie, penalize reasoning errors. Do not prefer shorter or longer responses."
- F3 "Judge the final answer first: does the chosen option letter match the correct option? Then assess whether the reasoning is valid. A bare correct letter ties a correct worked answer."
- F4 "1. A response that is empty, truncated or states no letter has no final answer and loses to any correct final answer.\n2. Compare final answers with the correct option; verify the reference.\n3. If both final answers are correct, the response with sounder reasoning wins; if equally sound, TIE."
- F5 "Each response commits to a single letter as its final answer; only the letter it commits to is compared with the correct option. Then weigh the soundness of the reasoning."

**On the builder's specific choices**
- **exact_single_letter** requires uppercase or capital. The narrowing is fine for the contract wording, but alone it lets B1 and B6 through. It is kept, with the exclusivity pattern below added beside it.
- **only_the_letter** requires an output verb. It lets B2 ("consists solely of") and B10 (the postposed "letter only") through. It is kept; (c) catches both.
- **no_credit_reasoning** catches only the phrase "no credit for".
- **penalise_form**: the object list lacks bare "explanation(s)", commentary, elaboration, "additional/other text", and "includes reasoning" (B3, B8, B9, B11). The verb list lacks score 0, lowers, violates, loses and fails.
- **reward_form** lacks concise, brief, terse and shorter, and misses the reversed word order "the shorter response wins" (B5, B7).
- **Negation guard.**
  - (1) The disclosed KNOWN LIMIT is real (B8 passes): a cue in one half of a contrastive clause excuses the other half.
  - (2) A defect not disclosed: the CUE has no "do not prefer" or "do not favour", so a rubric that DISCLAIMS brevity (F2) fails V5 and burns an attempt. With only 3 attempts, that risks a spurious UNDETERMINED sent to the author.

**Required changes before READY**
1. **(c), a new REQUIRED clause: a positive reasoning criterion.** At least one match of a reasoning-quality term within 60 characters, in either order and inside one clause (no . ; ! ? or newline in between), of a reasoning noun.
   - Reasoning-quality terms: sound*, valid*, rigo(u)r*, coheren*, error(s), mistake(s), flaw*, unsupported, gap(s), justif*, logic*.
   - Reasoning nouns: reasoning, step(s), derivation(s), argument(s), working, logic.
   - This is fidelity to the registered instruction ("then soundness of the supporting reasoning"), not a new criterion.
   - In the probe, (c) ALONE fails all 12 unfit texts (B0-B11) and passes all 6 fit texts (F0-F5). It is the most robust single addition, because a format spec does not describe reasoning quality.
2. **Split guard clauses at contrastive conjunctions** (\bbut\b, \bhowever\b, \bwhereas\b, \byet\b), so that B8 FAILS.
3. **Add to CUE:** `\b(?:do|does|must|should|will|may)\s+not\s+(?:prefer|favou?r)\w*`, `\bnot\s+(?:be\s+)?preferred\b` and `\bneither\s+helps?\s+nor\s+hurts?\b`, so that F2 PASSES.
4. **Widen the guarded penalty family.**
   - Verbs: add score\w*\s*(?:0|zero), lowers?, violat\w*, loses?, fails?.
   - Objects: add explanations?, commentary, elaboration, working, (additional|extra|added|other)\s+(text|words|content|output), and (includ|contain|add|provid|show)\w*\s+(any\s+|an?\s+)?reasoning(?!\s+(errors?|mistakes?|flaws?|gaps?)).
   - Widen the guarded reward family to objects (more\s+)?concise, brief*, terse*, short*, minimal, "without elaboration", with the verbs wins?, prefer*, favo(u)r*, reward*, better, higher, in either order within the clause.
5. **Add an unguarded EXCLUSIVITY pattern.** "letter(s)" followed within 60 characters by nothing else | no (additional|other|further|extra|added) \w+ | solely | by itself | alone; or (solely|just) … letter. Do NOT include a bare "only": it trips the contract wording in F5, as probed.
6. **Pin the probe corpus.** Put B1-B11 (must FAIL) and F1-F5 (must PASS), verbatim as above, into induce_run_2_selftest beside C-V5-neg (ef9c9e87) and C-V5-pos (CONTROL_FIT_TEXT). Any miss refuses the READY. The regex list sha is re-pinned by the registrar after the builder's change.
   - My scratch prototype of (1) plus (3)-(5), layered on the builder's gate, gave FAIL on all of B0-B11 and PASS on F0, F1, F3, F4 and F5. F2 failed only on the builder's own reward_form, which fix (3) addresses. The builder writes the final regexes; the corpus is the acceptance test.
7. **Scope statement for the record.** A lexical gate is a screen and cannot be complete. The registered fitness read by the reviewer stays the backstop. A post-run reading of UNFIT makes the artefact NOT ADOPTED and sends the slot to the author. It is never a fourth attempt: a re-roll decided by a human reviewer would be best-of-n.

**Consequences for the record**
- Re-pin INDUCTION_SYSTEM's sha, the payload's sha, the induction.py blob and REGEX_LIST_SHA256, by bracket, as READY-stage pre-call corrections.
- The pilot's C0(c) re-derivation, already owed, covers the induction.py change.
- None of this needs the author.

**What this does NOT show**
- That a V5 PASS means a rubric is fit. The gate is lexical and the probe corpus is mine, not exhaustive.
- Anything about any rubric's effect on verdicts.
- The final regex text: the builder writes it and the READY reviewer checks it against the pinned corpus.

> ### (b) Effect on C1
> **A pick-only contestant is disadvantaged relative to its correctness, even when the reference is correct.** The data object is GROK-CALIB (grok_calib.db, 9,142 grok verdicts, x12 schedule; every match carries the grok-reasoning reference). I joined it to `eval_results` by (question_id, model_name). I used key-decidable matches only (one side correct). "Short" means a trace under 40 characters; nearly all are "The answer is (X)", which the loader's RESOLVED injection turns into option text, the closest analogue of record to the placeholder. "Long" means 300 characters or more. Intervals are question-clustered bootstraps, B 2,000, seed 42.
>
> | Matches where the reference is correct | n / questions | judge credits the correct side (C) | wrong side (W) | TIE (T) |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | long correct vs long wrong | 2,307 / 1,180 | 0.926 | 0.020 | 0.054 |
> | SHORT correct vs long wrong | 115 / 89 | 0.678 | 0.052 | 0.270 |
> | long correct vs SHORT wrong | 36 / 32 | 1.000 | 0 | 0 |
>
> - The short-correct penalty is **−0.248 [−0.345, −0.148]**, mostly converted into TIEs.
> - When the reference is wrong, the penalty is similar: −0.240 [−0.327, −0.136].
> - So the short side loses credit when it is right and loses anyway when it is wrong. That pushes its board position below its key position.
> - **Other evidence of record:**
>   - TRACE-TRUNCATION (f5676d4; MATH; exact checker reference): truncating the correct side cost 0.069 [0.039, 0.100]. It too is almost all TIEs (26:5).
>   - With no reference, the archive Math run (Mistral-Large-3 judge, the same kind of stub) picked the side with text 863 of 868 times (99.4%), whatever the key said.
>   - About 71% of v2 EVAL variants carry no reference (review M2). For those, the no-reference number is the relevant precedent.
> - **The effect is confined to k 46.** The 6 are in 255 of 1,035 pairs per anchor and 0 of the 66 ARENA12 pairs; the 9 are in 369. ARENA12's own exposure is arx_0314, with 18.9% short outputs, and it sits on both rungs.
> - **So it cannot cancel in β. Its sign on ν(46) is unknown.** Two things pull in opposite directions:
>   - pushing the 6 far down creates confident edges;
>   - penalty-compressed edges between strong text-less models (gpt4o, opus, sonnet-3.5) and mid-board models add nominal.
> - It also feeds ties into |m| (cert.cbud_v), so C1b is directly exposed.
>
> ### (c) The options
> - **(i) Keep and disclose: refused.** A bias of known presence and unknown sign sits on only one of the two rungs of the primary. The pilot would measure ν for a board the engine itself refuses to load, and the bias would carry into stage-1 reuse.
> - **(iii) Exclude their matches from the C1 readout: refused.** The BT fit of the other 40 is shifted by their matches with the 6. And a k 46 board with 6 edgeless models is really k 40 paid for at about 1,020 extra matches (about 2,040 calls).
> - **(iv) Repair: right in principle, wrong for this pilot.**
>   - It needs a new ingest source (the zips are outside the sealed manifest), a re-sealed corpus_v2 / eval_view / gen_view, and re-pinning of e35b7518 and the manifest 912eaa5f. That is a rebind and so an author decision.
>   - It needs a rule for the sonnet duplicates.
>   - After the repair, flash probably fails the engine's substantive-text bar anyway.
>   - Queue it as its own registered item. It can readmit models at stage 1 under a new roster decision.
> - **(ii) Drop: recommended.** Recomputed with the amendment's own planning constants, which reproduce the registered 0.26 / 0.73 at k 46:
>   - **k 40:** 780 pairs; M bar 2.0512; SE_dec 0.279 after the 1.25 inflation; MDE 0.78 against a P-M separation of 0.99, so SCOREABLE. 3,120 matches, 6,240 calls.
>   - **k 37:** 666 pairs; M bar 2.0529; SE 0.293; MDE 0.82 against 0.99, so SCOREABLE with a thinner margin. 2,664 matches, 5,328 calls.
>   - **k 46, for comparison:** 4,140 matches, which needed the trim.
>   - Both options are under 4,000 matches and the 8,000-call cap, and no trim is needed apart from exhausted pairs.
>   - The amendment must re-register:
>     - the M bar at the new k (P stays 1.06);
>     - ln(k/12) in β;
>     - the roster sha and the "12 inside the roster" C0 assert;
>     - the fact that the stage-1 roster equals the pilot's (the reuse condition);
>     - C2 printing short-output counts per model (under 40 characters and empty).
>   - The CV at k 40 / 37 (0.195 / 0.20) is my interpolation, a planning value only.
>
> ### (d) Whose decision?
> The author's, plainly. k is the board-size variable. The pilot exists to measure ν at the roster's k for the board-size question, and its verdicts become stage-1 data only if the roster is unchanged. So choosing 46, 40 or 37 is a board-size decision. (iv) also touches the rebind-or-disclose decision on the view of record. No option goes over 4,000 matches.
>
> ### What this does NOT show
> - The effect on grok under GENERIC_SYSTEM with the author's rubric slot. The table above is the x12 STACK-v2 recipe with the anchor rubric, and every match carries a reference.
> - The size or sign of the effect on β or ν. Nothing was judged.
> - That the zip `response` / `rationale` texts are the models' true original outputs. It looks that way from samples; it was not verified against a publisher's record.
> - A clean placeholder test. The short-side sample is mostly arx_0314 (105 of 115 reference-correct short-correct matches), so model and format are confounded.
> - Anything about the no-reference cell under grok.
>

THE REGISTERED FITNESS READING — CHECKLIST. Performed by the post-run reviewer; the judge-design-specialist reads independently and blind to the reviewer's result. Render the FULL system turn with payload.build_system(load_rubric(artefact)), the user turn (rejudge_grok USER_TEMPLATE) and SCHEMA_INSTRUCTION; read in full; walk each item against three code-rendered cases with no EVAL text: (i) reference-bearing match; (ii) reference-NONE match; (iii) one side the robust_trace placeholder. Each item CLEAR or FOUND with quoted rubric text and the template clause it meets.
K1 (U1) any clause defining a correct/wrong final answer by agreement with the reference, or making the reference decisive: FOUND = UNFIT.
K1b (converse) any clause telling the judge to ignore/distrust the reference by default, or to let its own working override the reference whenever they disagree (re-weights verify-first the other way): FOUND = UNFIT.
K2 (U2) in correctness-tied matches (both right OR both wrong), a response favoured for having reasoning/explanation or its depth/thoroughness/fullness, or a bare letter/placeholder penalised for none: FOUND = UNFIT.
K2b (absence reward; INDUCE-1 and C2 D1-D3) brevity reward; anti-explanation/anti-reasoning rule incl. one excused by "ignore/regardless of"; format demand incl. one not built on "letter": FOUND = UNFIT.
K2c (placeholder walk, case iii) the rubric makes a bare/placeholder response win or lose AUTOMATICALLY on a correctness tie beyond the template's "fewer errors or unsupported steps": FOUND = UNFIT; a mere restatement records the inherited property (a bare letter contains no errors) as a DISCLOSURE.
K3 (U2) TIE restricted to identical, forbidden, discouraged, or narrower than the template's "If neither has any, output TIE" and the user turn's "genuinely equivalent -> TIE": FOUND = UNFIT.
K3b (over-tie) TIE directed where the template directs a preference (both right, one with fewer errors/unsupported steps): FOUND = UNFIT.
K4 (M1) any positional default or order-dependent criterion: FOUND = UNFIT; names other than Model A/B WITHOUT a default: MEDIUM, disclosed.
K5 (M2) on case (ii) every criterion defined? correctness criterion undefined without a reference: UNFIT; any other undefined criterion: MEDIUM, disclosed.
K6 (L4) any criterion about options the judge is not shown: LOW, disclosed.
K7 (template walk) each clause of V2_SYSTEM_TEMPLATE, the user turn and SCHEMA_INSTRUCTION in turn (bias suppression; evaluation order A, then B, compare, decide; verify-first; both-right rule "a short correct response ties a long correct response"; confidence lines; "reasoning quality … logical rigour and domain soundness"; TIE confidence <= 0.5; JSON output shape): any CONTRADICTION = UNFIT; a restatement is CLEAR.
K8 (L4 of the -2 READY) an output-format instruction to the judge conflicting with SCHEMA_INSTRUCTION = UNFIT; a merely redundant echo = LOW.
VERDICT RULE: FIT iff no item reads UNFIT in EITHER reading; if the readers disagree on any UNFIT item the reading is UNFIT (conservative), both recorded. MEDIUM/LOW disclosed, not by themselves UNFIT. UNFIT -> NOT ADOPTED. RULE 1: any EVAL-side number a reader computes is a post-run DIAGNOSTIC, never an input to any future induction. ## 1. The question

The registration (L13064-L13067) defines five classes. It defines UNCERTIFIABLE as "neither raw text nor a combined column". D7 (L14201-L14246) prints P4 under five reasons: R1 the registered definition, R2 combiner not verified, R3 call-site argument not verified, R4 duplicate key, and R5 a pair outside the registered pairs. The code has a sixth, RX. It fires when a stored vote label is neither a position ("Model A" / "Model B"), nor TIE / INVALID / NULL, nor a contestant name that the instrument's name profile can map to an order-1 position. RX was never registered, ruled or READY-examined. The question: what class does a unit get when some or all of its stored labels are unresolvable, and how is that class printed and counted?

## 2. The ruling

R-1 RX IS ADMITTED AS THE SIXTH REASON OF UNCERTIFIABLE, BY INSERTION, ON THE PRECEDENT OF D4 (duplicate key, L14221-L14225). Code R6. Label: "stored labels unresolvable (a name-profile gap: instrument knowledge, not frame)". The literal "RX" and the label "OTHER ... outside the five, for the registrar" are retired. P4 is printed under SIX reasons. A cache is counted under each reason its tables carry (unchanged).

R-2 THE TRIGGER IS ANY UNRESOLVABLE LABEL, NOT ZERO RESOLVED ROWS. A dual-order unit is UNCERTIFIABLE (R6) if ONE OR MORE stored labels on its deciding tally are unresolvable. The deciding tally is:
- for LONG, the rows under the registered pair;
- for a WIDE unit decided by E-COMB, the combined column.

This holds whatever the parse of the row. The count and the resolved-subset tally are printed beside as DESCRIPTIVE. They decide nothing. This replaces the build's `n2_inf == 0` condition. It closes abf4db5 D4 (a table "certified" on a silently shrunk denominator). The registered bar is 100% of informative rows. A row whose parse is decisive but whose stored label cannot be placed is an informative row that has not been checked. A certificate over the rest is a certificate over a subset the registration did not name.

R-3 PRECEDENCE: MIXED BEFORE R6, AND R6 BEFORE CERTIFIED OR AMBIGUOUS. The resolved rows are evaluated first. The unit is MIXED, with MIXED's registered consequence, if they show either of these:
- an order-1 contradiction; or
- an order-2 contradiction under both hypotheses.

A contradiction on a resolved row is frame evidence, and an unresolved row elsewhere cannot cancel it. R6 applies only when the resolved rows are themselves consistent (CERTIFIED-* or AMBIGUOUS on the resolved subset). This corrects a defect of the merged build: at `n2_inf == 0` it overwrites an order-1 MIXED with UNCERTIFIABLE (the override follows `order1_note` without checking the class). On the record it is not exercised: the one RX unit of c731836 had order-1 0/0.

R-4 R6 IS NOT AMBIGUOUS AND NOT A REFUSAL.
- NOT AMBIGUOUS: the registered AMBIGUOUS means "both hypotheses reproduce, e.g. every informative row degenerate", and the structural leg (L13090) makes it "AMBIGUOUS AT ANY BUDGET". An R6 row is not degenerate. Its raw parse discriminates, and only the instrument's name map is missing. The condition is cured by instrument knowledge, not by budget. AMBIGUOUS would also remove the unit from P4's count. That would hide the gap rather than print it. The build's current path (AMBIGUOUS overridden to UNCERTIFIABLE) is therefore kept in direction and given a registered name.
- NOT A REFUSAL OF THE RUN: E2 requires every enumerated cache to carry exactly one class, and the registration requires exclusion "only through the certificate class". A run-level refusal on one unmapped file would make E2 unscoreable for the other 61. It would also turn a per-cache gap into a census failure.
- NOT MIXED: MIXED asserts row-level frame contradiction and flags consumer readouts for re-read. An unresolvable label gives no frame evidence (the D4 reasoning, verbatim in substance).

R-5 AN R6 UNIT IS EXCLUDED FROM EVERY INDEX BY CLASS, IS COUNTED IN P4's TOTAL, AND IS PRINTED ON ITS OWN LINE. The outcome must state whether P4 is carried by R6. Like the pin-timing case of R2, an R6 is "UNCERTIFIABLE by instrument knowledge, not by frame", and no reader may take it for a frame problem. The cure is a name profile, keyed by content or by writer. That profile is a change to a READY blob and needs a delta READY. It is never a hand exclusion.

R-6 THE WIDE SECONDARY (an E-COMB tally beside a deciding E-RAW):
- If it carries unresolvable labels, it is printed as "UNCERTIFIABLE (R6), secondary, n resolved of m informative". It is never printed as CERTIFIED.
- Its resolved rows keep ONE power, the power to downgrade. If they certify the OTHER frame, the EVIDENCE CONFLICT -> MIXED rule applies as now. If they are MIXED, the WARNING applies as now.
- A resolved-subset agreement is never cited as corroboration.
- The secondary never enters uncert_breakdown or P4 (unchanged: only primary units are counted).

R-7 FAIL CLOSED, NO DEFAULT REASON. An UNCERTIFIABLE unit without a reason code is an instrument defect. The run REFUSES. uncert_breakdown's default `u.get("uncert_reason", "RX")` is removed.

R-8 THE SHARED READER. unit_votes (vote_frame_cert.py, used by position_index_all.py) may not drop a match silently. Under R-2 a CERTIFIED unit has 0 unresolvable labels on its paired rows by construction. A `None` at read time can therefore only mean drift between certificate and reading, for example a source constant (arena13.NEW, placebo_entry.GEM) edited after the certificate. On a None the reader REFUSES, naming the unit and the first key. It does not `continue`.

R-9 DESCRIPTOR. An R6 unit's `label_space` reads "unresolved" (abf4db5 D5). It does not read "positions".

Both arms get byte-identical prompts. Secondary: does the gain differ across JudgeBench's four categories? "Specialised" here means test-time reasoning, not domain specialisation. No domain-specialised judge is tested.

   The paper's scoring is dual order: "A>B + A=B" counts as A>B, and inconsistent answers or two ties count as wrong. That is more lenient than our combine_orders, which scores any disagreement between the orders, including tie vs decided, as TIE.

On its own Table 3 the thinking gain is structurally compressed on HARD (about 0 to +10pp) and large on EASY (about +20 to +30pp). UNPARSED means parse INVALID, finish_reason length (NON_TERMINATED), content_filter, or the STOP-TRUNCATION class (finish_reason stop with no parseable JSON verdict; the 4.5% class of REF-FORM-BY-CELL). The guard prints its count and bar on every run. It REFUSES above 5%, i.e. at 2 or more of an arm's 24 pilot posts.

SUPPORT (the specialist's; the arithmetic is shown).
 Deciding denominator: 350 JudgeBench GPT-split pairs. One pair per unique question (350 unique question strings, verified). The two orders collapse to one verdict per pair and arm. The unit is the pair.
 DEFF 1.00 (source: structure; no question carries two pairs in this split). n_eff = 350.
 Paired SE = sqrt((d - delta^2) / n), where d is the discordant-pair rate (planning 0.33; range 0.25-0.40). Sources for d: it is at least |delta|; J1 against Mistral on MMLU-Pro was 121 / 946 = 0.128 at a 7.5pp gap; JudgeBench pairs sit near 0.5 accuracy, so discordance is higher.
   At delta 0.11, d 0.33: SE = sqrt(0.3179 / 350) = 0.0301. MDE (80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05) = 2.80 x 0.0301 = 8.4pp (range 7.3-9.3pp over d 0.25-0.40).
   C1's decision needs point >= 5.7pp and p < 0.05, so power is governed by the 8.4pp MDE (above the floor). The predicted +12pp exceeds the MDE: C1 is SCOREABLE.
 C2 INTERACTION: SE = sqrt(0.33 x (1/140 + 1/210)) = 0.0627, MDE 17.5pp (15.3-19.3). The predicted +15pp is INSIDE the MDE, so the interaction is DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY, as registered.
   The difficulty contrast: SE = sqrt(0.33 x (1/252 + 1/98)) = 0.0684, MDE 19.1pp; predicted about +2pp; DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY.
   Per category (MDE at d 0.33): knowledge 13.0 / reasoning 16.2 / math 21.5 / coding 24.8pp; DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY. The bill's 10-14pp was optimistic.
   Adding the Claude split (620 pairs, 91 shared questions, DEFF about 1.1) brings the interaction MDE to about 13.6pp. That is still at or near the prediction, so the key question is DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY at any size this side test can afford.

H1 (HIGH) AND THE ORCHESTRATOR'S DECISION:
 - THE FINDING (the review's "## Findings", H1): the screen rejects natural negated restatements of S6-S9, and each rejection burns one of three attempts. Held-out: fit_neg FP 5/14 under jv2-v5-4 vs 0/14 under jv2-v5-3. The reviewer's POST-HOC probes (written after reading the regexes, so adversarially biased and NOT held-out) show the same class on direct echoes of the prompt: "Never default to Model A or Model B" fires f:positional_by_default (the adjacency guard knows "not" / "n't", not "never"); "A response is not favoured merely for giving more reasoning, nor penalised merely for giving none" fires e:presence_reward and e:depth_reward; "No preference or penalty merely for giving no reasoning or more reasoning" fires e:depth_reward; "A correct final answer is not one that merely matches the reference" and "An answer that disagrees with the reference is not wrong for that reason" fire d1:agree_with_reference. 5 of 12 S7 paraphrases FAIL; 2 of 3 simulated full replies in the -2 reply's style FAIL. The reviewer's estimate: a per-attempt V5 rejection of plausibly 0.2-0.4 on echo-style replies, against the ~0.1 implied by P1 = 0.70; attempts are correlated (same body). It is a design risk the registration accepted, not a build defect; the READY is not refused.
 - THE OPTIONS OFFERED: (A) run as registered (a burn lands on the pre-decided GENERIC_RUBRIC, never on an unfit artefact); (B) before any call, register a narrow amendment of the regexes (add "never" to the (f) negation lookbehinds; allow "not <participle> merely", "nor <participle> merely" and "no preference or penalty" in the (e) cue; allow "not wrong / can still be correct ... differs from the reference" in the (d1) cue). (B) costs a new list sha, re-pins and a delta READY, and it SPENDS the held-out set: any later re-score is in-sample. The reviewer: "(B) is cheap (zero calls) and protects the author's chosen route; (A) is what was registered. Not my call."
 - THE DECISION: THE ORCHESTRATOR CHOSE (A), RUN AS REGISTERED (relayed to the registrar 2026-09-25; the merge message 0b512e3 carries it). Its reasons, as relayed: (1) two prior rounds showed that regex tuning on non-blind probes does not generalise (the -2 build: 0/0 in-sample, then FP 11% / FN 76% on its held-out set, L16477-L16503); (2) (B) would tune on the reviewer's own biased probes and would spend the held-out set; (3) the worst case of (A) is the author's pre-decided GENERIC_RUBRIC fallback, never an unfit artefact; (4) every attempt's text is disclosed (reply sha, finish_reason, class, V5 legs and patterns), so a falsely burned fit reply stays visible to the author.
 - STANDING OF THE DECISION: taken by the ORCHESTRATOR under the author's night authorisation of 2026-09-25 (quoted at L17333: "You can register tests for the whole night like the last big session if you identify new good relevent onces you can start them as long as they are not too expensive"). IT IS NOT AN AUTHOR DECISION. It changes no registered text, pin or prediction: P1 stays 0.70 as registered and is scored at the outcome as registered. First, determine the correct option letter by independently solving the question, using the reference solution (if provided) only as one possibly erroneous input among others. Correctness of final answer is primary: prefer the response matching the judge's correct letter; TIE if both match or neither does. If final answers differ in correctness, the correct one wins regardless of reasoning. If both correct or both incorrect, compare reasoning quality only: prefer the one with fewer factual errors, logical gaps, or unsupported steps; TIE if reasoning error counts are equal. Ignore length, formatting, or presence/absence of explanation. Responses may end with a clear letter choice (possibly followed by option text), state no letter, or be truncated/empty (noted as selecting none or a letter). Call verdict 'A', 'B', or 'TIE'."

### 0. The claim, and why it is new
CLAIM UNDER TEST: on LCB v6 (1,055 problems, AtCoder / LeetCode / Codeforces), with regions = cells of an anchor-free, label-free tree built on TRAIN problem texts only, the (model, problem) pass rates carry a model x region interaction that (G1) survives a family-block permutation null after absorbing each problem’s difficulty AND each model’s difficulty slope, within input-format x difficulty strata, and (G2) produces order reversals of practical size (>= 5pp legs each way, i.e. a >= 10pp difference-in-differences) beyond what the null produces.
Why it matters: the author’s question (does a SPECIALISED judge beat the GENERIC judge on hard regions) is only askable where models excel on different regions; the eventual judged stage (~8.5k cce for a 10pp DiD, NOT part of this stage) is costed for exactly the G2 size. STAGE 0 decides whether that stage is registered at all.
Rule-4 statement (closed lines, CONTEXT.md §5): this reopens NOTHING closed. It is not a rubric, reference, sub-anchor profile, frontier order, escalation, order or temperature test; no judge is involved. Nearest record lines, all read and not contradicted by this design: (a) PROFILE-TREE-ROBUST / KEY-SUBANCHOR-SCALE (sub-anchor profiles closed): distinguished — new corpus, NO anchors, an executed checker as the key, and regions coarsened to >= 130 TRAIN problems (anchor-scale support, not sub-anchor); (b) TOPIC-PARTITION-20NG C1 FAILED (tree no better a partition than k-means at matched k): hence the k-means comparator below, and no "tree beats k-means" claim is registered as a criterion; (c) MC-LEAF / ROUTER-CLEAN-POLICY (leaves do not beat declared domains; the tree adds split discipline and support, not accuracy): hence the format x difficulty comparator; (d) PROFILE-RELIABILITY-INTERACTION (a logit-additive null carries an accuracy-scale interaction from curvature): hence the statistic is on the logit scale with a slope term, and the practical criterion is an order reversal, which no monotone link can manufacture; (e) the R2 atlas / crossdomain interaction (model x domain interaction on MMLU-Pro designed domains, p_perm 0.002): a different corpus, designed domains, judged board — not a test of text-derived regions on code.

### 4. The interaction test
Data object: TRAIN problems x eligible models; ybar_mp as in D5. Denominator: INFORMATIVE TRAIN problems (0 < sum_m ybar_mp < M); the count is printed with the all-pass and all-fail counts beside it. Cluster = family (H1); sensitivity cluster = family ∪ contest_id (union-find).
NULL FIT (never sees the regions): the rank-1 "difficulty-slope" model logit pi_mp = a_m + s_m * delta_p (delta_p free per problem, standardised), a unit-weight fractional-logit (quasi-binomial) fit. Rasch (s_m = 1) is REFUSED as the primary null. In synthetic worlds with NO topic interaction but 2PL slope heterogeneity (SD 0.5 in log units), Rasch + platform x difficulty strata rejects at 0.32 at alpha 0.01, a GO for difficulty rather than for branches. Rank-1 + the strata below holds 0.053 / 0.020 at 0.05 / 0.01 (arena-specialist, scratchpad lcb_s0/sim_null2_*.json, 300 worlds, SYNTHETIC). [AMENDED 2026-09-25, BEFORE ANY OUTCOME IS INGESTED, by the LCB-STAGE0 build ruling (arena-specialist; zero calls; synthetic evidence only): THE REGISTERED FIT HAS NO FINITE OPTIMUM ON THIS ROSTER. Maximised jointly over a_m, s_m and a free delta_p with no penalty (joint ML), a model with binary outcomes (an n = 1 file) whose row is nearly ordered by difficulty drives s_m to infinity while the delta_p re-order to separate it. On roster-shaped synthetic worlds (16 n = 1, 9 n = 10, 1 n = 4 files; ~630 TRAIN problems) the build's fit_rank1 fails in 67/600 base, 34/300 twin-heavy, 204/300 slope and 286/300 strong-slope null worlds, and in 22/40 base GATE fits. THE NULL FIT OF RECORD IS THEREFORE THE MARGINAL RANK-1 FIT: logit pi_mp = a_m + s_m x_p, with x_p ~ N(0, 1) integrated out per problem (41-node Gauss-Hermite quadrature on N(0, 1); EM with a Newton M-step on (a_m, s_m); rows at unit weight, quasi-binomial, as registered), s_m > 0, and a Gaussian prior of SD 1.0 on log s_m around the roster's mean log-slope. pihat_mp = E[pi_mp | Y_p], the posterior mean of pi_mp over the quadrature nodes given problem p's model vector. U_mk, I_mk and T are computed from this pihat exactly as registered. The fit never sees the regions. It is CONVERGED iff the max |gradient| of the penalised marginal log-likelihood over (a_m, s_m) is < 1e-6 and every |a_m| and s_m is <= 50; the support block's "rank-1 fit converged" reads this, printed with the iteration count and max s_m. The same fit, refitted on each data object, serves S1, S2, S3, Z1, Z2, R-REP (each side), the Delta-D base and the common null of section 6. The Rasch fit (dhat and T under Rasch) is unchanged. The build's joint fit is printed beside as a diagnostic (converged: yes/no, and its p_T when it converged) and never decides. WHY THE MARGIN: difficulty treated as random cannot be re-ordered to separate one model's row (the standard cure for the inconsistency of joint 2PL estimates); it converged in 3,850/3,850 roster-shaped TRAIN fits (1,500 null, 1,600 power at M = 26, 300 at M = 25, 450 diagnostic) and in 119/120 GATE and 120/120 first-sample fits. WHY THE PRIOR: without it, the marginal fit still fails in 105/300 strong-slope null worlds and in 11/40 slope-world GATE fits; with it, 0 failures on TRAIN and 1 in 120 GATE fits across the three families. It binds only at the extremes: in every base-null world p_T with and without the prior differs by <= 0.013 and the G1 decision is identical (600/600). Where the registered joint fit does converge, it agrees with the amended fit (p_T correlation 0.968-0.985; G1 decisions agree in 99.2-100% of worlds). ALTERNATIVES REFUSED: a ridge or lognormal prior on s inside the joint fit (finite but degenerate: s = 65 at SD 0.5 in a slope world); one shared slope for the n = 1 files (converges, but gives up the slope absorption for 16 of 26 models: G1 size 0.099 at 0.01 in strong-slope worlds, Rasch 0.123).] [CORRECTED 2026-09-25 (build ruling): those figures were measured with core.fit_2pl at a FIXED 80 iterations and never checked for convergence (an early-stopped joint fit, an implicit regulariser), not with the registered estimator, and at M = 35 with half the files at n = 10. At the real roster shape under the amended fit (B = 2,000, K = 4) G1 rejects at 0.01 in 9/600 base (0.015, CP95 0.007-0.028), 6/300 twin-heavy (0.020, 0.007-0.043), 2/300 slope (0.007, 0.001-0.024) and 1/300 strong-slope (0.003, 0.000-0.018) null worlds; pooled 18/1500 = 0.012 (CP95 0.007-0.019; P(X >= 18 | alpha = 0.01) = 0.25). At 0.05, G1 alone rejects at 0.075 (base) and 0.077 (twin-heavy): mildly liberal, and read only at its registered 0.01. The joint GO size is 2/600, 2/300, 0/300 and 1/300 (each CP95 upper <= 0.024).]
G1 STATISTIC (Rao score): U_mk = sum_{p in P_k} (ybar_mp - pihat_mp); I_mk = sum_{p in P_k} pihat_mp (1 - pihat_mp); T = sum_m sum_k U_mk^2 / I_mk. Reported beside it:
- the LR Delta-D of model + problem + model x region, with a ridge of 0.5 on the region block (null correlation with T 0.987-0.998 in simulation); [QUALIFIED 2026-09-25 by the registrar, applying the LCB-STAGE0 build ruling's reading (c) (section "## Registrar's record 2026-09-25 (insertion only; zero calls; BEFORE ANY OUTCOME IS READ) — LCB-STAGE0-INTERACTION PRE-DATA AMENDMENT ...", below): Delta-D is taken on the AMENDED MARGINAL base, Delta-D = 2 x [penalised marginal log-likelihood of (amended null + g_mk, ridge 0.5 on the region block) minus that of the amended null]; the "null correlation with T 0.987-0.998" was measured on a different base (problem fixed effects + model x PD strata, M = 35, 12 worlds x 199 permutations; sim_lr_vs_score.py) and is NOT a property of this Delta-D. The ruling's words; nothing re-simulated.]
- T under the Rasch null. A "Rasch passes, rank-1 fails" reading means "the interaction is difficulty slope, not branches".
NULL (permutation):
- Families are permuted AS BLOCKS, so each problem’s full model vector stays intact. A family’s region is its members’ majority region (ties to the lowest question_id); split families are counted. [RULED 2026-09-25 (build ruling): p_T and p_X2 compare the null with the observed T and X2 evaluated at the FAMILY-MAJORITY labelling (every member of a family at its family's region, L17752), the identity element of the permutation set; T and X2 at each problem's own routed region are printed beside with the split-family count. Region sizes (P6, the >= 130 rule) and the descriptive per-region boards stay at own regions.]
- The permutation runs WITHIN strata = input format (stdin incl. Codeforces vs functional) x quintile-within-format of dhat_p. dhat_p is the Rasch problem effect, which never sees the regions.
- B = 2,000; permutation seed "LCB-STAGE0-PERM:<the same HEAD sha as H2>"; p = (1 + #{T* >= T}) / (B + 1).
- G1 PASSES iff p_T <= 0.01.
G2 STATISTIC (practical size, scale-free): for a model pair (A, B) and region k:
- g_k = mean over P_k of (ybar_Ap - ybar_Bp);
- SE_k, family-clustered, = sqrt[F_k/(F_k - 1) * sum_{f in k} (S_f - n_f g_k)^2] / n_k;
- leg b_k = max(0.05, 2 SE_k);
- X2 = #{A < B : there is a region k with g_k >= b_k and a region l with g_l <= -b_l}.
Every counted reversal is a >= 10pp DiD by construction. p_X2 comes from the same B permutations. G2 PASSES iff p_X2 <= 0.05. Reported beside it: X1 (legs max(0.05, 1 SE)); X2 restricted to pairs of two n = 10 models; X2 excluding frontier-frontier pairs, where the frontier of a region = the models whose region CI overlaps the region’s best.
REFUSED as criteria, with the null evidence (SYNTHETIC):
- max DiD >= 10pp: 100% of null worlds exceed it (null median 0.23-0.30);
- "top model differs across regions with bootstrap stability >= 0.80": under the null there are 1.8 distinct tops over 6 regions, and 47% of cells reach 0.80;
- a parametric bootstrap under the additive fit: size 0.41 / 0.19, because it ignores problem-level interaction.
DECISION RULE (joint size at tau = 0: 0.00-0.01, synthetic):
- GO iff G1 and G2 pass and the support block holds.
- STOP (clean negative; the line ends on this corpus) iff G1 fails with support held.
- STOP-SUB-PRACTICAL iff G1 passes and G2 fails. An interaction exists but produces no 10pp reversals beyond noise, so the judged stage as costed cannot use it. This is also a STOP. [AMENDED 2026-09-25 (build ruling), pre-data: STOP-SUB-PRACTICAL is written "G1 detects a model x region interaction at p_T <= 0.01 (synthetic G1 size 0.003-0.020 at the real roster), but G2 finds no 10pp reversals beyond noise AT ITS POWER (GO power 0.57-0.85 at tau 0.20, K = 3-4, synthetic); the judged stage as costed cannot use it. This is also a STOP."]
- TREE=FORMAT iff every region is nested in one input format and there is exactly one region per format. The within-format permutation is then degenerate (T = T*). This is NOT a clean negative about branches: it is reported as "the tree re-expresses input format", with the model x format interaction read descriptively under the common null (§6). The line on text-derived branches is UNDETERMINED.
- UNDETERMINED iff the support block fails (including K < 2). [RULED 2026-09-25 (build ruling): ORDER OF PRECEDENCE, first match wins: (1) the support block fails -> UNDETERMINED; (2) otherwise, TREE=FORMAT holds -> TREE=FORMAT; (3) otherwise GO / STOP-SUB-PRACTICAL / STOP as registered (mutually exclusive). The structural fact "tree = format: yes/no" is printed in EVERY outcome as an annotation, and when (1) and TREE=FORMAT both hold, the model x format reading under the common null is published as DESCRIPTIVE with the failing support condition named beside it. Reason: the support block is the precondition for reading any inferential verdict, and both words leave the line on text-derived branches UNDETERMINED, so the order changes the word, not the consequence. The registrar's reading at L17973 (TREE=FORMAT, not STOP, when G1 fails under TREE=FORMAT) is CONFIRMED and is forced: when each input format holds exactly one region, every stratum carries one label, so T* = T and X2* = X2 for every permutation and p_T = p_X2 = 1. (A family whose members straddle the two formats can make the permutation non-degenerate; TREE=FORMAT governs regardless of p_T.) Prediction scoring: Q2's "the TREE=FORMAT outcome" is scored on the structural condition; Q4's "UNDETERMINED or TREE=FORMAT" is one clause and is unaffected.]
A STOP is written in these words and no stronger: "no model x region interaction of about >= 0.2 logit SD beyond difficulty slope and input format (80% power on the synthetic calibration at K = 4-6), i.e. fewer than about 7-15 model pairs with a true 10pp reversal". Never "no interaction". [AMENDED 2026-09-25 (build ruling), pre-data: at the real roster the STOP sentence reads "no model x region interaction of about >= 0.2 logit SD beyond difficulty slope and input format (80% power of G1 on the synthetic calibration at the real roster, K = 3-4), i.e. fewer than about 2-7 model pairs with a true 10pp reversal". Never "no interaction".]
R-REP (GATE; an annotation only, which never creates or cancels a GO):
- r_rep = the weighted correlation of the TRAIN and GATE one-step estimates gamma_mk = U_mk / I_mk, each side from its own rank-1 fit, with weights (1/I_T + 1/I_G)^-1.
- Null: GATE families permuted within format x dhat-half.
- One-sided p <= 0.05 -> "GO, GATE-replicated"; otherwise "GO, GATE UNDETERMINED at its power" (power 0.44-0.59 at tau 0.15 and 0.71-0.87 at tau 0.2, synthetic).
REGISTERED SENSITIVITIES (read beside the verdict; none moves it; each is named in the outcome):
- Z1 contamination proxy: strata = format x dhat-tercile x contest-date half. A G1 pass that disappears here reads "confounded with contest date".
- Z2: family ∪ contest_id clusters.
- S1: first sample only.
- S2: the n = 10 / temp 0.2 roster.
- S3: pass-without-code recoded as fail.
DESCRIPTIVES:
- per-region boards (ybar_mk with family-clustered bootstrap CIs, B >= 2,000; the frontier shown as a BAND, never as ranks);
- region difficulty (mean dhat) and size per side;
- the X2 / X1 reversal lists by pair, with the null median beside;
- the top model per region with bootstrap stability, labelled descriptive, with its null reference;
- the tree’s certificate per site.

### 5. Support
Denominators and design effect:
- Informative TRAIN problems (~630 before the informative filter), eligible models M (~35-45), cells ~22k-28k.
- Cluster = family. DEFF is registered at 1.0-1.1. Kish 1.214 over all 1,055 is an UPPER BOUND at rho = 1, not a measured DEFF; the synthetic median is 1.00 and the max 1.04.
- DEFF is MEASURED on TRAIN at readout. The contest-level DEFF is unknown (BFCL registered 1.37 and measured 3.60). If the measured family DEFF > 1.3, every SE and MDE below is recomputed before any verdict is read.
- n_eff = informative TRAIN problems / DEFF.
Per-contrast precision: SE(DiD) = sqrt(DEFF * v * 2K / n_TRAIN) and MDE80 = 2.80 SE, where v is the per-problem pair-difference variance (synthetic: 0.065 for two n = 10 models, 0.17 median, 0.29 for two n = 1 models).

| K | MDE80 at v = .10 / .15 / .25 |
|---|---|
| 3 | 9.1 / 11.1 / 14.3pp |
| 4 | 10.5 / 12.8 / 16.5pp |
| 6 | 12.8 / 15.7 / 20.3pp |

GATE per-contrast MDE80 is 22-64pp.
Scoreability:
- G1 and G2 are aggregate and SCOREABLE. Power for GO is 0.40-0.70 at tau 0.15 and 0.86-0.99 at tau 0.20, for K = 4-6 (synthetic). [CORRECTED 2026-09-25 (build ruling): at the real roster shape (M = 26: 16 n = 1, 9 n = 10, 1 n = 4 files; ~630 TRAIN problems; the amended marginal null) and K = 3-4, power for GO is 0.17-0.38 at tau 0.15, 0.57-0.85 at tau 0.20 and 0.79-0.98 at tau 0.25; G1 alone 0.55-0.75 at tau 0.15 and 0.91-0.99 at tau 0.20 (synthetic, 150 worlds per cell). K = 6 is unreachable (6 x 130 > ~630 TRAIN problems); K <= 4. The registered 0.40-0.70 / 0.86-0.99 was computed as G1 and X1 (not X2) at M = 35 with half the files at n = 10, K = 4-6. Cells ~16.4k. The single-contrast SCOREABLE class is unchanged (two n = 10 models, K <= 4: MDE80 8.6pp at K = 4, 7.5pp at K = 3).]
- A SINGLE contrast (one pair x one region pair) at 10pp is SCOREABLE only at K <= 4 and only for pairs of two n = 10 models (MDE ~8.5pp).
- Every other single contrast, and every GATE contrast, is DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY.
- Per-region claims need >= 130 TRAIN problems per region. The region rule enforces this, inside the 120-190 floor of the query-support design effect.
Support block (all must hold for GO or STOP to be read):
- M >= 20 and K >= 2;
- every region >= 130 TRAIN problems;
- informative TRAIN problems >= 400;
- measured family DEFF <= 1.3, or the recomputation done;
- every D6 ingest assertion passes;
- the rank-1 fit converged (max |gradient| printed). [AMENDED 2026-09-25 (build ruling): "the rank-1 fit" is the amended MARGINAL fit (L17747 bracket); converged = max |gradient| of its penalised marginal log-likelihood < 1e-6 and every |a_m|, s_m <= 50, printed with the iteration count. The registered joint fit's non-convergence is a printed diagnostic, never a support failure.]
Structural reachability at infinite budget:
- The problem pool is fixed, so "infinite budget" means infinite samples per problem. v then falls to its between-problem part (~0.04), giving a floor MDE of ~6.3pp at K = 4 and ~7.7pp at K = 6.
- The floor of 2 SE_k for a single region gap is ~0.039, below the 0.05 leg, so G2 is reachable. G1 is reachable.
- Both are unreachable only if the roster is a strict chain in every region, which is the correct STOP.

### 6. Comparators and the secondary
"Tree beyond input format" is BUILT INTO G1 through the format strata, so it needs no separate test.
"Tree beats format x difficulty" and "tree beats k-means at matched K" are DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, not registered secondaries, for three reasons:
- two partitions of the same problems are not exchangeable, so no permutation exists for "tree > comparator";
- the C-FD cells ARE the strata of the primary null;
- the comparison is powerless at the relevant sizes: even the true generating partition beats a degraded partition (65% agreement) at dz > 2 only 13% of the time at tau = 0.1, and 83% at tau = 0.2 (synthetic, sim_comp_tau*.json).
Published for each partition (tree, C-FD, C-KM seeds 0-4) under ONE common null (rank-1 residuals, family permutation within dhat quintiles only, no format strata), with family-bootstrap CIs:
- z = (T - mean T*) / sd T*;
- excess per df = (T - mean T*) / ((M - 1)(K - 1)).
Never written: "the taxonomy beats the trivial split" or "beats k-means".

### 7. Predictions (scored even when a criterion passes)
- Q1: the depth-1 split of the tree = input format (LeetCode vs AtCoder + Codeforces) at >= 90% purity. P = 0.75.
- Q2: K in {3, 4, 5}, P = 0.70; the TREE=FORMAT outcome, P = 0.10.
- Q3: G1 passes under the rank-1 null, P = 0.75; T would pass under the Rasch null, P = 0.90.
- Q4: G2 passes, P = 0.45; joint GO, P = 0.40; STOP or STOP-SUB-PRACTICAL, P = 0.45; UNDETERMINED or TREE=FORMAT, P = 0.15.
- Q5: given GO, R-REP replicates. P = 0.50.
- Q6: the tree’s excess per df lies above the C-FD point, P = 0.45; above the median C-KM seed, P = 0.50.
- Q7: the tree’s root certifies against its site null. P = 0.60, because of the format signal; the 20NG pair 512 / 0.0145 did not certify there.
- Q8: measured family DEFF <= 1.1. P = 0.85.

### 8. Falsifiers (what each overturns)
- F1, STOP (G1 fails with support): overturns the premise of the specialised-vs-generic-judge line on LiveCodeBench, namely the web survey’s reading that LCB is a corpus where models excel on different branches of a text-derived partition (at the stated power). The judged stage (~8.5k cce) is NOT registered on LCB.
- F2, STOP-SUB-PRACTICAL: overturns the judged stage’s costing premise, that a 10pp DiD is available on some model pair and region pair. A re-costing at a smaller DiD would need its own registration and the author’s go.
- F3, a G1 pass that vanishes under Z1: the interaction is read as a contest-date (contamination) artefact, not a topic branch. No GO is written without Z1 beside it.
- F4, "Rasch passes, rank-1 fails": the interaction on LCB is difficulty slope, not branches (predicted against at 0.15 = 0.90 - 0.75).
None of these touches a closed line or a result of record on MMLU-Pro or the union.

### 9. Cost
- Judge calls 0; solves 0; embeddings local (Ollama): 0 cce. The 4,000-match rule does not apply, and no spend go is needed.
- Machine time:
  - download of 1.37 GB: 5-15 min;
  - ingest: 5-10 min;
  - closure and draw: under 1 min;
  - embedding ~1,055 texts on a cold cache in the worktree: 2-6 min;
  - build: 4-7 min;
  - site null: 3-8 min;
  - analysis: 10-30 min (the score statistic costs one matrix multiply per permutation; the rank-1 refits serve R-REP and the sensitivities);
  - comparators and bootstraps: 10-20 min.
  - Total ~1-2 h wall clock, of which ~30-45 min (backup, build, site null, pins) sits in a rule-7 window.
- Agent time (cost-estimator):
  - registrar: 15-20 min;
  - engine-coder: 60-70 min (drawer, ingest, DatasetType.LIVECODEBENCH, analysis);
  - adversarial-reviewer READY: 45-60 min;
  - run-operator: ~40 min;
  - post-run review: 15-25 min;
  - registrar outcome: 10-15 min.
  - Total ~3.5-4 agent-hours.

### 12. What this result will NOT show (pre-stated; the outcome carries it verbatim)
- Anything about a judge, specialised or generic; any judged accuracy; that a specialised judge would beat the generic one on any region.
- Anything about EVAL, whose outcomes are never read; transfer of any TRAIN interaction to EVAL, to another roster or to another corpus.
- That the regions are topics. A GO says the model x region structure exceeds difficulty slope and input format; higher-rank model x problem structure aligned with the regions passes whether or not it is topical.
- That the tree beats format x difficulty or k-means: those readings are descriptive only, and powerless at the relevant sizes.
- Any frontier order, any per-question rank, or any single model-pair x region-pair contrast outside the scoreable class (K <= 4, two n = 10 models).
- That the interaction is free of contamination. Z1 is a proxy (contest-date halves), not a per-model cutoff, and LCB’s own release_date field is unusable.
- Anything about LCB’s graders. The key is the upstream graded_list, accepted as-is; the pass-without-code rows are disclosed and sensitivity-tested, not re-executed.
- A clean negative in the absolute. A STOP is bounded by the stated power (~0.2 logit SD); it never means "no interaction".

F3 (MEDIUM): P3b, analysis.py L465 `sc("P3b", "M EXCLUDED" in words, "C1 reads 'M EXCLUDED' (0.13; ...)")`, scores P3b HELD WHEN C1 READS "M EXCLUDED". THE REGISTERED TEXT, READ IN FULL:
 - the registration 3a12115 (L15946): 'P3 C1 reads "P EXCLUDED" (point probability 0.55) and not "BELOW M" (0.7)': the M-side event PREDICTED was the NEGATION of the falsifier's event ("BELOW M" fired the falsifier, L15948);
 - amendment 2296877 (L15975-L15983): 'P3 "P EXCLUDED" (0.85), "M EXCLUDED" (0.15)', restated BEFORE DATA when the falsifier's event was renamed "M EXCLUDED";
 - amendment 0761cfa (L16921-L16924): '"P EXCLUDED" 0.79 and "M EXCLUDED" 0.13', with a DECLARED MODEL, beta-hat ~ N(1.9, sqrt(0.255^2 + SE_dec^2)), that gives the PROBABILITY OF EACH READING OCCURRING (0.753 / 0.139 at k 37), the registered values shifted by the model's change.
 So 0.79 and 0.13 are the forecast probabilities of the two readings occurring. The registered text is NOT ambiguous about that; it is silent only on how a forecast probability below one half is scored HELD / FAILED, and the programme's own convention settles it: a prediction's number is the probability of the predicted event (P1 "C0 PASS (point probability 0.9)", HELD iff C0 PASSES), and a probability of 0.13 attached to a named reading is a forecast of its COMPLEMENT at 0.87. Scoring P3b HELD on the 13% event (the code's reading) would score the prediction as confirmed exactly when the falsifier fires (FALSIFIER: "M EXCLUDED" overturns ruling 3 (a)'s planning) and when P2's own point (1.9 < 2.0529) is contradicted; the lineage (3a12115's "and not BELOW M") says the same. The review's option (a) (print the readings beside 0.79 / 0.13, no HELD / FAILED) is DECLINED: an outcome scores every prediction HELD / FAILED explicitly.
 RULING OF RECORD (the registrar, 2026-09-25, BEFORE ANY DATA; nothing judged, no store exists: `experiment_results/archv2/pilot_k46` absent at 286a1b0):
  P3a HELD iff C1 reads "P EXCLUDED" (the widened interval's lower end > 1.06); FAILED otherwise (including "UNRESOLVED AT THIS n"). Forecast 0.79.
  P3b HELD iff C1 does NOT read "M EXCLUDED" (the widened interval's upper end >= 2.0529, the exact bar, compared unrounded); FAILED iff C1 reads "M EXCLUDED". Forecast 0.87 (= 1 - 0.13). P3b FAILED if and only if the FALSIFIER FIRES.
  BOTH UNDETERMINED iff C1 gives no reading: C0 FAILS (UNDETERMINED BY VALIDITY) or K7's fail-closed rule fires (a non-finite replicate or point).
  THE INTERVAL DECIDES (C1's words are defined on the widened interval's ends; there is no point clause), stated here in ONE place (rule 7). The two parts are scored separately; if the interval excludes both bars (possible when the measured SE_dec is below about 0.25), P3a is HELD and P3b FAILED. The realised reading and the forecast probabilities (0.79; 0.13, i.e. 0.87 for its complement) are printed beside the scores; no proper score (Brier, log) is registered, and none is computed.
 APPLICATION: the post-run review applies this ruling. The instrument's P3b line at 64ff708 is INVERTED relative to it; it may be corrected only AFTER the run and BEFORE --analyze under a delta check (as F2's option (i)); if it is not, the outcome records the instrument's P3b line with a dated bracket "[P3b re-scored by the ruling of 2026-09-25: HELD iff NOT 'M EXCLUDED']". ## Q1. The rank-1 null: the fix, and the evidence

### Why the registered estimator does not exist here
The registered fit, logit pi = a_m + s_m·delta_p with delta_p free and no penalty, is joint ML (JML) for a 2PL. The "items" are the 26 models and the "persons" are the ~630 problems. For a binary row (an n=1 file) that is nearly ordered by difficulty, the joint fit re-orders a few delta_p until the row is separated, and s_m then goes to infinity.

The attractor is cheap. In a slope-scenario world (dbg2.py, seed 1, world 2), one n=1 model at pass rate 0.48, whose row correlates 0.81 with the Rasch difficulty, gains 151 log-likelihood units at s = 65. The other 25 models lose almost nothing.

That is also why a ridge on s inside the joint fit fails. With a lognormal prior of SD 0.5 on s in the joint fit, the same world converges to a stationary point at s = 65.4, because the prior costs about 20 units against a gain of 151. At SD 1.0 the slope reached 247 in that world. The optimum is finite but degenerate: that model's pass pattern is written into delta_p, so it leaks into every other model's residuals.

Failure rate of the registered fit (the build's `fit_rank1`, unchanged, with the refusal at |s| or |a| > 50), roster-shaped worlds (16/9/1 files, ~630 TRAIN problems, K = 4):

| data object | base | twins | slope (log-slope SD ~0.45) | strong slope (~0.9) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TRAIN, null worlds | 67/600 fail | 34/300 | 204/300 | 286/300 |
| TRAIN, power worlds (tau 0.15/0.20, K 3-4) | 10-29/150 per cell | | | |
| GATE (~105 problems), 40 worlds | 22/40 | | 33/40 | 38/40 |
| S1 (first sample only; all binary), 40 worlds | 4/40 | | 31/40 | 39/40 |

So even in the mildest world, the registered fit reads UNDETERMINED for numerical reasons in about 11% of TRAIN fits, and it fails in most GATE fits. That breaks R-REP and S1 as registered.

### The fix of record (the text the registrar records; exact)
Insert after L17747 (the "NULL FIT" paragraph):

> [AMENDED 2026-09-25, BEFORE ANY OUTCOME IS INGESTED, by the LCB-STAGE0 build ruling (arena-specialist; zero calls; synthetic evidence only): THE REGISTERED FIT HAS NO FINITE OPTIMUM ON THIS ROSTER. Maximised jointly over a_m, s_m and a free delta_p with no penalty (joint ML), a model with binary outcomes (an n = 1 file) whose row is nearly ordered by difficulty drives s_m to infinity while the delta_p re-order to separate it. On roster-shaped synthetic worlds (16 n = 1, 9 n = 10, 1 n = 4 files; ~630 TRAIN problems) the build's fit_rank1 fails in 67/600 base, 34/300 twin-heavy, 204/300 slope and 286/300 strong-slope null worlds, and in 22/40 base GATE fits. THE NULL FIT OF RECORD IS THEREFORE THE MARGINAL RANK-1 FIT: logit pi_mp = a_m + s_m x_p, with x_p ~ N(0, 1) integrated out per problem (41-node Gauss-Hermite quadrature on N(0, 1); EM with a Newton M-step on (a_m, s_m); rows at unit weight, quasi-binomial, as registered), s_m > 0, and a Gaussian prior of SD 1.0 on log s_m around the roster's mean log-slope. pihat_mp = E[pi_mp | Y_p], the posterior mean of pi_mp over the quadrature nodes given problem p's model vector. U_mk, I_mk and T are computed from this pihat exactly as registered. The fit never sees the regions. It is CONVERGED iff the max |gradient| of the penalised marginal log-likelihood over (a_m, s_m) is < 1e-6 and every |a_m| and s_m is <= 50; the support block's "rank-1 fit converged" reads this, printed with the iteration count and max s_m. The same fit, refitted on each data object, serves S1, S2, S3, Z1, Z2, R-REP (each side), the Delta-D base and the common null of section 6. The Rasch fit (dhat and T under Rasch) is unchanged. The build's joint fit is printed beside as a diagnostic (converged: yes/no, and its p_T when it converged) and never decides. WHY THE MARGIN: difficulty treated as random cannot be re-ordered to separate one model's row (the standard cure for the inconsistency of joint 2PL estimates); it converged in 3,850/3,850 roster-shaped TRAIN fits (1,500 null, 1,600 power at M = 26, 300 at M = 25, 450 diagnostic) and in 119/120 GATE and 120/120 first-sample fits. WHY THE PRIOR: without it, the marginal fit still fails in 105/300 strong-slope null worlds and in 11/40 slope-world GATE fits; with it, 0 failures on TRAIN and 1 in 120 GATE fits across the three families. It binds only at the extremes: in every base-null world p_T with and without the prior differs by <= 0.013 and the G1 decision is identical (600/600). Where the registered joint fit does converge, it agrees with the amended fit (p_T correlation 0.968-0.985; G1 decisions agree in 99.2-100% of worlds). ALTERNATIVES REFUSED: a ridge or lognormal prior on s inside the joint fit (finite but degenerate: s = 65 at SD 0.5 in a slope world); one shared slope for the n = 1 files (converges, but gives up the slope absorption for 16 of 26 models: G1 size 0.099 at 0.01 in strong-slope worlds, Rasch 0.123).]

The registered joint fit's non-convergence is a printed diagnostic, never a support failure.]

Reading:
- At the registered alpha 0.01 the size is consistent with alpha: pooled 0.012, upper CP95 0.019. So it is at most about 2x alpha, and the point estimate is 1.2x. This is "consistent with <= alpha at the resolution of 1,500 worlds", not "confirmed <= alpha".
