## Q2. Rule (ii) and Gemini-Flash-2.0-Exp: M = 26

- D4 applies eligibility first ("Eligible = a folder whose file has exactly 1,055 records ... Then, in order: (i) ... (ii) ..."), and rule (ii) is a DEDUPLICATION rule ("drop the n=1 duplicates"). A file is a duplicate only relative to a kept representative.
- The representative rule (ii) names (the `_10_` file, 880 records) is not eligible, so its premise is void. Nothing in D4's intent (full coverage, one entry per distinct model, the thinking or highest rung where variants exist) excludes this model.
- D5/A2 pool n=1 files at unit weight, so an n=1 representative is fully admissible.
- Rule (vii) is the registration's own tie-break for identical files ("keep the lexicographically first name"). The ruling applies that tie-break by name, so the outcome does not depend on the matrix leg of (vii), which reads outcome values.
- The decision uses record counts and folder names only.

Text for the registrar (insert after L17722):

> [RULED 2026-09-25 by the LCB-STAGE0 build ruling (arena-specialist), BEFORE ANY OUTCOME IS READ: rule (ii) presupposed that the (N=10) folder's _10_ file is eligible; it holds 880 records and fails the 1,055-record eligibility, so (ii)'s premise is void and it does not remove the model. Gemini-Flash-2.0-Exp stays on the roster through ONE n = 1 file: the Scenario.codegeneration_1_* file of the folder "Gemini-Flash-2.0-Exp" (the lexicographically first of the two folders, (vii)'s tie-break applied by name). The _1_ file of "Gemini-Flash-2.0-Exp (N=10)" is dropped as its duplicate, WHETHER OR NOT the two files are byte-identical; the roster TSV records the file sha256 equality (a file hash, not an outcome) and the rule text "(ii) kept: n=1 file of the lexicographically first folder; the (N=10) _10_ file is not eligible (880 records)". M after (i)-(vii) at texts = 26 (16 n = 1, 9 n = 10, 1 n = 4), not 25. D5's pooling and S2 (the n = 10 roster, which excludes this model) are unchanged.]

For the build, in ingest.py `apply_roster`: when `GEMINI_EXP_KEEP` is not eligible, keep `("Gemini-Flash-2.0-Exp", n=1)` and drop the other. Add a selftest fixture with an 880-record `_10_` file. The present selftest fixture gives `_10_` the full 1,055, so it never exercises this branch.

## Q3. Precedence in the decision rule

Text (insert after L17771):

> [RULED 2026-09-25 (build ruling): ORDER OF PRECEDENCE, first match wins: (1) the support block fails -> UNDETERMINED; (2) otherwise, TREE=FORMAT holds -> TREE=FORMAT; (3) otherwise GO / STOP-SUB-PRACTICAL / STOP as registered (mutually exclusive). The structural fact "tree = format: yes/no" is printed in EVERY outcome as an annotation, and when (1) and TREE=FORMAT both hold, the model x format reading under the common null is published as DESCRIPTIVE with the failing support condition named beside it. Reason: the support block is the precondition for reading any inferential verdict, and both words leave the line on text-derived branches UNDETERMINED, so the order changes the word, not the consequence. The registrar's reading at L17973 (TREE=FORMAT, not STOP, when G1 fails under TREE=FORMAT) is CONFIRMED and is forced: when each input format holds exactly one region, every stratum carries one label, so T* = T and X2* = X2 for every permutation and p_T = p_X2 = 1. (A family whose members straddle the two formats can make the permutation non-degenerate; TREE=FORMAT governs regardless of p_T.) Prediction scoring: Q2's "the TREE=FORMAT outcome" is scored on the structural condition; Q4's "UNDETERMINED or TREE=FORMAT" is one clause and is unaffected.]

For the build, `decide()` replaces the `refuse(...)` branch with this order and always returns `tree_is_format` beside the verdict.

## The builder's readings (a)-(f)

**(a) T at each problem's own region: OVERRULED for the p-value.**
- The permutation set assigns labels BY FAMILY (a family's region = its members' majority region; L17752).
- The observed statistic must be the statistic at the identity element of that set. Only then is p = (1 + #{T* >= T})/(B + 1) exact under exchangeability.
- T at own regions (with split families) is a labelling the null never generates.
- Text:

> [RULED 2026-09-25 (build ruling): p_T and p_X2 compare the null with the observed T and X2 evaluated at the FAMILY-MAJORITY labelling (every member of a family at its family's region, L17752), the identity element of the permutation set; T and X2 at each problem's own routed region are printed beside with the split-family count. Region sizes (P6, the >= 130 rule) and the descriptive per-region boards stay at own regions.]

- With 0 split families the two coincide.

**(b) Ties to the lowest question_id = the lowest surrogate id: CONFIRMED.**
- H5 defines the surrogate as the rank over sorted (platform, question_id). That is the registration's only integer order on problems, and any fixed pre-data rule keeps the test valid.
- Disclose that within LeetCode the order is H5's sort order of the id field. Whether that is string or numeric order is as built; state it in the manifest.

**(c) Delta-D on the rank-1 base: CONFIRMED, on the amended base.**
- Delta-D is "reported beside" T, and T is the score test at the rank-1 null. A companion likelihood ratio on another base would test a different hypothesis, and the Rasch contrast is already reported separately.
- Delta-D = 2 x [penalised marginal log-likelihood of (amended null + g_mk, ridge 0.5 on the region block) minus that of the amended null].
- The build's `fit_rank1_region` (joint, initialised from `fit_rank1`) inherits the divergence and must move to the marginal base.
- The registered "null correlation with T 0.987-0.998" was measured on a different base (problem fixed effects + model x PD strata, M = 35, 12 worlds x 199 permutations; sim_lr_vs_score.py). It is not a property of this Delta-D and is written as such.

**(d) Frontier = family-clustered normal CI, overlap with the region best's CI, recomputed under every permutation; a pair is frontier-frontier when both are on the frontier of a common region: CONFIRMED.**
- Observed and null use the same definition, which is what the variant needs.
- The published per-region BAND in the descriptives uses the bootstrap CIs (B >= 2,000). The two may differ at the margin, and the outcome says which one each number uses.
- It is a reported-beside variant and never decides.

**(e) G2 on the informative TRAIN problems: CONFIRMED.**
- That is section 4's stated data object and denominator.
- The per-region informative counts are printed beside the P6 counts. P6's >= 130 rule counts all TRAIN problems.

**(f) DEFF = the median over model pairs of clustered / iid variance of the mean pair difference: CONFIRMED.**
- It is the definition the registered synthetic calibration used (sim_mde.py, deff_med). The build's F/(F-1) factor changes it by about 0.1%.
- The support block reads the median. q90 and max are printed beside, as built.
- Synthetic at the real roster: median 1.00 (base), 1.02 (twins), max 1.04.

## RULING

1. **Q1: No. The structural proof, as filed, does not reach everything the byte run would, so option (b) is NOT recommended.**
   - The golden DAG tests (AnchorFreeInertnessTest, ConstructionOrderInertnessTest) build an `MMLUDatasetFetcher` on a throw-away DB, then feed a SYNTHETIC corpus straight into the engine. After the change they execute the fetcher's init, which now registers 6 sources, and they execute the construction core.
   - They do NOT execute these five steps for any existing corpus:
     - (i) the headless TOML parse to `DatasetType.valueOf`;
     - (ii) the changed `when` in `MmluProCorpusSource.fetch` (CorpusSource.kt L53-L59);
     - (iii) loadFromDb / finalizeData / the split;
     - (iv) pool recording through `ReservedPool.canonicalLine` -> `CorpusDomains.sourceOfKey`, whose membership set `CorpusRegistry.KNOWN` CHANGED (it gained "LIVECODEBENCH");
     - (v) snapshot save.
   - The ordinal and offset assertions pin two maps, not a run. "initDatabase untouched" is true (it hard-codes 5 corpus tables plus eval_question_link, and has no registry reference).
   - My read-only audit of every channel finds NO path by which an existing arm's output can change. The audit is below. It reaches the orchestrator's four failure modes ANALYTICALLY, but analysis is not the registered proof form (P1 / A5: "proved by a byte-inertness run WITH an execution discriminator").
   - D7 adds code that executes on EVERY existing arm: the `lcbWorkDir` property initialiser runs in every `MMLUDatasetFetcher` instance. That includes every build, every site null and every golden test.
   - The registered form costs about 15 minutes of machine time.
   - **Ruling: discharge D9 by (a), the byte run specified in Q2.** The audit is recorded as the prediction the run tests, not as a substitute for it.

**Arm.** `experiment_configs/topic_partition/ag_news_smoke_s42.toml`, UNCHANGED (blob efd82bda). This is the cheapest arm that executes channels (i)-(v):

- `git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/d9-legB <B>`

## What this does NOT show
- It does not show that the byte run will pass. The audit is an analytical prediction; nothing was executed.
- It does not show that PinnedPoolsReproduceTest or the golden tests ran on the ed948d6 classes. The builder's "41/41" set was not re-listed here.
- It does not cover the MMLU-Pro offset-0 path through mmlu_pro_dataset_cache_v2.db, a multi-corpus union run (LeaderboardCorpusSource, untouched), the TUI, or the site-null harness. The AG smoke run covers these only through the shared fetcher init and the shared `when`.
- It does not show that `fetchLiveCodeBench` / `lcbWorkDirGuard` behave correctly. That is the LCB test's and the LCB window's job (L5, L8), not D9's.
- It does not show that the D7 edit compiles. It is uncommitted and nothing was compiled here.
- The embedding-miss expectation (0 misses) is inferred from the 09-22 run, not read from the cache.

0.1 WHERE THE ONE-POSTER ASSUMPTION LIVES. The brief says the judge_v2 writer owns the journal, the ceilings, the rollover stop and the preflight. It does not. Only the drain is in the writer layer; the rest is in the K46 driver package archv2_pilot, at the build of record 5e9de0f (NOT MERGED; worktree agent-a572e076e3586743c):
 - judge_v2/writer.py (main, blob:6db4ab3207a24aa61a1d4ea43ca6f2da2c68e547 = 5e9de0f's) L336-L358: run() -> self.store.drain(poster), with no pool.
 - data_v2/verdicts.py (blob:1013804233b7ccfc0df699acdcaf518b089ad526, pinned in judge_v2/_base.py ED_PINS) L269-L291: drain() iterates pending() once, in key order, calls poster(slot) and records each attempt or verdict on the one connection.
 - archv2_pilot/accounting.py @5e9de0f: _ddl L121ff. The trigger `invocation_unresolved` (L131) ABORTS any invocation while an earlier one is unresolved. The journal therefore ENFORCES ONE CALL IN FLIGHT AT THE DATABASE LEVEL: a second concurrent PENDING row is refused before its post. `invocation_cap` (L129) is the per-test ceiling trigger. wrap_call (L255-L289) does, in order: rollover check -> journal PENDING commit -> posts["n"] += 1 -> call_full -> resolution.
 - archv2_pilot/pilot.py @5e9de0f: launch() L1221. posting_day_ok L1232, transport_preflight() L1235 (before the journal, store and ledger), guard_day L1324, wrap_call L1329, writer.run L1330, the ledger append in finally L1335.
 - accepted_tests_ledger.append (L126-L147): a read-modify-os.replace with NO cross-process lock. Two processes appending on the same day can lose a row. JudgeBench's runner (85a2d9f) added a LedgerLock for exactly this reason.

A connection touched from a worker thread raises ProgrammingError. The single-writer design below relies on this.
 - rejudge_reasoning.call_judge_full (blob:1339592a, pinned) L111-L165 retries INTERNALLY on 408/429/500/502/503/504: 6 attempts, sleeps min(2^a x 3, 60) s = 3, 6, 12, 24, 48 s, and IGNORES Retry-After. So a 429 is INVISIBLE to the caller unless all 6 attempts fail. The returned latency is the successful attempt's only, because t0 is reset each attempt, so backoff sleeps are hidden from the store's latency_ms. "4,005 of 4,005 attempts HTTP 200" (K46) therefore means 4,005 invocations; it says nothing about 429s absorbed inside them.

0.3 FOUR CORRECTIONS TO THE BRIEF, carried into the texts below.
 (i) "No double post on crash or relaunch" is NOT achievable against a non-idempotent HTTP API. A request that reached Azure and whose reply died with the process cannot be told apart from one that never left. Today's sequential code has the same hole, bounded at 1. The achievable invariant, registered below, is: AT MOST ONE VERDICT PER SLOT (the store's PK and triggers); every re-post COUNTED (journal ORPHAN -> ledger); re-posts after one crash <= the in-flight bound N (today 1).
 (ii) The journal's one-in-flight trigger must change for N > 1. That is a SCHEMA change to a driver file (archv2_pilot/accounting.py), not only to the writer.
 (iii) 429 handling "within the registered transport-error rules" means within rr.call_judge_full's rule (L16002, L17385). Honouring Retry-After inside rr would change a pinned module with Kotlin parity (rule 9), so it is out of scope. Retry-After is honoured at the POOL level instead (E-5 below).
 (iv) "Duplicates of already-cached calls" are unsuitable probe payloads, for two reasons. Every cached judge call is on an EVAL / reserved item (CANARY, TRACE, GROK-CALIB, K46: p2dca or SPLIT-2 EVAL), so re-posting them judges EVAL items for nothing. And identical bodies hit the provider's prompt cache, which distorts latency and token accounting. The probe uses SYNTHETIC-DEV payloads (1.4).

======================================================================================================================
## 1. Registered 2026-09-25 (before any code or call) — JV2-RATE-PROBE: at how many concurrent in-flight calls does the grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning deployment stop buying throughput today, and is the gain worth a parallel writer?
======================================================================================================================

1.1 QUESTION. On the probe day, alone on the deployment, with payloads the size and shape of the recipe's: what is the largest in-flight count N* in {1, 2, 4, 8, 12} whose HTTP-429 share, exhausted-429 invocations and p95 invocation latency stay inside registered bounds? What is its throughput gain G = rate(N*) / rate(1)? This is an ENGINEERING measurement of a transport. It decides NOTHING about any board, recipe, reference, judge or model. No verdict is read as data.

1.2 HYGIENE.
 - NO ITEM OF ANY CORPUS IS JUDGED. Payloads are SYNTHETIC-DEV. The QUESTION is generated by a seeded generator (`JV2-RATE-PROBE:<registration commit>`): 10-option MCQs with a computed key (arithmetic, unit conversion, simple kinematics). There are two RESPONSES, templated worked solutions (one reaches the key, one a distractor), and a REFERENCE (a templated solution rendered through rejudge_reference.with_reference, never retyped). A CONTENT GATE refuses the launch if any generated question's stem_key (split_side.stem_key, CK-CLOSE-v1 key) equals any item's in the MMLU-Pro and union corpora (0 hits required, printed). No reserved, EVAL, GATE or TRAIN item is posted.
 - THE SYSTEM TEXT IS THE RECIPE'S, BYTE FOR BYTE. The K46 recipe's system message is built by judge_v2.payload's builder: the v2 template, persona GENERIC_SYSTEM, rubric slot GENERIC_RUBRIC 67f843eb..., schema instruction. Its sha256 must equal the K46 store's verdict.system_template_sha / rubric_sha (printed). The shared prefix therefore behaves as in production. Every user message is distinct, so there is no whole-body prompt-cache hit.
 - SIZE MATCHED. Target user-message byte lengths are the q10 / q50 / q90 of the K46 store of record's posted bodies (decompressed body_zlib LENGTHS only, read from the COMPLETE store after the K46 outcome, mode=ro; no content read). The three quantiles are printed and pinned in the dry-run.
 - THE CALL OF RECORD. Every post goes through rr.call_judge_full (rule 9), after rr.payload_bytes(system, user) == the pre-built body is asserted. Temperature is OMITTED (Amendment 1 D2; never 0, unlike the Mistral sweeps), cap 8192, model grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning, provider azure. Transport comes from archv2_pilot.pilot.load_transport + transport_preflight as at 5e9de0f, IMPORTED, not retyped; the preflight line is printed before anything else (READY-TEMPLATE-TRANSPORT (a)/(b)).
 - SINGLE ORDER PER CALL. Only the transport is measured and no match verdict is formed, so dual order and TIE-on-flip do not apply. This is NOT an ORDER-1 test (closed line) and reads nothing about position.
 - EXCLUSIVITY (a FAILED PRECONDITION when breached, never an outcome). X1: at launch and at every step boundary, a process list (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process) shows no other python process running a tools/analysis posting script (K46 finished: its process gone and its journal unresolved 0; JudgeBench not running). X2: the probe's day is not a JudgeBench posting day. X3: other Azure consumers of the same resource outside this machine cannot be seen; this is disclosed, not controlled.
 - ACCOUNTING. The unit of record is the INVOCATION (L1'(b), L18409ff). A write-ahead journal with the 5e9de0f semantics runs, its unresolved bound set to the step's N (the probe's own DDL; see 2.3 E-2). A per-test ceiling of 400 invocations is enforced by the journal trigger (CEILINGS["JV2-RATE-PROBE"] = 400 via accepted_tests_ledger, by 3-way merge as JudgeBench did, never by path restore). The day cap (iii) is 14,000 on the posting date, read at launch: day total + 400 <= 14,000. On 09-25 after K46: 26 + 5,328 + 400 = 5,754, which fits. The ledger append is under JudgeBench's LedgerLock (cross-process). ledger == journal is checked at the start and the end. HTTP attempts, 429s included, are counted and printed as a DIAGNOSTIC. They are not the ledger unit, and a 429 generates no tokens.
 - ROLLOVER. As at 5e9de0f: the day is fixed at the launch. No reservation after the local date changes, and every in-flight send re-checks the date before it posts. Relaunch resumes the ramp at the step that was stopped.

1.3 INSTRUMENT (tools/analysis/jv2_rate_probe.py, new; imports only; no judge_v2 file is changed).
 - WIRE COUNTER. A thread-local wrapper around urllib.request.urlopen (JudgeBench's reviewed pattern) records every HTTP attempt: ticket, attempt number, send and end times, status, Retry-After, and the NAMES and VALUES of any x-ratelimit-* / retry-after-ms headers. It never records api-key or authorization, and the resource host only as already printed (G4). It asserts that the attempt's request body bytes equal the ticket's journaled body (body fidelity at the wire). rr is unchanged and its internal retries run as registered. The counter only makes them visible.
 - THE RAMP. Steps S1..S5 at N = 1, 2, 4, 8, 12 with 24, 36, 48, 64, 76 invocations (248). The first 12 of S1 are the PILOT 12. The pilot guard (the truncation guard's rule) refuses above 5% unparsed (rj.parse_judge on rr.strip_think), any finish_reason "length" or content_filter, and any non-200 exhausted invocation. Steps are separated by a 60 s idle gap, so a per-minute window resets.
 - ADMISSIBLE STEP. A step is admissible iff all three hold: (a) HTTP-429 attempts <= 2% of the step's HTTP attempts; (b) 0 invocations exhausted on 429; (c) p95 of the INVOCATION wall latency (reservation to return, rr's backoff sleeps included) <= min(1.5 x p95(S1), 10 s).  - Cost ceiling 248 + 150 = 398 <= 400.

1.4 READOUTS (outcome file experiment_results/jv2_rate_probe/JV2_RATE_PROBE_outcome.txt, write-once from a complete probe; a stopped ramp is complete by its own rule; a pilot to _PILOT.txt).
 - Per step: N, invocations, HTTP attempts, 429 attempts and share with its exact Clopper-Pearson 95% upper bound, exhausted-429 invocations, calls/min (invocations over the step's wall), median / p95 / max invocation latency, median completion_tokens, median user bytes, unparsed share.

 - Realism line: probe median user bytes vs K46's q50 (+-10%), probe median completion_tokens vs K46's (+-30%).
 - NOT READ: accuracy, ties, leakage. There is no key of record, no reference of record and no contestant, so the 5.7% test-retest floor, both tie conventions and the CONSENSUS-FIT REF coefficient do not apply. This is stated in the outcome's header.

1.5 CRITERIA (scored HELD / FAILED).
 C0 VALIDITY. V1 exclusivity held (X1 printed at every step). V2 content gate 0 hits. V3 ledger == journal and invocations <= 400. V4 pilot guard PASS. V5 realism within the bands.
  V1-V4 failing VOIDS the probe (it is re-registered, not re-read). V5 failing leaves the numbers DESCRIPTIVE with the size caveat printed beside N*.

 C2 VALUE. G >= 1.5 -> "build JV2-PARALLEL-POSTING". G < 1.5 -> "the parallel writer buys < 1.5x on this deployment today; build DEFERRED unless the author decides otherwise". The author may override C2 either way; the override is recorded as the author's. 1.6 PREDICTIONS (the specialist's, before any call).
 P1 (the 09-24 regime persists; confidence about 60%): N* in {1, 2}; the rate at N = 4 < 35 calls/min, i.e. < 2x S1.

## 2. Registered 2026-09-25 (before any code; zero calls) — JV2-PARALLEL-POSTING: a bounded worker pool for the judge_v2 posting path, byte-inert at --workers 1
======================================================================================================================

2.1 QUESTION (engineering). Can the judge_v2 posting path (writer + driver accounting) post with up to N calls in flight while every guarantee of record holds unchanged? The guarantees are: write-ahead journal per invocation, per-slot idempotence, ledger == journal, ceilings, the day-rollover stop, the transport preflight, body fidelity, the six-way classification, and a store whose content is independent of completion order. And is the path BYTE-IDENTICAL to today's at --workers 1? No verdict, recipe, prompt, reference, cap, temperature, order or combiner changes.

2.2 HYGIENE.
 - Zero judge calls in the build, the selftest and the inertness proof. All posting is to a fake call_full or a localhost stub.
 - No DB of record is opened read-write. The inertness legs use judge_v2's selftest DEV fixture view (temp dir), never a view of record, so no rule-7 window is needed. If the reviewer wants the SPLIT-2 view for realism, that leg is a view read under W1-W5.
 - Worktree only. The merge is gated by F5 (L18065): no commit touching tools/analysis/judge_v2/* reaches main before the K46 OUTCOME is written. archv2_pilot/* is not touched on main before the K46 outcome either (L2': no change to archv2_pilot* until the run has finished posting; the outcome re-reads C0 (c)).

2.3 INSTRUMENT (the design of record; alternatives at 2.3.9).
 E-1 DISPATCH. writer.run(call_full, out=print, workers=1). At workers == 1 the CURRENT code path is executed verbatim: self.store.drain(self._poster_factory(call_full)), with the plain callable and nothing new printed except one registered line, "[POOL] workers 1 (sequential path)". At workers > 1 the pipelined path (E-3) runs, and it needs a TWO-PHASE transport (E-2).
  `workers` is NOT a recipe-identity key: a relaunch may change N, for example after E-5's halving. It is recorded per launch: the launch label ("... w=N"), the [POOL] line, and journal v2 launch metadata.
 E-2 TWO-PHASE TRANSPORT AND JOURNAL v2 (archv2_pilot/accounting.py; the protocol in a new judge_v2/pool.py so every driver implements the same contract). wrap_call's single callable is split into three parts:
   reserve(system, user) -> ticket. MAIN THREAD. In order: the rollover check; the slot_of lookup; the journal PENDING insert + commit (the cap trigger and the unresolved-bound trigger fire HERE, before any post); posts["n"] += 1; body = rr.payload_bytes asserted equal to the stored body.
   send(ticket) -> the call_full tuple. WORKER THREAD. It touches NO sqlite connection (enforced by check_same_thread=True: a worker touching one raises ProgrammingError), sets NO rr global, re-checks the local date, and on a change returns NOT_SENT without posting. Then rr.call_judge_full.
   resolve(ticket, outcome). MAIN THREAD. RETURNED / RAISED / ORPHAN as today. A send-time rollover is resolved RAISED with the note "DAY ROLLOVER: not sent" (counted, disclosed; the invocation unit of L1'(b)).
  JOURNAL v2 DDL: the trigger `invocation_unresolved` becomes "abort if (unresolved count) >= meta.max_inflight". meta.max_inflight is written at creation and is the registration's maximum N, e.g. 16.
  At --workers 1 the journal is created with TODAY'S DDL TEXT and NO new meta row, so it stays byte-inert. A launch with workers > max_inflight, or with workers > 1 on a v1 journal (max_inflight absent = 1), is REFUSED before any post.
 E-3 THE PIPELINE (store.drain UNCHANGED; data_v2/verdicts.py UNCHANGED, pin kept).
  The pipelined poster takes the same pending list drain iterates (self.store.pending(), once, so _OnlyStore's pilot restriction holds). It keeps at most N tickets reserved-and-unresolved.
  drain calls poster(slot_i) in key order. poster asserts slot_i's key == the i-th expected key (an in-order contract; a mismatch refuses). It tops up reservations to i + N - 1: each is built by _payload_for in the MAIN thread, so the scan witness, the payload-reproduces-schedule check and the material checks are unchanged. It waits for ticket i's future, resolves it, classifies it (writer.classify, unchanged), and returns the same ("verdict", ...) / ("error", ...) tuple drain records today.
  CONSEQUENCES. Store rows are INSERTED IN KEY ORDER at any N, identical in order to the sequential run. The unresolved invocations at any instant are <= N. The poster-scan witness `pscans == posted` holds.
  Cost: head-of-line blocking. A slow slot i holds reservation i + N; under 429 storms that is useful back-pressure.
 E-4 STOPS UNDER CONCURRENCY. On any stop condition (DAY ROLLOVER at reserve, the cap or unresolved trigger, a guard's SystemExit, RATE STOP), the pipeline makes NO further reservation. It keeps feeding drain the already-reserved tickets until the last one is recorded, then raises the stop. A clean stop therefore records every in-flight result instead of orphaning it. KeyboardInterrupt does not wait: in-flight tickets become ORPHANs on the relaunch (<= N), counted and disclosed, and the finally appends posts["n"] (= journal rows of this launch) to the ledger as today.
 E-5 RATE CONTROL (only at workers > 1; at workers == 1 behaviour is today's). For N in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16} x 20 seeded latency permutations, the store PROJECTION must be identical to the N = 1 run: every column of schedule, attempt and verdict, and every run_meta key, except created_at, latency_ms and session_id. Given E-3 the insertion order is identical too, so the canonical .dump differs only in those three columns.
 2.3.9 ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED AND NOT CHOSEN.
  (A) Out-of-order recording (record each completion as it lands). It would need a writer-side copy of drain's bookkeeping (a second, unpinned copy of pinned logic) or a new VerdictStore.record_result extracted from drain (changes verdicts.py -> re-pin in _base -> an E-D change). It is faster under stalls.
  (B) Worker threads writing SQLite under a lock. It multiplies failure modes, and check_same_thread would have to be disabled.
  (C) Multi-process posting (JudgeBench's arm pattern). It needs cross-process journal locking; not needed for one deployment.

2.5 CONCURRENCY SELFTEST (python and python -O; a localhost stub server for the wire, rr.call_judge_full REAL with time.sleep patched to a fast fake, plus the pure fake for E-8). Invariant -> its mutant (each must be KILLED):
 I1 write-ahead: the stub, on receipt, finds a PENDING unresolved journal row with that body sha (separate read-only connection). Mutant: send before reserve.
 I2 one verdict per slot / no in-launch resubmission: mutant 1, re-reserve an errored slot within the launch; mutant 2, reserve from a stale pending snapshot on relaunch.
 I3 ledger == journal: mutant, count posts at completion instead of reservation. Killed by a KeyboardInterrupt with N in flight.
 I4 rollover: the clock flips between reserve and send. Mutant 1, the check only at launch start; mutant 2, reserve-time check only. Kill criterion: 0 stub requests received after the flip.
 I5 preflight first: mutant 1, preflight after the pool starts; mutant 2, preflight skipped when workers > 1.
 I6 ceilings: cap 50, N 8, 60 pending, 1,000 stress trials: exactly 50 journal rows and <= 50 successful stub requests. Mutant 1, a Python counter in the workers instead of the trigger; mutant 2, the unresolved trigger off (observed unresolved > N).
 I7 429: the stub serves configured 429 shares and bursts with Retry-After. Exhausted -> an error attempt row, never a verdict, re-posted next launch; cool-down and halving fire. Mutants: a 429 classified INVALID; retries beyond 6; no halving; Retry-After ignored by the gate.
 I8 order invariance (E-8): mutant, bind future j's result to slot i.
 I9 single writer: mutant, record a verdict from a worker (ProgrammingError / thread assert).
 I10 body fidelity: mutant, send the previous ticket's body. Killed at the reserve assert and at the wire counter.
 I11 rr globals frozen: mutant, a worker sets rr.TEMPERATURE = 0.
 I12 crash: a subprocess os._exit at 50 seeded points with N = 8. After the relaunch: verdicts per slot <= 1, re-posts <= N, orphans disclosed, ledger == journal after reconcile. Mutant: resolve orphans as RETURNED.
 I13 identity: a store created by leg A code is REFUSED on relaunch by the build ("recipe identity differs: writer_blob"). Mutant: writer_blob dropped from IDENTITY_KEYS.
 Also required: judge_v2 selftest ALL PASS; archv2_pilot --part all; lint_opens 0 findings.

2. THE PRE-READY AMENDMENT OF E-5 (RATE CONTROL). WHO DECIDED WHAT: THE AUTHOR authorised the build on 2026-09-25 ("Go for 350 and build it anyway I'll find a way to increase the quota"; plan Amendment 24; section "## Author's decisions 2026-09-25 (recorded by the registrar; zero calls; insertion only) — (1) JUDGEBENCH-REASONING-SIDE SIZE = 350 ...", L19341-L19376) and OBSERVED, as relayed by the orchestrator (the author's words are NOT recorded verbatim; the registrar holds the relay), that spamming Azure with requests causes slowdowns and timeouts. THE ORCHESTRATOR then imposed rate-control requirements on the build (the "coordinator's HARD REQUIREMENTS of 2026-09-25 (items 1-6)" named in judge_v2/pool.py's docstring at 5373858). This is THE ORCHESTRATOR'S PRE-READY AMENDMENT under the author's authorisation of 2026-09-25, NOT AN AUTHOR DECISION: the author chose none of the values below. It changes the INSTRUMENT (the transport's pacing and retries on the pooled path), not a criterion, prediction, falsifier or recipe; no verdict, prompt, reference, cap, temperature, order or combiner changes. Where it departs from the registered E-5 (L19127-L19132) it is recorded as an amendment (the builder's deviation 4; each re-read by the registrar against pool.py's docstring at 5373858, which carries the values below):
 A-E5.1 (amends E-5 (b)) RETRY-AFTER honoured in BOTH forms (delta-seconds and HTTP-date), floored at 3 s. With NO header, EXPONENTIAL BACKOFF WITH FULL JITTER, uniform(0, min(60, 2 x 2^k)) s, i.e. ceilings 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 60 s, floored at 3 s, REPLACES the flat 3 s; the same backoff on 408 / 5xx / a network error / a timeout. ONE 429 PAUSES THE WHOLE POOL (the global cool-down gate holds every worker's next attempt and every new reservation), not only new reservations.
 A-E5.2 (new) A GLOBAL TOKEN BUCKET, --max-rpm, default 20 (capacity 1, one token per 60 / max_rpm s, shared by all workers).
 A-E5.3 (amends E-5 (c); SUPERSEDES "It never rises within a launch") ADAPTIVE CONCURRENCY: the in-flight bound HALVES (min 1) on an invocation exhausted on 429 (as registered), on a timeout, or on 3 HTTP 429s within 30 s (the latter two at most once per 10 s); it RISES by 1 per clean 60 s (no 429, timeout or halving) up to --post-workers. E-5 (d) (the RATE STOP) is kept; its reading is D6 below.
 A-E5.4 (new) A PER-REQUEST TIMEOUT, min(rr's 600 s, --request-timeout-s), default 120 s; and a CIRCUIT BREAKER, K = 8 consecutive HTTP attempts that timed out or got 429 (any success resets): the pool stops cleanly and the relaunch resumes (--breaker-k).
 A-E5.5 (amends E-5 (a) and the registered "rr's 6 attempts") THE POOL OWNS RETRIES: rr's internal retry loop is NEUTRALISED on the pooled path (a retryable failure is re-raised as PoolRetry, a RuntimeError call_judge_full does not catch), so rr makes EXACTLY ONE attempt per call and never sleeps; the pool retries the SAME invocation (same journal row, ticket and body) up to 6 HTTP attempts. A 400 (content_filter included) passes through unchanged (rule 10). EVERY HTTP ATTEMPT is journaled (http_attempts, http_429) and counted against an HTTP-ATTEMPT CAP (the journal's cap minus the attempts already booked; beyond it, a clean stop). LIMIT (recorded as such): THE DAY LEDGER AND THE DAY CAP REMAIN IN INVOCATION UNITS; HTTP attempts are journaled, not ledgered.
 A-E5.6 (amends the E-5 header "only at workers > 1; at workers == 1 behaviour is today's", and E-1) RATE CONTROL AT workers = 1: when any rate flag (--max-rpm, --request-timeout-s, --breaker-k) is given, the launch is POOLED even at --post-workers 1 (the pooled path at bound 1, on a journal v2). Only --post-workers 1 WITH NO RATE FLAG is today's path.
 REGISTRAR'S READINGS ON THE AMENDMENT (binding unless objected to by a dated bracket on this line before the READY): (i) EC1 (2.4) is scored at --workers 1 WITH NO RATE FLAG; a rate-flagged workers-1 launch is the pooled path and is NOT claimed byte-inert (its journal is v2 by design). It is the only paragraph the registration labels "decided by C1' and C2 together", and the FALSIFIER defers to its object-level rule in its own words: "How C2 disambiguates: a C1' difference on an object that C2 shows stable reads the change (F1); on an object that C2 shows unstable, it reads non-determinism (F2), never the change. Under that rule an object in S_AB minus S_AA reads the change whatever else S_AA holds; reading the mixed cell as UNDETERMINED would let a difference on an object that A/A2 shows stable escape attribution because a DIFFERENT object varied, which the object-level rule forbids.

The consequences are compatible (both: no merge); the verdict word is F1's.

3. RULING A2 (P6's pairs and denominator). The text (L19701): "TotalDasguptaCost DIFFERS in BOTH pairs (A/B and A/A2) (...), and every |relative TDC difference| over the three legs is <= 0.6% (the record's bareq512 range 0.577%); every |DendrogramPurity difference| <= 1e-13 and every |SphericalSilhouette difference| <= 1e-15."
 RULED: (a) the DIFFERS clause is scored on the two pairs it names, A/B and A/A2. (b) The three bound clauses ("every |relative TDC difference| over the three legs", "every |DendrogramPurity difference|", "every |SphericalSilhouette difference|") are scored on ALL THREE PAIRS, A/B, A/A2 and B/A2. THE ORCHESTRATOR'S READING ("over the three legs" = the two scored pairs; B/A2 descriptive) IS OVERRULED: within one prediction the sentence switches from "BOTH pairs (A/B and A/A2)" to "over the three legs", and its stated source, the bareq512 0.577%, is a RANGE over three builds (docs/campaign_review_2026-09-10.md L252, _as_of 4a5227f: TotalDasguptaCost 6.32024797272398E10 / 6.3315516862810326E10 / 6.2952338063323456E10), i.e. the largest of the three pairwise differences; B/A2 is not implied by the other two (|B - A2| can reach |B - A| + |A - A2|). A prediction is not narrowed pre-data without a reason in its text, and there is none. (c) Relative TDC difference = |TDC_x - TDC_y| / TDC_A, leg A's value AS WRITTEN IN THE SAME SOURCE, for all three pairs (leg A is the control of record). The denominator choice is immaterial at the record's scale: the R9 0.141% (L19607) is 0.14105% of the first value (2.2409421312346172E8) and 0.14124% of the second (2.2377813825989264E8). (d) Sources: every clause is scored on BOTH written sources the compare reads, the MAIN_taxonomy_quality.csv row and the tuning_ledger.csv last row. P6 HELD iff every clause holds on every pair it covers in both sources; FAILED otherwise, naming the failing (clause, pair, source); a value that is not numeric in both legs makes its clause UNDETERMINED (unscoreable), never HELD. P6 stays DESCRIPTIVE with no bar on D9 (as registered).
 REQUIRED CODE CHANGE R2 (d9b_compare.py, --verdict mode): the B/A2 P6 lines print the relative TDC difference against leg A's TDC of the same source (today p6_lines divides by the pair's first leg, B for B/A2), labelled "of A"; the A/B and A/A2 lines are unchanged (already of A). A test asserts the B/A2 relative value is computed on A's value.

 (a) A listed file (of the 21) absent in BOTH legs: INSTRUMENT REFUSAL (exit 2), nothing scored, the pair VOID (a failed precondition, never an outcome). The builder's 0.47-0.60 for S2-S6 and about 0.13 for reaching S3 admissible are simulation figures, relayed, not recomputed.  F2 (CONFIRMED). (a) "429 attempts <= 2% of the step's HTTP attempts" with one 429 in a step of n invocations gives n + 1 attempts at least; 1 / 25, 1 / 37, 1 / 49 are 4.0%, 2.7%, 2.04%, all > 2%: S1-S3 are admissible only at ZERO 429s. S4 (1 / 65 = 1.54%) and S5 (1 / 77 = 1.30%) admit one; S6 (3 / 153 = 1.96%) admits three.
 F3 (CONFIRMED). The registration counts every HTTP 429 attempt alike (1.3 (a); 1.2 ACCOUNTING) and rr ignores Retry-After (the finding of record GROK-NR-THROUGHPUT, L18908); N* is therefore a reading of the deployment UNDER rr's retry schedule and does not transfer as-is to judge_v2/pool.py, which honours Retry-After and paces by --max-rpm. The registration's X3 already reads "the probe then reads the DAY, not the deployment's quota" (Support (g), L19084).
 F4 (CONFIRMED). C1's bar on the step 8 -> 12 is rate(S5) >= 1.3 x rate(S4) while N grows 1.5x: 1.3 / 1.5 = 0.867, i.e. N* = 12 needs >= 86.7% scaling efficiency from 8 to 12 (the 1.3x bar on a doubling needs only 65%). N* = 12 is reachable but harder than the registration's "a doubling that buys < 30% is not taken" suggests (the last step is not a doubling; the knee line already prints "x1.5 in N, not a doubling").
 F5 (ARITHMETIC CONFIRMED; the hypothesis NOT established). If Azure books max_tokens (8,192) plus the prompt (about 1,400 tokens at the 5,369-byte median body) against 500,000 TPM, the ceiling is 500,000 / 9,600 = about 52 calls/min, reached at about S3 (rate(S1) = 60 / 3.63 = 16.5/min; x4 = 66 > 52). Under that hypothesis the falsifier's 50 calls/min at S3 stands within 4% of the ceiling, G <= about 52 / 16.5 = 3.2, and C1's 1.3x rule stops N* at 4 once the ceiling binds. The v290 record brackets the booking-based estimate as "too pessimistic" (about 58/min ran with no 429 on 09-23; L20210): the hypothesis is recorded as a reachability bound, not a fact.

The record shows that three evaluation fields vary run to run on identical code, config, seed and inputs (FRAMEWORK.md L297, the "Stage 2 determinism" Traceability row, and its two brackets; D9's R9 and D9b's C2 pair; the D9 post-run review's code cause). The recorded cause, identified by reading code and NOT yet shown by an instrumented run: (1) TaxonomyOperations.reassignQueries (TaxonomyOperations.kt L278 ff.; `leaf.queries.add(emb)` at L309, _as_of 7c6c588) appends to GraphNode.queries (a Collections.synchronizedList, GraphNode.kt L41) from parallel `async(Dispatchers.Default)` chunks, so membership and weights are deterministic but the LIST ORDER is thread-completion order; (2) TaxonomyMetrics.generateReport inherits that order (queryToEmbeddings, a LinkedHashMap, filled by iterating leaf.queries, L123-L129; uniqueQueryTexts = queryToEmbeddings.keys.toList(), L186); computeTotalDasguptaCost (AdditionalMetrics.kt L100-L149) draws 5,000 of C(m,2) pairs BY INDEX with Random(0) (L138) over that order, so a permuted list gives a different Monte-Carlo sample; computeTripletAccuracy (L235 ff., Random(seed) at L248) does the same; (3) dagDendrogramPurity (HierarchicalMetrics.kt L98 ff.; `pureSum += match.toDouble() / seen` at L160) and the silhouette block (TaxonomyMetrics.kt L282-L296, calling StatisticsUtils.calculateSphericalSilhouette at L292; `silhouetteSum += s` at StatisticsUtils.kt L606) accumulate floating-point sums in list order. Does a change that imposes a canonical order at exactly those four sites, and nowhere else, make the two files that carry these fields byte-reproducible, without moving any other output byte?

NOISE STATEMENT (the pre-change estimator noise; stated as a CV with its n and its source, never as a range, per the D9b post-run review's requirement (i)). Source: docs/reviews/POSTRUN_lcb_d9b.md at 5a51d52, section "**What the TDC spread says about the record's 0.6%.**" (and the D9b outcome L19897-L19974). TotalDasguptaCost on the AG_NEWS smoke arm (m = 1,400, 5,000 sampled pairs): CV 0.332% over n = 3 builds (D9b legs A / B / A2; range 0.640%) and CV 0.292% over n = 6 builds (D9b's three plus D9's three recoverable values; range 0.723%); a pairwise build-to-build difference has SD about sqrt(2) x 0.29% = 0.41% and a two-sided 95% band of about +/-0.8%. The bareq512 figure (the record's "0.58%", FRAMEWORK.md L297) is a RANGE of 3 builds (CV 0.29%, POSTRUN_lcb_d9.md "Magnitude"). DendrogramPurity: differences about 1e-14 absolute (max 2.0e-15 over D9b's pairs); SphericalSilhouette about 1e-16 or less (max 2.8e-17). THE MARGIN OF RECORD: max(1%, 2.8 x CV) = max(1%, 2.8 x 0.292% = 0.818%) = 1.0% of TDC (with the n = 3 CV: 2.8 x 0.332% = 0.930%, still 1.0%); 2.8 = 1.96 x sqrt(2) rounded, the two-sided 95% band of a difference of two builds. The margin binds every PRIOR TDC value, in any cross-build or Pareto comparison: a TDC difference below 1.0% of the smaller value is within noise and is not a decision. DP and SS differences below 1e-13 / 1e-15 absolute are within noise.

SCOPE OF THE DISCLOSURE (carried into the outcome, the ledger row and the record's does_not_show).
 (1) AFTER the change, TotalDasguptaCost and TripletAccuracy are a DIFFERENT (canonical) Monte-Carlo sample and DendrogramPurity / SphericalSilhouette a different summation order: post-change values will NOT match earlier values digit for digit, and a post-change value is not "the corrected" value of a pre-change one; both are draws of the same estimator (TDC relative difference expected within the 1.0% margin).
 (2) The recorded values that carry the old jitter (the D9 post-run review's list, "## Prior recorded numbers that may carry this jitter", re-counted by that review, not re-counted here): 149 MAIN_taxonomy_quality.csv files on disk across 29 run families outside _backup (largest h9_sweep 34, anchorfree 20, hygiene 12, multicorpus 10, dimsweep 10, splitratio 8, perf_replay 8), 17 git-tracked; 13 tracked tuning_ledger.csv copies; the *_thesis_metrics.csv / .json files (tracked: arena_math_frozen, arena_math_paired); the snapshot metadata (TaxonomySnapshotManager stores dendrogramPurity, sphericalSilhouette, totalDasguptaCost and tripletAccuracy per snapshot; snapshots_frozen.db is never modified by anything); the *_BASELINE_taxonomy_quality.csv files of cal_iso (KMEANS, WARD, RANDOMNULL; same metric code, thread dependence of their leaf.queries NOT verified). In the prose record: no numeric TDC, DP or SS value in docs/ or report/ except the D9 / D9b records themselves and the P7 caveat; the thesis appendix C (C_Metric_Definitions.tex L109-L119) only DEFINES the sampled estimator. Builds before cd037c0 (P7-FIX) also carried STRUCTURAL non-determinism. NOTHING RECORDED IS REVISED BY THIS CHANGE; no prior value is recomputed.
 (3) What the change does NOT remove: the Monte-Carlo ESTIMATOR error of TDC (5,000 of 979,300 pairs on this arm). It makes TDC reproducible for a fixed tree and input; between two DIFFERENT trees on the same point set the canonical order gives common random numbers (the same index pairs), which reduces but does not remove the estimator error of the difference, and no criterion here measures it. So the 1.0% margin stays the interim floor for cross-tree TDC comparisons AFTER the change too, until an estimator-SE study or a paired design replaces it.
 (4) tools/tuning/pareto.py (dominates() L105 ff., objective lists at L112-L113 _as_of 7c6c588, the D9b review's "L110 / L113"; blob:a6e82bcdcefd39c44603c7dcf5c5f8d7a784cd3b / sha256-lf16:380027e573f31349, working tree CRLF) minimises TotalDasguptaCost RAW and also maximises DendrogramPurity and SphericalSilhouette and minimises KappaShrinkageMean with no tolerance, so "strictly better" can be decided by jitter in the last digit. [REGISTRAR DECISION] The noise floor is a SEPARATE ITEM, PARETO-NOISE-FLOOR (queued in the same commit, drafted, NOT registered), NOT part of this change: it is a Python tool with its own reviewer scope, it must hold for every PRIOR ledger (which carries the jitter forever) and for post-change cross-tree comparisons (3), and binding it to this Kotlin change would put a criterion on a tool the legs never execute (a vacuous criterion under rule 8). Its requirement, carried from the D9b review: flag or refuse any dominance decided by a TDC difference below the margin of record (1.0%) or a DP / SS difference below 1e-13 / 1e-15, and print the margin on every run. UNTIL IT MERGES, the words of record for any pareto.py output are: "TDC-decided dominance below 1.0% is within noise and is not a decision".

Against the RECORDED mechanism (an unfixed order dependence in TDC): TDC differed in 9 of 9 pre-change build pairs on this arm; the one-sided 95% lower bound on the per-pair firing rate is 0.05^(1/9) = 0.717, so P(R1 = R2) <= 0.283 and C1's power to fire on an unfixed TDC is >= 0.717 at that bound and about 1 at the observed rate (and P(R1 = R2 = R3) <= P(R1 = R2)). Against an UNKNOWN residual non-determinism that moves a build with probability q (independently, to a distinct value): C1 misses it iff all three R legs agree, P = (1 - q)^3, so 80% power needs (1 - q)^3 <= 0.2, q >= 1 - 0.2^(1/3) = 0.415 (arithmetic: 0.2^(1/3) = 0.585). The resolution for a deterministic difference: one byte, power 1.

QUESTION. The site null draws from SeparationNullBySizeTest.kt `withinNodeCloud` (L553-L577 _as_of 3bee93b, file blob:0b6e176f; called by the test "siteNull - site-level and deflated nulls on every accepted split of the frozen artifact"): mu + C^T g / sqrt(m) over the site's own centred members, renormalised to the sphere, i.e. a ONE-component Gaussian at the site's own mean and covariance. Each draw is then scored by the separation of the production splitter's best cut, and "dJ rewards elongation" (TaxonomySplitter.kt L456-L462), so a genuinely bimodal node, whose covariance is elongated along its own between-mode axis, is scored against an inflated null (separation_null_by_size.md "### Limit on the interpretation"). A full-covariance Gaussian likelihood ratio is invariant to linear maps of the space it is computed in, so the node's elongation lies INSIDE H0 there. This test KEEPS H0 (the same generator) and changes ONLY the statistic.

HYGIENE. Geometry only. NO label, key, judge verdict, board or eval result is read; no LLM call, no embedding call. SUPPORT.
 (a) Deciding denominator: C1 = 3 sites of the frozen tree (members n = 549, 402, 292), each decided by B = 199 independent null draws (999 on escalation). No cluster structure among draws (independent seeded streams): Kish mean cluster size 1. The descriptive D1-D6 run over 66 / 69 / 60 / 87 NESTED sites (a site's members include its descendants'), which are not independent units.
 (b) DEFF and its source: C1: 1 BY CONSTRUCTION (independent parametric draws; declared, not transported, not measured). D1-D6: > 1 through nesting, NOT measured, declared unknown.
 (c) n_eff = n / DEFF: C1: 199 / 1 = 199 draws per deciding site (999 on escalation). D1-D6: not stated (DEFF unknown).
 (d) The SE reported (the Monte-Carlo SE of q at the bar): sqrt(0.05 x 0.95 / 199) = sqrt(0.0002387) = 0.0155 at B = 199; sqrt(0.0475 / 999) = sqrt(0.00004755) = 0.0069 at B = 999. For D3 (two proportions near 0.2 at 69 and 60 sites, nesting ignored, so a LOWER bound): sqrt(0.2 x 0.8 / 69 + 0.2 x 0.8 / 60) = sqrt(0.002319 + 0.002667) = sqrt(0.004986) = 0.0706.
 (e) MDE at 80% power (two-sided 0.05; 2.80 SE): C1 per site 2.80 x 0.0155 = 0.043 at B = 199 and 2.80 x 0.0069 = 0.019 at B = 999: after escalation a site whose exact tail probability lies outside [0.031, 0.069] is resolved at 80%. D3: 2.80 x 0.0706 = 0.198 (a lower bound).
 (f) VERDICT LINE: C1 is SCOREABLE per site at the point: the prediction P2 (CS at the floor, q_LR = 0.005) lies 0.045 from the bar, above the B = 199 MDE of 0.043, and a Philosophy site's q is scored against the B = 999 MDE of 0.019 whenever it falls in the escalation band. The branch predictions P1 and P3 are probabilities over the outcomes of a scoreable criterion and are scored HELD / FAILED as events. D1-D7 are DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY (no bar; nested units; D3's MDE of 0.198 is ten times the J difference of +0.0196, so no transfer sentence is licensed either way).
 (g) STRUCTURAL LEG (reachable at infinite budget?): YES. As B grows, q_LR converges to the exact tail probability of the observed LR under each site's own Gaussian null, and nothing in the statistic ties the three sites to the same side (each is computed on its own members against its own null). Two structural limits, neither of which makes C1 unreachable: EM gives a local maximum (the same fitting on the null draws keeps the test calibrated; a missed optimum costs power); and the smallest deciding site (n 292) has 2.2 points per parameter of the 2-component model at p = 10 (131).
 SCOPE LIMIT (carried into every sentence of record): the LR is invariant to linear maps ONLY INSIDE the top-p PCA subspace of the site; elongation outside those p axes and the curvature of the sphere projection are NOT covered by the invariance and enter only through the generator.

READOUTS AND CRITERIA (the TOPIC-PARTITION-20NG C1 form, L10286-L10287; in each clause the POINT decides the seed-spread leg and the INTERVAL decides the CI leg, and the two legs are ONE conjunctive clause stated once per criterion; no UNDETERMINED branch exists).
 C1 PURITY: HELD iff M1(T) - M1(V0) > spread_V(M1) AND the paired bootstrap 95% CI of M1(T) - M1(V0) excludes 0 on the positive side; FAILED otherwise. The observable that fails it at the planned n: a difference at or below the V seed spread, or a CI that reaches 0 (e.g. T 0.727 against V0 0.725 with a spread of 0.008).
 C2 KEY INFORMATION: HELD iff M2(T) - M2(V0) > spread_V(M2) AND F6's paired bootstrap 95% CI excludes 0 on the positive side; FAILED otherwise; the failing observable likewise.
 L1 LOSS FLAG (the limitation reading; scored): FIRES iff for M1 or for M2, M(T) - M(V0) < -spread_V(M) AND the paired 95% CI excludes 0 on the negative side.
 BESIDE, REPORTED ONLY: the same three against K0 (with spread_K); M3 and M4 for every arm; O on every measure; the V nearest-mean assignment.
 M4 IS DESCRIPTIVE BY DESIGN: V maximises the training likelihood of exactly this model family, so M4 favours V by construction; a T deficit on M4 is expected and is not a limitation; a T advantage would be reported as notable, not scored.

The seed-spread leg does NOT shrink with n (it is a property of V's optimiser), so C1 / C2 are reachable only if the true difference exceeds spread_V; if spread_V exceeds every plausible difference, a WIN is unreachable at any budget and (T-1) is the only readable outcome.   p_site = (k + 1) / (reps + 1) (the add-one p; smallest 1/301 = 0.003322).
  CP: the exact two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson interval on the null exceedance probability from k of reps (beta quantiles; [0, 1 - 0.025^(1/300)] = [0, 0.012221] at k = 0).
  FLAT BH: the Benjamini-Hochberg step-up at q = 0.05 over the m sites of ONE tree (m = 70 / 69 / 60 / 66), per tree separately; the Benjamini-Yekutieli count (c(m) = sum 1/i) printed beside, DESCRIPTIVE (BH over nested sites assumes positive regression dependence, not shown).
  HIERARCHICAL (PREFIX-CLOSED) BH: the site ancestors of a site are the sites reachable upward along parentIds (every path); its FAMILY is keyed by its nearest site ancestor along parentIds[0], and the TOP FAMILY is the set of sites with no site ancestor (the anchor sites of an anchored tree, whose anchored root is not a site; the root of an anchor-free tree). BH at q = 0.05 is run in the top family; a site enters its family's BH only when ALL its site ancestors are rejected, and a family is run once its key site is rejected; iterate to the deepest level. The rejected set is prefix-closed by construction. Multi-parent sites are counted and printed. The tree-wide FDR of this set is NOT claimed to be 0.05 (the per-family level is; Yekutieli 2008 bounds the tree-wide rate by a multiple of q that is not estimated here). [PRE-DATA RULING 2026-09-26 (A3, the orchestrator; recorded by the registrar, insertion only): the builder's multi-parent family rule is accepted (a family runs once every outside site ancestor of its members is decided; a member not yet eligible is not counted in m_f); inert on the data of record (0 multi-parent sites). 3. THE RULINGS ON MIX-LRT-SITE (the orchestrator's; each checked against the registration).
 A1 SEED STREAM. SeedSequence(20260926, spawn_key=(tree_index, row)) per site; draw b = its b-th spawned child, spawn_key=(tree_index, row, b); tree_index 0..3 in the REGISTERED tree order (frozen, af_clean_s42, o0_clean_s42, af_bareq512_s42: the order of INPUTS PINNED NOW, L20607-L20610, and of the script's TREES); row = the 0-based data-row index of the site in its CSV; the observed fit's random_states from the site's own SeedSequence. REGISTRAR: CONSISTENT, and it CORRECTS a departure: the registration says "One numpy SeedSequence per (tree, site)" (L20617), whereas the build's spawn_key=(row,) gave row r of every tree the SAME stream. A1 departs from the builder's provisional choice, not from the registration.
 A2 LEAF-FIT SEEDS. SeedSequence(20260926, spawn_key=(tree_index, 1000000 + node number)), node number = the integer of the leaf id (n00000013 -> 13). REGISTRAR: CONSISTENT (the registration is silent; no key collides with a site key, whose second element is a row index < 1,000,000, or with a draw key, which has length 3).
 A3 FAILED FITS. A failed fit in a null draw or at a leaf is EXCLUDED AND COUNTED; if MORE THAN 1% of a site's draws fail, or the observed fit fails, the site is VOID; at a deciding site VOID applies as already registered. REGISTRAR: CONSISTENT (the registration names VOID only for the deciding sites, L20622; for the other sites it had no handling, and the build refused the whole analysis with "no registered handling; registrar ruling needed"). The registrar's READINGS of A3 (binding on the build unless the orchestrator overrules them before the READY): (i) "failed fit" is the build's definition, an exception in the fit or a non-finite log-likelihood; a non-converged EM is NOT a failure (it is counted and printed; the null draws are fitted the same way); (ii) at a non-deciding site, p = 10: with f failed draws the site's q is (1 + c) / (B - f + 1) over the B - f admitted draws, and f is printed beside it; at B = 199, "more than 1%" means f >= 2 (1 / 199 = 0.50%, 2 / 199 = 1.01%), so f <= 1 is admitted and f >= 2 VOIDs the site; (iii) at a DECIDING site (frozen n00000013, n00000014, n00000055), ANY failed p = 10 fit, observed or null, up to the site's final B, VOIDs C1 as registered ("a failed fit at a deciding site"); the 1% allowance does not apply there; (iv) the descriptive p = 5 / p = 20 legs (B = 49): 1% of 49 is 0.49, so ANY failed fit in a leg VOIDs that leg's q at that site (printed VOID), never the site's p = 10 row; (v) a VOID site is excluded from D1-D7 and COUNTED: every per-tree denominator is printed net of VOID sites ("n of 66 - v VOID"); (vi) a failed leaf fit is excluded from its site's leaf median and counted; a site whose qualifying leaves all failed reads NA for D5 (printed with the count). [RULING 2026-09-26 (the orchestrator's, pre-data, accepting delta READY 1's proposal, e8a9eed DC2 (b); recorded by the registrar, insertion only): a cell whose relative eigengap at the deciding p is below 1e-10 counts as a FAILED FIT under A3 (so, by reading (iii), it VOIDs C1 at a deciding site); no code change; inert on every measured cell (deciding sites observed 1.22e-2 / 9.09e-2 / 2.86e-2 at p = 10, their 2,997 draws >= 4.47e-4, the smallest measured anywhere 1.28e-4); the post-run review re-derives the 282 observed sites' gaps. See docs/judge_v2_program.md L21276-L21324 (section "## Registrar's record 2026-09-26 (insertion only; zero calls; nothing run; BEFORE the fresh re-run) — MIX-LRT-SITE DELTA READY 1 ...", _as_of the commit that writes it, parent 5e57cd2, re-grepped), item 3.]

The reading of record is PER-TREE: (R-a) applies only if C1 HELD and, ON EVERY TREE, the D2 superset share >= 0.8 and D1 exceeds the J count; the pooled-superset reading is printed beside it, marked "not of record". The EIGEN-FACTOR GENERATOR mu + Z diag(s) V^T / sqrt(m) (C = U diag(s) V^T the thin SVD of the site's m x sliceDim centred member matrix, Z n x rank(C) iid N(0, 1), then unit-normalised) is ADOPTED for the null draws: before normalisation each row is Gaussian with mean mu and covariance V diag(s^2) V^T / m = C^T C / m, the same law as the literal mu + g C / sqrt(m), so it is EXACT IN DISTRIBUTION (not draw for draw); the orchestrator's figure is about 47 CPU-min for the p = 10 leg, within the cap (not re-derived by the registrar; the patched dry-run re-projects it).  B5 C1 HELD WITH L1 FIRED (ON M2). RULED BY THE REGISTRAR, DERIVED (not AMBIGUOUS): (T-5) takes precedence; the outcome is recorded JOINED as "C1 HELD / L1 FIRED on M2", reading (T-5), NO SENTENCE, the research-lead's synthesis. DERIVATION from the registration's own text: (1) L1 cannot fire on M1 when C1 HELD (M1(T) - M1(V0) cannot be both > spread_V with a CI above 0 and < -spread_V with a CI below 0), so the case is exactly "a WIN on purity with a LOSS on key information"; (2) (T-5)'s own example (L20706) is "C2 HELD with L1 fired on M1", a win on key information with a loss on purity: the case at hand is its mirror image under the exchange M1 <-> M2, and nothing in the registration treats the two measures asymmetrically for this purpose (C1 and C2 have the same form, L20696-L20697; L1 is symmetric over M1 and M2, L20698); (3) every other reading states L1's status ((T-1) and (T-2) "L1 not fired", (T-4) "L1 FIRED"), and (T-3)'s parenthesis "(with or without C2)" qualifies C2 ONLY: it is silent on L1, so (T-3) does not claim the L1-fired case, while (T-5) claims "any mixed pattern"; (4) (T-3)'s sentence "the tree is a better partition on MMLU-Pro" would be written beside a registered LOSS flag on key information, which the table's structure (a win reading and a limitation reading are separate rows) does not license. CONSEQUENCES, unchanged by the ruling: F1 FIRES (C1 HELD and L1 FIRES, L20727: both triggers printed); P7 FAILED (HELD only on (T-1), L20724); the second-seed requirement of (T-3) is moot because no sentence is written. O1 (REGISTRAR'S OBJECTION, to the brief's premise, not to its request): L1 is NOT descriptive: the registration calls it "L1 LOSS FLAG (the limitation reading; scored)" (L20698) and F1 fires on it (L20727); B5 is ruled on the table's own example and does not depend on L1's status.

Gaps: eigh at n < d, ordering, ties"; not the registrar's and not the author's). RULING: A CELL WHOSE RELATIVE EIGENGAP AT THE DECIDING p IS BELOW 1e-10 COUNTS AS A FAILED FIT UNDER A3. The relative gap is the READY's: (lambda_p - lambda_{p+1}) / lambda_p, lambda the Rayleigh quotients ||X_c v_i||^2 of the axes `pca_basis` returns. 9. THE WORDS OF RECORD (for the talk, the thesis and the paper; verbatim from the review, section "## 5. Talk words").
 MAY SAY: "We tested whether a Gaussian-mixture likelihood ratio (1 vs 2 full-covariance components in each split's top-10 PCA subspace, calibrated against the same Gaussian site null) could tell a contaminated split from a genuine topic. It could not. It certified every split on all four trees (282 of 282, each at the minimum p-value 1/200), including the Philosophy sites it should have left uncertified, and a reviewer check found it rejects the same null inside the leaves too. The embeddings are non-Gaussian everywhere (skewed and clumpy), so a mixture LR measures texture, not modes. It cannot discriminate. The size-matched J site null remains the certificate, and its certified splits are a strict subset of the LR's (6/66, 14/69, 11/60, 10/87)."
 SHORT FORM: "A Gaussian-mixture LR certifies every split, so it cannot discriminate; the matched J site null (splitter-statistic null) remains the discriminating certificate." THE LONG FORM OF RECORD (verbatim from the file's section 0.1; inserted ONCE here, as the ruling's section 5 item 1 asks; it governs the programme by rule, as rule 12 did, so no inline brackets are required):

> [P-FAM — RULED 2026-09-27 by the judge-design-specialist (docs/reviews/RULING_w0_p2dca_family.md; plan A4 / B6 W0 / B7 item 6; insertion only; zero calls; no recorded number moves). THE p2dca JUDGED FAMILY IS HISTORY, NOT EVIDENCE.
> MEMBERSHIP. A readout is in the family if any of three things holds.
> (a) It contains a judge verdict, or a reference or judge solve scored against the key, produced on matches drawn from pool p2dca21ab5f4ef3ae as the held-out side of the split of record. The judge, recipe, prompt, schedule, language and date do not matter. The r8-era runs (x8, x12 v1, R2, the rubric line, the J-series) are in, and so is the post-incident STACK-v2 work (R3, ARENA-V2 x12 and x20, ARENA-13, GROK-CALIB, the Kotlin board, the v1 canary, placement).
> (b) It is computed on the schedule or judged-question set of such a run in order to bound, compare with or fit a judged number (e.g. ORACLE-BOARD, KEY-NOISE-CEILING).
> (c) It imports a quantity from (a) or (b) into its criterion, scale, comparator or simulation parameters. The bracket then attaches to that quantity only (e.g. K46's nu / beta scale; BFCL-JUDGED-PILOT's NONE and CACHED_SOLVE rungs).
> Membership follows the run's split. It does not follow the question's id or a printed pool id. A verdict produced under another split, on a question that is also in p2dca, is not a family verdict (K46's ONE class, split pv2_41dbd3dbcd399df0). CERT-CORPUS prints p2dca but reads GEN-ARENA's union re-derivation, so it is not in the family either.
> Key-only readouts on p2dca are NOT in the family. They carry rule 12's "id-disjoint only" and, where tree-filed, "filed by a qwen3 tree". Frozen-tree geometry is governed by the r8 paragraph and its geometry-only carve-out.
> WHY. Every member is on an id-only split: 37 exact / 70 norm-v1 EVAL texts sit among bareq512_s42's members. The family's central objects carry further defects:
> - The x12 schedule, and every board and sample drawn from it (R3; ARENA-V2 x12 / x20; GROK-CALIB; the Kotlin board), was cut on the 87 cells of the frozen tree 20260727_042523. That tree's routing was in-sample for 2,437 of the 3,445 judgeable questions.
> - The r8-era cell rubrics were induced on corpora that held those questions with the answer ticked. The STACK-v2 anchor rubrics withheld p2dca by id only, with 28 twins in their induction corpora.
> - The recipe of record was selected on R3's 944 key-decidable pairs with no family-wise control; 0.865 is that sample's maximum (FW L79).
> - Every family board is among the 51 of 58 caches that cannot tell NON_TERMINATED from wrong (JUDGE-FINISH-AUDIT).
> The directions of these biases are unsigned. Content-closed replacements are registered or drafted (RP04, RP19, RP20, RP21).
> USE. A family number is written in only four ways:
> (1) DISCLOSURE, in the one first-iteration paragraph.
> (2) DESIGN PROVENANCE, in the voice of a decision ("the recipe was fixed, and the lines of CTX §5 closed, on the first-iteration sample"), never in the voice of a finding.
> (3) A PLANNING PRIOR inside a registration (Support, prediction, power, threshold). A content-closed outcome may withdraw it and may never promote it.
> (4) An ENGINEERING FIXTURE for byte-identity and regression tests of code.
> It is never a clause of the claim table, an abstract or results sentence, a licence, a thesis board, or a deciding comparator of a new criterion ("within delta of" or "above" a family number). No content-closed number is written as confirming, replicating or "consistent with" one.
> Methods, estimators, rules and guards developed on family data carry no bracket; their family-fitted parameters do. The record's refusals stand without the family. The lines closed in CTX §5 stay closed, and this bracket is not a reason to reopen them.
> A later bracket on a family row may change the row's number or words, but not its membership. Only a bracket naming this ruling can change the class.]

QUESTION AND KIND. A claim registration: it fixes, before any of its deciding tests is registered or run, which outcomes move the taxonomy clause of the framing of record (SQ3), so no reading is chosen after the fact. It computes nothing itself; every criterion is scored from the outcome file of a named deciding test. Plan R-A; framing copy L104 (bracketed B6).
THE EXPECTED SENTENCE (registered verbatim; the partition clause is the licensed sentence of the FLAT-MIX-MMLU outcome attached to its object): "the taxonomy buys filing, a certificate, support and names; on MMLU-Pro its cells are a worse partition than a flat mixture at the same granularity (af_clean_s42, one draw; the anchored control ties, reported only; mechanism not identified); no routing gain is shown." It widens only through the registered reading tables of FLAT-GENERALITY, EMBEDDER-CROSS-FLAT and SUPERGPQA stage 1; it is NEVER generalised to "trees" or "this construction" (plan B8 words).
HYGIENE. None of its own; each deciding test carries its split word (CK-CLOSE-v1 for the v2 tree; rule 12). Declared arena cells stay the default (S1).
INSTRUMENT. None; the deciding outcome files are: UNION-AF-ROUTE's outcome (queue UNION-AF-ROUTE, drafted, not registered; script absent) for lever leg L-1; ARCH-V2-E-T's G13 and G12 outcomes (queue ARCH-V2-E-T, drafted) for L-2 and N-1. F-TAX is scored by the registrar when the LAST of them is adjudicated.
READOUTS AND CRITERIA (each leg: the INTERVAL decides the CI clause and the POINT decides the spread clause, stated once, conjunctive; no leg can fire together with another leg over the same bar).
 L-1 (lever, routing): FIRES iff UNION-AF-ROUTE's two-stage 95% interval of G_AF - G_K,per-source lies wholly above 0 AND the point exceeds spread_K (max - min of G_K over the comparator's registered seeds). Comparator: k-means within source at AF's per-source leaf counts, seed policy registered there. Fails to fire (observable at the planned n): an interval that reaches 0, or a point <= spread_K.
 L-2 (lever, filing): FIRES iff ARCH-V2-E-T's G13 paired interval of flatLeaf filing precision minus class-conditional k-means at matched per-class prototypes lies wholly above 0 AND the point exceeds the comparator's seed spread. Fails likewise.
 N-1 (narrowing, certificate): FIRES iff on the v2 MMLU-Pro tree the hierarchical-BH set at per-family q = 0.05 (300 reps; CERT-RESOLUTION's instrument) contains NO depth-1 site. Printed beside, never deciding: the per-site p95 count against its binomial null (P(>= 5 of 70 | 5%) = 0.272). UNDETERMINED-BY-SUPPORT when the tree's top family cannot reach p <= 0.05 / m at 300 reps (1/301 <= 0.05 / m iff m <= 15) or the corpus is below the site-null floor; UNDETERMINED until reps are raised by registration. Fails to fire: any depth-1 site in the set.
 READING TABLE (fixed now): L-1 or L-2 fires and N-1 does not -> the sentence moves to "the taxonomy is an evaluation lever: <the leg that fired>" with its object; N-1 fires and neither lever -> "a filing device only" (the certificate clause is withdrawn for the presented tree); neither -> the expected sentence stands; a lever AND N-1 -> recorded joined, no sentence, the research-lead's synthesis. "Parity" of any kind is written only through a TOST with delta and interval form registered before code; otherwise "neither a cost nor parity is shown".
SUPPORT (F-TAX adds no inference; each leg's Support is its deciding test's and is registered there).
 (a) Deciding denominators: those of UNION-AF-ROUTE (6,153 union EVAL items of pv2_1575de61bb20e977 if it is re-pointed to v2, else 6,482 paeec, id-disjoint only) and of the E-T tree's held-out set and site table; not fixed here.
 (b) DEFF and source: carried by each deciding registration; none declared here.
 (c)-(e) n_eff, SE, MDE: carried; none computed here (a number computed here would be a second, unregistered instrument).
 (f) VERDICT LINE: F-TAX is a READING RULE, not a scored test: DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY in itself; each leg is SCOREABLE or not by its own registration's verdict line, and a leg whose deciding test registers DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY cannot fire (it reads "not fired, by support"). GPQA, LCB, 20NG, BFCL, Multi-SWE, the v2 split stores): colliding families EXCLUDED from both sides and counted per store (registrar's reconciliation (ii)). Policy: per scored discipline, the TRAIN argmax model (tie-break: higher pooled TRAIN accuracy, then name); best single: the pooled TRAIN argmax; EVAL items of unscored disciplines take the best single (they contribute 0 to G). SELECTION RULE (GATE; fixed now). For each embedder, d* = the slice maximising mean-over-seeds fine NMI on GATE (GATE items filed to TRAIN centroids), averaged over the 3 corpora: ONE slice per embedder. Ties within 0.001 go to the smaller d. The selection is written and hashed before EVAL is opened; per-corpus GATE maxima are printed, never used.

READOUTS AND CRITERIA.
 EQ1 (deciding; TOST; the INTERVAL decides EQUIVALENT, POINT AND INTERVAL decide DIFFERENT; stated here once). Per corpus D_q = mean_{s=0..19} NMI_EVAL(Q8, d_q*) - mean_{s=0..19} NMI_EVAL(Q4, d_q*) at K_f. delta_c = the corpus's IN-RUN qwen3 seed spread at d_q*, defined as max - min over seeds 0-4 of the Q4 arm's EVAL fine NMI (the family's spread, the one every embedder contrast's bar used; the identity precondition makes it 0.01428 / 0.00417 / 0.01043; the 20-seed spread of each arm is printed beside, DESCRIPTIVE). SE_total = sqrt(SE_boot^2 + var_seed / 20), SE_boot = the BASIC component bootstrap SE of D_q (B 2,000, partitions fixed, S0's C1 rule), var_seed = the sample variance over s = 0..19 of the per-seed difference NMI_EVAL(Q8, s) - NMI_EVAL(Q4, s). EQUIVALENT iff D_q +/- 1.645 x SE_total lies inside (-delta_c, +delta_c); DIFFERENT iff |D_q| > delta_c AND D_q +/- 1.96 x SE_total excludes 0 (direction printed); NEITHER otherwise (the two are exclusive: EQUIVALENT forces |D_q| < delta_c). VERDICT: NOT-A-CONFOUND iff EQUIVALENT on >= 2 of 3; CONFOUND-CANDIDATE iff DIFFERENT on >= 2 of 3; MIXED (UNDETERMINED, a registered outcome) otherwise. The two named verdicts cannot fire together (each needs 2 of 3 corpora).
 EQ2 (DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY): per text, cos(Q8, Q4) after slicing to d_q* and renormalising; median and min over the 57,350 texts, and per corpus.
 Fail observables at the planned n: EQ1 MIXED or CONFOUND-CANDIDATE (F-EQ fires on CONFOUND-CANDIDATE).

     true source (paired on that intersection, its n printed).
  A3 depth curve. Frontier F(d) = union nodes at depth d plus leaves shallower than d, d = 2..7. Tree filing at depth d =
     the flatLeaf leaf's ancestor in F(d), named by the TRAIN-majority class of the TRAIN items filed (flatLeaf, train CSV)
     into its subtree. Depth-matched comparator KC(d)_s: KC with k_c(d) = max(1, #F(d) nodes whose TRAIN majority is c).
     D(d) = P_tree(d) - P(KC(d)_0). At d = 2, k_c = 1 for every class, so KC(2) = NCC exactly (asserted). d = 1 prints
     source accuracy only (a corpus root names one class; not a class filing). Also printed: D13 stratified by the depth of
     the item's flatLeaf leaf (2, 3, 4, 5, >= 6; EVAL items per stratum fixed in Support).
  A4 (the depth contrast) Delta = D(leaf) - D(2) = D13 - [P_tree(2) - P_NCC], paired.

DATA LEG REQUIRED (NOT registered here): a closed-set intent-classification solve (60 MASSIVE intents) by a roster of R models on N TRAIN items stratified by S0's K_f 60 cells (planning 30 per cell, N = 1,800, seeded), keyed by gold intent; calls = N x R (7,200 at R 4; 21,600 at R 12, above the 14,000 day cap); PAID, PRICED BY THE COST-ESTIMATOR, roster / prompt / decoding fixed in its own registration, the author's go needed above the day cap. Only TRAIN items are solved: the decision for an EVAL item is its cell's TRAIN policy, so neither the originals nor the variants need an answer.
PRIOR RESULTS TOUCHED (none revised). INTENT-TRANSFER-S0 C4 FAILED / F4 FIRED (S 0.7598; supervised-centroid label stability 0.834, kNN-1 0.829; random same-intent co-filing 0.692); INTENT-S0-SLOTSWAP-MECH M1 / M2 HELD (flips track boundary distance and swapped share). No routing gain on intent corpora is of record.
HYGIENE. Cells, variants and components exactly S0 C4's (S0 pins; qwen3 256 seed 0; CK-CLOSE-v1 hash sides); the policy fitted on TRAIN items only (the data leg's file, sha-pinned); EVAL origins and variants read once; nothing writes a DB of record.
INSTRUMENT. tools/analysis/slotswap_decision.py, TO BE BUILT once the data leg's file exists, importing intent_transfer_s0.py (blob:f662ceb19738f515972871f5963f5dcfc764a271) UNCHANGED for the C4 cells and variants. Policy: best(c) = argmax_m acc_TRAIN(m, c) over the roster, ties to the globally better model, a cell with fewer than 20 solved TRAIN items backed off to the global best model (count printed). R_dec = share of variants with best(cell(v)) = best(cell(o)); R_flip = the same share among variants whose cell changed; R_chance = the same share for the origin cell against a cell drawn at random in proportion to EVAL origin mass (excluding the origin cell). Two-stage bootstrap B 2,000: TRAIN items resampled within cells (the policy refitted per draw, so the argmax's noise enters) x variant components. Outcome write-once experiment_results/intent_transfer/slotswap_decision_outcome.txt.
 PRECONDITION DEGENERATE (a failed precondition, not an outcome): SD1 reads NOT EVALUABLE if the TRAIN policy has fewer than 2 distinct best models each owning >= 10% of EVAL origin mass, or R_chance >= 0.90 (decisions would be stable because there is nothing to route).
READOUTS AND CRITERIA.
 SD1 (DECIDING; the INTERVAL decides): D_dec = R_flip - R_chance. HELD ("when a slot swap moves the cell, the routed model stays more often than chance") iff the 95% interval lies wholly above 0; FAILED iff wholly at or below 0; UNDETERMINED otherwise. Fail observable at the planned n: an interval reaching 0 (for HELD).
 SD2 (DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY, never a criterion): R_dec with its interval beside S 0.760. R_dec >= S holds by construction (an unmoved cell keeps its decision), so a criterion on R_dec against S would be vacuous (rule 8).
 READING (fixed now): SD1 HELD -> "addresses move, decisions stay more often than chance: of the variants whose cell changed, R_flip kept the routed model (chance R_chance)"; UNDETERMINED -> "not shown"; FAILED -> F-SD.
SUPPORT (planning; the data leg's N and R fix the final figures, re-stated at its registration).
 (a) Deciding denominator: the flipped variants, about (1 - 0.760) x 3,222 = 773, in about as many components (Kish 1.0093 on the 3,222).
 (b) DEFF 1.0093, MEASURED by S0 / SLOTSWAP on the same components; the policy's argmax noise enters through the TRAIN stage of the bootstrap (no closed form).
 (c) n_eff = 773 / 1.0093 = 766.
 (d) SE: R_flip at 0.40: sqrt(0.40 x 0.60 / 766) = 0.0177; R_chance from the policy refits, a DECLARED pilot assumption 0.030 (30 TRAIN items per cell); SE(D_dec) <= sqrt(0.0177^2 + 0.030^2) = sqrt(3.13e-4 + 9.00e-4) = 0.0348 (conservative: the two are positively correlated across refits).
 (e) MDE80 = 2.80 x 0.0348 = 0.097 (bar 0).
 (f) VERDICT LINE: SD1 SCOREABLE, thin: the predicted +0.15 lies 0.053 beyond 0.097; DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY if the data leg's N falls below about 20 per cell (R_chance's SE then exceeds about 0.04). SD2 DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY.
 (g) STRUCTURAL LEG: unreachable when DEGENERATE (one model wins nearly every cell, R_chance -> 1 and D_dec <= 0 by construction): stated now; otherwise reachable, and more TRAIN items per cell shrink only the R_chance term.
PREDICTIONS (80% intervals; probabilities by Brier; priors weak, no intent answers exist). P1 DEGENERATE 0.35 (strong LLMs classify MASSIVE intents at similar accuracy; one model may win most cells). Conditional on not DEGENERATE: P2 R_flip 0.40 [0.20, 0.65], R_chance 0.25 [0.10, 0.50], D_dec +0.15 [-0.05, +0.35]; SD1 HELD 0.55, UNDETERMINED 0.40, FAILED 0.05. P3 R_dec 0.86 [0.80, 0.93].
FALSIFIER. F-SD fires iff SD1 FAILED. It overturns the reading "addresses move, decisions stay" for cell routing on the easiest known answer: slot swaps that move the cell move the routed model at least as often as a random cell change; F4's qualifier ("surface-sensitive") then extends from cells to routing decisions. No recorded number is revised.
WHAT THIS RESULT WILL NOT SHOW (fixed before data). A routing gain on intent corpora (no gain is computed); anything about tree leaves, capability text or MMLU-Pro; natural paraphrase (slot swaps only); judged decisions (the policy is keyed accuracy); robustness of the decision's VALUE (only its identity); any roster beyond the data leg's.
COST AND CONSEQUENCE. Readout: 0 calls, CPU minutes. Data leg: N x R solve calls (planning 7,200-21,600), PAID, UNPRICED, UNREGISTERED: the cost-estimator prices it, the research-lead fixes the roster and prompt in its own registration, the author decides (day cap, and the 4k rule's spirit for a paid leg of this size). Agent time: engine-coder about 2 h after the data exist. Consequence: whether SQ5's F4 qualifier extends to routing decisions or stops at cells.
